author: raorbit
body:
## What

The app showed two stacked title bars: the native Windows frame on top and the renderer's custom `WindowFrame` chrome (with inert placeholder min/max/close glyphs) below it.

- `main.ts`: create the `BrowserWindow` with `frame: false` and add `window:minimize` / `window:maximizeToggle` / `window:close` IPC handlers, registered with the same `removeHandler` + `handle` idempotent pattern as `dialog:selectFolder`.
- `bridge-contract.ts` + `preload.ts`: expose `minimizeWindow` / `maximizeToggleWindow` / `closeWindow` on the sandboxed contextBridge.
- `WindowFrame.tsx`: the placeholder glyphs become real buttons with aria labels; they no-op outside Electron (plain browser dev) where the bridge is absent.
- `window-frame.css`: button reset + hover states (Windows-style red close), controls bled to the bar's top-right corner.

## Why

The custom title bar was always the intended chrome (mockup section 07); the placeholder comment in `WindowFrame.tsx` explicitly deferred wiring the controls through the main process. With the native frame gone, the duplicate bar disappears and the custom controls do the real work.

## Reviewer notes

- **Close still hides to the tray.** The custom X calls `mainWindow.close()`, which flows through the existing `close` handler (preventDefault → hide → tray hint), so recording survives a close exactly as before.
- Dragging and double-click-to-maximize already worked: the CSS had `-webkit-app-region: drag` on the bar and `no-drag` on the controls. Resize borders stay native (`thickFrame` default).
- **Known trade-off:** a fully frameless window loses the Win11 Snap Layouts flyout on hover over maximize (that requires native/overlay caption buttons). Win+arrow and edge-drag snapping still work. The alternative (`titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` + `titleBarOverlay`) was considered and rejected to keep the mockup's custom glyphs.
- Verified: `npm run typecheck` and the app vitest suite (246 tests) pass. Visual check needs an Electron relaunch; this touches the Electron main, so a packaged install needs a rebuilt installer, not a core-jar swap.

author: jtb75
body:
**PR 2 of the caregiver Firebase→Authentik wave.** Extends the dual-run to caregivers. Fully inert when `auth_provider=firebase`. Stacks on #76 (`trusted_contacts.external_subject_id`).

## Design (from the prior investigation)
- **Targets the LIVE caregiver auth path** — the email-based `dashboard/activity/alerts` + `/my-charges` — **not** the dead `contact_id`-claim path in `get_current_caregiver` (unreachable; guards only stubs; left untouched).
- Caregivers have **no `users` row**: they authenticate as the PERSON (opaque Authentik subject) and act for a member via the existing explicit `user_id` gate (`caregiver_authorized_for_member`), unchanged. Member selection is preserved exactly.

## Changes
- **`/auth/login` admits caregivers** (`auth_authentik.py`): after the member lookups (by sub, then email) miss, `_try_caregiver_login` matches the **verified** email against active `trusted_contacts` rows on the **maintenance/BYPASSRLS** session, lazy-backfills `external_subject_id=sub`, and mints a session. A row already bound to a **different** subject → 403 (rolls back, no overwrite — mirrors the member subject-mismatch guard). Neither member nor caregiver → the existing `signup_refused` 403.
- **Refactored the member session-mint into `_mint_session`** (shared cookie/CSRF/mobile-gating). Member path byte-identical — all 40 existing auth tests pass.
- **`resolve_caregiver_session(request) → email | None`** (`principal.py`): inert when firebase (first line); resolves session subject → verified email via the maintenance session (a `users` row by subject for a member-who-is-also-caregiver, else an active `trusted_contacts` row). Email is IdP-verified (bound only after `email_verified`). CSRF already enforced in `resolve_session_subject`.
- **Wired** `dashboard/activity/alerts` + `/my-charges` to prefer the caregiver session, else the verbatim Firebase bearer path.
- **Tests**: caregiver login admission + backfill, subject-mismatch refusal, end-to-end caregiver-session `/my-charges`.

## Inertness
`resolve_caregiver_session` and `_try_caregiver_login` are reached only when `auth_provider=="authentik"`. With firebase, every caregiver endpoint and `/auth/login` behaves identically to before (40 auth tests + 3 new caregiver tests green; ruff clean; app boots).

## Reviews
Needs **niru** (code) + **safety-privacy-reviewer** (mandatory — auth boundary + caregiver→member identity binding + the `/auth/login` change admitting caregiver emails).

## Not in this PR
The `collaboration` stubs + dead `get_current_caregiver` are left as-is (migrating stubs adds risk with no user benefit). Mobile has no caregiver client. Cutover gates (#2 TLS, #3 XFF, #6 CORS, real redirect_uri) still pending before any flip.

author: marchenaangulojoseluis-dev
body:
## El problema

El estado del checklist se guardaba **por índice**: `tareaStatus[eq] = {0:true, 2:true}`, doc-ids `EQ|PERIODO|AÑO|IDX` en `mtto_plan`/`mtto_ejecuciones`, y `mantenimiento_fotos.tareaIdx`.

Quitar una actividad de la lista **corre los índices de todas las siguientes**. La marca que decía *"hice la #2"* pasa a apuntar a otra actividad. Y producción **ya permite quitar actividades** (13 usos de `quitadas`) sin remapear nada — o sea que hoy eso mal-apunta en silencio, para siempre.

Hay **cinco escritores** de ese estado (checklist, autosave, bot de WhatsApp, itinerario, registrador de KPIs), así que cada uno era una carrera distinta.

## Qué cambia

La marca va pegada al **NOMBRE**. Cambiar la lista ya no la mueve — las 5 carreras se vuelven estructuralmente imposibles, y se borra la maquinaria de remapeo.

- `actKey` escapa `%`, `|` y `/` de forma **inyectiva**: dos actividades distintas nunca colapsan en el mismo doc-id.
- **Lectura retrocompatible** (`tareaHecha` acepta el nombre y el índice viejo): el código nuevo funciona con los datos sin migrar desde el minuto cero.
- La app **nunca** reinterpreta un índice viejo por su posición de hoy — eso cristalizaría la corrupción. Esa conversión la hace **una sola vez** el script de migración, y **con evidencia**: `mtto_ejecuciones` y `mantenimiento_fotos` guardan `tareaIdx` **y** `tarea`, o sea qué nombre tenía esa posición *en el momento* del registro.
- Una actividad quitada **conserva su marca** (inerte): volver a agregarla la recupera.

## La feature que destapó todo

Nueva colección **`mtto_actividades_periodo`**: ajuste de las actividades de un tipo en una sede, **solo para ese período** (*"este bimestre, a las cortinas de Atocongo hay que hacerles además X"*). Vence con el período. El resolver queda en 3 capas: plantilla del cliente → ajuste del período → ajuste del equipo.

## Council (Codex): 14 rondas → APROBADO

Encontró **2 bugs que ya estaban en producción**, ninguno de esta rama:

1. **El autosave pisaba al bot.** El técnico reportaba una actividad por WhatsApp, el bot la marcaba en Firestore, y el autosave de la app (que tenía el mapa viejo en memoria) la sobrescribía. Sin error, sin rastro.
2. **El backup de `mantenimiento` estaba roto desde siempre.** Exportaba `r.tarea_status`, un campo **que no existe** → todo respaldo salía con el checklist vacío, y restaurarlo lo borraba. Justo la red de seguridad que el cutover da por sentada.

**Escrituras concurrentes:** `doSave` y el script van por transacción y con `update()`, **no** `set(merge:true)` — Firestore hace merge **profundo** de los mapas anidados, así que con merge una clave *borrada* sobrevive (destildar no se persistiría, y los índices viejos no se limpiarían nunca). Verificado contra Firestore, no asumido.

## Tests

Todos extraen la función **real** del HTML/bot/script y corren contra un Firestore falso con semántica fiel (transacción, `update`, merge profundo), o contra el **Firestore real**. Cada fix se verificó **reinyectando el bug** y confirmando que el test se pone **rojo**.

| | |
|---|---|
| `test_atribucion` | 23/23 |
| `test_autosave_ctx` | 17/17 |
| `test_backup_mantenimiento` | 11/11 |
| `test_migracion_carrera` | 20/20 |
| `test_toggle_legacy` | 15/15 |
| `test_acts_guardar` | 23/23 |
| `test_bot_lista_cambiada` | 18/18 |
| `test_actividades_periodo` | 14/14 |
| `test_mtto` | 81/81 |

Contra Firestore real: `resolver_typos` 42/42 · `gemini_no_desempata` 11/11 · `plantilla_por_cliente` 7/7.

## ⚠️ Cutover

El script de datos se corre **justo DESPUÉS del merge a main, no antes**: Firestore es uno solo y producción todavía lee por índice, así que migrar primero dejaría el checklist en blanco para los técnicos.

1. Merge a `main` (producción pasa a leer por nombre, con fallback a índice).
2. `node migrar_indices_a_nombres.js` → **simulacro**. Hoy reporta: 14/19 docs, 124 evidencias, **cero índices corridos**, 26 planes, 116 ejecuciones, 53 fotos (2 realineadas por evidencia, 0 huérfanas).
3. `node migrar_indices_a_nombres.js --confirmar`.

## Hallazgo aparte (NO incluido acá)

El shim `window.__fb` tiene `setDoc: (ref, data) => ref.set(data)` — **ignora el tercer argumento**. Los paneles de Gestión de accesos llaman `setDoc(..., {merge:true})` sobre `usuarios/{email}` → hacen un overwrite completo → **cambiarle el rol a un usuario le borra su `apps[]`**, y un SUPERVISOR queda sin acceso a ningún módulo. Es preexistente, transversal a 4 módulos (`configuracion`, `inventario`, `itinerario`, `mantenimiento`) y de otra área: va en su propia rama.

author: tyronehou
body:
Removes the scroll threshold from wheel page navigation, per request: *"Don't have threshold for scrolling; any scrolling should trigger page navigation."*

## What changed

Previously a flip required **240px of accumulated wheel delta** at a page edge, followed by a **400ms cooldown**. Both are gone. At the top/bottom edge, a single wheel event changes page immediately.

Two behaviors were kept deliberately, confirmed with the requester:

- **The edge requirement stays.** Mid-page wheel input still scrolls the container natively, so a zoomed-in page taller than the viewport remains readable top to bottom. Only wheel events *at* an edge navigate.
- **No cooldown.** One trackpad flick emits many wheel events and will now walk through many pages. This is intended.

## The stale-closure fix

Dropping the cooldown exposed a latent bug. Many wheel events fire before React re-renders, so every event in a flick read the same `currentPage` from state and computed the same target — a 30-event flick would advance exactly one page instead of thirty.

`currentPage` is now mirrored into a ref that the handler advances synchronously, so N events move N pages. This also drops `currentPage` from the effect's dependency array, keeping the listener stable across page changes.

`wheelDeltaPixels()` was removed along with it — only the sign of `deltaY` matters now, and `deltaMode` never affects the sign.

## Verification

`npm run build` (`tsc && vite build`) passes clean, with no unused-symbol errors from the removed constants. Wheel behavior itself was reasoned through rather than driven in the Tauri shell — worth a manual pass with a trackpad before merging, particularly the multi-page flick.

author: kazimurtaza
body:
## Problem
The CSV export's year banner cell started with `=` (`"=== Financial Year: YYYY-YYYY ==="`). When the file is opened in Excel, cell A1 is parsed as a formula (`#NAME?`), mangling the year header. RFC 4180 quoting does **not** prevent Excel formula evaluation of a leading `=`.
Reword the banner so no emitted cell begins with a formula char (`= + - @`): `"Financial Year: YYYY-YYYY"`. One-line change in `buildYearCsv` (`js/storage.js`), with a comment explaining the trap.
Also includes `.gitignore` hardening so personal tax-data exports (`backups/`, `tax_data_*`, `drive-download-*.zip`) can never be committed to this public repo.
- Rebased on top of v1.7.0 (no conflicts); `origin/main` still had the buggy banner.
- `npm test`: **243/243** passing; coverage 99.5% stmts / 92.5% branches (above thresholds).
- Confirmed via real `exportData` output that A1 no longer starts with `=` and all section headers are intact.

- [ ] 기능 추가 / 기능 삭제 / 리팩토링 / 버그 수정 / 의존성, 환경 변수, 빌드 관련 코드 업데이트 / 기타

---

## 💡 주요 변경사항
### 미니홈피 메인 조회
- `GET /api/minihompy/{ownerId}` - 미니홈피 메인 조회
  - 본인 최초 접근 시 미니홈피 자동 생성 (지연 생성)
  - 접근권한(PRIVATE/FRIEND/ALL) 체크, FRIEND는 일촌 도메인 연동하여 실제 일촌 여부 확인
  - 방문 시 자동으로 방문 기록 생성 (본인 제외, 비로그인 제외, 하루 1회만 카운트)
  - 응답에 방문자수(Today/Total) 포함

### 프로필 사진
- `PUT /api/minihompy/profile-image` - 프로필 사진 업로드/변경
- `DELETE /api/minihompy/profile-image` - 프로필 사진 삭제
- 공용 `StorageService` 사용, 확장자 화이트리스트 검증(jpg/jpeg/png)

### 미니홈피 설정
- `PATCH /api/minihompy/settings` - 공개범위/소개글/기분 한번에 수정

### 방문자
- `GET /api/minihompy/visitors` - 최근 방문자 목록 조회 (닉네임, 방문시각), 홈피 주인 전용

### 기타
- domain/dto 계층 분리 (Minihompy, Media, VisitLog / MinihompyMainResponse 등)
- 미니홈피 도메인 에러코드 추가 (MINIHOMPY_NOT_FOUND, MINIHOMPY_FORBIDDEN)
- `V4__update_minihompy_table.sql`, `V5__add_visit_log_daily_unique.sql` 마이그레이션

## 🔍 관련 이슈

- 병합 대상 브랜치: dev
- 현재 작업 브랜치: feature/BE/minihompy-main

body:
## 요약

자막메이커(Video Caption Studio) 번역 엔진 드롭다운에 **로컬 MLX Qwen 2종**(`Qwen 9B`/`Qwen 4B`)을 추가합니다. 실리콘맥에서 네트워크·과금 없이 온디바이스 LLM으로 EN→KO 자막을 번역합니다. 라이브 자막용으로 이미 있던 MLX 워커 인프라를 재사용합니다.

- 전사(모델) 계층은 **변경 없음** — whisper(tiny~large-v3) + Apple 온디바이스 유지.
- "세부모델" = 같은 번역 드롭다운의 두 항목(9B/4B) — `apple`/`apple_hifi` 패턴과 동일.
- **실리콘맥 전용**. 인텔맥·윈도우·구버전 macOS에서는 목록에 **보이되 비활성**(`available=false`).
- 전부 **additive·하위호환** — 라이브 자막(하이브리드 B) 동작 불변, `mlx_lm`은 워커 서브프로세스 안에서만 import(인텔/윈도우/CI 임포트 안전).

## 변경 (커밋별)

| 커밋 | 파일 | 내용 |
|---|---|---|
| `60cda93` | `mlx_worker.py` | MLX 워커에 범용 raw-generate 요청 타입(`{id,prompt}`→`{id,text}`) 추가. 기존 라이브 `{en,context}`→`{ko}` 경로 불변 |
| `8a6e364` | `mlx_live_translate.py` | `MlxWorkerClient`에 `model_id` 인자 + `generate(prompt,timeout)` 메서드 추가 (additive; `translate()` 불변) |
| `c467580` | `translate_mlx.py` (신규) | `QwenMlxTranslator`(배치 `TranslationProvider`, 글로서리+의성어+환각 가드) + `qwen_mlx_available()` 게이팅 + `QWEN_MLX_MODELS` |
| `652c069` | `translate_cli.py` | 드롭다운 2항목(`qwen`/`qwen_lite`) + `create_translator` 라우팅 (지연 import) |
| `232fa27` | `pipeline.py` | 잡 종료 시 워커 `aclose` (try/finally) |
| `51888b1` | `translate_mlx.py` | 최종 리뷰 반영: 워커 기동 실패 폴백 하드닝(어떤 실패든 원문 유지) + 미사용 import 정리 |

프론트(`apps/desktop`)는 **코드 변경 없음** — 서버 `available` 플래그로 자동 비활성 렌더. MLX 모델 다운로드는 기존 서버 콘솔 `MlxModelPanel` 재사용(서버=컨트롤 플레인).

## 설계·계획
- 스펙: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-video-caption-qwen-mlx-translate-design.md`
- 계획: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-14-video-caption-qwen-mlx-translate.md`

## 테스트
- 신규 단위 테스트(전부 mlx 미설치/페이크로 CI·인텔맥 통과): worker raw round-trip, `MlxWorkerClient.generate`/model_id, `QwenMlxTranslator`(파싱/개수불일치/가드/워커재사용/기동실패/OSError 폴백), 게이팅 진리표, 엔진목록+라우팅, 파이프라인 aclose.
- 전체 서버 스위트 **666 passed**(기존 무관 실패 1건 `test_viewer_spa_mount`은 main에도 존재).
- import 오염 점검: `translate_cli`/`translate_mlx` import 시 `mlx_lm` 미로딩 확인.
- 최종 전체 브랜치 리뷰: **Ready to merge = YES** (0 Critical / 0 Important).

## 남은 검증 (자동 테스트 밖 — 실리콘 실기기)
- [ ] 서버 콘솔 MlxModelPanel에서 Qwen 9B 다운로드
- [ ] 자막메이커 클라에서 "Qwen 9B (MLX 로컬)" 활성 확인(4B는 미설치 시 비활성)
- [ ] 짧은 영상 base 전사 + Qwen 9B 번역 완주 → 품질/의성어/용어 확인
- [ ] 인텔맥/윈도우 빌드에서 두 항목 비활성으로만 노출

> 참고: `QWEN_MLX_MODELS`(py) ↔ `MLX_MODELS`(serverConfig.ts)는 함께 수정 필요(양쪽 주석 표시). 배포 시 서버 번들 재동결 필요.

author: bearyung
body:
## Summary

- scope Visual Input asset choices to connected Extract Assets results
- replace the node title-bar link action with disconnect-only behavior, including grouped multi-link selection
- add workflow authoring undo/redo for graph and configuration edits, with coalesced node dragging and atomic multi-link disconnects
- route Edit menu and keyboard undo/redo to the active workflow surface
- keep generated results, provider execution, run/review history, and viewport navigation outside authoring undo
- provide a five-second Undo action after disconnecting links

## Why

Workflow links need a safe, explicit way to be broken, and accidental authoring changes should be recoverable without treating external generation or execution results as reversible editor operations. Visual Inputs connected to an extraction node should also only offer assets produced by that extraction.

## Impact

Workflow authors can disconnect a single link immediately or choose among grouped input/output links when several exist. Authoring changes now support undo/redo, while execution side effects and run history remain authoritative.

## Validation

- `npm run check` — 0 errors and 0 warnings
- `npm test` — 97 Vitest files / 1,012 tests passed; 96 Node script tests passed
- `npm run build` — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed
- manual workflow UI testing — passed by product owner

author: dougchansan
body:
## Summary

- reconstruct fn_8019F7F0 recursive HSD joint-flag clearing
- reconstruct modelApplyAnimation__FP8_GSmodel animation/blend application

## What made them match

### fn_8019F7F0

- recovered that the routine clears flags recursively but does not descend through JOBJ_INSTANCE nodes
- changing JOBJ_CLASSICAL_SCALE must propagate matrix-dirty state before the flags are cleared
- mirrored the adjacent set-flags family, including its different dirty-check helpers at successive recursion levels
- reproduced MWCCs bounded recursive inlining with scoped optimization level 1, inline depth 5, and use_lmw_stmw; this was the compiler-shape key to the 0x2FC body

### modelApplyAnimation__FP8_GSmodel

- recovered the early skip and two-model blend path, including animating both blend trees before calculating the blended model
- derived animation and texture rates independently, including the 60 FPS/fractional-frame gates
- restored separate HSD_ForeachAnim masks for joint and texture rates, then read the current AObj frames back into both requested-frame fields
- reset part-animation mixes only for active model animation and propagate dirty matrices for both the selected child and root joint
- declaration/lifetime shape for the two late dirty checks resolved the final r3/r4 allocation swaps without dummy code

## Match impact

- fn_8019F7F0: 100%, 764/764 bytes
- modelApplyAnimation__FP8_GSmodel: 100%, 776/776 bytes
- +1,540 exact bytes and +2 exact functions
- all 63 hsd_jobj and 45 gs_model_anim siblings audited; zero regressions

## Validation

- configure/all_source/report pass
- full ninja retail SHA-1 matches
- quality suite: 24/24 passed
- source-only scope; no .inc, config, split, symbol, or generated-file changes

Both functions are natural semantic C; no asm, dummy/no-op, or identity-wrapper tricks.

author: sebtardif
body:
## Summary

Main tip looked red even though CI and a later Scoop smoke succeeded. Cause: `Test Scoop install` used `cancel-in-progress: true` on `test-scoop-${{ github.ref }}`. A push-triggered run was cancelled by a later `workflow_dispatch` on the same ref; GitHub attaches the cancelled suite to the commit and `statusCheckRollup` becomes FAILURE.

## Change

- Keep cancelling superseded runs on PR branches
- Never cancel in-progress Scoop smoke on `main`
- Slightly clearer concurrency group key (`workflow` + `ref`)

## Test plan

- [x] Diff reviewed
- [ ] PR CI green
- [ ] After merge, main rollup no longer stuck red solely from cancelled Scoop (new tip supersedes old suite)

author: dek3rr
body:
## What

Adds a **parallel, non-deploying** Zensical docs build so we can track [Zensical](https://zensical.org) (the MkDocs + Material for MkDocs successor) as it matures — **without touching the live docs**. MkDocs still builds and deploys the site via `docs.yml`.

## Why not just cut over?

Zensical is pre-1.0. A real trial build against our unmodified `mkdocs.yml` (v0.0.50, exits 0 in ~4s) shows it's closer than its docs imply, but two things break the majority of the site today:

- **All 6 notebook examples vanish** — `docs/examples` is a symlink Zensical copies verbatim as an 11-byte text file, *and* there's no `.ipynb` renderer yet → dangling nav links.
- **External API cross-refs lost** — `hippogriffe` (jax/equinox/numpy refs) isn't supported.

What already works: the 4 hand-written pages, math (arithmatex + MathJax), all 15 mkdocstrings API pages **with working internal cross-refs**, theme/palette/fonts/search.

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/docs-zensical-trial.yml`** — builds `mkdocs.yml` with Zensical on docs PRs + manual dispatch, uploads `site/` + build log as an artifact. `permissions: contents: read`, never deploys.
- **`pyproject.toml`** — new `docs-zensical` extra (`pip install .[docs,docs-zensical]`).
- **`.github/ZENSICAL_TRIAL.md`** — ground-truth status + cutover checklist for when Zensical reaches parity (~Phase 3).

## Try it

This PR triggers the trial job (it touches `docs-zensical-trial.yml` + `pyproject.toml`). Download the `zensical-trial-site` artifact from the run to inspect Zensical's output on our content.

body:
## Summary
Adds motion-preference handling — the repo previously had zero (no `@media` in CSS, no `matchMedia` in JS), so three JS-driven smooth scrolls fired regardless of the OS "Reduce Motion" setting.

- **js/ui.js**: new `scrollBehavior()` helper returns `'auto'` when `(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` matches, else `'smooth'`. Wired into all three call sites found by grep:
  - active-card scroll on toggle (`block:'nearest'`)
  - completion banner scroll (`block:'center'`, #44/#77)
  - reset scroll-to-top (`window.scrollTo`)
  An explicit `behavior:'smooth'` bypasses any CSS-level rule, so the JS side is guarded in code. Evaluated per-call so a mid-session preference change is honoured.
- **css/styles.css**: appended a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block neutralising transitions/animations and forcing `scroll-behavior:auto` (the file's only `!important`). No press-scale transform on rows to suppress.
- **sw.js**: `CACHE` bumped `v42` → `v43` (js/ + css/ touched).

## Verification
- `node --check` on js/ui.js and sw.js — pass.
- All existing tests (`node tests/*.test.js`) — pass.
- Live-verify via headless Chromium + CDP `Emulation.setEmulatedMedia`:
  - Reduce **OFF**: `scrollBehavior()` → `smooth`, CSS transition-duration `0.15s` (unchanged).
  - Reduce **ON**: `scrollBehavior()` → `auto`, CSS transition-duration `0.01ms` (neutralized).
- Grep-confirmed: every `scrollIntoView` / `scrollTo` site uses `scrollBehavior()`; no unguarded literal `'smooth'` remains.

Closes #79

author: qiuethan
body:
## Problem
`POST /chat` was guarded by `require_api_key` — any valid, active, non-revoked key was accepted regardless of scopes. Keys are minted with a `chat` scope model (`mint_key.py --scopes`), and a scope-enforcing dependency `require_scope` already existed and was re-exported from `src/api/auth.py`, but no router used it. A consumer key minted with **empty scopes** could still call `/chat` and spend Bedrock budget.

## Fix
- `services/llm/src/api/routers/chat.py`: replace `Depends(require_api_key)` with `Depends(require_scope("chat"))`. `require_scope` yields the same `AuthedKey`, so no handler wiring changes.
- The env-bootstrap key carries the admin/wildcard scope (`factory.py`), and `AuthedKey.has_scope` treats `admin` as satisfying any scope — so local dev and admin callers keep working (verified in code and by test).
- `services/llm/src/mint_key.py`: `--scopes` help now notes that `chat` is required to call `POST /chat`.

## Tests (TDD — written failing first)
- key **without** `chat` scope → **403** on `POST /chat`
- key **with** `chat` scope → 200
- admin/wildcard (env-bootstrap) key → 200

Provider layer is mocked (`_FakeProvider`), so no real AWS call happens.

## Verification
- `uv run pytest -q` → 65 passed
- `uv run ruff check .` → All checks passed
- `uv run ruff format --check .` → 33 files already formatted

## Zone
Only files under `services/llm/` are touched.

author: austinywang
body:
## Summary

Adds the shareable **orchestration template** layer: a packaged, versioned format that captures a whole way of running fleets of coding agents (prompts, workspace shapes, agent commands, provisioning style), so one user can share their setup as a git repo and another can install and run it. This is the template/packaging layer described in the Fleet plan (related: #7361); it is deliberately independent of the fleet engine skeleton in #7374 (no dependency on `Packages/macOS/CmuxFleet`, no file overlap beyond the shared CI package list / workspace registration lines) and exposes clean seams (`OrchestrationRunPlan`, per-task agent command + prompt + cwd + caps) the engine can consume later.

## What's included

**`Packages/macOS/CmuxOrchestration`** (new pure SwiftPM package, Swift 6, dependency-free, 75 tests):
- `orchestration.json` manifest model with versioned `schemaVersion`, actionable parse errors, and unknown-key detection.
- Parameters (install-time interview: `string`/`int`/`bool`/`path`/`choice`/`agent`, defaults, typed coercion). Resolved values live per-install in `~/.cmuxterm/orchestrations/<name>/install.json`, never inside the template.
- Substrates: `worktree` (git worktree per task), `clone-pool` (v1: fresh clone per task), `script` (template-supplied provision script — the SSH/cloud escape hatch).
- Validator: referenced-file existence, path traversal rejection, placeholder resolvability, script executable bits, duplicate ids, secret-material scan (error severity), layout JSON parse.
- Store: install/list/info/remove/update over seam protocols (`OrchestrationFileSystem`, `OrchestrationGitClient`, `OrchestrationProcessRunner`) with in-memory fakes — the CmuxControlSocket testing shape. Update keeps parameter answers, drops stale keys, and resets trust confirmation.
- `{{placeholder}}` rendering (strict: unknown placeholders fail at validate/plan time), shell quoting, run planner (branch/directory naming, prompt file, `CMUX_ORCHESTRATION*` env, `minCmuxVersion` gate), provisioner, `init` scaffold.

**`orchestration.*` v2 socket domain** (CmuxControlSocket + app):
- `orchestration.list` / `orchestration.info` / `orchestration.plan` / `orchestration.run`, following the coordinator seam pattern (`ControlOrchestrationContext` + fakes + 8 coordinator tests).
- App side: `TerminalController+ControlOrchestrationContext` plans via the package and enforces the trust gate; `OrchestrationRunController` provisions sequentially off the main actor, then creates workspaces **unfocused**, grouped in the sidebar, with the agent command delivered as typed terminal input (`initialTerminalInput`, or the layout's setup command when the template ships a layout). Completion/failure lands as a cmux notification (strings localized en/ja).

**`cmux orchestration` CLI namespace** (`CLI/CMUXCLI+Orchestration*.swift`):
- `init`, `validate`, `install`, `list`, `info`, `remove`, `update`, `configure` run locally (no socket needed) with an interactive parameter interview; `plan`/`run` go through the socket. `run` prints the full plan (workspaces, agent commands, scripts, substrate) before executing.
- `CLI/cmux.swift` may not grow (900-line hard cap), so the option-parsing helpers were extracted verbatim into `CMUXCLI+OptionParsing.swift`; net −60 lines. No budget TSV changes.

**Trust model (enforced in code):**
- Install/update never execute template code — files are cloned/copied and parsed only, and invalid templates never reach the store.
- The first run of a template (and every run after an update) requires explicit confirmation of the scripts, agent commands, and substrate; `--yes` skips the prompt; the socket method errors with `needs_confirmation` until confirmed.
- Validation rejects secret material in templates; agent commands run with the user's own auth.
- All run-path workspace creation is focus-false.

**Example + docs:** `Examples/Orchestrations/issue-fleet` is a real worktree-substrate template that package tests validate and plan on every CI run (the format's living fixture); `docs/orchestrations.md` documents the format, placeholders, trust model, CLI, socket API, and storage; `docs/cli-contract.md` gains the namespace row and a no-socket help probe.

## Scope cuts (explicit)

- **Steps execution**: manifests support the linear `steps` chain (parsed, validated, tested), but v1 `run` executes the first step only and says so in the plan notes. Full chain execution + success-condition supervision (`pr-exists`, `hook-event`, `exit-code`) belongs to the fleet engine.
- **Clone-pool reuse/reset**: v1 provisions a fresh clone per task; pool reuse belongs to the engine.
- **`instructions/` fragments**: validated and documented, not yet auto-applied to workspaces.
- **Interview UX**: plain readLine prompts (TTY only); non-TTY installs print the `configure` command instead.

## Testing

- `swift test` — CmuxOrchestration: 75 tests, 11 suites, all passing (manifest, validator, store, planner, provisioner, placeholders, scaffold, example fixture).
- `swift test` — CmuxControlSocket: 234 tests passing including the new orchestration coordinator suite.
- Guards run locally: `swift_file_length_budget.py` (merge-base mode, green), `check-workspace-package-groups.py`, `check-package-resolved-policy.py`, `check-pbxproj.sh`, `lint-pbxproj-test-wiring.sh`.
- Localization audit: the only new user-facing UI strings are the three run-completion notification strings, added to `Resources/Localizable.xcstrings` for en and ja. CLI stdout is exempt per existing convention; no web/docs message catalogs are affected. App-target build is validated by CI (no local xcodebuild per task constraints).

Related: #7361

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: guilherme-andrade
body:
## What

Three attendee bugs in the outbound calendar sync path, found while building guest invites (follow-up feature PR is stacked on this):

1. **Google `build_payload` pushed empty attendee objects.** Stored attendee rows are string-keyed jsonb (`"email" => …`), but the payload builder read symbol keys (`a[:email]`), so every update of a synced event that has guests sent `attendees: [{}, …]` — which Google rejects with a 400 ("Missing attendee email"), wedging the write job.
2. **Updates and RSVPs reset other guests' responses.** The full-list write omitted `responseStatus`, so Google reset every guest back to `needsAction` whenever we pushed an event or RSVP.
3. **Zoho writes dropped attendees entirely** — `build_payload` had no attendee mapping.

## How

- `Calendars::EventWriter` now emits one canonical symbol-keyed attendee shape (`email`/`name`/`rsvp_status`) regardless of how rows were stored, and each provider client maps it to its own wire format (incl. response statuses in both our enum vocabulary and the provider's own, since inbound sync stores the provider's).
- The guest list is only written back for events the user organizes (or the first push of an app-created event) — pushing it on a received invite could clobber the organizer's copy with our stale one.
- RSVP patches still send the full list (providers require it), now with everyone's actual status preserved.

## Tests

- `event_writer_spec`: canonical shape, organizer-only gating, no-email row dropping, RSVP self-merge preserving other guests.
- `google/calendar_client_spec`: payload mapping from all stored shapes, RSVP patch body.
- `zoho/calendar_client_spec`: attendee mapping + ICS status translation, omission when the writer sends none.

⚠️ Zoho side remains marked unverified against a live grant, same as the rest of that client.

author: yizhaodev
body:
## Why is this PR needed?

RHCL 1.4 has two compatibility issues with the demo deploy scripts on OpenShift:

https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/CONNLINK-1300
https://redhat-internal.slack.com/archives/C04J77H00TD/p1784022859796999

1. **Gateway pod OOMKilled**: The RHCL 1.4 wasm plugin requires more memory to compile than the default 1Gi limit set by istiod. Gateway pods (openshift-ai-inference, batch-internal-gateway, data-science-gateway) crash with OOMKilled after Kuadrant policies are applied.

2. **Rate limiting silently skipped**: TokenRateLimitPolicy (inference token limit) and RateLimitPolicy (batch request limit) counters use `auth.identity.user.username` to track per-user usage. The wasm shim needs to read this value at runtime. In RHCL 1.3, the wasm plugin was injected via Istio WasmPlugin CR, which automatically passed Authorino ext_authz response metadata into the wasm CEL context -- `auth.identity` was available without extra configuration. RHCL 1.4 switched to injecting the wasm filter via EnvoyFilter, which breaks this automatic data passing. Now the AuthPolicy must explicitly populate `auth.identity` through its `response.success.filters.identity` section. The auto-generated AuthPolicy (created by odh-model-controller when enable-auth is true) does not include this section, so the wasm shim fails with `NoSuchKey("identity")` and silently skips rate limiting for both the inference TokenRateLimitPolicy and the batch RateLimitPolicy.

## What does this PR do?

**Gateway memory (OOM fix):**
- For inference gateway, batch internal gateway, and data-science-gateway: adds `__configure_gateway_proxy_resources()` that uses Gateway API `infrastructure.parametersRef` to override proxy memory to 2Gi via a ConfigMap with strategic merge patch. This approach survives istiod reconciliation (unlike direct deployment patches).

**Rate limiting (wasm identity fix):**
- For LLMInferenceService: removes `security.opendatahub.io/enable-auth: "true"` annotation so odh-model-controller does not create a Gateway-level AuthPolicy that lacks identity filters.
- For inference route: adds `apply_inference_auth_policy()` that creates an HTTPRoute-level AuthPolicy with K8s TokenReview authentication, SubjectAccessReview authorization, and `response.success.filters.identity` to populate the wasm shim CEL context. This makes the inference TokenRateLimitPolicy (500 tokens/1m per user) work correctly.
- For batch route: adds `response.success.filters.identity` to the batch-route AuthPolicy so the batch RateLimitPolicy (20 req/1m per user) also uses `auth.identity.user.username` as the counter.

**Other fixes:**
- For RHCL installation: switches to `install_connectivity_link` (RHCL 1.4 latest) instead of pinned 1.3.5.
- For batch rate limit test: breaks on first 429 instead of sending all 25 requests.

Tested: 13/13 tests pass on OCP 4.20 + RHOAI 3.5.0-ea.2 + RHCL 1.4.1.

author: buffalog
body:
Replaces #71, which GitHub auto-closed when #70 merged and deleted its base branch. Identical content — the same three commits cherry-picked onto post-#70 `main`, clean, no conflicts. **Test-only: zero `app/` changes.**

Verified green on CI **four consecutive runs** on the previous branch: `775 passed, 0 failed`, conclusion `success`.

## Part A — the 13 drift fixes

| Test | Drift |
|---|---|
| `ProviderResourceTest` ×3 | Providers hold a *set* of disciplines via the pivot; the form field is the required multi-select `disciplines`. The edit test also needed its factory provider to actually hold one. |
| `ProviderProfilePageTest` ×3 | Wizard field is `discipline_ids` (multiple). |
| `ProviderProfilePageTest` ×2 | RBAC overhaul moved clinician nav to its own panel, so `shouldRegisterNavigation()` is hardcoded `false`. Dropped those assertions, kept `canAccess()`, renamed the tests to match what they now verify. |
| `DashboardNavigationTest` ×1 | Groups renamed `Dispatch` → `Cases`, `Credentialing` → `Our Providers`. Expectations taken from the **live** navigation, not guessed. |
| `DisciplineSpecialtyTest` ×1 | `TenantTaxonomySeeder` folds `CPR Certification` → `CPR/BLS`. |
| `FindMatchesActionTest` ×1 | Asserted status `assigned_pending`, which no longer exists in the enum. `AssignmentService` sets `STATUS_MATCHED`. |
| `PublicReferralSourceFormTest` ×2 | Heading copy changed; and the 404 test could never pass — `FeatureTest::setUp()` calls `withoutExceptionHandling()` globally. |

## Part B — the email-collision flake, killed at the root

Tests minted `'existing'.rand(1, 10000).'@example.com'` into one shared, never-rolled-back DB with a UNIQUE index on `users.email`. ~1% birthday collision per run, on `main` too.

It wasn't stably random either: **Faker draws from PHP's global `mt_rand`**, so any change to how many tests run re-rolls every subsequent `rand()`. That's why merely *adding* tests kept detonating unrelated files — `ReferralFlowTest` in #69, `SubscriptionCheckoutFormTest` in #70. Same bug both times.

`FeatureTest::uniqueEmail($prefix)` mints from a per-process counter whose lifetime matches the `migrate:fresh`'d database — collision-proof by construction. No `RefreshDatabase` (the documented `pdo_sqlsrv` deadlock landmine).

## 🚩 Part C — CI was configured to fail on a green suite

Reaching 0 failures exposed this. The first fully-passing run still reported **failure**:

```
Tests:  775 passed (2187 assertions)
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

**PHPUnit 11 defaults `failOnPhpunitWarning` to `true`.** `tests/Unit/ExampleTest.php` (empty Laravel stub) and `tests/Feature/FeatureTest.php` (our base class) both match the `*Test.php` suffix but declare no test methods → *"No tests found in class"* → two warnings → exit 1.

This had **always** been failing the build; real test failures were masking it. Excluded the two non-test files from the suites rather than switching the flag off — it's worth keeping, it catches a misnamed test method that silently never runs.

author: 0xdeafcafe
body:
## Problem

Rebuilding map projections via ops replay (`ops.startReplay` → `replayOptimized`) was effectively unusable in production:

- **Weeks-long runs.** `MapAccumulator.drain` grouped buffered records per **aggregate** and sequentially awaited one `bulkAppend` per group. For `spanStorage` the aggregate is a single trace, so each trace's handful of spans became its own awaited ClickHouse INSERT with `wait_for_async_insert: 1` (~200ms) — one at a time, for millions of traces.
- **Global freeze.** `replayOptimized` paused ALL selected projections and drained ALL discovered aggregates **before the first batch**, and only unpaused after the last — live processing for those projections was frozen for the whole run. ADR-015 intended a "seconds per batch" pause window (the non-optimized path already did it per batch).
- **No partition pruning.** `event_log` is `PARTITION BY toYearWeek(EventOccurredAt)`, but the cutoff/load queries filtered only on `TenantId`/`AggregateId` — full partition scans (including S3 cold storage), repeated per batch.
- **Sequential per-tenant I/O** within each batch.
- **Lost lock, per-aggregate progress spam.** The 1h ops replay lock was never refreshed, so runs longer than an hour silently stopped updating status (`lockHolder !== runId`); every aggregate also triggered multi-round-trip Redis status writes.

## Fixes

1. **Bulk map writes per tenant** — `MapAccumulator` now flushes one `bulkAppend` per tenant chunk (default 5000 records, many aggregates per call). The `AppendStore.bulkAppend` contract takes a tenant-scoped `BulkAppendContext` (no `aggregateId` — no store used it; records carry what stores need per row). The live `append()` path and the no-`bulkAppend` fallback are unchanged.
2. **Per-batch pause windows** — `replayOptimized` pauses, drains **only the current batch's aggregates**, replays, and unpauses in a per-batch `finally`, so a batch failure can never leave projections frozen. The replay marker protocol (pending/cutoff/done — unchanged) guarantees correctness across the unpaused gaps. ADR-015 amended.
3. **Partition pruning** — each batch first computes the `EventOccurredAt` min/max over ALL events of its aggregates (`getAggregateOccurredAtBounds`, a cheap key-column-only read filtered on the full `TenantId`/`AggregateType`/`AggregateId` primary-key prefix; empty bounds — zero-event aggregates — skip the cutoff/load queries entirely) and threads that range into `batchGetCutoffEventIds`, `loadEventsForAggregatesBulk`, and `batchLoadAggregateEvents`. This bound is provably safe: every event those queries must see existed when the bounds were computed, and later appends fall after the cutoff and are handled live. (Bounding by the replay's `since` would be unsafe — fold rebuilds need history predating `since`.) The non-optimized fold/map batch paths get the same pruning.
4. **Parallel per-tenant I/O** — cutoff and event-load queries within a batch now run across tenants with bounded parallelism (`pMapLimited` under the same `concurrency` cap as the apply step).
5. **Lock heartbeat + progress throttle** — new `ReplayRepository.refreshLock` (atomic holder-checked TTL extend); the ops service refreshes it on every batch completion and time-gated (60s) from progress emits. Replay-phase progress emits are throttled to every 100 aggregates (plus batch end) instead of every aggregate. A refresh that reports the lock lost aborts the stale run via the existing cancellation path, and finalization is skipped when another run holds the lock, so a superseded run can never clobber its successor's status.

## Spec / docs

- `specs/event-sourcing/projection-replay.feature`: new scenarios for per-batch pause windows, batch-failure unpause, bulk writes, and lock lifetime.
- `dev/docs/adr/015-projection-replay-coordination.md`: amendment documenting all of the above.

## Tests

- `replayExecutor.unit.test.ts`: per-tenant single-call flush (regression for the per-aggregate INSERT storm), cross-aggregate chunking on incremental writes.
- `replayService.integration.test.ts` (testcontainers): paused-during-write / unpaused-between-batches across a 2-batch optimized run; batch failure unpauses; existing scenarios updated for the tenant-scoped bulk contract.
- `replayEventLoader.integration.test.ts`: `getAggregateOccurredAtBounds` and bounded-vs-unbounded parity for cutoff/load queries, plus a narrow-bounds exclusion test proving the predicate is wired into the SQL.
- New `replay.redis.repository.integration.test.ts`: the `refreshLock` Lua check-and-extend script against real Redis (holder extends TTL, foreign runId refuses and leaves TTL untouched).
- New `ops/__tests__/replay.service.unit.test.ts`: lock refreshed once per completed batch and time-gated from progress emits; stale-lock run does not clobber the new holder's status; a run whose lock refresh reports the lock lost aborts instead of replaying alongside its successor. `replayService.integration.test.ts` also gained a multi-tenant `replayOptimized` batch test covering the per-tenant cutoff/load fan-out.

`pnpm typecheck` clean; event-sourcing unit suite (166 files / 6826 tests), ops unit suite, and the replay integration suites all pass locally.


## Deployment Impact

No deployment impact — runtime behaviour change only. No env vars added or changed, no helm values added or changed, vanilla `helm install` behaviour is unchanged, and there is no BYOC dataplane impact. The changes alter how ops-triggered projection replays execute (bulk ClickHouse writes, per-batch pause windows, partition-pruned queries, replay-lock heartbeat); the ADR edit documents that behaviour. Operators will notice replays completing far faster and live projection processing no longer freezing for the duration of a replay.

- **New Features**
  - Improved projection replay performance with tenant-scoped bulk writes and pause/drain coordination per batch.
  - Added occurred-at bounds to partition-prune cutoff and replay event loading.
- **Bug Fixes**

  - Replay lock is refreshed during long runs, and stale runs no longer overwrite the status of a newer lock holder.
- **Tests**

- **Documentation**

## Summary

A kubelet device plugin that turns "an app pod that can draw on the containerized desktop" into a one-line resource request:

```yaml
resources:
  limits:
    desktop.local/display: 1
```

- **`device-plugin/` (Go)** — registers `desktop.local/display` (name/slots/DISPLAY/paths configurable). `Allocate()` injects the `/tmp/.X11-unix` + `/run/desktop-audio` mounts (rw — unix `connect(2)` needs write access to the socket inode) and `DISPLAY` / `PULSE_SERVER` / `PIPEWIRE_REMOTE` env, so client pods need no volumes or env of their own. 10 virtual slots by default (shareable display; count = max concurrent client pods). Device health mirrors whether the X socket exists, so clients stay Pending until Xorg is actually serving. Re-registers after kubelet restarts.
- **`Containerfile.plugin`** — multi-stage build to a 14MB scratch image.
- **`charts/desktop-device-plugin/`** — non-privileged DaemonSet chart (kubelet plugin dir rw, X socket dir ro for health checks, `system-node-critical`).
- **`examples/x11-client-pod.yaml`** — xterm-on-the-desktop demo pod.
- README section: install, slots/health semantics, ALSA-client caveat, software-GL scope (no render-node injection by design).

## Verification

- Go end-to-end test: runs the real plugin loop against a **fake kubelet registration server** over gRPC unix sockets; asserts registration (resource + endpoint), the 10-device Unhealthy→Healthy flip when the X socket appears, and the exact Allocate payload (2 rw mounts, 3 envs, 0 DeviceSpecs). `gofmt`/`go vet` clean.

author: cevvin7
body:
The smeared pixel art wasn't missing image-rendering: pixelated (it was already set) -- it was the room's fluid width:100%/max-width:480px sizing, which almost never lands on an exact integer multiple of a 32px sprite frame. Nearest-neighbor sampling at a non-integer ratio duplicates some source pixels more than others, producing the flat/smeared look.

Room now renders at a fixed pixel size (native art resolution x an integer scale factor), with entity sizing (cat, placed items) computed the same way. A new localStorage-backed toggle in the header switches between 1x and 2x. Position remains percentage-based against the now fixed-size room, only size changed.

Also adds a new bookshelfTall catalog item (1x1, onFloorAgainstWall) using the color-fallback rendering path already built for items without real sprite art yet.

## Summary

Completes the authoritative Phase 6 NPC candidate-validation documentation without changing runtime behavior. Section 25A remains the single normative source; development status and changelog contain post-merge summaries only.

This update resolves both blocking review findings:

1. The exact validated-candidate value and closed validation-result union are defined under Validated candidate runtime contract and Validation result union.
2. DEVELOPMENT_STATUS.md now states durable post-merge truth and no longer treats this branch or PR merge as the next task.

## Authoritative decisions

- ValidatedNpcReactionCandidate has one exact nested shape: strict engine-owned binding, detached normalized candidate, engine candidate fingerprint, and strict validation context.
- The validation context records the engine-computed projection fingerprint, captured closed role-disclosure policy, and literal engine-owned permission/applicability results.
- Provider echoes are comparison input only. No provider object, nested array, raw body, or diagnostic object is reference-shared with the validated value.
- NpcReactionCandidateValidationResult is a strict validated/rejected union. The rejection member uses the engine-expected binding, a closed rejection code/stage/location contract, literal retryable false, and at most eight diagnostics with no free-form message.
- Only a future coordinator may retry separately classified transient network/unavailable failures or timeouts. Candidate validation never weakens that policy.
- Both result members are runtime-only and nonauthoritative: zero new authoritative IDs, zero registry/state writes, zero version increments, no NpcReactionPlan, publication, display, provider/retry/timeout call, or fallback.
- A validated value expires on reset/destroy, session/turn/phase/version replacement, attempt supersession, or any logical terminal state. A later engine-owned preparation stage must repeat live applicability and policy checks.
- The authoritative graph remains at player-committed N+1; validation never performs N+1 to N+2.

## Audit matrix

| Review finding | Authoritative location | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact validated candidate and validation result missing | Section 25A: Validated candidate runtime contract, Validation result union, Validation-only boundary, Phase 6 invariants and acceptance tests | Exact type names, fields, nested-only binding, types/bounds/nullability/enums, additionalProperties false, ownership, detachment, lifetime, trust boundary, closed failures, retry ownership, and normative success/rejection JSON |
| Development status was branch/PR-local | DEVELOPMENT_STATUS.md: Current State, Next Recommended Task, Current Git/GitHub State | Records the contract as defined, production validation as unimplemented, the old implementation Goal as not resumed, and the next step as a new approved validation-only Goal from latest master |

- Conflict markers: 0
- Privacy/secret/credential scan: passed
- Production/test/runtime/package diff: 0
- GitHub Actions (Validate and create review bundle) on current head: **SUCCESS**

No real API was called.

## Self Review

- The validated candidate shape and result union each have one implementation interpretation.
- Binding placement is nested only; no top-level alternative is permitted.
- All failure codes, stages, locations, result members, and diagnostic fields are closed.
- Success and rejection examples conform to their normative shapes and reuse the exact existing IDs/schema/fingerprint rules.
- Normalized candidate, candidate/projection fingerprints, validation outcome, permission result, and final applicability result are engine-owned.

- Validation success is not commit success and cannot authorize later preparation without fresh live checks.

## Deferred findings

- Pure authoritative preparation, N+1 to N+2 commit, publication, and renderer migration remain later stages.

## Risks

A future implementation must reproduce the nested binding, detached value construction, exact fingerprint inputs, closed rejection mapping, zero-mutation lifetime boundary, and fresh pre-preparation live checks. Treating a provider echo, validation-time permission, or validation success as commit authority would violate this contract.

## Summary

- keep release checkouts free of persisted Git credentials
- validate release ancestry through the read-only GitHub compare API

## Root cause

author: cd-ultra
body:
## Summary
This PR adds two major audio processing and visualization features: formant-preserving pitch shifting and an interactive spectrogram underlay.

## Key Changes

### Formant Preservation for Pitch Shifting
- Added `preserveFormants()` function in `audio.js` that uses cepstral analysis to lock the source's spectral envelope onto pitch-shifted audio
- Implements a spectral-envelope estimation via low-quefrency cepstral liftering, then applies bin-by-bin gain correction to match source formants
- Uses 75% overlapping STFT frames with Hann windowing and adaptive frame sizing based on the fundamental frequency
- Gain corrections are clamped to ±12 dB to avoid artifacts
- Added `setPreserveFormants()` method to `AudioEngine` to toggle the feature and trigger re-render
- Integrated into the pitch-shift pipeline: when enabled and a fundamental is detected, formants are preserved after TD-PSOLA shifting
- Added UI toggle button ("Formants") that persists state and shows status messages

### Spectrogram Visualization
- Created new `spectrogram.js` module that computes STFT magnitude spectrograms using the existing FFT
- Spectrogram data includes per-bin magnitudes in dB, frame count, bin frequency resolution, and dynamic range parameters
- Added `_buildSpecBitmap()` and `_drawSpectrogram()` methods in `renderer.js` to render the spectrogram as an offscreen bitmap
- Maps spectrogram time/frequency axes to the piano-roll view coordinates, allowing seamless zoom/scroll
- Uses a perceptual "magma" color ramp (dark purple → magenta → orange → yellow) for visual clarity
- Spectrogram is computed lazily on first display and cached until audio changes
- Added UI toggle button ("Spectrogram") with lazy computation and visibility control

### FFT Enhancements
- Added `inverse()` function to `fft.js` for in-place inverse FFT using the conjugate-symmetry identity
- Required by the cepstral envelope estimation in formant preservation

### UI and Integration
- Added two new toggle buttons in the toolbar with active state styling
- Integrated spectrogram invalidation into audio load/import workflows
- Added status messages for both features
- Updated README with documentation of the new features

## Implementation Details
- Formant preservation uses cepstral analysis with a lifter cutoff below the pitch period to isolate the spectral envelope while preserving pitch
- Spectrogram bitmap is built once per audio load and scaled via `drawImage()` for efficient rendering during playback
- Both features are optional and can be toggled independently without affecting core pitch detection/editing
- Formant preservation only activates when a usable fundamental frequency is detected; otherwise falls back to standard pitch shifting

body:
## What

Answers: yes — a turn now auto-regenerates on an LLM error or safety-filter block, a configurable number of times.

New **`OpenRouterSettings.auto_retry_count`** (default **2**, range **0–5**; Config → Agents & Tools; 0 = off, i.e. the manual RETRY button as before). OpenRouter errors and safety-filter blocks both surface as `RuntimeError` from the model call, so both are covered.

**Per-model-call retry** (the safe design): two helpers in `openrouter.py` — `agent_turn_with_retry` (agentic Narrator + Editor) and `stream_with_retry` (legacy text path) — re-invoke a *fresh* stream on failure. Because the transcript is only appended after a **successful** result, a retry never re-runs tools that already committed (the agentic loop commits tools per round, so a naive full-turn retry would double-apply — this avoids that). A partial attempt emits a `discard` (client clears the half-written text) then a `retry` event → the chat shows "Retrying (n/N)". Applies to the **Narrator** (agentic + legacy) and the **Editor**.

Additive migration for the new column; the PUT clamps to 0–5.

## Verification

- **Retry-helper unit tests**: retry-then-succeed emits the right `discard`/`retry` events and the final result; exhaustion re-raises after N+1 attempts; `retries=0` = single attempt; legacy text path recovers and concatenates correctly.
- **Config**: migration defaults to 2 on an existing DB; PUT round-trips; `99 → 5` clamp.
- **Playwright**: a mocked turn that emits a `retry` event recovers cleanly — final narration rendered, discarded partial gone, no error surfaced.
- `tsc -b` + `vite build` clean; server modules compile.

author: brudnerm
body:
## What changed

**Fix: dropped players surfacing as swap candidates.** Yahoo's `roster;week=N` includes everyone who touched the roster that week; players with no lineup slot today were dropped mid-week. They still appear in Home matchup panels (they contributed week stats) but Strategy now excludes them from all recommendations.

**Sharper recommendation heuristics:**
- Rate-category z-scores (AVG/OBP/ERA/WHIP…) shrink toward league average by playing time — AB parsed from the H/AB display stat, IP from the IP display stat — so tiny hot samples can't top the value board. Stat lines now lead with volume ("95 AB · …" / "19.2 IP · …").
- Slump flags require meaningful samples behind both the month (≥40 AB / 8 IP) and the season baseline (≥100 AB / 25 IP), plus a severity floor (30-day value + trend ≤ −0.6). Good pitchers with thin-win months no longer get flagged; the list is sorted worst-first.
- IL-slotted players are excluded (they don't occupy an active spot); hurt players in active/BN slots still flag.
- Risers must be genuinely playing this week (≥8 AB / 3 IP over the last 7 days).

**Player profile drawer** — tap any player in Strategy tables, swap cards, or Home roster panels:
- Fantasy production across all four stat windows with AB/IP.
- Statcast expected stats (xBA/xSLG/xwOBA, xERA for pitchers) vs actuals with due/overperforming coloring, plus exit velo, hard-hit%, barrel%, sweet-spot%.
- Live season splits vs LHP/RHP, last-10 game log, and transaction news (IL moves, activations, trades), fetched in the browser from statsapi.mlb.com — it sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so this data is always current with zero pipeline lag. Links to the player's Yahoo page for editorial news.
- Bottom sheet on mobile, side panel on desktop; light + dark themes.

**New pipeline: `fetch:mlb`** (wired into the refresh workflow) — joins the MLB StatsAPI player directory with Baseball Savant expected-statistics and statcast leaderboards by MLBAM id into a league-agnostic `data/mlb/players.json` (~6 requests, no auth). Yahoo players match by normalized name with team-abbreviation disambiguation — 99.5% hit rate; the drawer degrades gracefully for unmatched call-ups.

## Reviewer notes

- Abbreviations are used only to recognize rate categories and locate volume display stats (H/AB, IP) — scoring direction still comes exclusively from Yahoo settings per the repo rule.
- Statcast quality-of-contact data isn't available from Yahoo's fantasy API, and neither is news content; StatsAPI transactions are the best free factual feed.
- Typecheck clean, 64 tests passing; verified in preview on desktop/mobile, light/dark.

body: Adds one universal `cmux://run` primitive for creating a new workspace, tab, or split and running an exact shell command. Existing focus-only links remain confirmation-free. Security model: - strictly parse one link at a time and reject unknown, duplicate, ambiguous, hidden-character, oversized, remote, and changed-target requests - resolve the directory and target before approval, then revalidate both before execution - show the full command, canonical directory, placement, and target in a critical dialog - require an explicit review checkbox for every command - always create a new terminal and pass the reviewed command as one quoted `/bin/zsh -lc` argument - do not remember raw-command approvals Verification: - tagged `runlnk` app build succeeded - unit test target build succeeded - parser, localization, project wiring, and policy guards passed - tagged runtime created and retained a workspace, tab, and right split with distinct markers - background-target split focused the newly created pane The leased Mac cannot execute XCTest because `com.apple.testmanagerd.control` is unavailable, so focused suites were build-verified and the behavior was exercised through the tagged app and debug socket. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds `cmux://run` deep links to open a new terminal and run a reviewed command with a confirmation dialog. Also isolates the terminal’s startup state and environment for reviewed commands to prevent inherited state from leaking in. - New Features - Added `cmux://run` with required `command` and `cwd`; optional placement/target for `workspace`, `surface`, or `pane` (with direction). Launches via `/bin/zsh -dflc`, cd’s to canonical `cwd`, verifies device:inode identity, then runs the exact command (whitespace preserved). - Confirmation shows command, canonical `cwd`, placement, and target; checkbox‑gated Run; localized strings. Docs in `docs/deep-links.md`. - Bug Fixes - Central external-link admission: single intent classification for run/ssh/non‑run; clear errors for multiple run/ssh/non‑run links; non‑modal busy alert when run handling or any modal is open. - Startup/new‑window: flush pending run links after navigation on startup (including a final flush hook); bypass restore deferral for cold‑start workspace runs; bind the approved command to the created terminal via `TabManager.initialTerminalCommand`. - Directory/shell hardening: single‑process `cwd` verification with timeouts and bounded retries; expose verifier unavailability; avoid signal‑escalation races; bypass Ghostty bootstrap and zsh startup files; alias‑proof guards; keep shell scope unchanged; sanitize terminal inheritance for reviewed commands (no workspace env or config leakage). - CI/Release: serialize universal builds (`-jobs 1`) to avoid overlapping arm64/x86_64 Swift frontends. - Tests: support stricter `Data` base64 decoding. Written for commit 5b281722c4c39345f7106733c5b20f931b9a4aca. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added secure `cmux://run` deep-link support to execute a command in a newly created terminal context (workspace/tab/split) with placement and direction options. * Added a localized confirmation alert with a checkbox-gated “Run Command” button and a read-only command preview. * **Bug Fixes** * Improved external-link routing and startup restoration behavior for command links, with more precise handling of ambiguous/multi-link inputs. * Added clearer localized error messages for invalid parameters and execution-blocking states. * **Documentation** * Updated deep-link documentation for `cmux://run` and focus-only formats, including required parameters, examples, and validation/permission behavior.

author: mellanon
body:
## The misprovisioning bug

arc provisions agent identity fragments (`agents.d/<id>.yaml`) and personas **into** cortex's config tree. The live cortex reads that tree via its own existence-gated `resolveConfigDir` (cortex `src/common/config/config-path.ts`, XDG wave-4 cortex#1869): canonical `~/.config/metafactory/cortex` if migrated, else the legacy trees.

arc's cortex host hardcoded the pre-move `~/.config/cortex` (`hosts/cortex.ts:50`) and the `--stack` base (`cortex-config-split.ts`). So on a **migrated** box, arc wrote to a tree the running cortex no longer reads → agents **silently vanished from the roster**. This unblocks the agent-pack sweep (cortex#1910) and completes the wave-4 arc-side audit-zeroing (G-18).

## The fix — mirror cortex EXACTLY

A single existence-gated resolver, `src/lib/hosts/cortex-config-dir.ts`, byte-mirrors cortex's `resolveConfigDir` precedence:

1. `$CORTEX_CONFIG_DIR` (trimmed; blank/whitespace ⇒ unset) — **verbatim**, self-contained root, no legacy probe
2. canonical `~/.config/metafactory/cortex` — if it exists
3. legacy flat `~/.config/cortex` — if it exists
4. legacy `~/.config/grove` — if it exists  *(grove level confirmed present in cortex's DIR resolver)*
5. canonical default (fresh host)

It **deliberately hardcodes `.config`** and does NOT consult `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` — because cortex's config-dir resolver doesn't either. Reusing arc's `xdg-paths.configDir` (which honors `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`) would make arc and cortex disagree on the live tree. Byte-matching is the whole point.

### Wired through
- **`hosts/cortex.ts`** — DEFAULT `configRoot` routes through the resolver (+ injectable `{home,env}` seam). Explicit `configRoot` / `--stack` / `--config-dir` / `ARC_CONFIG_ROOT` overrides keep their precedence **above** the default; only the DEFAULT gains existence-gating.
- **`cortex-config-split.ts`** — the `--stack` base is existence-gated: byte-identical `~/.config/cortex/<name>` on a pre-cutover box, `~/.config/metafactory/cortex/<name>` on a migrated one. `--config-dir` (a full user-supplied path) stays verbatim.
- **`provides-target.ts`** — new **`{cortex-config}`** token → the live cortex config dir, **DISTINCT** from arc's own `{config}` (`metafactory/arc`). Agent-pack manifests use `{cortex-config}/agents.d/<id>.yaml`.
- **`docs/agents-md/core-concepts.md`** — documents `{cortex-config}` + its precedence.

## arc does NOT move cortex's config

arc only **resolves** cortex's tree — no copy/migration here. cortex owns the physical move (cortex#1869). Per-agent state (`~/.config/cortex/agents/`) is #1903 state-class, **excluded** from the config move, and arc already matches cortex's current hardcoded behavior there (verified against cortex's `resolveInstanceDir`). Both `agents.d/` and `personas/` ARE carried together by the config move, so arc's single existence-gated `configRoot` for both is correct.

## Tests (hermetic — never touch real `~/.config`)
- **Drift oracle**: `resolveCortexConfigDir` asserted byte-equal to an independent reimplementation of cortex's `resolveConfigDir` across all tree-presence stages (canonical-only / legacy-only / grove-only / legacy+grove / all-three / neither / `$CORTEX_CONFIG_DIR` set / blank-env).
- `cortex.ts` + `cortex-config-split.ts` provisioning targets the gated dir (pre-cutover → legacy, canonical-present → canonical).
- `ARC_CONFIG_ROOT` / explicit `configRoot` / `--stack` / `--config-dir` overrides still win.
- `{cortex-config}` resolves to the gated dir and is distinct from `{config}` (unchanged).

Full suite **1536 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail** (the `arc-284-fixture-does-not-exist-xyz` 404s are intentional fixtures); typecheck + eslint clean.

### 1. 카톡용 요약 복사

- 주간 현황 탭: 보고 있는 주의 요약(항목별 이행 일수, 아침 준비 주간 판정, 평균 사용시간, 학습량 합계, 일별 이행+메모)을 복사
- 전체 기록 탭: 선택된 월 필터(또는 전체 기간) 기준 이행률·평균값·학습량 총합 복사
- 비동기 Clipboard API + `execCommand('copy')` 폴백, 성공/실패 인라인 메시지

### 2. 학습량 기록 (problemCount / wordCount)

- 오늘 입력 탭에 "학습량 (선택)" 필드 — 문항 풀이 수 · 단어 암기 수
- 주간 표 행·주간 합계, 기록 목록 상세, 월간 요약(총합·일평균), 복사 텍스트, CSV 열에 반영
- 기존 저장 기록(필드 없음)은 미입력으로 안전하게 처리

### 3. 자녀별 기록 분리

- 탭 위에 김민우/김민준 전환 버튼
- 저장 키: 김민우는 기존 `behaviorLog` 키 그대로(기존 데이터 자동 승계), 김민준은 `behaviorLog:김민준`
- 전환 시 입력 폼·주간 현황·전체 기록 모두 해당 자녀 데이터로 갱신, 마지막 선택은 새로고침 후에도 유지
- 저장/덮어쓰기/삭제 확인 문구, 복사 텍스트 제목, CSV 파일명에 자녀 이름 포함

### 4. 자녀별 판정 항목 구성 (CHILD_ITEM_KEYS)

- 김민우: 5개 항목 전체 (이행수 n/5), 김민준: 기기 사용시간·국영수 확인·아침 준비 3개 (이행수 n/3)
- 김민준 선택 시 공기계 제출·올림피아드 입력 필드 숨김, 저장 시 null
- 주간 표 행, 기록 뱃지, 월간 요약, 복사 텍스트, CSV 열/이행수 헤더가 항목 구성에 맞춰 자동 조정
- 기록 점수 색상 기준도 항목 수에 비례(80%/40%)로 변경

## 검증

Playwright(Chromium, 모바일 뷰포트)로 실제 구동 확인:
- 기존 `behaviorLog` 데이터가 김민우 기록으로 그대로 표시 (하위 호환)
- 김민준 전환 시: 입력 폼 2개 필드 숨김, 저장 메시지 "이행 0/3", 주간 표 3개 항목 행, 복사 텍스트·월간 요약·CSV(이행수 3개 기준, 열 제외) 반영
- 김민우 복귀 시 5개 항목·CSV 열 원복
- localStorage 두 키 분리 저장, 같은 날짜 독립 저장, 새로고침 후 선택 유지
- 학습량 입력·복원, 주간/월간 클립보드 텍스트, CSV BOM·이스케이프

Follow-up to the Conductor config PR (#706). Fills the remaining repo-settings tabs.

## What

**Scripts — admin dev server as a run button.**
- New run button `admin` on `$CONDUCTOR_PORT+2`, against the same isolated `ws_p<port>` DB.
- `scripts/generate-admin-env.sh` generates `apps/admin/.env.local` — shares the workspace DB + Better Auth secret with web, runs under admin's own origin, and `setup.sh` sets `ADMIN_WORKSPACE_ALLOWLIST` to the **seeded workspace id** so `owner@example.com` can enter admin (the allowlist fails closed on empty).
- Verified end-to-end: fresh DB → seed → workspace-id query → generated env (allowlist matches) → **admin boots, HTTP 200 on `/auth/login`, "Ready in 219ms"**.

**Actions — committed `[prompts]`.** Repo-wide instructions for Conductor's Review / Create PR / Fix errors / Resolve conflicts / Branch rename / general-chat buttons. Encodes our most-missed conventions: conventional titles + allowed scopes, one CHANGELOG Unreleased bullet, CHANGELOG-conflict handling, merge `--no-verify`, RLS/`Money<Currency>`, no `organization_id` in AI schemas. AGENTS.md stays the full source of truth.

**Stop auto-running a dev server on workspace creation.** Dropped `default = true` from the web run button — Conductor auto-starts the *default* script, which wasted Mac resources on the many coding-only workspaces. Now nothing auto-runs; pick web/admin/api from the Run menu on demand.

## Not included
- `apps/admin/.env.example` — the tooling blocks writing `.env*` paths; `scripts/generate-admin-env.sh` (fully commented) + the runbook document admin's env instead.

## Tabs left as-is (intentional)
- **Environment**: empty. Our per-workspace `DATABASE_URL` can't be a static Conductor env var (values don't interpolate `$CONDUCTOR_PORT`; per Conductor's own "same across workspaces" guidance it doesn't belong there), and secrets can't be committed. The generated `.env.local` is derived from committed templates, so a local wipe is harmless.
- **Misc → Preview URL / Files-to-copy**: Preview URL is a UI-only convenience (Next auto-detects its URL anyway); `.env*` files-to-copy is harmless (setup `--force` regenerates).

## Verification
shellcheck clean; admin boot smoke green; no TS touched (typecheck/knip unaffected). `apps/admin/.env.local` stays gitignored.

author: risacaph
body:
# Description of Changes

**What was changed**

- Adds a new **Headers & Footers** tool (id `headersFooters`) under Standard Tools → Page Formatting.
- Users can fill any of six slots — header and footer × left / center / right — with shared **font size**, **text colour**, **margin**, and **page-range** controls. Empty slots are skipped.
- Slot text supports the same `@`-tokens the add-stamp endpoint understands (`@page_number`, `@total_pages`, `@date`, `@date{dd/MM/yyyy}`, `@time`, `@filename`), so common cases like `Page @page_number of @total_pages` and dated footers work out of the box.

**Why**

- Fills an Adobe-Acrobat-parity gap: a focused running-header/footer workflow rather than the general-purpose watermark-style stamp tool.

**How it works**

- Implemented **entirely on the frontend** as a custom-processor tool. It composes the existing `/api/v1/misc/add-stamp` endpoint, chaining one text stamp per non-empty slot and feeding each stamped result into the next call so every slot lands on the same document.
- Header slots map to add-stamp grid positions 1–3 (top of page) and footer slots to 7–9 (bottom), matching the endpoint's `calculatePositionY` layout.
- Because it reuses an existing endpoint, no new API surface is introduced and the generated tool-models are unchanged.

**Files**

- New: `useHeadersFootersParameters.ts`, `useHeadersFootersOperation.ts`, `HeadersFootersSettings.tsx`, `HeadersFooters.tsx`
- Edited: `toolId.ts`, `useTranslatedToolRegistry.tsx`, `en-US/translation.toml`, `og-metadata.json`

## Summary

Complete rewrite of `tools/benchmark` (WORKLIST W-11, absorbing X1's benchmark half) into a hospital-day stress instrument, plus the real product fixes it surfaced.

### The instrument
- **Workload = a simulated ward day** on official openEHR CKM templates (Vital signs, Generic lab result, ePrescription, eReferral, GP data set — vendored OPT exports with provenance; committed example skeletons keep requests byte-identical across SUTs): admissions, q4h vitals, medication rounds, lab CONTRIBUTION batches, chart-review reads + AQL dashboards, corrections, discharges (~70:30 read/write; smoke/hour/day profiles; empty→1M scale ladder).

- **Saturation knee** (`bench knee`): ascending load-factor ladder to the SLO breach, with generator-bound detection (dispatch-lag) and died-under-load detection — a crashed SUT is a recorded finding, never a hang.
- **Cross-SUT comparison** (`bench compare`): throughput/memory/CPU/cold-start bars, CPU+RSS over-the-run overlays, per-class p50-p99.9 table, efficiency ratios, computed both-direction wins ledger, workload-lock mismatch warning.

author: minion1227
body:
## Summary

`calculate` renders every non-integer result with a hardcoded 6 decimal places, so common divisions come back with a string of trailing zeros — `10 / 4 = 2.500000` instead of `2.5`. Since the voice formatter doesn't normalize numbers, this is spoken digit-by-digit ("two point five zero zero zero zero zero").

## The bug

```rust
// Format nicely: drop trailing zeros for integers.
if result == result.floor() && result.abs() < 1e15 {
    Ok(format!("{} = {}", expr, result as i64))
} else {
    Ok(format!("{} = {:.6}", expr, result))   // <-- always 6 decimals, trailing zeros kept
}
```

The integer branch already drops trailing zeros (its comment says so), but the decimal branch never did.

- `"10 / 4"` → **`10 / 4 = 2.500000`** (should be `2.5`)
- `"7 / 8"` → **`7 / 8 = 0.875000`** (should be `0.875`)

This is the common calculate path — any non-exact division/fraction (bill splits, unit conversions) hits it, and `crates/genie-core/src/voice/format.rs` does not strip the zeros, so the mangled number is what the user hears/reads.

## Changes

- Extract `format_calc_result(f64)`: integers print without a decimal point (unchanged); non-integers render to at most 6 places with trailing zeros and any bare trailing `.` trimmed.
- Add the first tests to this module (it had none).

## Real Behavior Proof

- [x] I have built and run the affected code locally (or noted why I could not).
- [x] I have NOT verified on Jetson hardware, and I explain the equivalent verification path or validation gap below.

Tested profile / hardware (check all that apply):

- [x] `laptop`

Deterministic string formatting with no device/network surface; unit-testable directly, which is the equivalent verification. No Jetson-specific path is touched.

### What I ran

Linux laptop, x86-64, on this branch (based on current `main`):

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy -p genie-core --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test -p genie-core --locked
# regression proof: revert format_calc_result to the raw {:.6} and re-run the new test
```

### What I observed

- fmt clean; clippy clean under `-D warnings`; **all 1035 genie-core tests pass, 0 failures.**
- New tests: `"10 / 4" -> "2.5"`, `"7 / 8" -> "0.875"`, integers unchanged (`"2 + 2" -> "4"`), and `"1 / 3" -> "0.333333"` (still capped at 6 places).
- **Regression proof:** with `format_calc_result` reverted to `{:.6}`, the new test FAILS with `left: "10 / 4 = 2.500000"` vs `right: "10 / 4 = 2.5"`; restored, it passes.
- Confirmed no other test in the workspace depends on the old `2.500000`-style output.

## Notes for reviewers

Integer results and the 6-place cap on repeating decimals are unchanged; only trailing zeros (and a bare trailing `.`) are trimmed. This finishes the "drop trailing zeros" the integer branch's comment already promised.

Fixes the playtest bug: during casting, after finalizing a headshot the flow says "continue the interview" and **hangs**. They're module-level once-guards; a season reset is a **soft SPA restart with no page reload**, so left set they stayed `true` forever → season 2+ the opener and the post-photo resume cue never fire → hang (a page reload masked it — "not sure why"). Mirrors the sibling `_resetAuthorWarmGuard` re-arm. - Test: `test_soft_restart_rearms_the_post_photo_resume_cue` (drives resume → `_orwellMarkRestart()` → asserts a 2nd cue fires) + a source-pin for both latches. Fails-before/passes-after demonstrated. ## Fix 2 — dead stream-busy guard (deterministic; latent, masked by a bad stub) `streamBusy()` called `hasActiveStream()` with **no session id**; the real `hasActiveStream(sessionId)` compares `_streamSessionId === sessionId` (null when idle) → always false → the "defer the cue until the in-flight stream settles" guard was dead in prod, hidden by a test stub that ignored the arg. author: lqvcohan
body:
## What changed
- Added a checkout compatibility guard for combo cart lines, which intentionally do not reserve inventory and therefore have no `holdExpiresAt`.
- Before the canonical checkout resolver runs, combo lines are validated against the authenticated user's active server cart and receive a short synthetic expiry so the existing cart-hold validator can process them.
- Rebuilds the combo checkout payload from the server-side cart snapshot and quantity instead of trusting client-provided combo pricing/snapshot data.
- Restores the original combo hold expiry when checkout fails; successful checkout continues to remove the cart line through the canonical transaction.
- Added tests for combo detection, the five-minute compatibility expiry, pass-through behavior for regular items, resolver wiring, and failure restoration contract.

## Root cause
`addComboToCart` deliberately skips inventory reservation and stores combo rows with `holdStatus: "active"` but without `holdExpiresAt`. The canonical `createCheckoutOrders` resolver checked `holdExpiresAt` before its combo-specific branch, so every combo checkout was rejected as an expired or mismatched cart item.

## User impact
Customers can now add suggested combos to the cart and continue to checkout without receiving the misleading “Món trong giỏ đã hết hạn…” error.

## Validation
- Added `cohan-restaurant-backend/tests/comboCheckoutHoldCompatibility.test.js`.
- Local execution was not available in this environment; CI should run the repository test suite on this draft PR.

💡 What: Replaced static imports with `next/dynamic` for the view components (`ResumenEjecutivo`, `AnalisisCanales`, etc.) in `dashboard/app/page.tsx`.

🎯 Why: The dashboard uses state-based routing instead of Next.js file-system routing. By statically importing all heavy views, they were bundled together and loaded on the initial page load, which bloats the bundle size and slows down the first paint.

📊 Impact: Reduces initial JavaScript bundle size significantly. Code for specific views (like the heavy charts) is now only loaded when the user navigates to them, improving Time to Interactive (TTI).

🔬 Measurement: Run `cd dashboard && pnpm run build`. Next.js output will show a smaller initial chunk size for `app/page.tsx`, and the views will be split into separate chunk files. Inspecting network tab on page load will also show a smaller initial payload.
