author: alexpropp
body:
Completes the ROADMAP **Hardening & release** section.

## What's here

- **Garbage-decode proptests** — pins "decode is total" (Ok or `Corruption`, never panic) for `Key::decode`, `decode_value`, and `unframe`: pure random bytes, valid-subspace-steered bytes, and single-byte corruption of valid keys. The value macro now generates a garbage-decode case per message type.
- **Real object storage tests** — `crates/moraine/tests/object_storage.rs` runs the public API against a real S3 endpoint; `cargo xtask s3` downloads pinned MinIO server/`mc` static binaries (no docker), serves on `127.0.0.1:9124`, and runs the suite un-ignored with hard count assertions. New CI `s3` job.
- **Extension distribution** — the DuckDB pin is single-sourced in a repo-root `DUCKDB_VERSION` file (read by `build.rs`, xtask, and CI cache keys). `cargo xtask package` emits the DuckDB-repository-shaped `dist/<version>/<platform>/` tree; `extension.yml` builds four platforms (linux amd64/arm64, osx arm64/amd64) on `v*` tags and attaches per-platform zips to the GitHub release. Assets are zips because the inner filename is load-bearing for the entry symbol. Signing stays zero: DuckDB accepts only its own core/community keys, so signed distribution is a future community-extensions submission (new roadmap item).
- **Armed crates.io release** — `release.yml` now triggers on push to main; release-plz tags as `v{version}` (matching `extension.yml`'s trigger), `moraine-duckdb` is `publish = false` (distributed as an artifact, not a crate), and `moraine` gained readme/keywords/categories.

## Verification

- Store suite: 82 passed (new proptests hold)
- `cargo xtask s3`: 2 passed against live MinIO, clean teardown
- `cargo xtask e2e` on the refactored pin: 1 + 15 passed through real DuckDB + DuckLake
- Packaged artifact loads: `duckdb -unsigned -c "LOAD '<abs>/dist/v1.5.4/osx_arm64/moraine_duckdb.duckdb_extension'"` → ok
- `cargo publish -p moraine --dry-run --locked`: packages and compiles cleanly (protox is pure Rust, so docs.rs builds work)
- Full local gate green (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, workspace tests, doc, deny, e2e)

## Before/after merge

- **Before first release:** add the crates.io token — `gh secret set CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`
- After merge: release-plz opens the `v0.1.0` release PR; merging it publishes, tags, and `extension.yml` attaches the four platform zips. Run `gh workflow run extension.yml` once post-merge to validate the matrix (`macos-13` is retired; the matrix uses `macos-15-intel` for `osx_amd64`).

author: kouakou-christ-axel
body:
## Problème

Le serveur MCP (`/api/mcp`) fonctionne comme connecteur custom dans claude.ai mais échoue depuis **ChatGPT** et **Claude Desktop**.

## Diagnostic

L'hypothèse initiale (absence de Dynamic Client Registration) ne tient pas : le plugin `mcp` de Better Auth 1.6.11 supporte déjà le DCR (RFC 7591, `POST /api/auth/mcp/register`, annoncé via `registration_endpoint`), PKCE S256, et valide les `redirect_uri` contre ceux fournis par chaque client à son propre enregistrement (aucune allowlist figée). claude.ai s'auto-enregistre déjà par ce mécanisme.

Les vrais écarts, prouvés dans le code :

1. **Aucun CORS ni handler `OPTIONS` sous `/api/auth/…`** — or c'est l'URL annoncée dans le `WWW-Authenticate` du 401 (`/api/auth/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`). Le catch-all n'exportait que `GET`/`POST` (préflight → 405) et les endpoints du plugin ne posent pas d'`Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. Les clients qui font la découverte côté navigateur/renderer (Claude Desktop) échouaient à la première requête ; claude.ai (découverte côté serveur) n'était pas affecté.
2. **Pas d'`OPTIONS` sur les routes racine `/.well-known/*`** : le SDK MCP envoie l'en-tête `MCP-Protocol-Version` qui déclenche un préflight → 405.
3. **404 sur les variantes « path-inserted »** `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/api/mcp` et `/.well-known/openid-configuration/api/mcp`, essayées par certains clients (dont ChatGPT).

## Correctifs (additifs — flux claude.ai inchangé)

- `lib/mcp/cors.ts` (nouveau) : helper CORS partagé (reflet des en-têtes demandés + préflight 204), extrait de `app/api/mcp/route.ts` sans changement de comportement.
- `app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts` : CORS + `OPTIONS` **limités** aux chemins `/api/auth/.well-known/*` et `/api/auth/mcp/*` (les endpoints session/OTP gardent la posture d'origine).
- `OPTIONS` ajouté aux 4 routes racine `/.well-known/*` existantes.
- 2 nouvelles routes path-inserted : `app/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/api/mcp/route.ts` et `app/.well-known/openid-configuration/api/mcp/route.ts` (même gabarit que leurs jumelles racine).
- Doc : tableau des 8 URLs de découverte + note DCR dans `app/api/mcp/README.md`, consigne d'exploitation nginx (`/.well-known/` doit être proxifié vers Next, pas avalé par une `location` statique certbot), mise à jour `CLAUDE.md`.

Hors périmètre volontaire : pas de réécriture du `WWW-Authenticate`, pas de changement dans `lib/auth.ts` ni dans l'ordre d'auth de `/api/mcp`.

## Vérification (locale, build de production + Postgres local)

- `GET` **200 + `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`** et `OPTIONS` **204** sur les 8 URLs de découverte (racine, path-inserted, `/api/auth/…`).
- `GET /api/mcp` sans jeton → **401** avec `WWW-Authenticate` présent et exposé (`Access-Control-Expose-Headers`).
- **Enregistrement DCR réel** d'un client public type ChatGPT (`token_endpoint_auth_method: none`, `redirect_uri` chatgpt.com) → 201 avec `client_id`.
- `OPTIONS /api/auth/sign-in/email` → 405 (posture inchangée hors périmètre OAuth/MCP).
- `pnpm lint` et `pnpm build` passent.

## Après déploiement

Rejouer la checklist curl du README sur `https://eba.otw.ci` : si un chemin racine `/.well-known/*` reste en 404, c'est la config nginx qui intercepte (cf. note ajoutée au README), puis retester la connexion depuis ChatGPT (mode développeur) et Claude Desktop.

author: auo959
body:
## What

Adds a blocking step to `.github/workflows/queue-validation.yml` that runs `pytest --noconftest tests/test_work_queue_schema.py`, closing the **"Queue validation CI"** roadmap checkbox of #1131.

## Why this shape

Verification-first findings that drove the design:

- `tests/test_work_queue_schema.py` **already exists** and fully validates `queue.json` against `queue_schema.json` (plus negative cases). No new validator was written — this PR just changes *where it's enforced*.
- On PRs, that test only runs in Aurora CI (Minimal)'s **full-suite pass, which is `continue-on-error`** (the blocking "critical tests" step is filtered to `@pytest.mark.critical/smoke`). So a schema-violating `queue.json` could merge with all checks green.
- `queue-validation.yml` is path-scoped to `ops/work_queue/**` — exactly the set of PRs that can introduce a violation — and it previously checked only JSON parseability and view drift. Its comment claiming `sync_queue.py` does schema validation was inaccurate (`sync_queue.py` has no schema/jsonschema references); fixed.
- `--noconftest` because `tests/conftest.py` imports `fastapi` at collection, which would force a full `requirements.txt` install into this 5-minute-timeout job; the schema test file needs only stdlib + `jsonschema` and no conftest fixtures.
- `pip install jsonschema` lost its `|| true` — it's now a hard dependency of a blocking step.

## Verification

- Workflow YAML validated with `yaml.safe_load`.
- `pytest --noconftest tests/test_work_queue_schema.py` in a clean venv with only `jsonschema` + `pytest`: **5 passed in 0.08s**.
- Current `ops/work_queue/queue.json` validates against the schema with 0 errors, so this cannot break existing PRs.
- The workflow file itself is in the trigger paths, so the new step self-tests on this PR.

Refs #1131

body: ## Summary Fixes [elastic/rna-program#613](https://github.com/elastic/rna-program/issues/613): creating an Alerting v2 rule via **Agent Builder** against an index whose date field is not named `@timestamp` (e.g. `kibana_sample_data_flights`, which only has `timestamp`) failed with an **"Unknown @timestamp"** error. The root cause was shared across three code paths: the rule's time field was defaulted to `@timestamp` without checking whether the index actually has that field. Two earlier fixes patched the UI form paths ([#273113](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/273113) threshold builder, [#274135](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/274135) ES|QL query sandbox) with separate, slightly inconsistent logic; the **agentic (server) path had no resolution at all**. This PR introduces a single source of truth for time-field resolution, wires all three paths to it, and — crucially — **stops silently defaulting to `@timestamp`**. When a valid time field cannot be resolved, the value is cleared and the user (or the agent) is forced to pick/target a real date field rather than persisting a broken rule. In agent builder In rule builder In ESQL Rule ## Behavior `resolveTimeField` resolves the lookback time field from the date fields present on the index: - **No selection yet (`undefined`)** — auto-pick a sensible default: `@timestamp` if present, otherwise the first date field (sorted). - **A selection exists but is not on the index, or is explicitly empty (`''`)** — return `null`. We do **not** substitute another field; the caller must force a new selection. - **No date field on the index at all** — return `null`. Consumers treat `null` as "unresolved": - **UI** clears the form's `timeField`, shows a validation error on the Alert Condition step, and **blocks "Next"** until a valid date field is selected. author: chaodu-agent
body:
## Problem

`/models` on B0 fails with Discord's "The application did not respond" — the interaction response is rejected before it ever reaches the user.

B0's logs show the actual error:

```
ERROR openab_core::discord: failed to respond to slash command
error=Invalid Form Body (data.components.0.components.0.options.12.description:
Must be 100 or fewer in length.) category="model"
```

One over-long option invalidates the entire form body, so the whole menu fails — not just that option. Any backend can trigger this at any time by shipping a long model/agent description, so this is a defensive gap on our side rather than a data problem.

## Fix

- `truncate_for_discord(s, max)`: character-based (not byte-based — slicing on a byte boundary would panic on multi-byte UTF-8) truncation with a trailing `…`
- Applied to both option **label** and **description** in `build_config_select_menu`, capped at `SELECT_OPTION_TEXT_MAX = 100`

Pagination already handles the 25-option limit (`SELECT_MENU_PAGE_SIZE`), so no change needed there even though the model list has grown past 25.

## Tests

- exact in-the-wild case: the ~140-char `claude-fable-5` description truncates to exactly 100 chars ending in `…`
- boundary: 100-char string passes through unchanged
- CJK safety: 120 multi-byte chars truncate by character count without panicking

## Verification

## Highlights (dev .. main, non-merge)

- **Agents / supervision**
  - Centralize proactive supervision in Wendy + agent radar scheduler disabled by default (#515)

Only one file conflicted: \`.github/workflows/deploy.yml\`.

author: nh13
body:
Adds the `unum copy-number` subcommand — the Rust port of T1K's `t1k-copynumber.py` (Phase 9 of the strangler port, #1). It infers per-allele copy number from a single sample's genotype result, printed to stdout.

## What it does

Copy number is inferred by fitting a one-copy abundance distribution and scoring each allele against integer multiples of it:

1. Read `{prefix}_genotype.tsv`; per gene keep alleles with quality `> -q`.
2. Estimate one-copy `N(mean, var)` from a `sqrt`-transformed sample: `--nomissing` genes (assumed present on every chromosome) contribute all their alleles (a homozygous such gene contributes `sqrt(abund)/2`), extended by the lower quantile band (`--lower-quantile`/`--upper-quantile`) of the sorted heterozygous-allele abundances; variance scaled by `--adjust-var`.
3. For each allele, pick the copy number `c ∈ 1..=8` maximizing the log-likelihood of `sqrt(abund)` under `N(mean·c, var·c)`, reported with a confidence ratio (log-likelihood gap to the runner-up).

Copy-number inference is meaningful for the copy-number-variable **KIR** locus (genes present in 0..N copies); for the fixed-two-copy HLA loci it is degenerate. The algorithm is locus-agnostic (operates purely on abundances).

## Validation

Byte-identical to `t1k-copynumber.py` on the T1K KIR example genotype across every flag combination the Python can run (default, `--nomissing`, `--upper-quantile`/`--lower-quantile`, `--adjust-var`).

One intentional divergence (documented in `docs/DIVERGENCES.md`, mirroring the same bug in `t1k-merge.py`): `t1k-copynumber.py` crashes on any nonzero `-q` (`int(quality) <= args.qual` with `args.qual` left a string by argparse). `unum copy-number` parses `-q` as `i64`; the default `-q 0` path is byte-identical.

## Structure

- `unum_core::copy_number` — pure port logic (parse, one-copy estimation, per-allele argmax + ratio, formatting), unit-tested.
- `stages::copy_number` — thin CLI wrapper.
- No reads, no reference; pure post-processing over one genotype file.

## Tests / gates

5 core tests (parsing/slot-gating, homozygous-double-abundance → copy 2, quality filtering, nonzero-`-q` numeric filtering, and missing-slot/ratio formatting). `cargo ci-fmt` and `cargo ci-lint` clean.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added a `copy-number` command to infer per-allele copy numbers from genotype TSV input.
  * Supports anchored (`--nomissing`) genes, quality filtering, quantile band selection, and variance adjustment.
  * Outputs tab-separated, T1K-compatible rows with confidence scoring.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Added input validation for quantile and variance parameters, and clearer errors for degenerate anchor cases.
  * If no alleles pass filtering, emits sentinel placeholder slots instead of invalid numeric output.
* **Documentation**
  * Updated divergence notes to capture compatibility and parsing quirks for the new command.

author: vedhavyas
body:
The collapsed tool-group summary had two render paths: read nested one child row per file, but every other kind (bash, web, search, mcp) collapsed onto one row with a comma-joined target capped at three plus a `+N`, so the fourth bash in a run was invisible. This unifies them so every kind behaves like read. A genuine single call rides the kind row inline; anything with more calls or targets nests one clipped child row per instance, uncapped; a target-less kind shows `×N`. Nothing wraps now - each row is a single line clipped to fit, so the outer layout can't re-wrap and shear the tree. Read still relativizes its paths and clips with a middle-ellipsis to keep the filename; other kinds clip end-first to keep the head.

That let me drop the wrap and cap machinery (`wrap_words`, `hard_split`, `format_targets`, `kind_target_wraps`, `MAX_TARGETS_PER_KIND`, the search pre-clip) - the render collapses to one rule and the tally to an unconditional per-call push. The width-fence tests prove every emitted row fits its width at each tested pane size. The second commit updates forge-map's tool-group mocks, prose, and code notes to match.

author: flopeztancredi
body:
Closes #5.

## Problem

`src/routeTree.gen.ts` contributed 16 of 178 findings on a TanStack Start app: a file nobody wrote, nobody reviews, and `treat` cannot act on. It drags the score down for a condition the maintainer has no way to fix.

## Fix

Two signals, both cheap:

1. **Filename** (`isEligible`): `*.gen.*`, `*.generated.*`, `*_pb2.py` / `*_pb2_grpc.py`, `*.pb.go`.
2. **Header marker** (`scanFile`, first 5 lines): `@generated`, `Code generated by ... DO NOT EDIT`, `autogenerated ... DO NOT EDIT`.

Skipped files drop out before counting, so they no longer inflate "Scanned N files" either.

### What I did not implement, on purpose

The issue also suggests treating `/* eslint-disable */` **+** `@ts-nocheck` as a generated marker. I left it out: that is a plausible header for a hand-written legacy file, and skipping those would silently drop real findings from code someone *can* fix. It also is not needed, since `routeTree.gen.ts` already matches the filename pattern.

Suggestion 3 (honor `.gitignore` / linter ignores) is also out: gitignored files are already outside the scan, and parsing another tool's config to decide what slopmd looks at is a lot of coupling for little gain.

## Verification

Fixture with the same slop (`any`, `@ts-nocheck`, a hardcoded secret) in six files:

| file | result |
|---|---|
| `routeTree.gen.ts` | skipped (name) |
| `api.pb.go` | skipped (name) |
| `schema_pb2.py` | skipped (name) |
| `marked.ts` (`@generated`) | skipped (header) |
| `header.go` (`Code generated by ... DO NOT EDIT`) | skipped (header) |
| `legacy.ts` (`eslint-disable` + `@ts-nocheck`, hand-written) | **scanned**, findings reported |

`Scanned 1 file`, findings only from `legacy.ts`. `slopmd . --fail-under 100` on this repo still scores 100/100.

body:
## Summary

Adversarial verify on PR #1073 found 2 blockers. Both fixed here.

## Blocker 1: missing actAs on runtime-sa (blocks first terraform apply)

PR #1073 removed \`roles/iam.serviceAccountAdmin\` from runner but omitted the SA-scoped grant \`runner->runtime-sa serviceAccountUser\`. Terraform's \`google_cloud_run_v2_service\` / \`google_cloud_run_v2_job\` set \`template.service_account = var.runtime_sa_email\` on 3 resources; Cloud Run v2 API validates \`iam.serviceAccounts.actAs\` on both create AND update → fresh apply fails 403 on all 3 Cloud Run creates.

Fix: bootstrap step 9 に SA-scoped grant を追加 (project-wide にせず F1 structural closure 維持).

## Blocker 2: security regression (integrity) when Deny Policy optional

PR #1073 は Deny Policy を optional 化した (warn-and-continue) が、custom role D1 が \`versions.add/destroy/disable/enable\` を残していた → org-scope \`roles/iam.denyAdmin\` を持たない operator は Deny Policy skip → compromised runner が secret **書換え可能** (ENCRYPTION_KEY を差替 → 次 revision で attacker key で暗号化)。

Fix: custom role D1 から \`versions.add/destroy/disable/enable\` を削除。secret 値は project owner が gcloud で手動投入 (docs/runbooks/encryption-key-rotation.md) なので runner に write perm 不要。これで Deny Policy が真に optional に (integrity は role 定義側で enforcement)。

## Custom role D1 変化

- **Before (12 perm)**: secrets.CRUD(5) + versions.{access,add,destroy,disable,enable,get,list}(7) + projects.get
- **After (8 perm)**: secrets.CRUD(5) + versions.{get,list}(2) + projects.get

## Cleanup

- \`variables.tf\`: 未使用 \`var.terraform_runner_sa_email\` を削除 (PR #1073 の bootstrap-only refactor 後 dead)
- \`service_accounts.tf\`: docstring 更新

## Test plan

- [x] DRY_RUN で runner->runtime-sa serviceAccountUser 付与を確認
- [x] DRY_RUN で custom role D1 の permissions が 8 個に減っていることを確認 (versions.access/add/destroy/disable/enable 全部除去)
- [x] \`bun run validate\` 通過
- [x] lefthook pre-push (type-check + architecture-boundaries) 通過
- [ ] user が PR merge 後 bootstrap 再実行して custom role update + 新 SA-scoped grant + deny policy attempt (skip予定) を確認

body:
## 问题

SynieDataGrid 数值列(integer/decimal)列头右对齐,但单元格内容仍左对齐。

## 根因

- HeroUI Pro DataGrid 的 `align: 'end'` 通过 `data-align=end` 在 th/td 上设置 `text-align: end`,靠 CSS **继承**作用到内容;
- 列头内容是内联文本,正常继承 → 右对齐 ✓;
- 数值单元格走 `defaultCell` 默认分支进 `ClampCell`(35195ac 引入的超长文本截断组件),其 span 类名 `block max-w-80 truncate text-start` 中的 `text-start` 把继承的 `end` 覆盖成 `start` → 块内左对齐 ✗。

即使去掉 `text-start`,`block max-w-80` 的盒子在宽于 320px 的列里也会贴左,右对齐仍不贴 td 右缘。

## 修法

数值短、不会溢出,仿照 datetime 既有先例("日期短,不进 ClampCell"):integer/decimal 直接返回纯文本,继承 td 对齐。`SynieEditableTable` 复用 `defaultCell`,一并受益;CSV/打印走 `cellText`,不受影响。

## 验证

- 起 worktree 前端(3001,代理现有后端)用 Playwright 实测银行流水页「收入金额」列:修复前单元格内 span 计算样式 `text-align: start`、`display: block`;修复后为纯文本节点,继承 td 的 `text-align: end`,截图确认数字贴右。

body:
## Summary

Two related navigation changes plus four folded bug fixes, landing together as **v1.56.0** (MINOR — a mixed PR takes the highest type; feature + fixes = MINOR).

### 1. Favourites stage instead of auto-walking
Clicking a saved **GOTO favourite** used to immediately stop any running loop/auto-lair and walk straight there. Now it **stages** the favourite as the queued destination — exactly like picking a room from the search box: the map pans, the route preview draws, and **Run** arms. Commit with **Run**, discard with the **X**.

- `NavigationViewModel.GoToFavorite` mirrors `SelectSearchResult`: sets `Layout` / `SelectedRoomKey` / `QueuedDestination` and returns, instead of walking.
- Staging no longer stops a running loop/auto-lair — that interruption belongs to Run.

### 2. All three user walk-to methods share one engine
Map right-click already ran through `RouteChoicePrompt` (free-vs-shortcut route picker). The search box and favourites bypassed it — their **Run** commit walked direct. `RunStop` is now `async` and routes the queued destination through `RouteChoicePrompt.WalkAsync`, so **all three** user walk-to methods (map right-click, search box, favourites) share one engine and surface the picker when a shorter gated shortcut exists. Only *how the walk is confirmed* differs. Engine-driven walks (loops, auto-lair, deposit/stash/train, item-acquisition detours) still bypass the picker and auto-pick the free-preferring route.

- Removed the now-unreachable duplicate queued-destination branch at the tail of `RunStop` (shadowed by the top branch since #176's first commit).

### 3. Picker names the buy-detour shop
When a shortcut crosses a carry/ticket gate whose item the walk will **auto-buy** (`BuyIfNeededForPath` + a reachable shop stocks it), the picker's requirement line now names the shop the run will detour to — e.g. `a raft (buy at General Store)`. The shop is chosen with `PathItemShopRouter`'s own fewest-added-steps rule (extracted to a shared `TrySelectShop`), so the promise matches the actual detour. Keys and hazard counters never get the tail — only Item/Ticket gates post a buy-triggering path-item need.

### Folded bug fixes (4 paradigm reports)

- **Loop skips a hidden exit (paradigm-20260713-174151)** — a loop leg crossing a `SearchableHidden` exit failed the whole lap. `LoopRunner` now shares the walker's `HiddenExitRevealManager` (`SetHiddenSearchEnqueuer/Stopper`, wired in `MainWindowViewModel`), mirroring the existing door sub-FSM: `_awaitingHiddenReveal` gates the tracker handler so the `sea` re-observations aren't read as a landing, and `OnHiddenRevealReply` re-fetches the exit and crosses once it appears. Pre-checks `ObservedExitDirections` to skip an already-revealed exit; harnesses that leave it unbound keep the fail-loudly path.
- **Fighting chip sticks on monster self-flee (paradigm-20260713-193205)** — the `RoomEntryDeparture` regex only matched a drag-out (`… walks out of / exits the room to <dir>`). A mob fleeing on its own (`The big forest spider scuttles out to the west!` — `<verb> out to <dir>`, no "the room") never matched, so the Combat gate the mob held never dropped and the "fighting" state stuck. Folded the self-flee verb into `\w+`, mirroring the arrival line. Wording taken verbatim from the capture.
- **Auto-lair markers linger after Stop (paradigm-20260713-174024)** — `StopAll` never called `AutoLair.Clear()` (`Stop()` early-returns from build mode), so lair marks stranded on the map. `StopAll` now clears them, matching `ToggleLairMode`'s own clear.
- **Bone key not picked up (paradigm-20260713-195905)** — `DoorOpenManager` blindly sent `use <key> <dir>` with no possession/floor awareness. Added a `holdsKeyItem` predicate (`AppServices.HoldsKeyItem`: name-match against the inventory keyring + carried list, article-stripped, biased-false on uncertainty). When the key isn't held it sends `get <key>` before `use` — the server processes them in order, and `get` is a harmless no-op when the floor has none. This is the narrow slice; a broader "grab every key opportunity in the room" is deferred.

The three larger reports handed over alongside these (buff-strip room spell, auto-lair room-clear detection, levers-before-door) are feature-scale and will each get their own PR after a game-mechanic confirm.

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet build` clean (0 warnings, 0 errors)
- [x] `dotnet test` green (4857 passing; +2 self-flee departure tests, +2 get-before-use door tests, +6 `RouteChoiceDialogViewModelTests`)

- [ ] Live: a shortcut needing an auto-buy carry/ticket item shows `(buy at <shop>)` naming the shop the run actually detours to
- [ ] Live: a loop leg through a searchable-hidden exit reveals it with `sea` and continues instead of failing the lap
- [ ] Live: a mob self-fleeing the room clears the fighting chip; Stop wipes auto-lair markers; a keyed door with the key on the floor gets it before use

body:
This PR optimizes the serialization performance of the AdalFlow library by refactoring the `to_dict` utility and improving recursive serialization in the base `Component` class.

Key changes:
1.  **Optimized `to_dict`**: Replaced the inefficient `json.loads(json.dumps(obj))` round-trip in `adalflow/adalflow/utils/serialization.py` with a direct recursive traversal. This avoids unnecessary string encoding and decoding.
2.  **Enhanced Component Serialization**: Updated `Component.to_dict` in `adalflow/adalflow/core/component.py` to recursively process values. This ensures that nested sets, tuples, and dataclasses are correctly converted into JSON-compatible formats.
3.  **Correctness Fix**: Fixed a bug where `Component.to_dict` would return raw `set` and `tuple` objects, which are not natively serializable by the standard `json` library.

Performance Impact:
- Benchmark testing showed a ~3.4x speedup for the general `to_dict` utility.
- `Component.to_dict` output is now guaranteed to be JSON-serializable.

All changes were verified against the existing test suite (87 tests passed) and documented in the Bolt performance journal.

Follow-up to #69 (already merged). An adversarial review of #69's hooks found real false positives; this hardens both guards and reconciles with the #53/#54 `--delete-branch` fix that landed in parallel.

## Guard hardening (from review)
**`worktree-checkout-guard.sh`** — matched too broadly. Now denies only a *plain* switch-to-default: anchored to a command boundary, no flags before the branch name, end/separator terminator, regex-escaped branch. Verified live in a worktree:

| command | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `git checkout main && git status` | deny | **deny** ✓ |
| `git checkout main -- file` | deny ✗ | **allow** ✓ |
| `git checkout --detach main` | deny ✗ | **allow** ✓ |
| `git checkout main.ts` | allow | allow ✓ |
| `echo git checkout main` | deny ✗ | **allow** ✓ |

**`rebase-guard.sh`** — detected pushes by substring (so `git log --grep "git push"` was denied when behind). Now **tokenizes each simple command** to find the real subcommand, and the direct-push-to-default deny is **refspec-aware** (bare push while HEAD is default, or explicit `<remote> <default>` / `…:<default>`); `--dry-run` and non-default pushes pass.

**`op-agent.sh`** (PAT probe) — keep the PAT off curl's argv (auth header via `-K -` stdin); only HTTP 401 = dead (403 is rate-limit/SSO on a live token → advisory). Finished the "Render MCP" comment cleanup.

author: sachiniyer
body:
Fixes #1724.

## The bug
`ParseCron("0 0 15 * */1")` fired **every day** instead of only on the **15th** of each month — AF and robfig disagreed on the same expression.

Root cause: `normalizeDOWField` rewrote a pure single-part wildcard-step DOW field like `*/1` into an explicit value list (`0,1,2,3,4,5,6`). That destroys robfig cron's `starBit`. In robfig/Vixie semantics, DOM/DOW is **AND** when one of DOM/DOW is a wildcard and **OR** only when both are restricted. `*/1` is a wildcard base (equivalent to `*`), so with DOM=15 the schedule must AND → fire only on the 15th. Rewriting it to an explicit list made DOW look *restricted* → OR semantics → fired daily.

Introduced in #1016 (f097d27), which correctly expanded numeric-base steps like `1/2` (#1007) but inadvertently caught wildcard-step forms that also expand to include 7 yet need no normalization.

## The fix
Add an **early return** in `normalizeDOWField` for comma-less `*/N` forms, *before* the expansion/list-rewrite path, so robfig keeps its wildcard flag:

```go
if !strings.Contains(field, ",") && strings.HasPrefix(field, "*/") {
    return field
}
```

- This **enforces** the #1007 fix rather than re-breaking it: #1007 dropped Sunday by *not* normalizing an expanded 7; only pure wildcard steps pass through here.
- Comma-separated forms mixing a step with ranges/lists (e.g. `*/1,5-7`) still take the existing per-part path (which is a *restricted* list → OR, matching Vixie).
- Sunday `7→0` normalization and all other existing behavior are preserved for non-early-return cases.

## Tests
A load-bearing matrix compares AF's `ParseCron` against **robfig directly** over a full year of ticks so the semantics can't silently drift again:
- `0 0 15 * */1` → fires only on the 15th (monthly), matches robfig — the reported bug is gone.
- Restricted-DOM × DOW variants (`*`, `*/1`, `*/2`, `1-5`, `0,3,5`, `*/1,5-7`) each with DOM=15 → AF matches robfig for a year.
- Both-restricted (DOM=15, DOW=1) → OR semantics preserved, matches robfig.
- `normalizeDOWField` unit cases updated (`*/1`, `*/7` now pass through); the #1007 Sunday-drop regression still passes.

Verified the matrix fails without the fix (`*/1` fires on the 2nd instead of the 15th).

## Gates
- `make test-container` — full suite green
- `make tui-driver-selftest` — 25/25
- `go build ./...`, `gofmt -l .` clean, `golangci-lint run --fast`, `deadcode -test ./...` — all clean

body:
Closes #64.

## What I built

`classifyProjection` (`src/project.ts`) homed a **root** skill correctly but classified a **nested-workspace** skill as `unclassified`. Root cause: `isSkillFile` tested `dirOf(dirOf(path)) === CANONICAL_HOMES.skill` against the **full, root-anchored** path, so `workspaces/<role>/.claude/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md` never matched `.claude/skills`.

The fix is the one the issue directed: `isSkillFile` now tests the **workspace-relative** path (`pathWithinWorkspace(path, tree)`), the same nearest-enclosing-workspace frame that PR #61 (B1) gave rows 9 to 13. Row 3 joins that frame; rows 1, 2, 4 to 8 stay root-anchored / basename. A root skill is unchanged (its workspace-relative path equals its full path).

Spec-driven, so `SPEC.md` moves in the same PR: §8.2 row 3 is annotated `(workspace-relative)` and the table prose now groups row 3 with the workspace-home rows. This is a classifier-rule change, so it bumps **SPEC v1.3 -> v1.4** (title, §6 declaration + changelog entry, `SPEC_VERSION`) and **package 1.3.0 -> 1.4.0** (package.json, lockfile self-entries ×2, `cli.ts .version`). The pre-existing uncommitted lockfile reconcile (self-entries lagging at 1.2.0) is carried to 1.4.0 in the same edit.

## How I verified

- **New classifier test** (`tests/project.test.ts`): a nested-workspace skill homes `skill / pass_through`. Confirmed red before the fix, green after.
- **Full gate**: `typecheck` clean, `lint` clean, **289/289 tests** pass (`SPEC_VERSION` assertion updated to `v1.4`).
- **Both sanitize modes re-verified end-to-end** on a real on-disk tree with a nested workspace that owns its own skill (`workspaces/oss/.claude/skills/deep/SKILL.md`):
  - `--mode support`: 5 classified, **0 unclassified**, gate PASS, exit 0; the nested skill emitted `skill / pass_through` verbatim. (Pre-fix: aborts.)
  - `--mode extract --include workspaces/oss/.claude/skills/deep/SKILL.md`: harvests the nested skill (byte-identical verbatim, confirmed via `diff`) plus its routing chain (both enclosing `CLAUDE.md`s, `shape_only`), gate PASS, exit 0. (Pre-fix: aborts on the unclassified included file.)

## Surfacing (out of scope, your call)

While confirming the bug I found the **general harness row (4, `.claude/**`)** has the *identical* root-anchoring gap: `isUnderDir(filePath, '.claude')` is root-anchored, so a nested workspace's non-skill harness file (e.g. `workspaces/<role>/.claude/hooks/pre-commit.js`, `workspaces/<role>/.claude/settings.json` not under `.claude/`... i.e. any nested `.claude/**` that is not a `SKILL.md`) also classifies `unclassified` and fails both modes closed on any tree containing one. Same fail-closed-safe blast radius as the skill bug.

I scoped this PR to the skill row per issue #64 and did **not** touch row 4. The SPEC change is written to state plainly that row 4 stays root-anchored, so the behaviour is documented rather than silently drifted. If you want the harness home to also recognise the nested frame, I can take it as a follow-up (or fold it in here if you'd rather) — flagging for your decision since it widens scope beyond the issue.

author: pmcfadin
body:
Closes #2299

## Problem
Compaction of uncompressed SSTables (CQLite's entire production write surface) peaked at **410 MiB heap vs a 128 MiB budget**. The filed root cause was stale — `V5_0NewBig` uncompressed already takes `requires_chunk_stitching()==true`, so the `iterate_all_partitions()` fallback named in the issue is not the path hit. dhat profiling of the real `WriteEngine::maintenance_step` path found **three stacked buffering contributors** (see the root-cause correction comment on #2299).

## Fix (410.78 MiB → 54.31 MiB peak, byte-parity preserved)
1. **Reader (within-partition):** resumable row-by-row driver `row_decoder/compaction_stream.rs` (`stream_partition_body_incremental` + `CompactionPartitionState`/`PartitionStreamStep`) drains the sliding window per-structure instead of buffering the whole partition. Splits partitions on both `END_OF_PARTITION` and a next-partition header (mirrors the buffered `drive_partition_sliding` exactly — no divergence).
2. **Writer:** `StreamingPartitionSession` promoted-index offsets changed from buffer-relative indices to flush-invariant **absolute** offsets + mid-partition scratch flush at promoted-index block boundaries (stops pinning the whole encoded partition in `DataWriter::buffer`).
3. **Merge write side:** direct row-stream write path taken **only when authoritative Statistics prove no input carries any deletion** (`min_local_deletion_time == i32::MAX`, all tombstone kinds registered) — byte-safe: no range markers to interleave. Otherwise the old buffered path.

## No-heuristics
The tombstone-free decision is from the authoritative `Statistics.db` histogram, not byte-guessing. Conservative granularity: any deletion in any input forces the buffered path for the whole merge.

## Tests
- `test_issue_2299_uncompressed_stream_memory.rs` (dhat-gated): pins the 410→54 MiB bound + N→1.
- `test_issue_2299_stream_readback.rs` (**default gate**, NOT dhat-gated): `direct_stream_wide_partition_reads_back_byte_identical` — compacts 2 wide (~640 KiB each, >10× the 64 KiB block threshold → forces a mid-partition flush) tombstone-free partitions across disjoint clustering ranges, reads back via `SSTableManager::scan`, asserts all 640 rows + full `(id,ck)→payload` value equality.
- Existing in-memory byte-identity suite (`data_writer/tests/streaming_partition.rs`): full Data.db byte equality vs whole-slice path for plain/static/range-tombstone/partition-tombstone/wide (≥2 block) cases + exhaustive pause/resume.

## Residuals (follow-up candidates, out of scope)
- One-shot CLI `KWayMerger::merge()` still whole-partition-buffers (only `maintenance_step` bounded here).
- Range-tombstone-bearing wide partitions still buffer whole-partition (documented #1668 residual).

## Gate / review
LITE PASS (commit 2dd5b1110). Full gate of record runs pre-merge via flow-closer.
Review-first: rust-reviewer APPROVE-WITH-NITS (byte-parity sound by construction); roborev round 1 (claude-code) — 2 blockers fixed (partition-boundary divergence + on-disk read-back test), nits addressed; final roborev confirmation in progress.
Note: codex roborev backend is down (revoked token + CLI version skew — needs `npm i -g @openai/codex@latest`); using claude-code agent.

author: nomixer
body:
## What

Automates the trigger for the D57 Java comment review so it cannot be forgotten (rationale in **D60**): a Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook in the repo's `.claude/settings.json` runs `scripts/comment-pass.sh hook` on every shell call and **denies PR creation** when three things hold: the command contains `gh pr create`, the branch's diff vs `main` contains `*.java` changes, and no attestation marker matches the current HEAD SHA.

The pass itself stays a judgment task — the script just makes it unavoidable and self-evident:

- `scripts/comment-pass.sh` — prints the D57-derived checklist (pin-or-tag, staleness, pre-D57 javadoc trims, new-file header rules) + the changed Java files.
- `scripts/comment-pass.sh done` — attests for the current HEAD (marker in `.git/`, per-clone, untracked). New commits invalidate it by construction.

Docs-only PRs never hit the gate (this PR is itself the demonstration — it contains no Java changes and was opened through the live hook).

## Why now

PRs #83/#84 touched `Thinlet.java` without the opportunistic `is()` javadoc trim D57 prescribes — recall does not survive sessions; harness hooks do.

## Verification

All four hook paths pipe-tested with synthesized stdin (non-match / match+no-Java-diff / match+diff+no-marker → deny JSON / attested → allow); live firing proven via a temporary sentinel, then removed; `jq -e` schema check green. No product source touched — build unaffected.

author: yjmantilla
body:
## Problem
The docs site (yjmantilla.github.io/neurodags) showed **`0.1.dev1+gd9b7c343c`** instead of the release. Root cause: `docs.yml` used `actions/checkout@v4` **without `fetch-depth: 0`**, so the checkout was shallow with no tags. `pip install -e .[docs]` then let hatch-vcs stamp its "no tags found" fallback (`0.1.dev1+g<hash>`), which `conf.py` reads via `importlib.metadata.version`. (`publish.yml` was unaffected — it already fetches depth 0, which is why the PyPI package versioned correctly.)

## Fix
1. **`docs.yml`**: add `fetch-depth: 0` so history + tags are available to hatch-vcs.
2. **`docs/conf.py`**: since the docs site tracks `main` (usually a few commits ahead of the last tag), even a correct hatch-vcs stamp would read as a dev version (`0.3.1.dev1+g…`). `conf.py` now displays the **nearest release tag** (`git describe --tags --abbrev=0 --match 'v[0-9]*'`), falling back to the installed dist version when git/tags are unavailable. The commit hash stays in the title for traceability.

## Verification
Local strict build (`sphinx-build … -W --keep-going`) succeeds; built `index.html` shows **`neurodags 0.3.0 (d9b7c34)`**, no `0.1.dev` anywhere.

On merge, `docs.yml` redeploys the site with the correct version.

body:
## Summary

- define the reactor version once as `<revision>0.3.0</revision>` in the root POM
- use Maven's CI-friendly `${revision}` placeholder for the root project and all 24 child parent declarations
- add `flatten-maven-plugin` with `resolveCiFriendliesOnly` so installed and deployed POMs contain concrete versions
- ignore generated `.flattened-pom.xml` files

## Why

Releases previously required updating the root POM and every child module POM. After this change, the Maven project version is updated in one place while all reactor modules remain aligned. The root project still has a Maven version through `<version>${revision}</version>`; the default resolves to `0.3.0`, and release builds can override it with `-Drevision=<version>`.

## Impact

Future releases only need to change the root `<revision>` value, or pass `-Drevision` from CI. Existing `${project.version}` references for internal reactor dependencies remain unchanged.

## Verification

author: raymondfeng
body:
## Problem
"Check for Updates…" produced **no visible response** whatever the outcome. Tracing the path: menu → `main.ts` → `updater.ts` sent status over `main → IPC → renderer onUpdate`, but **nothing in the console subscribes** to `onUpdate`, and errors were swallowed to `console.error` by design. So up-to-date, downloading, and error all looked identical: nothing.

## Fix
A pure, testable **update controller** + **native main-process dialogs**:

- **Manual check** → `Up-to-date` / `Downloading…` / `Update check failed` dialogs.
- **Download finished** → `Restart now / Later`. *Restart now* drains the core, then `autoUpdater.quitAndInstall()` through the **normal quit path** (sets `quitting` so `before-quit` passes through instead of force-exiting via `app.exit()`, which would skip Squirrel's install-on-quit hook).
- **Background startup check** stays silent until an update is ready.
- **Dev/unpackaged build** → a clear "Updates are disabled in development" dialog instead of the confusing "not packed" error.

The controller keeps the branching logic in `updater.ts` (no Electron) and the effects (dialogs, restart) in `main.ts`. A `manual` flag on the shared `autoUpdater` singleton scopes noisy dialogs to explicit user action; a ready download prompts either way.

## Why
Follow-up to the 0.6.0 release: a user on 0.5.0 clicked "Check for Updates" and saw nothing — the pipeline was actually working (0.6.0 downloads fine), but there was zero feedback UI.

## Tests
`desktop/src/__tests__/updater.test.ts` — drives a fake emitter through each lifecycle event under both manual and background checks (up-to-date/downloading only when manual; ready always; failure surfaced only when manual; in-flight guard; no unhandled rejection). **32/32** green across updater+ipc+menu; `tsc6` typecheck clean.

Not touched: the pre-existing `UPDATE_EVENT`/`onUpdate` IPC pair (has its own drift-guard test; left dead-but-harmless to keep the diff surgical).

> Note: desktop tests aren't in the `test (24)` CI gate (root `pnpm test` runs `dist/**` globs; desktop has its own vitest). Verified locally. Runtime dialog behavior needs a packaged build to click through — consistent with the repo's manual smoke-check practice for the updater.

author: jagp
body:
Turns the **fear-of-abandonment** plugin into a self-executing installer, modeled on the `claude-dashboard-statusline` `install.ps1`.

## What it does
`fear-of-abandonment/install.ps1` copies the plugin into Claude Code's plugins directory:

```powershell
.\install.ps1                 # global: ~/.claude/plugins/fear-of-abandonment
.\install.ps1 -ProjectPath .  # project-local: ./.claude/plugins/fear-of-abandonment
```

## Portability fixes vs. the dashboard template
The dashboard installer only runs under PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`). This one runs on stock **Windows PowerShell 5.1** too:
- `[System.IO.Path]::Combine(...)` instead of 4-arg `Join-Path` (the extra segments need `-AdditionalChildPath`, which is pwsh 6+ only).
- ASCII-only console output — a BOM-less UTF-8 `✓` gets mis-decoded by 5.1 and desyncs the parser.

## Verification
Ran end-to-end under Windows PowerShell 5.1 against a throwaway project dir: exit 0, and the full plugin tree (`plugin.json`, `bin/scan.sh`, `skills/.../SKILL.md`, `README.md`) landed under `.claude/plugins/fear-of-abandonment`.

author: savasp-agent[bot]
body:
Closes #291.

> **Stacked on #321 (#290).** Base is `codex/review-290-age-fts-v2`, so this diff is only #291. Auto-merge is intentionally disabled because GitHub immediately merges PRs whose base is an unprotected feature branch.

Makes AGE full-text search fast without changing behavior. Each label table gets one coarse, blob-level **GIN expression index** over `to_tsvector('simple', <graph>.age_fulltext_blob(properties))`, an `IMMUTABLE` per-graph-schema function returning all string values in the blob minus internal keys.

## What landed

- **`AgeFullTextIndex`** — `IMMUTABLE` function + both GIN indexes, idempotent (`CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`). Function in each graph's own schema so concurrent provisioning never races on a shared catalog tuple.
- **Phase-1 SQL** reads the base label table directly and AND-s a coarse conjunct (matching the index expression **verbatim**) with the precise per-type predicate; Postgres serves the coarse conjunct from the index and rechecks. Dynamic search *is* the coarse predicate. Single code path — correct seq scan when the index is absent.
- **Wiring** — indexes are created at graph provisioning. `IGraph.RecreateIndexesAsync` now drops and recreates both GIN indexes around replacement of the per-schema helper function, so it performs a real rebuild rather than an idempotent no-op.

Coarse ⊇ precise ⇒ byte-identical results with or without the index. No per-type/per-property indexes, triggers, or side tables (issue non-goals).

## Validation after review

- AGE full-text and index focused lane: 45 tests passed.
- Added an OID regression test proving `RecreateIndexesAsync` rebuilds the physical indexes.
- The helper and coarse predicate include JSON string values only and exclude `Id` and internal metadata, preserving parity with precise typed and dynamic search.
- Combined stack: 2,504 tests with 0 failures on the first full run; portable local CodeQL is clean.

## Migration

None. Internal execution optimization.

author: ohassen
body:
## Why

Investigating why **NVDA** and **MSFT** show up as BDS-friendly in `constituents.csv` surfaced two distinct problems:

- **NVDA** was screened (6/22) and the model returned **NOT_TARGETED** — a verdict under a definition that only counted *named consumer-boycott/divestment* campaigns.
- **MSFT** was **never given a real verdict** — it has sat at `UNKNOWN` since day one, and `classify_symbol` treats `UNKNOWN` exactly like `YES` (eligible/held). ~234 of the currently-held names are riding on `UNKNOWN`.

So the BDS step, as built, only ever *excluded* the ~20 names it positively confirmed as targets and held everything else. Material complicity in the Israeli military / occupation / settlements (e.g. cloud & AI for the military, chips) went uncaught because the old definition keyed only on named boycotts.

## What changed (`constituent_scan.py`, `constituent_scan.yml`)

- **Broadened `BDS_SYSTEM`.** A company is `TARGETED` if it is a named boycott/divestment target **OR** is materially complicit in the Israeli military, occupation, or settlements — supplying cloud/AI/chips/surveillance/weapons technology to the military, or operating in/servicing settlements. Grounded in AFSC *Investigate*, the UN OHCHR settlement-business database, *Who Profits*, and *No Tech / No Azure for Apartheid* coverage. A deliberate floor is kept: merely having customers, an office, or R&D in Israel is **not** enough.
- **Added `BDS_DEFINITION_VERSION` (=2), persisted in `bds_state.json`.** When the stored version trails the code, cached `YES`/`UNKNOWN` verdicts for names re-screened this run are invalidated so they're re-evaluated under the new definition — instead of waiting for the September quarterly refresh. The **permanent blacklist is never invalidated**, and the version is recorded only after a batch actually completes.
- **Replaced `_write_bds_refresh` with a merge-writing `_write_bds_state`** so `last_refresh` and `definition_version` coexist.
- **Added a manual `bds_only` run mode.** `SCAN_MODE=bds_only` skips the live HalalScreener Sharia re-checks and reuses cached grades, then runs the full BDS screen → state machine → force-sells → CSV/report update. Exposed as a `workflow_dispatch` **`mode`** input (`full` | `bds_only`) so the screen can be applied on demand instead of waiting for the nightly scan.

## How to run it on demand

Actions → **Constituent Scan** → **Run workflow** → set **mode = `bds_only`**. (Or dispatch the workflow with `{"mode": "bds_only"}`.) It re-screens the eligible S&P universe (~490 names, Opus + web search via the Message Batches API) under the broadened definition, flips newly-complicit names to `NO`, blacklists them permanently, and force-sells any held (**PAPER** account).

**Note on cost:** each `bds_only` (or quarterly) re-screen is one large grounded batch, on the order of tens of $.

## Testing

- `ast.parse` clean; YAML valid; no dangling `_write_bds_refresh` references; `SCAN_MODE` flag parses (`bds_only`→True, unset→False).
- Unit-tested the state helpers against the real `bds_state.json`: reads as v1 → re-screen triggers; version-only write preserves `last_refresh`; post-refresh write sets both and stops re-triggering.
- Verified invalidation clears non-blacklisted S&P verdicts (NVDA/MSFT) while preserving blacklisted `NO` entries.
- Triggered run #20 on this branch in `bds_only` mode to validate end-to-end; results commit back to this branch.

## Not addressed here (flagged for follow-up)

- `classify_symbol` still treats `UNKNOWN` as eligible; this PR narrows the gap by re-screening but doesn't change that policy.
- Already-blacklisted names (AME, CVX, HD…) get re-logged/re-"sold" daily because removed names drop out of the CSV carry-forward — a separate churn bug.

- `transform()` now takes `exploreState: ExploreState` (imported from `exploreReducer`, which is exactly what the sole caller passes) and returns `{ formData: QueryFormData; controlsState: ControlStateMapping }` instead of `any`.

- ...getFormDataFromControls(targetControlsState as any),

author: narek-keshishyan
body:
## I have read the [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) file.

YES

## What kind of change does this PR introduce?

Bug fix.

## What is the current behavior?

The `update` and `remove` functions in `packages/pg-meta/src/pg-meta-roles.ts` build a `do $$ ... $$` block whose not-found branch references an `id` variable that is never declared (the block only declares `old record`):

```sql
select * into old from roles where <identifier>;
if old is null then
  raise exception 'Cannot find role with id %', id;
end if;
```

So updating or removing a role that doesn't exist fails with a confusing `column "id" does not exist` instead of a meaningful message. The identifier can also be a `name` rather than an `id`, in which case referencing `id` makes even less sense. (The retrieve-by-id path is unaffected, which is why existing tests didn't catch it.)

Reproduced against Postgres 16:

```
=# do $$ declare old record; begin old := null;
     if old is null then raise exception 'Cannot find role with id %', id; end if; end $$;
ERROR:  column "id" does not exist
```

## What is the new behavior?

Both branches raise a static, identifier-agnostic message:

```sql
raise exception 'Cannot find role matching the provided identifier';
```

Adds tests asserting that `update` and `remove` on a missing role surface this message. Verified against a local Postgres (`roles.test.ts`: 5/5 passing, including the existing create/update/delete happy path).

## Additional context

Only the not-found error message changes; the success path of `update`/`remove` is untouched.

author: narek-keshishyan
body:
## I have read the [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) file.

YES

## What kind of change does this PR introduce?

Bug fix.

## What is the current behavior?

`AnimatedCounter` (`packages/ui/src/components/AnimatedCounter/AnimatedCounter.tsx`) zero-pads the in-flight value to the width of the target so the element keeps a stable width during the animation. For percentages it padded the **signed** string:

```ts
const targetString = targetValue.toFixed(1)   // e.g. "-13.4"
const currentString = currentValue.toFixed(1) // e.g. "-2.0"
const paddedCurrent = currentString.padStart(targetString.length, '0')
```

For a negative percentage the `-` sign is counted in the width, so the padding zero is inserted **before** the minus sign: a value of `-2.0` animating toward `-13.4` renders as `0-2.0%`. Negative values are a documented use case for this component (see the `prefix` prop docs).

## What is the new behavior?

The padding is applied to the numeric magnitude and the sign is re-attached afterwards, so `-2.0` toward `-13.4` renders as `-02.0%`. The formatting logic is extracted into a pure, exported `getPaddedCounterValue` helper.

Adds unit tests (`AnimatedCounter.test.tsx`) covering positive, negative (regression), full-width, prefixed, and plain-number cases.

## Additional context

Plain-number formatting is unchanged; only the percentage padding path is affected.

author: imlk0
body:
## Summary

Adds ingress-side `ohttp.tls` (bool) + `ohttp.tls_ca_certs` (list of PEM file paths) config so the ingress wraps its OHTTP-encrypted POST in HTTPS (`https://host:port/path`) when `tls: true`, terminating at a TLS-terminating gateway in front of the egress. Default (`null`/omitted/`false`) keeps plain `http://` — additive and backward compatible.

Motivation: a TLS-terminating gateway (e.g. an HTTPS load balancer) may sit in front of the egress. The ingress must post the OHTTP ciphertext to the gateway over HTTPS so the gateway can terminate TLS before forwarding the raw OHTTP-over-HTTP bytes to the egress.

The scheme lives on the OHTTP forwarding layer (not the endpoint), so it covers **every ingress mode** (Mapping / HttpProxy / Socks5 / Netfilter / Hook).

## Changes

- **`tng/src/config/ingress.rs`** — `OHttpArgs.tls: Option<bool>` + `tls_ca_certs: Vec<String>`. `tls_ca_certs` is `#[cfg(not(wasm))]`: a browser has no filesystem, so the field does not exist on wasm; providing it in a wasm config is a parse error (`deny_unknown_fields`). New serde unit tests for defaults + round-trip.
- **`tng/src/tunnel/ingress/protocol/ohttp/security/mod.rs`** — `scheme_from_tls(Option<bool>) -> &'static str` (`Some(true)⇒"https"`, else `"http"`); `build_ohttp_http_client` builds the reqwest client and (native) loads CAs via `reqwest::Certificate::from_pem_bundle` with fail-fast `with_context` labels at ingress startup; wasm builds a plain client (browser controls TLS). `construct_base_url` emits `{scheme}://{authority}{path}`. Errors preserve the chain (no string-formatting); logging uses `?error` structured form. Unit tests for CA-loading success / missing-path / malformed-PEM / no-CA.
- **`tng-testsuite`** — `AppType::TlsTcpProxy` TLS-terminating raw-TCP proxy fixture (tokio-rustls acceptor + bidirectional `tokio::io::copy`) mirroring `load_balancer.rs`; embedded webpki-compliant CA/server/key PEMs in `tests/ohttp/tls_fixtures.rs` (critical `CA:TRUE`+`certSign`+SKI/AKI on the CA; `CA:FALSE`+`digitalSignature`/`keyEncipherment`+`serverAuth`+SANs on the server). Dev-deps: `tokio-rustls`, `rustls-pemfile`, `tempfile`.
- **End-to-end test** `tests/ohttp/ohttp_tls.rs::test_ohttp_forwarded_over_tls` — `no_ra` on both sides, inserts the `TlsTcpProxy` between ingress and egress, and proves the full path: client → ingress (TLS-wrapped OHTTP POST to `https://192.168.1.1:20002`) → gateway (TLS termination) → plain TCP `127.0.0.1:20001` (egress mapping-in) → egress OHTTP decap → backend. Passes.
- **`docs/configuration.md` + `docs/configuration_zh.md`** — document both fields (bilingual).
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — ban hard-wrapping prose in human-readable Markdown.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- `cargo clippy -p tng -p tng-testsuite --all-targets` Finished (no new warnings from this change; pre-existing `tokio::spawn` disallowed-method lints are consistent across all existing `app/*.rs` fixtures).
- `cargo build -p tng -p tng-testsuite --tests` EXIT 0.
- `cargo test -p tng --lib security::` → 65 passed.
- `cargo test -p tng-testsuite --test ohttp_tls` → 1 passed (e2e).

## Compatibility

Additive only — new optional fields with backward-compatible defaults. No existing config/endpoint/protocol breaks. Not logged in `version_compatibility.md` (no breaking change).

author: jml-89
body:
## What this is

Documentation-only PR that sets the load-bearing decisions **before** any implementation, so the design is argued out while it's cheap to change. No code yet — the docs are the deliverable.

## Contents

- **`README.md`** — repo framing, stack at a glance, links to the docs.
- **`docs/decisions/0001-tech-stack.md`** — ADR recording the stack:
  - TypeScript + Vite + Vitest, static build → GitHub Pages.
  - **three.js with an orthographic camera** — reads as flat 2D today, but a real 3D scene underneath keeps depth/lighting/2.5D/post-fx open without a rewrite. Records why over Canvas 2D (too limiting) and PixiJS (WebGL effects but no real depth).
  - Rust/WASM considered and **declined for now** (no hot compute loop to justify the cost); revisit only as a learning exercise.
- **`docs/architecture.md`** — the structural stakes:
  - **Hexagonal**: pure `core/` kernel behind ports, impure `adapters/`, single `app/` composition root. The folder a file lives in *is* its purity contract.
  - **Time as an injected dependency** — fixed-timestep integer sim ticks (passed as data), render-time `alpha` (renderer-only), coarser AI time. Refresh-rate-independent, background-tab-safe loop.
  - **Randomness as a dependency** — seeded RNG port; same seed → same game.
  - **Input virtualized to intent** — devices → bindings/mapping → intent, behind the kernel; kernel consumes *intent*, never keycodes. Serializable bindings; absolute (`Steer`) + relative (`Turn`) intents with relative resolved in the kernel; buffered per tick with the one-turn-per-tick / no-180° rules in the kernel.
  - **Determinism & replay** — the game is a deterministic fold `finalState = intents.reduce(tick, initialState(seed))`. Recordings are seed + tick-stamped intents (lossless, rebind-proof), unlocking replay, demo mode, ghosts, bug-repro-as-artifact, tests-as-sessions. Guaranteed by the same lint boundary that enables testing.
  - **Rendering is a sink** — state in, pixels out, nothing back; called directly (no port ceremony), kept thin. The orchestration complexity lives upstream in the kernel.
  - **DI by hand** and **ECS-lite by hand** — no container, no query DSL, just manual wiring with seams for later.
  - **Enforcement** — `eslint-plugin-boundaries` for the pure→impure import ban (build failure), plus `no-restricted-globals` in `core/**`. Vitest over the kernel.

## Open questions — all resolved

1. ~~**Input as a port.**~~ ✅ Virtualized, layered intent model.
2. ~~**State serialization.**~~ ✅ Promoted to the determinism/replay goal: the game is a fold over `(seed, intent stream)`.
3. ~~**Renderer-as-port consistency.**~~ ✅ Renderer is a sink — called directly, no port ceremony, kept thin.

Design is settled. Ready to scaffold against once merged.

author: alexey-pelykh
body:
## Spike #150 — headless passkey reliability (the config-shape falsifier)

RESEARCH spike (typed exception SPIKE). **Deliverable:** `docs/decisions/spike-headless-passkey-reliability.md` — evidence-tiered `[VALIDATED]`/`[INFERRED]`/`[BLOCKED]`, mirroring #186. Docs-only; no runtime code touched.

**Question (the gate):** does a headless run of getreceipt's SELF-REGISTERED software passkey (`passkey-self` — own keypair, `attestation:none`, GetReceipt holds the key) need a CONFIGURED automatic per-run PASSWORD fallback resolved in the same run? A yes makes a keyed-by-kind / multi-credential-per-source `authKind` schema (a recorded **non-goal**) load-bearing.

### Answer: **NO** — no configured per-run fallback needed; the scalar `authKind` holds.

Method (issue-mandated order): cheap current-literature probe → getreceipt source analysis → **security-architect** consult (reliability + phishing-downgrade judgment).

- The clean-failure path is **already built**: `UnresolvedChallengeError` → `collect()` surfaces `reauth-required` `[VALIDATED]`.
- The feared intermittency is a **session-correlated STATE change** (RP de-enrollment / `max_auth_age` step-up / anti-bot escalation), **not** random per-run flakiness `[INFERRED, High]` — so a same-run password draw on the **same flagged session** hits the same wall, and a silent passkey→password fallback is a **phishing-resistance downgrade** besides.
- Correct model = the existing one: passkey fails → `reauth-required` → operator re-auths via the **separate, explicit** `--reauth` path (#247). MFA is already an orthogonal sibling, not a second `authKind` `[VALIDATED]`.
- **Scope caveat:** `passkey-self` is itself a self-managed authenticator the render-tier invariant (#258 / #279) said **not** to build (any assertion injection is anti-bot-detectable; programmatic `attestation:none` registration is ATO-attack-shaped) — _a fortiori_ strengthening the verdict.

**Empirical confirmation:** `[BLOCKED]` — needs a live passkey-enrolled account a headless spike cannot synthesize; scoped Open/Blocked with a concrete per-RP protocol (Amazon first). Not fabricated. The verdict is mechanism-grounded/robust across both passkey-viability branches, and the falsifier that would flip it (all four: RP accepts+asserts unattended · failure RANDOM · password succeeds independently on the same session · operator authorizes silent downgrade) is named.

### Recommendation (orchestrator decides close-vs-keep)

- **Recommendation: close the spike as answered.** The config-shape falsifier is answered NO; the keyed-by-kind trigger stays unmet. Do **not** open a keyed-by-kind / multi-credential-per-source follow-up. (Orchestrator decides close-vs-keep.)

## Why

Audit findings on job-status UX:
- `patch_job_step` marked a job **done** when at least one step succeeded and none were pending — prod had 4 failed card steps buried inside "done" deck jobs.
- Once a job left `generating`, no step could be claimed again — **the per-step Retry button on a finished job was a silent server-side no-op** (pre-#238 code had the same early-return, so this was broken since the pipeline shipped).

author: vjvarada
body:
Two things from your feedback: a build (priority pill on cards) and a cleanup (the confusing Urgency sort).

## 1. Priority pill on every Next-Actions card

The matrix-cell **pill** (🔥 Critical, 🚨 Urgent, 📈 High-Leverage, …) now shows on **every card in the list and board views**, among the other pills — previously it appeared only on the dedicated Priority view. So you can read a task's priority at a glance wherever you are.

The delegate/schedule/eliminate **nudge** badge stays **alongside** it — they're different signals: the pill is *what the task is* (its priority level), the nudge is *what to do about it*. On the Priority view (already grouped by level) the pill is icon-only and the nudge is hidden, to avoid repetition.

## 2. Dropped the Urgency sort

**Your question was the right one.** Here's the distinction:

- **Priority** = the matrix cell, computed from *important × urgent × leveraged*. The holistic "how much does this matter" rank.
- **Urgent** = a single derived boolean: overdue or due within 48h. It's just *one input* to priority, derived from the due date.
- **Due date sort** = orders by the raw deadline.

So **"Urgency" as a sort was redundant**: it only bucketed tasks urgent(0)/not(1), which "Due date" already does with finer resolution (soonest first), and which "Priority" already folds in. It added nothing but confusion. Removed it from the sort dropdown — **Priority** and **Due date** remain. (Urgency still exists as a *concept* — it drives the priority matrix and the ⏰ signal — just not as its own sort.)

Frontend-only. `priority.ts ↔ priority.py` CELL_META parity untouched. tsc + eslint clean; priority/parity backend tests pass.

author: deniskrizanovic
body:
## Summary

Authenticates the real-time Y.js sync WebSocket. The socket now shares the
Next.js app's origin/port (one custom Node server in `server.js`), so the
browser sends the httpOnly NextAuth session cookie on the `upgrade` request,
which the server verifies before joining any room. Unauthenticated or
malformed-room upgrades are refused with 401 before any document/awareness
state is sent.

Closes https://github.com/deniskrizanovic/collaborativegherkin/issues/32

## Changes

- **`server.js`** — custom Node server serving Next HTTP + the sync WebSocket
  on one origin; auth gate on `upgrade` via `authorizeUpgrade`; fails fast if
  `AUTH_SECRET` is missing. Y.js sync/awareness protocol relocated from the old
  standalone `y-websocket-server.mjs` (deleted).
- **`src/lib/wsAuth.ts`** (+ tests) — pure auth/authorization helper: verifies
  the `authjs.session-token` JWT and validates the `session-<id>` room name.
- **`e2e/websocket-auth.spec.ts`** — raw-ws tests for the anonymous, valid, and
  malformed-room paths.

## Code-review fixes (commit 2)

A `/code-review` pass surfaced five findings, all fixed:

1. **`ws` was a devDependency** but `server.js` is the prod entrypoint — moved
   to `dependencies` so `--omit=dev` installs boot.
2. **Awareness leak on disconnect** — removed `room.ydoc.clientID` (the server
   doc's id) instead of the departing client's ids. Now tracks each
   connection's `controlledIds` and clears exactly those on close, so ghost
   cursors don't linger.
3. **Phantom dependencies** — declared `@auth/core`, `@next/env`, `lib0` as
   direct deps instead of relying on transitive hoisting.
4. **Flaky/slow e2e** — the positive test idled to a 3s timeout; now resolves on
   first sync message (3.1s → 57ms), timeout kept as a backstop.
5. **Logger crash on unwritable `logs/`** — dev disk-logging degrades to stdout
   with a warning instead of throwing at import. (Prod was already stdout-only.)

## Verification

- Unit: 234/234 pass
- Typecheck: clean
- E2E: 105 passed, 1 skipped

body:
Closes all four open dependency-update issues. Issues #179, #180 and #181 are the same physical change (the three `drupal/core-*` packages move together), so they land in one commit; #182 is a separate contrib patch bump.

## Commits

**1. Drupal core 11.3.13 → 11.4.2** (#179, #180, #181)

The existing `"^11.3"` constraint already permits 11.4.x, so `composer.json` only changes for the item below — the version move itself is lock-file only.

Two things core 11.4 newly introduces:

- **`symfony/runtime` added to `allow-plugins`.** `drupal/core` 11.4 now requires `symfony/runtime ^7.4`, which ships a Composer plugin. Composer blocks unknown plugins by default, so the install aborted until it was trusted. Upstream Drupal's own `RecommendedProject` template trusts it in 11.4.x, so this mirrors upstream rather than working around the guard.
- **`web/autoload_runtime.php` gitignored.** A new drupal-scaffold generated file that wires Drupal's `DrupalRuntime` into the Symfony runtime component. Every other scaffold artifact (`index.php`, `autoload.php`, …) is already ignored in `web/.gitignore`; this follows that convention.

Config changes came from two core update hooks. They were **hand-applied to `config/sync`** rather than via `drush cex`, so that local dev drift (`views_ui`, `system.site` mail, dev `preprocess`/`max_age`) was not swept in:

- `system.performance` — `system_post_update_migrate_compress_setting` renames `css.gzip`/`js.gzip` to `css.compress`/`js.compress`. The `gzip` schema key is deprecated in 11.4 and removed in 12.0. Production values (`preprocess: true`, `compress: true`, `max_age: 3600`) are preserved.
- `config/sync/field.settings.yml` — deleted. `field_post_update_clear_purge_batch_size` removes the config object entirely when `purge_batch_size` is at its default of 50, since that was its only key. The setting now lives in `$settings['field_purge_batch_size']`.

**2. `drupal/media_image_display_entity_view` 1.0.4 → 1.0.5** (#182)

Patch bump, satisfied by the existing `^1.0` constraint. Lock-file only, no database updates, no config changes.

## Verification

- `drush updb` — `system_update_11400`, `system_update_11401` + 3 post-updates applied cleanly
- `drush status` — Drupal 11.4.2, bootstrap successful
- `composer audit` — no security advisories
- `ddev phpstan` — no errors
- `phpcs` (drupal + drupal-practice, via lefthook) — passing
- **Cypress: 15/15 passing** across `smoke`, `search`, `add-book`, `activity-lifecycle`
- `/` and `/user/login` return HTTP 200, no errors in watchdog

## Note (unrelated to this PR)

`ddev cy:test` fails from a clean state: npm's `allow-scripts` gate (added in 814f9f4 for the Dependabot alerts) blocks Cypress's post-install binary download, so `ddev cy:install` never actually fetches the binary. I worked around it locally with `cd tests && ./node_modules/.bin/cypress install`. Worth fixing separately if CI runs Cypress.

author: brocksinet
body:
The Store API MCP endpoint (`/store-api/_mcp`) advertised every registered tool flat, while the Admin endpoint uses progressive disclosure: a reduced `tools/list` (`shopware-tool-search`, `shopware-toolsets-list`, `shopware-toolset-enable`) with the rest discovered via search and activated with `shopware-toolset-enable`, which emits a `tools/listChanged` notification. This PR gives the Store API the same behaviour so both endpoints work identically for MCP clients.

It is done **additively**: the discovery classes are already constructed scope-neutrally, so the Store API gets its own behaviour by registering **second DI instances** pointed at the store-api registry, params and an isolated session registry. The Admin stack is untouched. A full scope-agnostic refactor was considered and rejected as disproportionate (no third API scope is expected, and it would rework Admin's tool discovery).

### Scope-neutral reuse

`McpAllowlistListRequestHandler`'s allowlist provider becomes nullable (null = unrestricted); a store-api instance is registered tagged `mcp.store_api.request_handler`. Store-api instances of `McpCapabilityCatalog`, `McpToolsetRegistry`, `McpSessionRegistry` (own cache namespace) and `McpListChangedNotifier` are wired against the store-api registry. No admin service definitions change.

### Per-scope analysis params

`McpToolDiscoveryCompilerPass` and `McpToolAnalysisCompilerPass` are parameterised by `(tag, param-prefix)` and run once per scope, so store-api tools get their own `shopware.store_api_mcp.*` group/dependency/privilege/advertised-tools maps alongside the admin `shopware.mcp.*` set.

### Store-api meta-tools

`StoreApiToolsetsListTool` and `StoreApiToolsetEnableTool` are added (thin subclasses — the SDK binds a tool to the class carrying `#[McpTool]` and the store-api service locator keys on the service id, so distinct classes are required). `StoreApiToolSearchTool` moves to the `default` group and carries the enable usage hint. The store-api `ToolsetEnableTool` fires the store-api notifier, and `StoreApiMcpServerController` registers the MCP session id so `listChanged` targets store-api sessions only — no cross-scope notification.

### Result

Store API `tools/list` now advertises only the meta-tools; `shopware-toolset-enable` reveals the rest and signals `listChanged`, matching Admin.

## References

Ref #17509
Blocked by #17997

Stacked PR: base is `feat/mcp-toolset-enable` (#17997), sibling to #18270. Merges after the stack. Note: this branch is based on #17997 (pre-flag-removal), so once #18270 lands the remaining `MCP_SERVER` references in the new files must be dropped.

author: arashi87
body:
## What

Closes the last acceptance criterion of the ghost-sweep re-bucketing bug: a live scenariotest regression covering the settled-bytes fold (DESIGN §3.5) and its hardest consequence, **MAC reuse** — a deleted VM's MAC reborn on a different tenant's port must neither inherit nor replay the old tenant's bytes.

The mechanism is general, not a one-off:

- **Step-scripted scenarios.** `Scenario.Steps` optionally replaces `run`'s classic drive-all/assert-all line with an ordered program executed between up and down. Empty steps = the classic loop, so the five zone scenarios are untouched. `Step` is an open interface — a future operational step (e.g. taking an agent down for a window) is one new type, no executor changes.
- **Vocabulary** (grown on demand, not speculation): `DriveStep`, `AssertStep`, `CaptureStep` (counter + settled-flows snapshot), `DeleteVMStep` (single-VM teardown, MAC recorded first), `AwaitSweepStep` (polls `cubecos_gc_settled_flows_total` past the captured base), `MonotoneStep` (every captured tuple ≥ its captured value — Contract 7, live), `MaxGrowthStep` (bounded growth: covers both "no re-bucket to unknown" and "reborn MAC starts from zero"), `BootVMStep` (realizes a `Scenario.Deferred` VM mid-script, optionally pinning a deleted VM's MAC), `SleepStep`.
- Steps declare required /metrics families; `run` refuses **before realizing anything** when an agent predates them — no mid-scenario timeout with a misleading cause.
- Harness plumbing: `PortSpec.MACAddress` + `Cloud.PortMAC` (explicit-MAC ports, MAC readback; the fake cloud models Neutron's per-network MAC uniqueness), `ScrapeResult.SettledFlows`.
- `mac-reuse` is an ordinary registry entry — one topology (vm-d deferred) plus a 12-step script; plain `scenariotest run mac-reuse` executes the whole thing. `list` gains a STEPS column.

## Tests

- Full-loop fixture over the scripted fakes (deferred VM booted by the step with the captured MAC, mid-run delete before the final down, all six check groups present in the report).
- **Regression-detector negative test**: a fake reproducing the pre-fix agent (history re-buckets to unknown, reborn MAC inherits) must produce failing monotone / unknown / zero-inheritance rows — the scenario detects, not just passes.
- Pre-fold-agent refusal happens before realize; sweep-timeout errors diagnosably and still tears down; the default script is pinned as Drive→Assert; registry invariants validate step-embedded expectations.
- `go build` / `vet` / `test ./...` green.

## Live validation (dev-cmp, 2026-07-14)

`scenariotest run mac-reuse` against the staging agent (settled-fold build): **PASS, 23/23 rows** —

- tenant A drive: tx +1,060,282 / rx +1,062,204 ≥ 1 MiB
- monotone across ghost sweep: all 7 tenant-A tuples unchanged after the VM delete + fold
- no re-bucket to unknown: `unknown/same_tenant` exactly unchanged
- reborn MAC starts from zero: tenant B's tuples flat (delta 0) after booting the deferred VM with the deleted VM's MAC
- tenant B drive: tx +1,061,456 / rx +1,062,516 ≥ 1 MiB
- old tenant unchanged after reuse: all tenant-A tuples still unchanged

The run also demonstrated **cross-run monotonicity**: baselines carried the previous validation run's settled bytes forward (tenant A `same_tenant/tx` 2,133,936 → 3,194,218 across two runs and two sweeps). Teardown clean (residual `cube:mgr` ports swept), projects kept, report persisted.

An earlier bespoke-runner variant of this scenario also passed live (22/22) before the rework to the general step model; the step-model run above is the current code.

Closes bigstack-oss/cube-cos-network-telemetry#111

author: zhengbrody
body:
## What

Fixes the **anthropic-topup persistence bug** found in the 2026-07-14 prod compliance sweep: `/admin`'s "set Claude balance after a top-up" (PR #103) has persisted **nothing** since it shipped.

- **Root cause**: the marker row uses `kind='anthropic_topup'`, but migration 0002's `usage_events_kind_check` only allows `('analysis','chat','tool_call')` — Postgres rejected every insert (23514) and the fail-soft telemetry writer swallowed the error, so the endpoint returned 200 while storing nothing (confirmed empirically against prod).
- **Migration 0010** widens the CHECK to include `'anthropic_topup'`.
- **Endpoint hardening**: `billing_admin_set_anthropic_topup` now reads the marker back after writing and returns **503 service_unavailable** when the write did not persist — this silent-200 class can't recur.
- **Tests**: persisted→200 · write-swallowed→503 · stale-read-back→503.

## Migration safety (flagging explicitly)

0010 is a `DROP CONSTRAINT` + `ADD CONSTRAINT` in one transaction (via `db-migrate.yml --single-transaction`). It is **constraint-widening only** — no data is read, modified, or deleted; every existing row already satisfies the wider check, so the ADD validates instantly. It is not byte-"additive" (it replaces a constraint), which is why it's called out here rather than merged silently.

## Deploy order

1. Merge → 2. `gh workflow run db-migrate.yml -f migration=0010_usage_event_kinds.sql` → 3. GHCR pull-only deploy → 4. prod-verify the topup endpoint actually persists (and cleanup the test marker).

Removes **28 methods across 6 files** in the matrix / can-i-deploy code that have **zero callers** anywhere in `lib/` or `spec/` (verified by exhaustive grep, including dynamic dispatch and decorator duck-typing).

Each change is a self-contained `chore(matrix): remove …` commit so they can be reviewed and cherry-picked individually:

| Commit | Removes |
|---|---|
| `remove dead Integration predicate/comparison methods` | `Integration#<=>`, `#to_hash`, `#to_s`, and all 5 `involves_*` methods |
| `remove dead MatrixRow instance methods` | `MatrixRowInstanceMethods#to_s`, `#pacticipant_names`, `#involves_pacticipant_with_name?` |
| `remove dead ResolvedSelector#most_specific_criterion` | `ResolvedSelector#most_specific_criterion` |

This came out of a **code-coverage review of the matrix/can-i-deploy test safety net in #966**. A full-suite SimpleCov run showed the HTTP/decorator layer at 100% but pockets of uncovered code in the query/reasoning engine. Investigating each gap, these methods turned out to have no callers at all — dead code rather than a behavioural coverage gap. With the dead code gone, the affected files rise toward full coverage: `integration.rb` 76→100%, `unresolved_selector.rb` 94→100%, `parse_query.rb` 98→100%, `reason.rb` 79→92%.
