author: sohumt123
body:
### Summary

A Google-style docstring whose summary line is **immediately followed by an `Args:` section with no blank line in between** silently loses every parameter description, and the raw `Args:` block leaks into the function/tool description.

```python
@function_tool
def get_weather(city: str, units: str) -> str:
    """Get the weather for a city.
    Args:
        city: The city to get weather for.
        units: Temperature units to use.
    """
    ...
```

Before this change:

- `params_json_schema["properties"]["city"]` has **no `description`**
- `tool.description` becomes `"Get the weather for a city.\nArgs:\n    city: ...\n    units: ..."` (the raw block)

So the model never sees any parameter description and gets a malformed tool description. Adding the (PEP 257 / Google-style) blank line fixes it, but the failure is completely silent, which makes it easy to ship a degraded tool without noticing.

**Root cause.** `generate_func_documentation` in `src/agents/function_schema.py` passes `inspect.getdoc(func)` to griffe's Google parser. griffe skips a section header when there is no blank line above it and the next line is indented, logging `Possible section skipped, reasons: Missing blank line above section`; the header and its body are appended to the summary text instead of becoming a parameters section. The numpy and sphinx parsers already tolerate the missing blank line, so this is a Google-only gap.

**Fix.** When the resolved style is `google`, normalize the docstring before building the griffe `Docstring`: insert a single blank line before a recognized section header (`Args:`/`Returns:`/`Raises:`/… as an exact `Header:` line) that directly follows non-indented top-level text (the summary) and is itself followed by an indented block. The anchor mirrors griffe's own recognition — column-0 header, case-insensitive section keys, indented line below — so inline mentions (`see Args: below`) and headers already preceded by a blank line or an indented body are left untouched. The helper returns the original string object unchanged when no insertion is needed, so well-formed docstrings stay byte-identical.

This is **not** the same as the closed PR #3795. That PR addressed a *different* variant (a docstring with no summary that opens directly with `Args:`), and its approach (prepending `"\n"`) was correctly closed by @seratch as a no-op because griffe applies `inspect.cleandoc()` internally, which strips the leading newline. This PR targets the distinct `Missing blank line above section` skip path (a header mid-docstring, after a non-empty summary) and demonstrates a real base failure. Out of scope and deliberately left unchanged: admonitions (`Note:`/`Warning:`), headers with trailing title text (`Examples: foo`), and griffe's separate `Extraneous blank line below section title` skip reason.

### Test plan

Added five tests to `tests/test_function_schema.py` covering `function_schema`, `generate_func_documentation`, and the end-to-end `@function_tool` path, plus a multi-section case and a byte-identity control for the already-well-formed docstring.

Running the new tests on the base (before the `src/agents/function_schema.py` change) reproduces the bug (griffe logs `DEBUG:griffe:<module>: Possible section skipped, reasons: Missing blank line above section`):

```
$ uv run pytest tests/test_function_schema.py -k "google_docstring" -q
>       assert properties["city"]["description"] == "The city to get weather for."
E       KeyError: 'description'
...
4 failed, 1 passed, 26 deselected in 0.13s
```

(The one passing test is the byte-identity control on the well-formed docstring, which correctly parses on base too.)

After the fix:

```
$ uv run pytest tests/test_function_schema.py -k "google_docstring" -q
5 passed, 26 deselected in 0.05s

$ uv run pytest tests/test_function_schema.py tests/test_doc_parsing.py \
      tests/test_function_tool.py tests/test_function_tool_decorator.py -q
99 passed in 0.84s
```

`make format-check` and `make lint` are clean; `mypy` and `pyright` pass on the changed source file. `.agents/skills/code-change-verification/scripts/run.sh` runs `make format` (clean), `make lint` (pass), and the full `make tests` suite (pass). `make typecheck` reports 6 errors, but all of them are pre-existing on the base branch in files this PR does not touch (`src/agents/sandbox/session/archive_ops.py` and two test modules that depend on an optional `any_llm` stub / a newer-Python `eager_task_factory`); I verified they are unchanged from base and unrelated to this change.

Validated against the locked `griffelib==2.0.1` (`griffelib>=2, <3`).

Disclosure: I used an AI coding assistant while investigating and preparing this change; I reviewed the diff, ran the tests, and stand behind the result.

### Issue number

No linked issue — self-discovered while reading `function_schema.py` (same discovery context as #3795, but a different, actually-failing variant).

### Checks

- [x] I've added new tests, if relevant
- [x] I've run `.agents/skills/code-change-verification/scripts/run.sh`
- [x] I've confirmed all verification steps pass (except pre-existing, unrelated `make typecheck` errors documented above)
- [ ] If using Codex, I've run `/review` before submitting this PR

author: thireus
body:
This is extended work on the on-demand tensor reload feature contributed by @magikRUKKOLA in #1989 — full credit to him for the core hot-swap machinery (tensor provenance tracking, mtime change detection, surgical buffer reload, MoE sibling resync, CUDA graph invalidation). This PR builds on top of it; nothing from #1989 is reverted or redesigned.

## Motivation

#1989 lets `llama-perplexity` loop autonomously: after each pass it re-checks the source GGUF files, reloads whatever changed (optionally after running `LLAMA_PERPLEXITY_PRE_RELOAD_SCRIPT`), and **exits when nothing changed**. That works well when the tool itself drives the experiment, but not when an *external* orchestrator does — e.g. per-tensor quantization calibration sweeps ([GGUF Tool Suite `benchmark_each_tensor.sh`](https://github.com/Thireus/GGUF-Tool-Suite)), which swap one tensor's shard at a time, need one cleanly separated log per benchmark, and must decide themselves when to reload, recompute or stop. Until now each of the thousands of benchmark rounds paid a full model load (10–20 min for large MoE models). #1989 was also only tested for PPL, not KLD.

## What this PR adds

**1. Signal mode for `llama-perplexity`** (`examples/perplexity/perplexity.cpp`)

When `LLAMA_HOTSWAP_ENABLED` is set together with the two new variables `LLAMA_HOTSWAP_CONTROL_FILE` and `LLAMA_HOTSWAP_STATUS_FILE`, the tool never terminates on its own. After each evaluation it publishes `done <iter> <seq>` to the status file and waits for a command in the control file:

* `reload <seq>` — reload changed tensors (via #1989's `llama_reload_changed_tensors`), then re-evaluate; if nothing changed, publish `reload_failed` and keep waiting
* `compute <seq>` — re-evaluate without reloading
* `exit <seq>` — terminate cleanly

Design notes:
* Plain files instead of POSIX signals, so the same protocol works unchanged on Windows, macOS and Linux.
* Monotonic sequence numbers make duplicate/stale command delivery harmless; status updates are published atomically (tmp + rename) and retried until they succeed, so a transient sharing violation (antivirus/indexers on Windows) cannot deadlock the driver.
* Timings are reset per iteration so each captured log reads like an independent run.
* The legacy #1989 loop mode (env var only, with the optional pre-reload script) is untouched — without the new variables behaviour is exactly as before. Works with all evaluation flavours; `--kl-divergence` is re-entrant (base logits re-read per pass), so KLD sweeps now work.

**2. Correctness fix in the reload core** (`src/llama-reload.cpp`)

The "returning to original" path decided by dtype alone (`curr_type == src.original_type`) and reattached the original in-memory snapshot **without reading the new file's bytes**. A swapped tensor whose on-disk dtype happens to match the originally loaded one — but with different data (e.g. same quant type produced with a different imatrix, or a quantization fallback landing on the baseline's dtype) — would silently keep the stale weights while still logging `reloaded tensor`. The returning path now also reads the tensor bytes and refreshes the (reattached) buffer, guarded against mmap-backed tensors which must not be written in place. A genuine restore copies identical bytes, so the #1989 sanity-check property (byte-identical restore ⇒ exact baseline PPL) is preserved and strengthened.

**3. Documentation** (`docs/development/on-demand-tensor-reload.md`)

The signal-mode protocol (states, commands, sequence semantics) and a driver-loop walkthrough.

## Testing

* Driven end-to-end on Windows by `benchmark_each_tensor.sh --hotswap` for per-tensor KLD calibration sweeps: model loaded once, each subsequent round reloads only the restored + newly swapped tensors before recomputing.
* Protocol exercised against a driver test harness covering: fresh start, reload, recompute-without-reload, `reload_failed`, process crash mid-compute, graceful exit, and stale/duplicate command delivery.
* This extended capability is being actively used in the tensor benchmarking of GLM-5.2 here: https://github.com/Thireus/GGUF-Tool-Suite/issues/90. Logs attached as evidence: 
[bench_hotswap_session.20260714_005941.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29996809/bench_hotswap_session.20260714_005941.log), e.g. see lines: 
```
main: hot-swap command received: reload
reloaded tensor 'blk.42.ffn_down_exps.weight'
reloaded tensor 'blk.76.ffn_gate_shexp.weight'
reloaded tensor 'blk.76.ffn_down_shexp.weight'
reloaded tensor 'blk.76.ffn_up_shexp.weight' 
```

author: code-yeongyu
body: ## Summary Fast-exiting foreground PTY commands could report completion before the reader thread had delivered their final output. This made valid output appear as `(no output)` and could cause the terminal workflow to abandon a healthy foreground shell. This PR makes exit completion wait for PTY output delivery and registers terminal listeners before session startup, so final output is observable before `waitExit` resolves. ## Changes - Close the PTY writer/master and join the reader before synchronous or background waits return. - Acknowledge N-API data callback delivery before allowing the native reader to advance. - Subscribe coding-agent terminal output and exit handlers before starting the session. - Add deterministic regressions for blocked reader drain and fast-session startup ordering. - Refresh the tracked Darwin ARM64 native prebuilds. ## QA / Evidence - **Failing-first Rust regression:** `background_wait_does_not_complete_before_reader_drain` failed before the fix with `background wait completed before the reader callback drained final output`, then passed after the ordering change. Artifacts: `local-ignore/qa-evidence/20260714-foreground-shell-wedge/red-focused.log` and `green-focused.log`. - **Failing-first TypeScript regression:** startup ordering observed `["start", "onData"]` before the fix and `["onData", "start"]` after it. Artifacts: `red-startup-ordering.log` and `green-startup-ordering.log` in the same evidence directory. - **Delayed live-callback regression:** blocking the live JavaScript environment for 5.5 seconds reproduced `waitExit` with empty output before the teardown-aware fix; afterward the native callback produced `LATE_CALLBACK_MARKER` before `waitExit`. Artifacts: `red-delayed-live-callback.log` and `green-delayed-live-callback.log`. - **Real foreground native PTY smoke:** 200 fast-exit iterations preserved every exact marker; empty output remained `(no output)`; exit code 7 was reported correctly; backend was native. Artifact: `foreground-fast-exit-smoke.log`. - **PTY QA channel:** `pty-drive.mjs --self-test` passed 7/7 on the native backend, including wait, stdin steering, resize/snapshot, registry teardown, no orphans, and unchanged real auth. Artifact: `pty-drive.log`. - **Adjacent suites:** `cargo test -p senpi-pty` passed 12 unit tests plus manual QA; `packages/pty` passed 42 tests; terminal extension passed 12 tests; native prebuild freshness passed. Artifacts: `final-teardown-aware-cargo.log`, `final-teardown-aware-pty-package.log`, `final-teardown-aware-terminal-extension.log`, and `final-teardown-aware-prebuild.log`. - **Repository checks:** `npm run check` exited 0, and deterministic mock-loop QA passed 5/5 without real provider calls. Artifacts: `npm-run-check-final.log` and `mock-loop-self-test.log`. ## Risks - Waiting for JavaScript callback delivery adds ordering synchronization to native output delivery. The delayed live-callback regression proves there is no wall-clock escape while the environment is live; the Worker teardown regression proves `ThreadsafeFunction::aborted()` releases the reader when the environment closes. - Closing the master before joining remains required for ConPTY. Existing resize, signal, timeout, cancellation, and process-tree tests remain green. - Listener registration now uses explicit construction plus `start()` instead of the convenience factory. The startup-order regression and terminal extension suite cover that lifecycle change. ## Secret safety Evidence contains no tokens, auth headers, cookies, environment dumps, or credentials. The QA harness verified the real `~/.senpi/agent/auth.json` hash was unchanged. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes a race where fast‑exiting PTY commands could finish before their last output arrived. Exit now waits for final output, listeners are registered before start, and native callbacks wait for the JS handler (or N-API teardown) to avoid leaked reader threads. - **Bug Fixes** - `senpi-pty`: drain output on exit by closing writer/master and joining the reader before returning from `wait` or background waits. - `senpi-pty`: data callback acknowledges delivery and only unblocks once the JS handler runs or the N-API environment is torn down; propagates callback errors and prevents reader advance or thread leaks (incl. Worker shutdown). - `@earendil-works/pi-pty` runtime: use `new TerminalSession()`, subscribe to `onData`/`onExit`, then call `start()` to capture fast output. - Added deterministic tests for reader drain, startup ordering, and native callback lifecycle with fixtures for delayed callbacks, callback throws, and Worker teardown; fixed the Windows fast‑exit command. - **Dependencies** - Refreshed Darwin ARM64 native prebuilds. Written for commit e67cc41c73503888567408675f85e709d4e632c8. Summary will update on new commits.

**CI perf harness** (`bench/perf-ci.mjs`): a `streamingBenches()` section that measures an end-to-end `wrapStream` drain (shell + 50 chunks + closing HTML; CPU ~4% RME, wall informational, alloc per drain) and the per-suspense-boundary patch render (CPU + alloc), against shipped dist like the existing signals. ## What's changed

- Add Windows path identity normalization functions to pathpackage:

- New tests verify the functionality for case variations, separator variations, long-path prefixes, empty paths, and that sibling/parent-child paths are not treated as duplicates

author: bugenzhao
body:
## Purpose

This draft explores migrating the Rust frontend from `hf-hub` 0.5 to 1.0.

The implementation follows the redesigned 1.0 API:

- reuse one `HFClient` and a typed `HFRepository<RepoTypeModel>`
- resolve cached files through `download_file().local_files_only(true)`
- classify structured `HFError` variants and preserve their source chains
- use the builder-based `info()` and `download_file()` APIs
- migrate the tokenizer benchmarks
- remove the unused `llm-multimodal` `hf-hub` feature so the dependency graph contains one `hf-hub` version

### Blockers

#### 1. Rust TLS and crypto violate the workspace dependency policy

`hf-hub` 1.0.0 has two paths that activate Rust TLS:

1. Its direct `reqwest 0.13` dependency keeps reqwest's default features, which select `default-tls -> rustls`.
2. Its unconditional `hf-xet` dependency reaches `xet-client`, whose default feature is `rustls-tls`.

`reqwest 0.13`'s `rustls` feature selects the AWS-LC provider. As a result, `cargo deny check bans` fails for:

- `rustls`
- `aws-lc-rs`
- `aws-lc-sys`

The Rust workspace deliberately uses `native-tls`/OpenSSL and bans these crates in `rust/deny.toml`. `hf-hub` 1.0.0 exposes no downstream feature combination that selects `native-tls` for both paths.

#### 2. Xet-backed cold-cache downloads stall on GCP

On a GCP GB200 host, a cold-cache download for `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5` consistently behaves as follows:

- `tokenizer_config.json` downloads successfully.
- The 2,795,286-byte Xet-backed `tiktoken.model` remains at zero downloaded bytes until the test timeout.
- Reducing Xet concurrency and setting explicit connect/read timeouts produces the same result.
- A direct HTTP range request to the same resolve URL returns `206` immediately.

Related upstream reports include [xet-core#800](https://github.com/huggingface/xet-core/issues/800) and [xet-core#869](https://github.com/huggingface/xet-core/issues/869). The proposal to make `hf-xet` optional was closed in [huggingface/hf-hub#181](https://github.com/huggingface/hf-hub/pull/181).

#### Dependency impact

The lockfile grows from 575 to 668 packages. The 93-package net increase comes from the unconditional Xet stack, `reqwest 0.13`, rustls/AWS-LC, and their platform-specific dependencies.

This PR will remain a draft while the two blockers above are active.

## Test Plan

```bash
cd rust
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run --workspace
cargo deny check bans
```

Cold-cache reproduction:

```bash
cd rust
HF_HUB_CACHE="$(mktemp -d)" \
  cargo nextest run -p vllm-text \
  tiktoken_real_kimi_k25_tokenizer_files_load_and_handle_special_tokens \
  --run-ignored ignored-only
```

## Test Result

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed
- `cargo nextest run --workspace`: 1,205 passed, 1 skipped
- cache-only resolution test with an unreachable endpoint: passed
- `cargo deny check bans`: failed on `rustls`, `aws-lc-rs`, and `aws-lc-sys` as documented above
- cold-cache Xet reproduction: stalled at zero bytes for `tiktoken.model`

---

- [x] The test plan is documented.
- [x] Test results and current blockers are documented.
- [x] Documentation impact was reviewed; this dependency migration requires no user-facing documentation update.

## Summary

- states the all-length grouped-sector dressed-adjoint identity as an explicit `notready` Chapter 20 theorem;
- records the required oriented-pair exchange `(a,b) -> (b,a)` and the reversal of the unmarked tail;
- distinguishes the all-length Hermiticity input for Lemma L from the single nonzero compression used only to prove coefficient positivity;
- separates raw weights `nu`, gauge phases `zeta`, positive grouped coefficients `c = nu zeta`, and the source notation `mu = c`;
- adds the independent retained-phase-class nonemptiness obligation needed for the empty-chain BNT clause;
- integrates the generic coisometry theorem from #3895 and states the remaining dimension transport, dependent-index flattening, and `finSigmaFinEquiv` adapter precisely;
- updates the Proposition 4.13 paper-gap note.

This change does not claim that Proposition 4.13 is formalized. Both newly isolated mathematical obligations remain `notready`, without Lean tags.

## Source

CPSV16 Proposition 4.13, especially lines 1909–1919 and Figures 7–8.

## Verification

- reader-facing prose check
- `leanblueprint pdf` with final Chapter 20 visual inspection
- standalone paper-gap PDF and visual inspection
- `leanblueprint web`
- `leanblueprint checkdecls`
- `git diff --check`

## Tracking

- reflected marked-chain theorem: #3890
- Proposition 4.13 capstone: #3674

> **Low Risk**
> Changes are blueprint and paper-gap prose only; no runtime or Lean proof code in the diff, and open steps stay explicitly `notready`.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Isolates the remaining Proposition 4.13 gaps** in Chapter 20 and the vertical CF grouping paper note, without claiming those steps are formalized.
> 
> Adds a **`notready` theorem** for the **all-length grouped-sector dressed-adjoint identity** (oriented pair `(a,b) → (b,a)`, reversed unmarked tail) and a separate **`notready` lemma** that a **retained vertical phase class is nonempty** (needed for the length-zero BNT clause). The capstone horizontal→vertical proof is rewired to depend on these obligations plus the **generic block-row coisometry** (`vertical_sector_coisometry`), with **source-specific adapter steps** (`hdim`, `(α,q)`, `finSigmaFinEquiv`) called out explicitly.
> 
> **Notation is split** along the grouping pipeline: raw weights **`ν`**, gauge phases **`ζ`**, positive grouped coefficients **`c = νζ`**, and source **`μ = c`**. Spectrally normalized sector statements use **`ν_k`** where they previously used **`μ_k`**.
> 
> The paper-gap note is aligned: **Lemma L needs self-adjoint compressions at every length**, not the single nonzero compression used only for coefficient positivity; **Gram/unitary normalization is conditional** on dressed-adjoint; coisometry assembly is **generic proved / adapter remaining**.

author: mikewalliser
body:
## What

Rewrites the public thesis surfaces so they articulate what Muster actually is now: an operating system for agentic software teams with a **local, private intelligent layer**.

### The intelligent layer (the new headline)
- Local RAG engine embedded in the stack: FastAPI on :9100, fastembed `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` (384-dim), Postgres + Qdrant + Redis. No API key, no data leaves the box.
- **Elk Chat**: an in-portal assistant over your own knowledge base and task data. The RAG is treated as an untrusted ranking oracle. Every result is re-gated through the portal's role-based permission filter using the caller's own token, so it can never surface a document the user is not allowed to see.
- Security hardening documented: read-key auth, a startup guard that fails closed in production, rate limiting, orphaned-vector reconciliation.

### URL cutover
- Every stale `34.220.64.149.sslip.io` / IP reference replaced with `musterr.dev` / `app.musterr.dev` / `cms.musterr.dev` (53 occurrences across 11 config/provision files, plus the public pages). Transitional "until DNS cuts over" hedging removed. The demo is live on real Let's Encrypt certs.
- `demo@muster.dev` login account left unchanged (it is an account, not a URL).

### Polish
- Public pages (README, `site/index.html`, `site/paper.html`, whitepaper) purged of em dashes per house style. `paper.html` regenerated from the cleaned template + whitepaper.
- Subtle author cross-links added: **Built by Michael Walliser** (walliser.me), **Muster by Analog Elk** (analogelk.com), and a footer photography link (wlsr.me).

## Surfaces touched
`README.md`, `site/index.html` + `site/paper.html` + `site/build-paper.py`, `docs/whitepaper/*`, `WHITEPAPER-LOG.md`, and the config/provision URL sweep (`caddy/`, `portal/`, `provision/`).

## Verification
- Public surfaces: 0 em dashes, 0 stale URLs (audited with an exact U+2014 / string scan).
- `build-paper.py` regenerates `paper.html` clean; JSON parses, Python compiles, shell scripts pass `bash -n`.

No UI-component code changed (static site + docs), so no app screenshot applies. Live-site verification after deploy in the follow-up.

author: gmdjlee
body:
## What

Speeds up Gap Compute "Save All Images" for large batches (1000+ gaps previously took ~26 min).

- **Parallel kaleido rendering**: the batch export worker now renders through a pool of per-thread `kaleido.scopes.plotly.PlotlyScope` instances (each = its own Chromium subprocess) instead of plotly's single global kaleido process. Worker count via `MATRIX2D_EXPORT_WORKERS` (default 4, clamped 1–8, capped at gap count). Falls back to sequential `fig.write_image` if the scope API is unavailable.
- **2D/3D checklist** ("Images") next to the renamed "Save All Images" button — 3D surface rendering is ~90% of the cost (~1.4s/image fixed WebGL overhead, size-independent), so 2D-only runs are dramatically faster.
- **Downsample dropdown** ("Downsample (max grid)": Off / ≤300 / ≤200 / ≤150 / ≤100) — stride-based (`values[::k, ::k]`), export-only, preserves the NaN/blank pattern; no core-layer change.
- **Thread-safety fix**: `helpers.get_gap`'s `_GAP_LRU` OrderedDict is now lock-guarded — the export pool calls it concurrently and an eviction racing `move_to_end` could raise KeyError. File loads stay outside the lock so parallel workers still read distinct OUT files concurrently.

## Why

Measured on a 12-core machine: 2D contour ≈ 0.17s/image, 3D surface ≈ 1.4s/image (fixed headless-Chromium WebGL cost — shrinking the image does not help). 1000 gaps × 2 images ≈ 26 min sequential. With 4 parallel scopes: ~7 min; 2D-only: ~1 min.

## Notes for review

- Progress polling contract unchanged: `_EXPORT["done"]` still counts completed gaps, the poller reads non-destructively, publishing stays side-effect free.
- Per-item failure isolation kept; failures collected as (index, message) and sorted so the status message is deterministic.
- kaleido v1 (built-in parallel API) was considered and rejected — requires Python ≥3.9, repo is pinned to 3.8.10 / kaleido 0.2.1.
- Each scope is a Chromium subprocess (~200MB RSS); default 4 workers.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest` — 277 passed (9 new `_downsample_for_export` unit tests).
- End-to-end in the running app (demo_data, 20 gaps): 2D+3D → 40 PNGs in 13.4s with 4 workers (vs ~32s sequential), 0 failed; 2D-only → 20 PNGs in 2.5s, no `_3D.png`; both kinds unchecked → "Select at least one image type (2D/3D)." error; spot-checked a PNG (title, blank pattern correct).

author: hari-hristov
body:
## Goal

Prep for a **standing local-server deploy** (k3s in WSL2). This is **PR-A** of two:
scripts + directory restructure now; Flux GitOps CD lands in PR-B. Closes the first
two of the three gaps raised: no single init entrypoint, and no easy config-change apply.

## What's in this PR

### New — `scripts/init.sh` (all-in-one bring-up)
Runs the whole stack in order on a fresh host: `install-tools` → `bootstrap-k3s` →
`deploy-stateful` → `deploy-app` → `deploy-ingress`. Idempotent and **resumable** —
if a step fails, `init.sh --from N` (1-5) skips the earlier steps. Prints the
Windows-hosts line at the end (not WSL's — per the known browser-resolution gotcha).

### New — `scripts/apply-config.sh` (change a config value)
```bash
apply-config.sh FRONTEND_ORIGIN https://fmi-codes.local   # patch one ConfigMap key + roll
apply-config.sh REGISTRATION_OPEN true
apply-config.sh                                            # re-apply manifests from disk + roll
```
Patches the `fmi-codes-backend-config` ConfigMap and restarts the backend so pods
pick it up (the exact "config staged but not live" gap from the previous phase).
**Refuses secret keys** — points at `rotate-secret.sh` (app secrets) or
`deploy-stateful.sh` (PVC-coupled DB/Redis). The value is JSON-encoded via `python3`
(hard dependency) so quotes/specials can't break the `kubectl patch`.

### Tooling — `flux` CLI added to `install-tools-wsl2.sh`
Pinned `v2.9.2` + checksum-verified, matching the kubectl/helm/k9s/sops/age pattern.
Consumed by the Flux GitOps CD in PR-B; added here so that PR doesn't need a second
tooling change.

### Restructure — `infra/k8s/` into concern-based subdirs
```
infra/k8s/
  scripts/       init, apply-config, rotate-secret, deploy-*, bootstrap, install-tools
  manifests/     namespace, backend, frontend, ingress
  helm-values/   postgresql-values, redis-values
  secrets/       secrets.enc.yaml   (.sops.yaml stays at repo root)
  README.md
```
Done with `git mv` (history preserved — shows as renames). Every script rewired to
resolve siblings via a computed `K8S_DIR`, so invocation location doesn't matter.
`.sops.yaml` `path_regex` and the README updated to the new paths.

## Verification performed (against the live k3s cluster)

- **Restructure**: SOPS decrypts at `secrets/secrets.enc.yaml` (proves `.sops.yaml`
  regex + `K8S_DIR`); `deploy-app.sh`, `apply-config.sh`, and `deploy-stateful.sh`
  all resolve their moved files and run.
- **init.sh**: `--from 3` correctly skips steps 1-2, runs 3-5 in sequence, prints
  the resolved ingress IP + hosts guidance. Arg validation + `--help` checked.
- **apply-config.sh**: secret-key rejection, no-arg manifest re-apply, single-key
  patch (value lands live), and restore all verified. Guard confirms `FRONTEND_ORIGIN`
  updates the live ConfigMap.
- **flux**: download + checksum + install proven (v2.9.2 runs).
- `bash -n` on all 8 scripts, infra comment-free grep, PII scrub — all clean.

## Review

Ran a review pass. One Should-Fix caught + fixed before commit: `apply-config.sh`
had an unsafe JSON fallback if `python3` were absent (raw-quote wrap → malformed
patch on values containing `"`). Now hard-requires python3 and drops the unsafe
fallback. Two other items were non-issues noted for completeness.

## Follow-up (PR-B)

Flux controllers + `flux/` CRs (GitRepository, Kustomization w/ image override,
Image{Repository,Policy,UpdateAutomation} ×2), `flux-bootstrap.sh`, wire `init.sh`
to call it, and `docker-cd.yaml` immutable `sha-<gitsha>` tags → per-service
auto-redeploy on merge.

author: sergk
body:
Enable optional single sign-on for Grafana over generic OAuth (Keycloak or any OIDC provider), keeping the bundle self-contained and secret-free by default.

- Wire Grafana generic_oauth (roles/groups claim mapping to org roles) behind an opt-in flag
- Source all SSO material from one grafana-sso Secret (admin creds + OAuth client secret), never rendered by the chart itself
- Add an optional External Secrets Operator path (aws, vault, generic SecretStore backends) plus a namespace-scoped ServiceAccount to materialize that Secret from a secret manager
- Add keycloakClient.create to optionally provision the OIDC client as a KeycloakClient CR via the KubeRocketCI keycloak-operator, replacing the confusing oidc.enabled/mode pair
- Preserve the isolated design: every SSO/ESO resource is opt-in and off by default

## 🔁 추가 작업 — 백엔드 API 연결 · 디테일 · 매체 선택 고도화 · 스토리북

> ⚠️ 위 3단계 위저드를 **실제 백엔드 API에 연결**하고 Figma 디테일을 정정했습니다. PR #5가 dev에 머지됨에 따라 **dev를 재머지해 동기화**했습니다 (상단 IMPORTANT 경고 해소 — base dev 복귀 가능).

### API 연결 (DV-142 · DV-182)
- `lib/campaign.ts` mock 제거 → `lib/team.ts`와 동일 패턴(axios `unwrap`·`CampaignApiError`)으로 실제 API 연결
- **소재 업로드(DV-142)**: presigned 2단계 — `POST /campaign-creatives/upload-url` → 스토리지 직접 업로드 → `creativeToken`. 업로드는 파일 선택 즉시 백그라운드로 진행
- **매체 목록·캠페인 등록(DV-182)**: `GET /media-units`(+`/regions`) · `POST /teams/{teamId}/campaigns`. teamId는 `useAuth().user.teamId`, 폼값→백엔드 필드 매핑
- 목록·지역 조회는 대시보드 컨벤션에 맞춰 react-query(`useMediaUnits`·`useMediaRegions`)로

### Step1 기본 정보 (DV-138)
- 영상 **썸네일 추출**(canvas 정지프레임) — 업로드와 독립. **다음 버튼 = 썸네일 표시 + 폼 유효** (업로드 성공은 최종 등록에서만 요구)
- Figma 대조: `InputField` 라운드 `rounded-x3`·패딩 `px-x4 py-x3` DS 값 정정, 업로드 카드 max-width

### Step2 매체 선택 (DV-139 · DV-140)
- **서버사이드 필터**: 지역 드롭다운 ← `/media-units/regions`, 검색어·시도·시군구 → 쿼리 파라미터. **송출기간을 함께 전송해 `available`(등록 가능 여부) 계산**

- 지도: 확대/축소 버튼, 핀 마커(photoUrl 이미지 + border, 기본/선택/미가용 색), 필터 결과 bounds 맞춤, 이미지 깨짐 fallback
- 리스트: rounded-x3 카드(지도 위 부유), 긴 이름 말줄임, 선택 매체를 객체로 보관해 필터 후에도 유지

### Step3 최종 확인 (DV-141)

author: bapatchirag
body:
Plain `go install github.com/bapatchirag/harharbinks/cmd/hhb@vX.Y.Z` applies no
ldflags, so main.version kept its "dev" default and `hhb --version` printed
"harharbinks dev" for installed binaries.

Add resolveVersion(): when no version is injected via -ldflags (goreleaser and
`make build` still take precedence), fall back to the module version recorded in
the binary's build info (debug.ReadBuildInfo().Main.Version), then to the "dev"
default for plain in-repo `go build`.

- go install ...@v1.0.1     -> harharbinks v1.0.1
- goreleaser / make build   -> unchanged (injected version wins)
- go build ./cmd/hhb        -> dev (untagged dev build)

Tests: cmd/hhb/main_test.go covers ldflags precedence and the non-empty fallback.

This pull request enhances the menu item update workflow by introducing real-time approval notifications for chefs, expanding inventory access permissions, and improving menu item status handling.

## Key Changes

### Menu Update Notifications
- Added `broadcastMenuUpdateApprovalToChef` to `WebSocketNotificationService`.
- Sends real-time notifications to chefs when their menu update requests are approved.
- Notifications include:
  - Menu item name
  - Approving admin's name

- Updated `MenuItemUpdateRequestServiceImpl` to trigger notifications after successful approval.
- Added an `adminName` field to `MenuItemUpdateDecisionDto` to include the approving administrator's name in notifications.

### Authorization Improvements
- Expanded access to the `getAllItemsByBranch` inventory endpoint to include users with the **ADMIN** role.

### Menu Item Status Handling
- Improved menu item status updates by safely parsing the requested status.
- Defaults the status to **ACTIVE** when the provided value is missing or invalid.

### Dependency Updates
- Injected `WebSocketNotificationService` into `MenuItemUpdateRequestServiceImpl` to support the new notification workflow.

author: codelesskris
body:
## Summary
- Lift the four content ink tiers (`--ink`, `--ink-body`, `--ink-secondary`, `--ink-faded`) one notch in all three themes. IM Fell English's hairline strokes render optically lighter than their nominal color, so small serif text needs roughly a level more contrast than a sturdy sans. All content text now clears WCAG AAA (7:1) on every paper stock: grimoire body 8.6–10.5:1, secondary floor 7.47:1 (note paper); vellum secondary 8.1:1; modern ≥9.8:1. `--ink-ghost` (placeholders/whispers) is deliberately untouched.
- Fix the stragglers that bypassed theme variables:
  - **PINNED button** ([detail.tsx](src/detail.tsx)) hardcoded `#6e5018` — the *light-theme* value of `--mustard-deep` — making it near-invisible on grimoire card stock. Now `var(--mustard-deep)` (pixel-identical on vellum, flips to pale gold on grimoire).
  - **Items kind color** ([data.ts](src/data.ts)) was the only kind with a hardcoded color; its legend swatch stayed dark on grimoire while all six siblings brightened. New themed `--gold-antique` (root `#8a6a28`, grimoire `#b6923e`), still distinguishable from quests' brighter mustard.
  - **Notice-board banner + `.note-scrap` borders** hardcoded the light-paper brown rim on themed paper — now `var(--card-edge)`.
  - **`.cleanup-row` separators** (Tidy the Codex) used a 15%-alpha dark brown, invisible on grimoire — new themed `--hairline` token next to `--card-edge`.

Deliberate "physical prop" palettes (sticky note, wax seal, tape, wooden board frame, bloodred primary button) hardcode background + ink together and are self-consistent in every theme; left as-is.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run build` typechecks clean
- [x] Verified all three themes in the browser (Known People roster, Items cards, Notice Board, Tidy the Codex panel)
- [x] Computed WCAG ratios for every ink tier × paper stock combination; content floor ≥7.47:1
- [x] Confirmed legend swatches, banner border, and cleanup separators resolve to the lifted grimoire values via computed styles
- [x] Grepped for remaining hardcoded text/border colors — none outside self-consistent props

author: teo1747
body:
What this changes
The userspace EmUI toolkit (ui/, ui/dsl/em*, the EM_APPLICATION/EM_WIDGET runtime) and the thin kernel surface under it — the compositor (kernel/gfx/compositor.c), the framebuffer driver (new fb_blur_region/fb_blit_uniform/fb_blit_over/fb_glow_rect), one keyboard change (extended scancodes), one window flag (EMBK_WINF_GLASS): adds V6 menus + a V7 text editor, a ~5x text-render speedup, and an opt-in compositor "glass/aurora" look, while keeping the home launcher on the simple fast path.

Why
EmUI is becoming the app framework but looked like a stock desktop and had no menus or text editing. The perf pass was forced by the no-KVM environment (3 Newton-loop sqrtfs per text pixel dominated frame time). The glass/aurora look lives in the compositor, not the app, because a window must frost the desktop behind it (pixels the app can't see); two compositing paths exist on purpose — opaque app windows use uniform-alpha (content stays readable), translucent widgets/desktop use per-pixel fb_blit_over (aurora shows through the gaps).

How it was proven
 Builds clean (make myos.img, make build/libembk.so, all app .elfs, make embkfs.img, make showcase-v2)
 Boots and runs in QEMU — headless myos.img + embkfs.img on IDE, virtio-vga 1280x800, driven over QMP (input-send-event + screendump); equivalent to make run-ui / run-embkfs-cow
 Existing selftests exercise the changed rasteriser/backend invariants: make backend-test scene-test font-test layout-test declare-test reactive-test — all 0 failures
 A new selftest for the V6/V7/glass features specifically — not added; proven behaviorally (host render + live serial/screenshot), see gaps
Proof (what would FAIL if broken):

Text/perf: font-test asserts glyphs inked at correct pen positions — the gamma-table blend fails it if the linearise/de-linearise tables are wrong; freestanding Newton-sqrtf microbench measured 5.12x (82.5 → 16.1 ns/px); make showcase-v2 renders text crisp (muddy if gamma broke).
V6/V7 live: serial Editor: first frame presented; screenshots show the File menu open with items+shortcuts and typed "hi teo" inserted at the caret with arrow-key nav — empty/wrong if the overlay panel or extended-scancode/ui_input_take path broke.
Glass/aurora live: the acrylic Editor shot shows home tiles + "EmbLink OS" blurred through the window (flat if fb_blur_region no-op'd); aurora shows a grained color field.
CloseGrip: serial Editor: closed by its own control and the next frame shows the window gone — still present if the gesture/teardown failed.
SDM / spec references
Extended-key decoding in kernel/drivers/input/keyboard.c reasons from PS/2 scan code set 1 0xE0-prefixed sequences (arrows/Home/End/Delete). Pixel work assumes the framebuffer's premultiplied EMBK_PIXFMT_BGRA8888_PRE layout (render_target.h). No Intel-SDM privilege/paging contract and no on-disk format change (the mkfs B-tree work keeps the existing EMBKFS byte layout).

Docs synced
 docs/PROJECT_STATUS.md — DSL iteration list extended to V6/V7, perf pass, glass/acrylic/aurora, demo apps
 docs/EMUI_GUIDE.md + docs/EMUI_INTERNALS.md (the UI subsystem's usage + architecture docs) — Menus, Text editor, Materials/glass, Acrylic windows, perf list, the two glass compositing paths
 docs/ARCHITECTURE.md root doc — not touched (UI architecture lives in EMUI_INTERNALS.md); add a pointer from the root if desired
 docs/TODO.md — modified this session; fold in the gaps below
Known gaps left behind
No dedicated selftest for the new UI features — V6/V7/glass are verified by host render + live serial/screenshot, not a machine assertion. Next: a headless "render showcase → assert non-flat / expected inked regions" host test to catch regressions without a boot.
Drag is heavy under TCG — a glass/glowing window re-blurs + re-glows its region each paint, so dragging one is sluggish without KVM. Follow-up: skip blur mid-drag, re-frost on release.
Aurora is static — animating it needs a periodic full-screen recompute+repaint, too heavy under TCG.
CloseGrip pointer-capture edge case — dragging the grip far outside the window can drop kernel pointer-capture under scripted input; an in-bounds pull is reliable. Harden capture for out-of-bounds drags.
Home is opaque again (this PR) — so the aurora is hidden and acrylic windows frost the dark launcher, not the wallpaper; the translucent-scrim home that reveals the aurora is available but off by default (a per-frame full-repaint cost).
Cosmetic: the "About" launcher tile is still an opaque placeholder; the acrylic close-fade dims toward the window bg rather than transparent.
Commit hygiene
 Commits are milestone-sized — this is intentionally one large commit across several features; splittable into V6 menus / V7 editor+kbd / perf / glass+acrylic / aurora+grain+glow / close-gesture on request
 git status clean — source is complete, but generated artifacts (*.img, boot/stage2/stage2.bin) show as modified; git checkout them or keep them out of the commit

body:
## 🔗 Ticket

Follow-up to [DEX-450](https://linear.app/rudderstack/issue/DEX-450/generate-data-gov-types-via-rudder-cli-without-control-plane) — resolves the interaction between #671 and #673, both now on `main`.

---

## Summary

#671 added `WithIgnoreUnknownKinds` (used by the `--local` typer) whose `isKnownKind` treated **import-manifest as always-known**, walking the providers unconditionally. #673 (landed independently) gates the import-manifest kind behind the `ImportMerge` experimental flag in `BuildRegistry`. With both on `main`, the two disagree about which kinds are "known".

**Reproducible bug on `main` today:** a `--local` project carrying a stray `import-manifest.yaml` with the flag **off** (the default) slips past the skip (`isKnownKind` says known) and is then rejected by `BuildRegistry` as an unknown kind — the exact failure `WithIgnoreUnknownKinds` exists to prevent:

```
error[project/spec-syntax-valid]: 'kind' must be one of [properties events categories custom-types tp tracking-plan]
  --> import-manifest.yaml:2:1 | kind: import-manifest
```

Does **not** affect rudder-data-gov (it has no manifest), so it didn't block the #671 release — but it's a live latent defect.

---

## Changes

- Extract the active-pattern set into a shared `activePatterns(provider, manifestProvider, importMergeEnabled)` helper, consumed by **both** `BuildRegistry` (which rules fire) and `isKnownKind` (which specs the local typer may skip) — single, flag-aware source of truth so the two can't drift.
- `isKnownKind` now takes the resolved flag; `parseSpecs` resolves it once from config.
- `BuildRegistry` builds its pattern set from the helper (local renamed `active` to avoid shadowing).

## Testing

- Regression test (`TestProject_Load_ImportManifestKind_RespectsImportMergeFlag`): with `WithIgnoreUnknownKinds`, a stray import-manifest is **skipped when the flag is off** and **recognized when it's on**.
- Binary-level: `typer generate --local` against a rudder-data-gov copy with an injected `import-manifest.yaml` — fails on `main`, succeeds here; clean rudder-data-gov unaffected.
- `make lint` clean (0 issues); project + typer + ruledoc + app tests green.

## Risk / Impact

Low. Pure refactor of "known kinds" into one helper + a flag-threading; no behavior change except the intended skip of unknown import-manifest under the local typer. `apply` untouched.

## Checklist

- [x] Ticket linked
- [x] Tests added/updated
- [x] No breaking changes

author: reakaleek
body:
## What

Replace the cross-run download of the `docs-build-check-metadata` artifact in `docs-deploy.yml`'s `preflight` job with a direct `repos.getCommit` call. Removes the artifact upload from `docs-build.yml` and the now-unused `actions: read` grant from `preflight`.

## Why

The `preflight` job downloaded a metadata artifact from the completed `docs-build` run just to read a single boolean (`effective_any_modified`) for push events. That cross-run `download-artifact@v8` hits the GitHub Actions artifact API (list → get-URL → download) and can fail under rate limits.

The `workflow_run` payload can't carry job outputs, so "use the payload instead" means re-deriving the signal from the REST API — which is exactly what the PR path already does via `pulls.listFiles`. This makes push consistent with PR and drops the only cross-run artifact dependency in the workflow.

## How

- **`docs-deploy.yml`**: push change detection now calls `repos.getCommit(head_sha)` and applies the same `matchesPattern`/`isIgnored` filters the PR path uses (hoisted to shared scope). `docs-build` already computes this signal via `tj-actions/changed-files` on a `fetch-depth: 2` checkout — i.e. last-commit-only — which `getCommit` reproduces exactly. The release-branch opt-in is preserved via a gated `compareCommitsWithBasehead`. Permission narrowed from `actions: read` to `contents: read`.
- **`docs-build.yml`**: dropped the `Write check metadata` / `Upload check metadata` steps. `effective_any_modified` stays for internal build gating.

Fallbacks keep the same safe posture as the old `continue-on-error` download: any API error, or a commit with ≥300 files (API truncation), defaults to `has-changes=true`.

**Version-skew safe** both ways — old deploy + new build falls back to `has-changes=true`; new deploy + old build simply ignores the artifact.

## Test plan

- Push with docs changes → `preflight` sets `has-changes=true`, build + deploy run.
- Push with no docs changes → deploy skipped (preserves the monorepo optimization).
- PR path → unchanged, still resolves via `pulls.listFiles`.
- Release branch (`use-release-branches`) → first push to a freshly-cut semver branch still builds so `links.json` is produced.
- `actionlint` clean on both files.

body:
## Summary
Stacked on #325 (crates/resilience core). Extends the resilience wiring to two more previously-unbounded external call boundaries:

- **provider-ollama**: `complete()` and the NDJSON streaming handshake retry transient failures (connection refused, network error, `429`, `5xx`) with backoff, sharing one circuit breaker per provider instance; `401/403/400/404` are permanent and never retried.
- **provider-openai-compat**: intentionally left untouched — its `complete()` is a stub that always errors without making any network call, so there's no real external call boundary there to wrap yet.
- **tool-registry's MCP client** (`RemoteMcpToolset`): had zero timeout or retry bounding `connect`/`tools/list`/`tools/call` — a hung remote MCP server hung the caller indefinitely. `connect` and `tools/list` are now timeout-bounded and retried (side-effect-free, safe to retry); `tools/call` is timeout-bounded and circuit-breaker-gated but **deliberately never retried** — MCP gives no idempotency guarantee, and a remote tool may have side effects that must not be silently duplicated by a resend.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p ardur-provider-ollama` — 27 tests incl. 4 new fault-injection tests (transient-500-retries-into-success, permanent-401-never-retried, open-breaker-fails-fast, connection-refused-retried-and-surfaced)
- [x] `cargo test -p ardur-tool-registry` — 73 tests incl. 2 new fault-injection tests (slow-tool-call-times-out-rather-than-hanging, repeated-timeouts-trip-breaker-then-fail-fast)
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` / `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean for both crates

author: vladjerca
body:
## What

Reshapes the merged-feed response (`hotReleaseResponseSchema`, used by `media` and `releases/hot`) from `z.union([movie, show])` to a single flat object with every field nullish (`released?`, `movie?`, `first_aired?`, `episode?`, `show?`).

## Why

Per @mike's report: OpenAPI codegen renders a union `oneOf` as a single model with **all** member fields required, so consumers generated a wrong schema (`movie`, `show`, `episode`, `season` all non-null). A flat object with nullish fields generates a correct optional-field model; callers null-check to discriminate. Documents the convention in a new `AGENTS.md` so it's applied to future polymorphic responses.

Follow-up to #850 (group=day). Bumps `@trakt/api` to 0.4.25.

author: davion-knight
body:
## Summary
Exposes the constant-product stake/unstake slippage math as a documented, **read-only** endpoint (Closes #5235, part of #5229). No new ingestion — the AMM pool reserves (`tao_in_pool_tao`, `alpha_in_pool`) already ship in the `economics.json` artifact.

`GET /api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/stake-quote?amount=&direction=stake|unstake` → expected alpha/TAO out, spot vs effective price (TAO per alpha), and price-impact percent. Pure math, no chain write, no custody.

## Deliverables
- **Constant-product formula + inverse** — `src/stake-quote.mjs`, implemented in its numerically-stable closed form `alpha_out = alpha_in·Δtao/(tao_in+Δtao)` (and the unstake mirror). This is algebraically identical to `alpha_in − k/(tao_in+Δtao)` but avoids the catastrophic cancellation that made dust amounts report a fake ~0.004% impact.
- **Root subnet (netuid 0)** → 1:1, zero-impact quote with null reserves (no AMM), rather than running the formula against nonexistent reserves.
- **Guards** → zero/absent liquidity and inputs over **1000× the relevant reserve** return `422`, mirroring the chain's own `InsufficientLiquidity` guard; a bad `direction`/`amount` returns `400`.
- **Handler** (`entities.mjs`) resolves reserves from the live economics KV tier with the committed `economics.json` R2 fallback, then maps the typed result onto the API envelope.
- **Schema + contract + OpenAPI** — new `SubnetStakeQuoteArtifact`, a `route()` + `artifact()` in `contracts.mjs`, regenerated `openapi.json`/types, registered as a computed (no-static-file) artifact.

## Validation
- `validate:schemas`, `validate:contract-drift`, `validate:openapi` (156 routes), `validate:openapi-examples` (156/156 ship a worked example) — all pass.
- `npm run build` clean; `eslint`/`prettier` clean.
- **Tests** (all green locally): `stake-quote.test.mjs` (pure math — root, dust, both directions, every guard, constant-product invariant), `subnet-stake-quote-handler.test.mjs` (handler over the live-KV *and* R2-fallback tiers + every error path), `subnet-stake-quote-api.test.mjs` (route dispatch through `api.mjs`). Verified **100% statement/branch coverage on every changed line** in `src/stake-quote.mjs`, the new entities handler/resolver, and the api.mjs dispatch.

Example — SN64, stake 1000 τ:
```
GET /api/v1/subnets/64/stake-quote?amount=1000&direction=stake
→ { data: { netuid: 64, direction: "stake", expected_out: 13458.6…, expected_out_unit: "alpha",
            spot_price_tao: 0.07395…, effective_price_tao: 0.07432…, price_impact_pct: 0.49…, is_root: false } }
```

Closes #5235

author: piotrgry
body:
### Linked issue
Closes #122

### Root cause
The DLQ alert was *declared* but not *verified operational*: (1) its comment claimed it queried `ContainerAppConsoleLogs_CL`, but the rule scopes the App Insights resource, so the KQL actually runs against the App Insights `traces` schema — misleading for anyone tuning it. (2) `ops_alert_email` had no validation, so an empty/typo'd recipient would make every alert silently undeliverable. (3) No documented procedure existed to prove the alert fires and the e-mail arrives.

### What changed
- `infra/terraform/monitoring.tf` — DLQ KQL: fixed the schema comment, added `severityLevel >= 3` so only the real `logger.exception("... enqueueing to DLQ")` error record matches.
- `infra/terraform/variables.tf` — `ops_alert_email` plan-time regex validation (fail fast on empty/malformed recipient).
- `infra/terraform/MONITORING_RUNBOOK.md` (new) — table-name verification, `terraform plan/apply` procedure, controlled DLQ test-alert procedure, evidence checklist.

Action group `ops` is already wired to all three alerts (error-rate, latency, DLQ) — verified, no change needed.

### Scope
Implements only #122 (R4-C). No application business logic changed.

### Out of scope
- Actually firing the alert / confirming e-mail delivery — requires `terraform apply` + a live staging deployment (owner action; documented in the runbook).

### Tests / validation
```
cd infra/terraform
terraform fmt -check            # clean
terraform init -backend=false
terraform validate              # Success! The configuration is valid.
```
Email regex sanity via `terraform console`: `owner@example.com` → true, `not-an-email` → false.

### CI status
Pending.

### Staging status
**Blocked (owner action):** `terraform plan`/`apply`, controlled DLQ test-alert, and e-mail-receipt evidence require Azure credentials + a staging deployment. Step-by-step procedure + evidence checklist are in `MONITORING_RUNBOOK.md`.

### Dependencies
**Depends on PR #130** (pillow). Base is temporarily `chore/bump-pillow-security`. **After #130 merges to `develop`, retarget this PR's base to `develop`.** Logically independent of R4-A/R4-B (no shared files) — may merge in any order among the R4 group once #130 is in.

### Merge order
Merge order: 3 of 9 (independent of R4-A/R4-B; the R4-A→R4-B→R4-C sequence is the plan's preferred order, not a technical constraint).

### Risks
- KQL change (`severityLevel >= 3`) is validated offline only; the runbook requires a live test-alert before treating the DLQ alert as operational.
- pillow-hash churn is not in this PR's diff (isolated to #130).

### Acceptance criteria
- [x] Terraform validate passes.
- [ ] Plan contains expected alert/action group changes. *(owner: run `terraform plan` — expect DLQ rule query update only)*
- [ ] Test DLQ event triggers the alert. *(owner: runbook §3)*
- [ ] E-mail reaches the configured recipient. *(owner: runbook §3–4)*
- [ ] Runbook records query, time window and correlation ID. *(template in runbook §4)*

### Motivation
- Deliver milestone A3 by adding a market pallet implementing the LMSR trading primitives, wrapper ledger plumbing, TWAP observations, fee routing, and Baseline market mapping as specified in docs 04 and 02 §5–§7.4.
- Provide a pure `no_std` runtime-side implementation that composes with the existing `pallet-conditional-ledger` and the `futarchy-fixed` fixed-point math crate so frontends and the runtime agree on types and events (`Traded`/`Observed`).

### Description
- Added a new workspace pallet `pallet-market` (`pallets/market/Cargo.toml`, `pallets/market/src/lib.rs`) and registered it in the root `Cargo.toml` workspace members. 
- Implemented market state, `BookKind` (Decision/Gate/Baseline), market lifecycle/`MarketPhase`, `buy`/`sell` wrappers that call `pallet-conditional-ledger` for branch-USDC flows, fee accounting (30 bps), maker-adverse rounding, and per-trade bounds. 
- Implemented LMSR integrations: fixed-point conversions, cost/price/displacement usage via `crates/futarchy-fixed`, observation/TWAP accumulation with slew cap and staleness accounting, `BaselineMarketOf` mapping, POL headroom seeding (`b·ln 2`), try-state validation, and runtime-benchmark stubs.

author: gmboquet
body:
## Summary

- Vectorize `NavierStokes3D._build_poisson`'s `diff_matrix` and `em_diffusion_3d`'s `_curl_matrix` / `_grad_matrix`: each replaces a triple-nested Python loop over grid nodes/faces/edges with a broadcast `meshgrid` + flat-index COO build, then one `csr_matrix(...)` call. Same operator, no Python loop over `O(n**3)`.
- Add a true perfectly-matched layer to `WaveEquation3D`: `pml_width` / `pml_profile` build a split-field CPML (per-axis damped second-order ODEs driven by the recombined field's directional second derivative, graded to zero away from the boundary) that actually absorbs outgoing waves instead of merely damping them. Fully backward compatible — default `pml_width=0` leaves the original sponge (`absorb_width`/`absorb_strength`) path, and the absence of both, unchanged.
- Add `mesh.telescoping_mesh(core_shape, spacing, *, pad=4, growth=1.3)`: a graded box simplex mesh with a fine uniform survey core and geometrically-growing padding cells outward to a large far field, without uniformly refining the whole domain. `box_simplex_mesh`'s Freudenthal tetrahedralization is refactored into a shared `_grid_simplex_mesh` helper so both mesh builders share one code path.

## Why

`_build_poisson` / `_curl_matrix` / `_grad_matrix` assembled their fixed sparse pattern with a Python `for i / for j / for k` triple loop — fine at the small grids the existing unit tests use, but the dominant cost long before a realistic survey-scale 3-D mesh. The wave solver's only absorbing boundary was an exponential sponge, which damps but never truly absorbs, so short/broadband pulses always leak some energy back into the domain — a real limitation for full-waveform-inversion-style forwards on a finite box. And there was no way to cheaply extend a fine survey-resolution mesh out to an absorbing far field without paying for uniform refinement everywhere.

## Test plan

DoD command (from the work order), run against the isolated worktree with `PYTHONPATH` pinned to this repo + core `mixle`:

```
PYTHONPATH=/Users/grantboquet/mixle/mixle:/tmp/mixle-exec/mixle-pde-c6 \
  /Users/grantboquet/mixle/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q mixle_pde/c6_scale_test.py
```

Result: **5 passed** — confirms:
- the vectorized `_build_poisson`/`_curl_matrix` are bit-for-bit identical (`np.allclose` + exact sparsity pattern) to a frozen Python-loop reference implementation, on a small `n=6` grid;
- assembly at `48**3` unknowns completes in well under 5s for both, with `nnz` density that stays flat across grid sizes (confirming `O(n)`/`O(N)` scaling, not a hidden superlinear path);
- the CPML leaves under 1% of a shot's launched energy in the domain, versus a substantially higher fraction for the exponential sponge on the identical shot.

Sanity-checked that this genuinely exercises the change: ran the same test file against the pre-vectorization code (the loop-based `_curl_matrix` and the `WaveEquation3D` without `pml_width`) and confirmed it fails — `TypeError` on the missing `pml_width` kwarg, and the 48³ `_curl_matrix` timing assertion fails at ~5.1s.

Broader regression suite (existing tests for every file touched, plus the mesh callers):

```
PYTHONPATH=/Users/grantboquet/mixle/mixle:/tmp/mixle-exec/mixle-pde-c6 \
  /Users/grantboquet/mixle/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/flow3d_test.py tests/em_diffusion_3d_test.py tests/wave3d_test.py \
  tests/mesh_test.py tests/fem_test.py tests/latent_test.py
```

Result: **70 passed**, no regressions.

`ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on all changed files.

## Notes (judgment calls)

- The frozen public API only adds `pml_width` and `pml_profile` to `WaveEquation3D` — no separate PML-only strength parameter — so the CPML's peak damping (`sigma_max`) reuses the existing `absorb_strength` knob, with a nominal unit wave speed folded in (matching how `absorb_strength` was already unscaled by physical velocity in the original sponge).
- When `pml_width > 0`, the legacy sponge (`_gamma`) is still computed in `__init__` but unused during `step` — `pml_width` takes priority over `absorb_width`, matching the "split-field CPML replaces the sponge" framing in the work order. Passing both is harmless, not an error.
- `_curl_matrix`/`_grad_matrix`/`_build_poisson`'s vectorized output is verified equal to the loop reference via a dense-array (`.toarray()`) comparison rather than an entrywise COO-ordering comparison, since the vectorized build legitimately emits entries in a different order than the old loop — the assembled sparse matrix (data + exact sparsity pattern) is what must match, and does.

body: A run with failed realise roots annotated `::error::` but concluded success, and `advance-cache-ready` moved the consumer pin over the hole: run 29295767529 (cc830c3c) shipped a broken codex closure to every darwin consumer (#3188). **What changed** - Both lanes (`push`, `darwin-build`) export their failed-realise-root count as a job output and stay green, so partial pushes still publish everything that did realise. Failing the lanes directly was rejected: a red `push` skips `darwin-build` (`needs: push`), and a red `darwin-build` skips `darwin-push`, losing the relay the lane just staged. - `advance-cache-ready` gains a publish-hole gate that fails the run before any ref move when either count is nonzero: the pin holds at the last fully-published rev and the run concludes failure. - The main-only pin guard moves from the job-level `if` into the script, so a non-main `workflow_dispatch` with failed roots also concludes failure instead of silently skipping the gate. - Watchdog: "ran green" and "published every root" now coincide (run conclusion is the signal); its header comment says so. A dedicated watchdog signal was skipped deliberately: the tracking-issue channel comments on every 15-min tick, so a chronic broken root would spam; red runs plus signal-3 pin drift already cover it. **Preserved properties**: the workflow stays non-gating for merges (runs post-merge on main), partial pushes publish before the run reports failure, and the fast-forward-only ref semantics are untouched. **Validation**: `nix run .#lint` green; `actionlint` (with shellcheck integration) clean on both workflows; `bash -n` on every embedded script; gate arithmetic exercised for empty/zero/nonzero outputs and BSD `wc -l` leading-space counts. Fixes #3195 (PR by an AI agent via Claude Code, Claude Opus 4.6) > [!NOTE] > ### Fail cache-push runs that leave publish holes in `advance-cache-ready` > - Linux and darwin build jobs now emit a `failed-roots` output counting any roots that failed to realise, without failing the job itself. > - The `advance-cache-ready` job gates on both counts: if either is greater than zero, it exits 1 and skips advancing the `cache-ready` ref. > - The branch guard (only run on main) is moved into the script so non-main runs still fail if publish holes are detected. > - Behavioral Change: previously, individual root failures caused silent success and pin drift; now they cause an explicit workflow failure. > > > > Macroscope summarized 481fae6. > >

author: bbatsov
body:
When evaluated code reads from stdin, `RET` sends a line, but there was no way to signal end-of-input: CIDER always appended a newline, so it could never send the empty string that nREPL turns into EOF. Code that reads to end-of-stream (`(slurp *in*)`, a `(read-line)` loop) therefore couldn't be satisfied interactively - the only escape was to interrupt the whole evaluation.

Adds `C-c C-d` at the stdin prompt to send EOF (an empty string). I verified against a live nREPL that this is genuinely distinct from `RET`:

| Code | stdin sent | result |
|---|---|---|
| `(read-line)` | `""` (C-c C-d) | `nil` (EOF) |
| `(read-line)` | `"\n"` (RET on empty line) | `""` |
| `(slurp *in*)` | `""` (C-c C-d) | completes (would hang otherwise) |

Also documents stdin handling - the prompt and its RET / EOF / cancel keys - in the Code Evaluation manual, where input handling was previously undocumented.

## Why

changeset check (mirroring the CI `unreleased-entry`/`Changelog` workflow),

`CONTRIBUTING.md`'s documented run order already lists the changeset check

author: anandumv
body:
## Summary
- `contrastColor()` in `static/widget.js` computes WCAG relative luminance directly from raw sRGB channel values (`channel / 255`) and compares it against the standard `0.179` threshold.
- That threshold is only valid for **gamma-corrected (linear-light)** luminance. Feeding it raw sRGB values systematically overestimates the brightness of dark colors, so mid-dark backgrounds (e.g. `#333333`) get scored as "light enough" for black text — exactly the black-on-dark-background issue in #351.
- Fix adds the standard sRGB → linear gamma correction step before computing luminance, so the existing `0.179` threshold now compares against the right quantity.

Verified with a quick script: `#333333` (a plausible dark launcher color) now correctly resolves to `#ffffff` instead of `#000000`; light colors like `#e5e7eb`/`#ffffff` still correctly resolve to `#000000`.

Closes #351

## Test plan
- [x] Manually evaluated `contrastColor()` against a range of hex swatches (near-black, dark gray, mid gray, light gray, white, saturated red/blue) and confirmed output matches expected WCAG-based contrast choice.
- [ ] Maintainer/CI to confirm no visual regression in the chat widget launcher icon across existing color presets.

author: chelojimenez
body: ## What Stacked on #3194. Changes non-XAA `auto` from "always OAuth" to the MCP spec's canonical discovery ladder: 1. **XAA configured** → XAA (unchanged — hard selection, mint failures surface, no OAuth fallback). 2. **Stored OAuth token / refresh token** → use it (existing oauth rails + refresh hook). 3. **Otherwise → connect unauthenticated.** An open server with Auto now just connects — no OAuth popup. 4. **Live 401 from the target** → structured `oauthRequired` signal → the client asks ("Continue with OAuth?") before escalating into the existing interactive flow. Once per session per server; a second 401 after a completed flow surfaces as a config error instead of looping (spec: clients SHOULD limit step-up retries). ## Server - `resolveEffectiveAuthMethod` gains a `"discover"` member for non-XAA auto. **All dispatch is equality-based, so every consumer was audited by hand** (`local-server-resolver.ts`, `web/auth.ts` — the only two production call sites). - Local resolver: tokenless discover attempts the silent hosted-token refresh but swallows *all* refresh failures (a pure-local deployment without `CONVEX_HTTP_URL` must still connect open Auto servers); a live 401 is re-thrown as the same tagged `{oauthRequired:true}` 401 envelope the pre-connect throw produces (`X-MCP-Auth-Required` header included). - Hosted `createAuthorizedManager`: tokenless discover servers connect bare with an `onUnauthorized` handler that converts the SDK's 401 into the tagged shape — one tagging point with full per-server context, shared by validate/chat/evals/swarm. (Plan originally put a catch in the validate route; the handler is strictly better — same shape, no per-route duplication.) - `mapRuntimeError`: raw target 401s now map to 401 UNAUTHORIZED instead of generic 500 — **without** `oauthRequired` (no per-server auth context there, deliberately). - Explicit **None** servers never escalate; their 401 message gains a hint to switch to Auto/OAuth. ## Client - Connect/reconnect failure handling reads the structured flag first (`connectFailureRequiresOAuth`), string heuristic kept as fallback. `WebApiError` now carries the error-body `details` so the hosted validate path preserves the flag (it was stripped before). - Confirm-before-redirect uses the app's persistent-toast-with-action pattern (same shape as the "Open XAA Debugger" failure action) rather than a new modal — the loop guard lives in `sessionStorage` because `initiateOAuth` leaves the page. - `ensureAuthorizedForReconnect` treats tokenless Auto as ready-unauthenticated unless the escalation was confirmed — otherwise the auto-connect loops (page load, client switch) would surprise-redirect open Auto servers into OAuth. ## SDK - Exports `isUnauthorized401` from the package root (additive). - New conformance test pinning that the escalation's state machine re-probes unauthenticated and honors the original `WWW-Authenticate`: `resource_metadata` URL preferred over the derived well-known path, challenged `scope` preferred over `scopes_supported`. ## Backend **No changes.** `deriveAuthBooleans`' `useOAuth: true` for non-XAA auto is what makes authorize-batch return stored tokens (rung 2) and allows token storage post-escalation — deliberately untouched. ## Tests 370 server + 259 client + 18 SDK oauth tests pass, including new coverage: resolver discover cases, tokenless-discover connect (local + hosted), 401 tagging vs none-hint, `mapRuntimeError` 401 branch, and the WWW-Authenticate conformance pair. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > Touches auth connect/reconnect across client, local resolver, and hosted routes; incorrect 401 tagging or escalation gating could block connects, loop OAuth, or redirect without consent. > > **Overview** > **Non-XAA Auto** no longer assumes OAuth up front. Effective auth resolves to **discover**: use a stored token when present, otherwise connect **without credentials**; only a live **401** triggers interactive OAuth. **XAA** when configured stays a hard pre-connect choice. UI copy in `AuthenticationSection` reflects discover-then-OAuth instead of “Auto will use OAuth.” > > **Server (local + hosted):** `resolveEffectiveAuthMethod` adds **`discover`** for non-XAA auto. Tokenless discover skips pre-connect OAuth failures, swallows silent refresh failures, and tags real 401s with **`oauthRequired`** (plus `X-MCP-Auth-Required`). Explicit **none** gets 401 with a hint and **`upstreamAuthRequired`** (no auto-escalation). `mapRuntimeError` maps raw upstream 401s to HTTP 401 without tags. > > **Client:** **`connectFailureRequiresOAuth`** prefers structured **`oauthRequired`**; **`WebApiError.details`** threads it from hosted validate. **`auto-oauth-escalation`** (sessionStorage + confirm toast) gates redirect once per project/server; reconnect passes **`interactiveOAuthConfirmed`** so background reconnects don’t surprise-redirect. Success toasts for Auto avoid claiming OAuth when none ran. > > **SDK:** exports **`isUnauthorized401`**; conformance test for WWW-Authenticate **`resource_metadata`** / challenged **scope** on escalation. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 178fa639d49bdecaa015b6c7069b3293e5fa2683. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). --- ## Summary by cubic Non‑XAA “Auto” now connects without credentials first and only escalates to OAuth on a real 401, with a session‑scoped confirm‑before‑redirect guard to prevent loops. Local and hosted paths tag 401s consistently; explicit “None” returns 401 with a hint and no escalation. UI text now explains the discover‑first behavior. - **New Features** - Discovery flow: `resolveEffectiveAuthMethod` returns `discover` for non‑XAA Auto; tokenless discover connects bare, stored tokens ride existing OAuth rails. Client detects escalation via `oauthRequired` (threaded through `WebApiError.details`) with a confirm toast; a sessionStorage marker keyed by project+server id survives redirects and clears on all terminal outcomes (success, init failure, post‑OAuth connect failure, still‑401). Stale reconnects don’t write marker state; falls back gracefully if storage is unavailable. - Server parity: Local resolver swallows silent refresh failures for tokenless discover and lets the connect 401 tag `oauthRequired`; hosted `createAuthorizedManager` connects tokenless discover bare and tags 401s via a single `onUnauthorized`. `executeLocalServerConnect` tags discover 401s (`oauthRequired`) and explicit‑None 401s (`upstreamAuthRequired`) and sets `X‑MCP‑Auth‑Required`; `mapRuntimeError` maps raw upstream 401s to 401 UNAUTHORIZED without tags. - Client UX: Reconnect path gates Auto escalation (respects non‑interactive reconnects) and passes `interactiveOAuthConfirmed` to the orchestrator to avoid surprise redirects; success copy avoids claiming OAuth when not used; dropdown descriptions updated to “connects without credentials, then OAuth if required.” - SDK/tests: Export `isUnauthorized401` from `@mcpjam/sdk`; add conformance tests for WWW‑Authenticate `resource_metadata` and challenged `scope`; add unit tests for the escalation marker lifecycle and new server paths. Written for commit 178fa639d49bdecaa015b6c7069b3293e5fa2683. Summary will update on new commits.

author: ritviksardana
body:
This PR contains two fixes for the editor suggestion popups: the popup not mounting in production builds, and `SuggestionExtension` dropping the `allowSpaces` option.

## 1. Suggestion popup never mounts in production builds

### Problem

The `@` mention and custom `{{` suggestion popups silently fail to open in **production builds** (they work in dev). No error is thrown; the popup component renders but is never attached to the DOM.

### Root cause

`createSuggestionRenderer` (`molecules/editor/extensions/shared/suggestion-renderer.ts`) attaches `renderer.element` to `document.body`. In `@tiptap/vue-3`'s `VueRenderer`, `element` is the mount wrapper's **`firstElementChild`**, computed once at construction.

`SuggestionList` renders through `EditorPopover` → reka-ui `FocusScope`. With **reka-ui >= 2.5**, `FocusScope` no longer exposes a synchronous first element child at render time, so `renderer.element` is `null` when `onStart` runs → the early-return guard fires and the popup is never appended. `onUpdate` only repositions, so it never recovers.

This is timing/reka-version dependent, which is why it reproduces only in prod builds (and why older reka, e.g. gameplan on reka 2.0.x, isn't affected).

### Fix

Attach and position the `VueRenderer` **wrapper** (`renderer.el`) instead of its `firstElementChild`. The wrapper always exists right after `new VueRenderer(...)`, and the popup renders inside it, so this is robust regardless of the popup component's root element or the reka-ui version. A late-attach fallback in `onUpdate` covers any case where the initial attach couldn't complete. The existing stale-query token / teardown guards are preserved.

## 2. `SuggestionExtension` drops the `allowSpaces` option

### Problem

The legacy `createSuggestionExtension` factory supported `allowSpaces`, which keeps the suggestion popup open when the query contains a space (e.g. typing `{{first response` to match a "First Response Time" field). The new `SuggestionExtension.configure` wrapper builds the tiptap suggestion config from a fixed set of keys and silently drops everything else, so consumers migrating to it lose this behavior: the popup dismisses the moment a space is typed.

### Fix

Add `allowSpaces?: boolean` to `SuggestionExtensionOptions` and forward it to the underlying `@tiptap/suggestion` plugin config, restoring parity with `createSuggestionExtension`. Covered by a unit test in `useEditor.test.ts`.

## How to test

1. Build an app that uses `RichTextKit` mentions or a `SuggestionExtension` (e.g. Frappe Helpdesk) in **production mode** with reka-ui >= 2.5.
2. In the rich-text editor, type `@` (mention) or a custom trigger like `{{`.
3. Before: no popup appears. After: the suggestion list opens and filters as you type.
4. For `allowSpaces`: configure a `SuggestionExtension` with `allowSpaces: true`, type a multi-word query like `{{first response`. Before: the popup closes on the space. After: it stays open and keeps filtering.

Verified in a Helpdesk production build for both `@` mentions and `{{` field autocomplete, and in dev for `allowSpaces` with the Saved Replies `{{` field autocomplete.

body: ## Summary Hardens Firestore security rules to mitigate the previously identified resource exhaustion vulnerability (denial-of-wallet attack via unbounded document writes). ## Changes **`firestore.rules`**: - **Users collection**: Replaced permissive `data.size() >= 2` with strict `keys().hasOnly(['email', 'createdAt'])` to prevent arbitrary field injection (mass assignment). Added email field-size limit (320 chars per RFC 5321) on both create and update operations. - **Generations collection**: Added `keys().hasOnly(...)` constraint to restrict documents to the known field set (`userId`, `type`, `createdAt`, `prompt`, `url`). Added `prompt` field-size limit (10,000 chars) and `url` field-size limit (800,000 chars) to cap base64 payload sizes and prevent storage abuse. ## Security Impact These changes reduce the blast radius of the Firestore resource exhaustion vulnerability by: 1. Blocking mass assignment of arbitrary fields to documents 2. Capping the maximum size of user-controlled string fields 3. Maintaining backward compatibility with all existing application writes

body:
> **Draft: stacked on #599 → #644.** The diff includes both parents' commits until they merge; the two commits to review here are "Fix code-block highlighting…" and "Single-source brand tokens…". Will be marked ready once #644 lands.

## What this does

Makes the SCSS the single source of truth for the GRASS brand tokens, and fixes two regressions surfaced by the migration (part of #600):

- **`_css-variables.scss`**: generates the `:root { --gs-* }` custom-property block from the `$gs-*` Sass tokens (each light/lighter/lightest ramp derived from its base color), so the served stylesheet finally defines the `var(--gs-*)` names the brand page documents. 73 custom properties emitted.
- **Deletes the orphaned `themes/grass/assets/css/style.css`** (2000 lines): hand-maintained, no longer served since #599, and already drifted from the SCSS. Its post-fork hot-fixes were ported into the SCSS in #599.
- **Reconciles token drift** at the source (primary-light/secondary-light ramp typos, support-color alpha) and fixes the brand page's `--gs-primary-ligh-color` typo.
- **Code-block highlighting fix**: re-links the highlight.js stylesheet (dropped in the migration) and disables Hugo's Chroma (`markup.highlight.codeFences = false`) so fenced code is no longer double-highlighted into dark-on-dark.
- **Timeline margin fix**: `mx-0` on the bare `.row` wrappers so Bootstrap 5's negative gutters stop squashing the releases/web-evolution pages.

## Verified

- Clean containerized build; the compiled CSS now contains the full `--gs-*` token set and tokens resolve at runtime on the brand page.
- Headless-browser QA 15/15; the new pixi instructions on the conda page render through highlight.js with no Chroma remnants.

Part of #600. Follow-up after this lands: export the same token block to the GRASS core docs (mkdocs/pygrass) and Quarto tutorials to replace today's hand-copied duplicates.
