author: bowenbaoshiqi
body:
## 问题

电脑浏览器打开 `/read/{id}`(foliate-js 阅读路径)时,正文不使用霞鹜文楷字体,显示默认 serif。Kindle 路径 `/read-html/{id}` 字体正常,本地直接运行也正常——仅在 Docker 部署 + foliate-js 路径下失效。

## 根因

两个独立问题叠加:

### 1. blob iframe 内 `@font-face` url 解析失败(主因)

foliate-js 用 `attachShadow({mode:"closed"})` 的自定义元素渲染 epub,内部 iframe 的 src 是 `blob:http://host/...`(blob URL)。`typography.to_css` 生成的 `@font-face` 用绝对路径:

```css
@font-face {
  src: url('/static/fonts/lxgw.ttf') format('truetype');
}
```

在 blob iframe 的上下文里,绝对路径 `/static/...` 会解析成 **blob origin 的根**(无效 blob URL),浏览器不发请求,字体静默失败(`lxgw.ttf` 零请求)。

Kindle 路径字体正常,因为它是普通 HTML 页面,`@font-face` 绝对路径正常解析。

### 2. Docker 容器内 `.ttf` 返回错误 MIME

Debian slim 的系统 mime 数据库不认 `.ttf`(`mimetypes.guess_type('x.ttf')` 返回 `(None, None)`),FastAPI StaticFiles 回退 `application/octet-stream`。Chrome 对 `@font-face src` 严格校验 MIME,`octet-stream` 被拒绝加载。

macOS 本地 mime 库有 `.ttf → font/ttf`,所以本地正常、Docker 内失效。

## 修复

| 文件 | 改动 |
|------|------|
| `app/static/reader.js` | `applyTypography` 把后端 CSS 里的 `url('/static/...')` 补成完整 origin URL `url('${location.origin}/static/...')`,blob iframe(同源,继承创建者 origin)能正确解析 |
| `app/main.py` | 启动时 `mimetypes.add_type` 补 `font/ttf`、`font/otf`、`font/woff`、`font/woff2` 四个字体 MIME |

## 验证

用 playwright headless 打开 `/read/{id}` 监听 `lxgw.ttf` 请求:

- 修复前:`lxgw.ttf` **零请求**(blob 上下文 url 解析失败)
- 修复后:`lxgw.ttf` **HTTP 200** 正常加载,字体生效

## 影响范围

- 仅影响 foliate-js 阅读路径(`/read/{id}`,电脑/手机浏览器)
- Kindle 路径(`/read-html/{id}`)不受影响(本来就正常)
- 本地开发不受影响(macOS mime 库已有 `.ttf`)
- 修复对 Docker 部署用户是实质性的

author: jamesdanielwhitford
body:
Migrates the Java Spring Boot API quickstart to Bluehawk LocalCode, and fixes what testing the guide turned up.

**A missing amount produced a 500.** `total` was declared optional and then used unconditionally, so `/make-change` with no query parameter threw a null pointer exception. The amount is now parsed in the controller, which returns 400 for a missing, malformed or negative value.

Parsing in the controller rather than binding a required BigDecimal is deliberate. Letting Spring reject the parameter forwards to `/error`, and that forward is itself subject to the security rules, so an unauthenticated request came back 403 instead of 401. Handling it in the controller keeps the existing 401 behaviour intact, which the end-to-end test checks.

**The end-to-end test only checked the happy path**, so it covered neither the missing-value case nor the response contents. It now asserts the breakdown for $1.02 and $0.29 and covers missing, non-numeric and negative amounts.

**Test harness.** Cleanup read LOGS_PID before it was assigned, so under set -u a failure in any earlier step aborted cleanup before docker compose down. The readiness loops had no timeout.

Verified against a real FusionAuth stack: all 13 checks pass, including 400 on the three rejection cases and 401 for an unauthenticated request.

author: lcp2
body:
Lee: *"the living details are not visible in the build."* He is right — and the reason is not that the code wasn't running. It was. The shaders resolve in WebGL, the factory installs, the wind is in the vertices.

Measured on the deployed build, at the camera the game is actually played from:

| | pixels changing by >8/255 over 2s |
|---|---|
| lawn | 0.02% |
| foliage | 0.02% |
| the factory | 0% (even at >30/255) |

The yard was running a wind no human eye could resolve.

## The real failure is how I measured it

When I shipped this I claimed **"12.6% of pixels moving."** That number was real and meaningless: it counted every pixel that changed *at all*, so a sub-pixel shift of a high-frequency grass texture — which dithers a hundred thousand pixels by one value each — came out as a triumph. I measured the wrong thing and called it done.

**Metres are the wrong unit.** The game is played from 25.1 m back through a 40° lens, where a metre of lawn is ~59 px on a 1080p frame. The only question is: *how many pixels does this cross?*

* **Foliage** — 11 cm of sway, normalised over 2.5 m of bend height. The yard is shrubs and tufts a knee high, so an actual bush reached a fifth of it: a pixel and a half. Now **26 cm over 1.4 m** → a typical shrub travels ~12 px, a tree canopy ~20.
* **Lawn** — 6 cm of blade lean, under two pixels, on the surface that *is* most of the screen. Now **18 cm** → ~10 px of grass detail leaning as the gust rolls across. The shimmer stays small: the ground may move as much as it likes but it may not gain contrast (Craft Bible, figure-ground).
* **Motes** — 4–12 cm dots at 30% alpha: pollen seen from thirty metres, i.e. nothing. Now **11–26 cm at 42%**, and more of them. The cheapest "the air is moving" cue there is, and the only one that works wherever the camera points.
* **The factory** — an 84 cm impeller (a 50 px disc with 4 px blades) and a wisp of exhaust, on a machine that sits half off the top edge of the frame. The impeller is now **1.5 m across a 3 m roof**, and the exhaust is a **plume** that climbs clear of it.

## The test this ticket needed and did not have

`WindVisibilityTests` converts the sway through the real rig and asserts it **in pixels** — on Lee's screen *and* on a 6-inch phone — with an upper bound as well as a lower one, because ambience that pulls the eye off a telegraph has stopped being ambience. Every existing wind test passed while the yard was dead, because they all asked about metres.

Depends on **YT-91** (merged): before it, none of this ran at all on any run after the first, because Replay rebuilt nothing.

`cc-verify` exit 0; EditMode 467/467, PlayMode 119/119.

### Motivation

- Silence a range of Rust compilation warnings emitted by `make engine` (unused imports/fields/functions, unnecessary `mut`, and Rust 2024 unsafe-operation warnings) so the engine builds cleanly.

### Description

- Mark intentionally-unused APIs and helpers with `#[allow(dead_code)]` across the engine registry, parser, control, editor, reader, UI, and related modules to avoid dead-code warnings (examples: `registry::*`, parser helpers, `cli_dispatch`, `cli_rpc`, `rehighlight_pending`).
- Rename retained-but-unused struct fields to `_`-prefixed names (e.g. `counts`→`_counts`, `streamed`→`_streamed`, `pack`→`_pack`) and replace unused locals/closures (`mut` removal, closure mutability) to remove unused-variable/mutable warnings in `gimir/gitdepot` and engine code.
- Wrap calls to unsafe functions and intrinsics in explicit `unsafe { ... }` blocks and use `unsafe` when calling `AtomicU32::from_ptr`, `libc::syscall` and futex operations to satisfy Rust 2024 `unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn` diagnostics in `engine/src/runner.rs`.
- Minor local cleanups to suppress unused-variable warnings: map unused tuple elements to `_verb`, rename `method`→`_method` in `wacz`, and remove an unused `use` import in `gitdepot::lib`.

### Testing

- Ran `git diff --check` to ensure no whitespace/format issues and it passed.
- Built the engine using the project `make engine` (which runs the vendoring steps and `cargo zigbuild --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`) and the build completed successfully after the fixes.

- Block all upgrade edges into `4.22.0-okd-scos.4`, `.5`, and `.6`. CRI-O 1.36.1 on these releases hangs during node shutdown (systemd watchdog timeout causes SIGABRT), causing a full container image store wipe on reboot. No forward upgrade edges can be created from these releases via CI.

The root cause is [cri-o/cri-o#9855](https://github.com/cri-o/cri-o/pull/9855) (continuous CNI STATUS polling introduced in CRI-O 1.36.0), which causes CRI-O to stop responding to systemd's watchdog during shutdown. The upgrade from `.4`/`.5`/`.6` to `.7` completes successfully despite the disruption, the cluster recovers on `.7` with the fixed CRI-O.

author: adminmadusa
body:
# UI-006 — Modal Animation Standardization

Fixes broken exit animations, eliminates an animation race condition on mobile, and formalises motion tokens in the shared design system. No consumer API changes.

## Defects Fixed

### Defect 1 — Missing Exit Animations (all 20 consumers)
`Modal.tsx` returned `null` immediately on `isOpen = false`, destroying the DOM before any CSS transition could run. Every close action (button, backdrop, Escape) caused an instant disappearance.

**Fix:** Introduced `useDelayedUnmount` hook that keeps the element in the DOM for `MotionTokens.modal.exit` (150ms) after `isOpen` becomes false, allowing the exit CSS transition to complete before unmounting.

### Defect 2 — AUTH-010 Mobile Animation Race Condition
`globals.css` contained a legacy CSS block (added in PR #377, June 2026) that targeted the Modal's DOM via class-selector specificity hacks and ran a competing `transform` animation on the same `transform` property as the shared `bottom-sheet` presentation. Traced to its origin: a consumer-side workaround added before `presentation="bottom-sheet"` existed in `@mad/ui`.

**Fix:** Removed the AUTH-010 block entirely.

### Defect 3 — Non-functional Tailwind Duration/Easing Classes
Nine components in `packages/ui/src` used `duration-base`, `duration-fast`, `ease-smooth`, `ease-bounce` — none of which were extended in the Tailwind preset. Verified as silent no-ops.

**Fix:** Extended `preset.ts` with `transitionDuration` and `transitionTimingFunction` mapped to the existing CSS custom properties in `shared.css`.

## Design System Improvements

- **`motionTokens.ts`** — New SSOT for animation timing constants. Components own their timing by referencing `MotionTokens.modal.exit` etc., never hardcoding ms values.
- **`useDelayedUnmount`** — Generic shared hook. Exported from `@mad/ui` barrel. Consumed by both Modal and Drawer for parity.
- **`transition-all` → `transition-[transform,opacity]`** — Scoped transitions on Modal and Drawer content to avoid unnecessary layout recalculations.
- **Drawer exit animation parity** — Drawer now uses the same `useDelayedUnmount` pattern with side-aware exit transitions.

## Files Modified

author: luisnunoperdigao-dotcom
body:
## What

Documents the **Digital Omnibus** amendment to **AI Act art. 4 (AI literacy)** in the `ai-act-compliance` skill:

- `references/11-art4-ai-literacy.md` — new **§1.1** with the adopted verbatim + analysis.
- `SKILL.md` — note on the art. 4 row in "Universal obligations".
- `CHANGELOG.md` — entry under `Unreleased`.

## Why

The skill currently quotes only the 2024 **in-force** text of art. 4. The Digital Omnibus (COM(2025) 836, 19 Nov 2025) amends art. 4; the amendment was **adopted** by the European Parliament (16 Jun 2026, `P10_TA(2026)0198`) and the Council (29 Jun 2026), but is **not yet published in the OJ**. Given this skill's `regulatory-drift` focus, flagging it early seemed useful.

## Key point

The obligation shifts from **“ensure … a sufficient level”** (result) to **“support the development of AI literacy”** (means), and expressly **does not require guaranteeing any specific level**. The verb stays **“shall”**; **providers and deployers remain the duty-bearers** (the Commission's proposal to move the duty to the Commission/Member States was rejected — they get a supporting role).

Adopted art. 4(1):

> “Providers and deployers of AI systems shall take measures to support the development of AI literacy … This obligation does not require providers or deployers to guarantee any specific level of AI literacy of any individual.”

## Safe-by-design

- The **in-force (lex lata) text is preserved**; the amendment is clearly marked as *adopted, awaiting OJ*.
- Reference-only; no change to the skill's execution profile.
- The Regulation's number/date and official language versions can be finalized once it is in the OJ (expected before 2026-08-02).

## Sources

- `P10_TA(2026)0198` — European Parliament adopted text (16 Jun 2026)
- Council press release, 29 Jun 2026 (“final green light”)

Migrates the Estonia-only ICD10-EST postfix import fix from `tehik-termx-server` (fork commits `234a750e`, `58ea7d2c`). Ported test-first (red → green).

## Change
A subsection's dagger/asterisk postfix `<sub>` codes are appended to each **leaf item** as child concepts (`item.code + <suffix after '*'>`), rather than parsed-and-discarded as base did. Adds `Node.getPostfix()` (`SubSection` returns its `sub`; others null) and `Icd10EstMapper.toPostfixConcept()`.

## ⚠️ Validation caveat
The shipped `icd10-est.xml` fixture contains **no `<sub>` postfix elements**, so this is covered by a **synthetic** unit test that encodes the fork's algorithm, not real Estonian source data. **Before trusting in production, re-ground it against a real ICD10-EST XML sample** with dagger/asterisk codes to confirm the `split("*")` / `parent.code + suffix` composition and the assumption that subsection-level (not item-level) subs are the postfixes.

- New synthetic spec `Icd10EstPostfixMapperSpec` (red on base → green after port).
- Existing `Icd10EstMapperTest` unaffected (no `<sub>` in the fixture).

author: joycai
body:
## What & why

The prompt library only holds prompts the user deliberately saved, so a prompt that was typed, submitted and iterated on was gone the moment it left the editor. This adds a **prompt history** to the workbench prompt header: the last 10 submitted prompts, offered back for reuse. Works for both image and video generation.

A clock icon in the prompt header opens a panel listing recent prompts, newest first with a relative timestamp. Tapping an entry opens a **preview** of the full prompt; only on confirming does it replace the editor's contents. A Clear History action sits behind its own confirmation.

## How

- **Recording** hooks into `submitTask` (`app_state_workbench.dart`), which both panels already funnel through — one hook covers both. It fires only after the task is actually queued, so a rejected submit leaves nothing behind.
- **Storage** is a new `prompt_history` table (schema **v27 → v28**) reached through the repository layer, following the `downloader_cookies` precedent for a bounded, recency-ordered list.
- **UI** is `PromptHistorySheet`, reusing the `PromptLibrarySheet` shell (bottom sheet when narrow, right-slide panel on desktop) since the two sit side by side.

## Decisions a reviewer should weigh in on

- **Re-submitting a prompt bumps it rather than duplicating it.** Iterating on one prompt is the common case; without this it would flush the other nine slots within minutes.
- **Image and video keep separate lists of 10**, trimmed per type, so a run of video generations can't evict image prompts.
- **History is excluded from backup and survives `resetAllSettings`**, matching the existing reasoning for `tasks` and cookies — local data that no backup carries, so clearing it destroys what no restore replaces. The Clear History button is the way out. Happy to change this if you'd rather it be included or wiped on reset.
- **The button is icon-only.** My first pass used a text label and overflowed the config sidebar by 40px — the 318px header can't fit two labelled buttons next to the Library button, so the "PROMPT" title got squeezed to zero width and wrapped one letter per line. The existing responsive layout test caught it.
- **The video panel still has no Library button.** That asymmetry predates this change and was left alone as out of scope.

## Testing

`flutter analyze` clean; full suite passes (68 tests, 16 new).

- `test/prompt_history_test.dart` (9) — the real SQL against an in-memory schema: ordering, dedup/bump, the 10-cap, per-type isolation, blank/whitespace handling, and that a **v27 install gets the table on upgrade**, not only on fresh install.
- `test/prompt_history_sheet_test.dart` (7) — drives the picker as a user does (tap → preview → confirm), pinning down that nothing is replaced until confirmed.

To let the first group exercise the real code rather than a copy, the history SQL bodies are split out behind `@visibleForTesting`, mirroring the existing `restoreBackupInto` / `importPromptDataInto` pattern.

## Notes

- All four locales updated (en / zh / zh_Hant / ja) via the `merge_l10n` + `gen-l10n` workflow.
- Version **not** bumped (still 2.17.1) — say the word if this should carry one.

author: dan2k3k4
body:
Fixes two billing-correctness bugs where a downstream failure permanently loses paid state. ## Lost Stripe events (webhooks.py, worker.py) The webhook committed the `DBStripeProcessedEvent` idempotency claim and returned 200 to Stripe *before* the work ran in a background task. Any failure in the background handler (which swallowed all exceptions) left the event marked processed but never applied, and Stripe never retried. - Process the event synchronously so a failure can be reported to Stripe. - Worker re-raises on failure instead of swallowing. - On failure, release the claim row and return non-2xx so Stripe re-delivers. ## Unrecoverable top-up (budgets.py) On LiteLLM sync failure the top-up ledger entry was deactivated but kept. Because `uq_periodic_ledger_topup_payment` makes `(team_id, region_id, entry_type, stripe_payment_id)` unique, the lingering row blocked the duplicate guard (409) and would collide on re-insert, so a captured payment could never be re-applied via the API. - Delete the ledger entry on sync failure so a resubmission runs fresh. Full backend suite passes (1102 passed).

Greptile Summary

 This PR fixes two billing-correctness bugs where downstream failures permanently lost paid state. It replaces background-task webhook dispatch with synchronous processing so Stripe receives a non-2xx on failure and retries, and it deletes (rather than deactivates) the periodic top-up ledger entry on LiteLLM sync failure so the unique constraint cannot block a clean resubmission. - **webhooks.py**: `BackgroundTasks` is removed; `handle_stripe_event_background` is now `await`-ed synchronously. On failure, an isolated inner `try/except` deletes the idempotency claim row and the original exception is always re-raised — even when the cleanup commit itself fails — so Stripe gets a non-2xx and retries. - **worker.py**: The catch-all `except` block now re-raises after logging, propagating failures to the webhook handler instead of swallowing them. - **budgets.py**: On LiteLLM sync failure, the `topup_entry` row is deleted rather than deactivated, removing the stale row that the unique index `uq_periodic_ledger_topup_payment` would have turned into a permanent block on any retry.

Confidence Score: 5/5

 Safe to merge. The three targeted changes are logically correct and address real billing-correctness gaps with no new regressions introduced. All three changes are narrowly scoped to their stated goals. The synchronous webhook processing with the isolated cleanup try/except correctly preserves the original exception in every code path, the worker re-raise is straightforward, and the ledger-entry deletion in budgets.py is well-reasoned — the deleted row is never accessed again (the error path always raises HTTPException before db.refresh). No new logic paths appear unsafe. No files require special attention beyond the existing review thread discussion on webhooks.py.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | app/api/webhooks.py | Switches from BackgroundTasks to synchronous await with isolated cleanup try/except on failure; core retry logic is sound but claim-cleanup failure remains an edge-case gap (previously flagged in review thread). | | app/core/worker.py | Adds re-raise after logging so callers receive the exception and can release the idempotency claim; finally block still closes the worker's own session correctly. | | app/api/budgets.py | Replaces deactivation with deletion of the failed ledger entry, unblocking the unique constraint so a resubmission can run the full flow fresh; db.refresh(topup_entry) after the except block is unreachable on the error path due to the always-present raise HTTPException. |

## Summary

The GoReleaser (and every `main.yml`) job emitted a GitHub Actions annotation:

> `Unexpected input(s) 'dissociate', valid inputs are ['repository', 'ref', 'token', ...]`

`dissociate: true` was being passed to `actions/checkout`, which has no such input, so it was **silently ignored** and only produced the warning.

The Namespace runner migration (`998e23c0a`) intended git's `--dissociate` behavior — detaching the checkout from the Namespace Git mirror cache (those runners have "Git Mirror Cache: Enabled"). But that flag is only exposed by [`namespacelabs/nscloud-checkout-action`](https://github.com/namespacelabs/nscloud-checkout-action), not GitHub's `actions/checkout`.

This swaps all 11 checkout steps to `nscloud-checkout-action@v9` (SHA-pinned, matching repo convention) and keeps `dissociate: true`, so the input is now **honored** and the warning clears.

- `actions/checkout@v7.0.0` → `namespacelabs/nscloud-checkout-action@445c25d…` (`# v9`) across `release.yml` (1) and `main.yml` (10)

Only `fetch-depth`, `dissociate`, and `ref` are used across the blocks — all three are valid `nscloud-checkout-action@v9` inputs.

author: mikaak
body:
## The problem

`Cache.TermEncoder.encode/2` was called in the generic `Cache` macro on every `put` and `decode/1` on every `get`. Because it lives in the macro, it applied to **every adapter** — including the ones that store Erlang terms natively, where the round trip buys nothing.

| Adapter | Stores | Encoding needed? |
|---|---|---|
| `Cache.ETS` | native terms | no — pure waste |
| `Cache.Agent` | native terms | no |
| `Cache.PersistentTerm` | native terms, zero-copy by design | no — encoding defeated its entire purpose |
| `Cache.ConCache` | ETS-backed, native terms | no |
| `Cache.Counter` | integers | already passed through |
| `Cache.DETS` | terms, but a durable on-disk format | **yes** — see below |
| `Cache.Redis` | bytes on the wire | **yes** |

The decode is not a rounding error. On a 500k-entry ETS table, a bare `:ets.lookup` of a ~10KB body costs **63 ns** while `binary_to_term` of that same body costs **~29,000 ns**. The decode was ~460x the cost of the lookup it was attached to, on the hot read path, for nothing.

## The design

Adapters now declare how they store values through an optional callback on the `Cache` behaviour:

```elixir
@callback native_term_storage?(adapter_opts :: Keyword.t()) :: boolean()
@optional_callbacks native_term_storage?: 1
```

The `Cache` macro resolves it **at compile time** from `@cache_adapter` and the configured opts, then compiles either a real encode or an identity shim — so there is **zero runtime branch** on the read/write path.

The callback is **optional and defaults to `false` (encode)**, so any third-party adapter keeps working with no change.

Two details worth calling out:

- **`sandbox?: true` resolves against the adapter it stands in for**, not against `Cache.Sandbox`. Otherwise a value would round-trip differently in test than in prod.
- **Runtime opts (`{app, key}`, MFA, zero-arity fun) fall back to encoding.** The capability can't be read at compile time there, so it takes the safe path, which is exactly the old behaviour.

### Composite adapters

- **`HashRing` / `RefreshAhead`** call the encoder directly, bypassing the macro. They now resolve the capability against the adapter they wrap, via `TermEncoder.maybe_encode/3` and `maybe_decode/3`.
- **`MultiLayer` needed no change.** Each layer is a full `Cache` module that owns its own encoding, so a `[ETS, Redis]` stack already stores a **term in the ETS layer and bytes in the Redis layer**. There's now a test asserting exactly that, reading both underlying stores directly, plus one asserting a value backfilled from Redis lands in ETS as a term.

## Benchmark

500k entries, ~10KB structured body (13,505 B encoded), 20k iterations, measured through the public API on `main` vs this branch:

| Op | Before | After | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `get/1` | 29,981 ns | **6,211 ns** | **4.8x faster** |
| `put/2` | 23,542 ns | **10,804 ns** | **2.2x faster** |

The win is not confined to large payloads:

| Payload | Before | After | |
|---|---|---|---|
| small map (41 B) | 2,105 ns | **302 ns** | 7.0x |
| session (375 B) | 2,179 ns | **363 ns** | 6.0x |
| api body (10.6 KB) | 28,284 ns | **6,152 ns** | 4.6x |

`Cache.PersistentTerm` also regains its zero-copy read — `:erts_debug.same/2` now confirms two reads return the *same* term rather than two independently decoded copies.

## The DETS decision: keep encoding

**`Cache.DETS` still encodes.** `:dets.insert/2` takes terms and would serialise them itself, so this is a redundant serialisation — and I kept it anyway.

Every `.dets` file written by an earlier version holds `term_to_binary` blobs as its values, and those files **outlive the upgrade — that is the entire point of a disk cache**. Switching to native terms would make the first read after upgrading hand back a raw binary where the caller expects a term. Silently. With no error to trace it back to.

I considered a read-side fallback (try `binary_to_term`, fall back to raw) and rejected it: it is unbackable-out-of, it guesses, and it would misfire on any value that is legitimately a binary. A version marker means rewriting the file format for an adapter whose whole job is to not do that.

The cost of keeping the encode is one redundant serialisation of data already headed for a disk write, which the I/O dominates. The cost of dropping it is corrupting every existing on-disk cache. That trade isn't close. There's a test asserting a file written in the old format still decodes correctly.

**The same reasoning applies to `Cache.ETS` with `:rehydration_path`** — that option dumps the table via `:ets.tab2file/2` and reloads it on the next boot, making it a durable format with the identical constraint. So `native_term_storage?/1` returns `false` for ETS *when that option is set*. Plain ETS is unaffected. (The repo's existing rehydration test, which writes a hand-encoded value into the dump file, still passes untouched — which is itself the proof.)

## `compression_level`

When set, encoding is deliberate, so **`compression_level` forces encoding on any adapter, native or not.** The user asked to compress; they get compression.

⚠️ **Worth flagging separately: `compression_level` is currently dead config on `main`.** It is not declared in *any* adapter's `opts_definition`, so `NimbleOptions` rejects it on compile-time opts; and via runtime opts the macro's `@compression_level` is only read when opts are a compile-time list, so it resolves to `nil` and never reaches the encoder. It's unreachable on every path. I have **not** fixed that here — it's an orthogonal bug and this PR is already load-bearing. The new code honours it correctly wherever it becomes reachable.

## The `TermEncoder` landmine (fixed)

`encode/2` regex-checks binaries against `~r/^{.*}$/` and passes JSON-looking ones through **unencoded**, while encoding everything else. `decode/1` then has to guess. It's genuinely broken, and it's worse than "guessing":

```elixir
# on main:
put(:k, ~s({"a": 1}))  |> get(:k)   #=> {:ok, %{"a" => 1}}   # put a String, got back a Map
put(:k, "{oops}")      |> get(:k)   #=> ** (Jason.DecodeError)  # crash on read
```

The first is a silent type change. The second is a **crash on read** for any brace-wrapped binary that isn't valid JSON.

I did not build on top of it. `decode/1` now uses `decode_json/1` (which falls back to returning the binary unchanged) instead of `Jason.decode!/1`, so the crash is gone. The remaining JSON-passthrough asymmetry only affects byte-storing adapters now, and its existing tests still pass — a full fix means picking a wire format and is a breaking change to Redis-stored data, which belongs in its own PR.

## Other bugs this fixes

Both were direct consequences of encoding unconditionally:

- **`ConCache.get_or_store/3` + `get/1` raised.** `get_or_store/3` writes through ConCache directly, bypassing the encode in `put/3`, so the matching `get/1` tried to `binary_to_term/1` a raw term and blew up. It works now.
- **The raw ETS API was broken.** `Cache.ETS` exposes `match_object/1`, `select/1`, `tab2list/0`, `foldl/2` — all of which saw opaque encoded binaries instead of the terms that were `put`. You could not match on a value. They now see real terms.

## Breaking change status

**Minor-breaking. Version bumped to 0.5.0.**

- `get/1`, `put/3`, `delete/1` round-trip **exactly as before** — the public API is unchanged.
- It *is* observable if you read the underlying store directly (`:ets.lookup/2`, `:persistent_term.get/1`, `ConCache.get/2`) or through the raw ETS API. Those now return terms — which is what they were always meant to return.
- **No data-migration hazard.** DETS and rehydrated-ETS keep their on-disk format. ETS, Agent, PersistentTerm and ConCache don't survive a restart, so there is no upgrade path on which a stale encoded value can be read back by the new code.

## Tests

21 new tests (`test/cache/native_term_storage_test.exs` + 2 in `multi_layer_test.exs`) covering: capability resolution per adapter; native ada

author: transfix
body:
When a PR touches `recipes/`, this builds the **changed recipes on the dev cluster** and reports back on the PR — so recipe changes are smoke-tested on real builders before merge.

## How
- Triggers on `pull_request` with `paths: [recipes/**]`.
- Runs on `[self-hosted, Linux, cvcpkg-builder]` (the runner with `incus`/LAN access to dev, same as `deploy-dev.yml`); **same-repo PRs only** so fork PRs never touch the runner or dev secrets.
- Diffs against the PR base to find changed recipe dirs, `cvcpkg recipe push` each to the dev server (URL resolved via `incus list cvcpkg-server`), then `cvcpkg builds submit-dag --allow-unschedulable --wait` across the platforms the dev cluster can serve.
- Comments a ✅/❌ summary + build log on the PR.

## Notes
- Uses `secrets.CVCPKG_ADMIN_TOKEN` (already used by deploy-dev).
- The dev cluster is linux-only, so `--allow-unschedulable` skips windows/macos-only recipes (they're reported as skipped rather than hanging). A future dev **windows** builder would let this also validate `openssh-win`.

## What

Switch `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`'s `skills` field from a hand-listed enumeration of all 22 skill directories to **directory form** — pointing at the two promoted buckets and letting Claude Code discover the skills one level down:

**FULL SEND follow-up to #202** — builds `openssh-win` from source instead of staging Microsoft's prebuilt zip, linking **our own** openssl + zlib recipes.

## What
- Source: `PowerShell/openssh-portable` @ `latestw_all` (pinned commit `e98b11e`, OpenSSH_for_Windows_10.0), sha256-pinned.

## ⚠️ Experimental — needs Windows-builder validation
The upstream Windows build is tightly coupled to its **vcpkg** crypto layout; substituting our OpenSSL is first-pass wiring (lib naming: solution wants `libcrypto.lib` + `zs.lib`; header/lib search paths) and will likely need iteration on a real Windows builder. I could not compile-test it here.

body:
Closes #302.

> Stacked on #305 / `gnanirahulnutakki/issue-300-recognition-fingerprints` because this slice consumes fingerprint health counters introduced there. Do not merge this PR before #305; retarget or rebase safely after the parent lands.

## What changed

- expose authenticated daemon-lifetime lifecycle, recognition, and fingerprint health counters without paths, argv, environment, payloads, or computed executable digests
- add a strict real-Linux recognition-off/on AB/BA benchmark with one warm-up and 20 measured pairs for low, sustained, and storm profiles
- record exclusive capture, classification, and fingerprint terminal ledgers plus workload wall time, daemon thread-group CPU, per-profile peak RSS, raw pairs, summaries, and artifact digest
- commit historical and corrected-method hosted evidence plus an evidence-bound budget with explicit wall, CPU, and RSS tolerances; loss is never tolerated
- add a bounded native workload, optional release profile, pinned-action read-only workflow, docs, changelog, and public evidence mirrors
- retry bounded `poll(pidfd)` `EINTR` interruptions instead of misclassifying ordinary signal interruption as unsupported; persistent interruption still fails closed after eight retries
- harden evidence boundaries: explicit disabled recognition health, valid duplicate-key fixtures, descriptor-relative no-symlink/no-replace Linux report publication, fail-closed non-Linux publication, per-profile `VmHWM` reset, and a 40-minute outer workflow ceiling around the 25-minute internal deadline

## Evidence lifecycle

### Historical first baseline

- run: https://github.com/ArdurAI/ardur/actions/runs/29321373911
- source: `967ba6702c721a351c9e52e665f16e591ac5d9b6`
- artifact: `60ec1e25e89375e323d6b564a91b74283aae3b2995a6878665e1ecdc3a399530`
- each arm ran 2,080 measured workload executions (4,160 total); the enabled arm delivered, recognized, and fingerprinted all 2,080
- zero producer drops, malformed records, rejection, mismatch, saturation, unavailable, in-flight, or unexplained work

### Defect evidence

Run https://github.com/ArdurAI/ardur/actions/runs/29322244528 failed twice at exact head `8fa7d084...`: storm reported two then three `unsupported` fingerprint outcomes. Performance and capture/classification ledgers passed. Linux `poll(2)` documents `EINTR` as ordinary signal interruption; the pidfd exit check had collapsed it into unsupported. The bounded retry fix made persistent interruption remain fail-closed while eliminating the transient misclassification.

### Corrected-method calibration

Review identified that `VmHWM` is cumulative for the process lifetime. Commit `203c1016dbec3740608e8f1a9a5ce71e90f5de78` resets it before each profile and hardens report publication.

- run: https://github.com/ArdurAI/ardur/actions/runs/29326060724
- artifact: `cd0a5e68b45757886e67d6f546de9e2be4bbf0f48f7fdaa1b9a0acbd279c9d23`
- passed prior budget digest `33aec8ad75d09e2831f9c65ad8dbfbe7e86a8fd6ef1e3b2b67c50ffba65fe94f`
- committed as `agent-recognition-benchmark-evidence-203c101.json`
- budget v2 binds every reference metric to this artifact while retaining all existing tolerances

## Final exact-head enforcement

Run https://github.com/ArdurAI/ardur/actions/runs/29327162327 passes at exact head `8dce4c52a55cd5a5ac1c0032a5bf6298e488fcb3`:

- gate `pass`; zero violations
- budget digest `42fae4ab6cf697cb1623a4eeb6132a143d8cb7c2fe4db5275f030b9b943b1d53`
- report artifact `20281ebc7f55948fd84c317d1b514a7be5be4a00ae96a420fd03a84abd03daad`
- archive digest `618ac3bcffb81f009d2209750146217fa1c22fd30ddbedcba1317c324fae5d86`
- Linux amd64, kernel `6.17.0-1018-azure`, Go 1.26.5, four CPUs
- enabled arm: 2,080/2,080 delivered, recognized, and fingerprint-success
- zero producer drops, malformed records, rejection, mismatch, saturation, unavailable, in-flight, or unexplained work
- wall p95 low/sustained/storm: 0.1774% / 0.1282% / 0.8258%
- enabled-daemon CPU p95: 11.89 ms / 44.88 ms / 159.32 ms
- per-profile peak RSS: 13,380 / 13,432 / 13,464 KiB
- privacy scan clean; embedded source SHA and budget digest independently verified

## Validation and review

- Docker Go 1.26.5 race tests and targeted vet for `pkg/kernelcapture`, daemon, controller, and workload: pass
- Darwin/arm64 cross-compile of the fail-closed non-Linux controller path: pass
- actionlint v1.7.12: pass
- source mirror: 116 pages / 117 artifacts verified
- Hugo 0.161.1, rendered-link validation, and `./scripts/check-local.sh --quick`: pass
- exact-head PR CI: 15 successful, one expected PR deploy skip, zero failures
- authenticated CodeRabbit uncommitted and committed reviews: zero remaining findings
- GitHub CodeRabbit status is skipped because the PR intentionally targets a non-default stacked branch; the local committed review is the applicable review evidence
- both new commits have good ED25519 signatures, DCO trailers, and passing pre-commit secret/private-key gates

## Claim boundary

This is host-specific observer-effect and loss-accounting evidence. It does not establish universal performance, classifier accuracy, agent identity, attestation, process adoption, or governance. Human review remains mandatory before the stack lands in `dev`, and promotion from `dev` to `main` remains separately human-gated.

author: petrcala
body:
Implements #159: `lintr`, `NlcOptim`, and `plm` leave `Imports`, so end users no longer install a dev-only linting tool and two single-code-path estimators just to use the package.

## Changes

- **DESCRIPTION**: `lintr`, `NlcOptim`, and `plm` moved from `Imports` to `Suggests` (version constraints kept).
- **lintr**: `R/linters.R` moved to `scripts/linters.R`, so the custom linters are no longer shipped with the package. `.lintr.R` now sources the new location using its existing repo-root walk-up. `make document` dropped the `importFrom(lintr, ...)` NAMESPACE entries and the three orphaned man pages. The linter unit tests now source `scripts/linters.R` through a shared helper and skip when the file is unreachable (e.g. tests running from a built tarball) or lintr is not installed.
- **NlcOptim**: the only call site (`inst/artma/calc/methods/elliott.R`) was already `requireNamespace`-guarded; the abort message now names the package with an install hint (same for its `quadprog` sibling).
- **plm**: the panel specs in `inst/artma/econometric/linear.R` (FE/BE/RE) now declare `required_packages = "plm"`, and `run_linear_models()` skips those sub-models with a clear install-hint reason when the namespace is unavailable, matching how `AER`/`ivmodel` gating behaves in `exogeneity.R`. The availability check is injectable, and a new test exercises the plm-missing path via that injection: panel models land in `skipped` with a reason naming `plm`, while the OLS variants still run.
- **R/zzz.R**: `register_runtime_dependencies()` no longer touches `NlcOptim::solnl`, `plm::plm`, or `plm::vcovHC`. No matching entries existed in `R/dummy_functions.R` or `R/globals.R`.

## The .lintr.R install trap

`.lintr.R` executes in every R session started at the repo root, because the repo `.Rprofile` calls `lintr:::read_settings(getwd())`. That includes CI `Rscript` steps, which is how removing `here` broke PR #178. Handled as follows:

- The `.Rprofile` call is guarded by `requireNamespace("lintr", quietly = TRUE)`, so a session without lintr skips settings loading entirely. Verified by sourcing the repo `.Rprofile` with `requireNamespace` shadowed to report lintr as absent: the session starts cleanly.
- When lintr is present, `.lintr.R` only needs lintr itself plus `scripts/linters.R`, which exists in every git checkout (it is only excluded from the built tarball). Verified that `lintr:::read_settings(getwd())` in a fresh session registers all 28 linters including the three custom ones.
- CI keeps lintr installed: `lint.yaml` requests `any::lintr` explicitly, and every other workflow uses `setup-r-dependencies` with the default `dependencies: "all"`, which installs `Suggests`. No workflow changes were needed.

## Verification

- `make lint`: no lints, custom linters loaded from the new location.
- `make test`: 0 failures (1098 passing); the linter and linear test files run without skips locally.
- `make check`: 0 errors and no new WARNINGs or NOTEs. The local run shows 1 pre-existing WARNING (clang "unknown warning group" noise from the homebrew toolchain during install) and 1 pre-existing NOTE (the `.git` pointer file of the development worktree); a baseline `make check` on master in the same environment produces exactly the same two findings, and neither applies to CI runners.

Note: #156 also edits DESCRIPTION, so expect a trivial merge overlap there.

Closes #159

author: davidnavalho
body:
## Summary

Adds a reusable `run-agents-in-sbx` skill for running Codex coding agents inside Docker's `sbx` with a host-controlled lifecycle. It turns the operating lessons from `jaf-forge` into a project-independent workflow for workspace ownership, ChatGPT-subscription authentication, bounded execution, evidence-based handoff, cleanup, recovery, and evaluation.

The implemented provider path is Codex CLI authenticated through a narrowly copied ChatGPT-subscription cache. Claude subscription, Claude API, and OpenAI API adapters remain explicit future work.

## What the skill does

- Keeps `sbx` creation, policy inspection, timeout enforcement, evidence collection, and cleanup under an unsandboxed host controller.
- Gives every writer a distinct workspace or worktree and refuses protected-branch writes unless explicitly authorized.
- Never mounts the host `CODEX_HOME`. It copies only file-backed `auth.json` to a staged guest path, changes it to `agent:agent` with mode `0600`, atomically installs it at `/home/agent/.codex/auth.json`, and verifies ChatGPT login status.
- Serializes runners that share an auth lineage. A caller can wait behind a live owner with a finite `--auth-lock-wait`; ambiguous ownership metadata is preserved for inspection rather than removed.
- Keeps unknown or adversarial code in a separate credential-free sandbox.
- Runs Codex noninteractively behind guest and host deadlines and requires a run-specific, validated JSON handoff plus independent host verification.
- Stops and preserves the sandbox if guest auth changed or became ambiguous. It never logs out automatically or overwrites the host cache.
- Removes only the exact owned sandbox after evidence collection and confirms its absence.
- Can install an exact guest Codex CLI version before credentials cross the boundary when the template CLI does not support the selected model.

## Reproducible evaluation methodology

This revision commits the evaluation method alongside the skill:

1. **Deterministic/mock lifecycle suite** — exercises runner, lock, auth, timeout, handoff, scorer, and cleanup branches without a real credential.
2. **Authenticated live boundary matrix** — uses generated trusted repositories to prove the actual mounts, postures, narrow auth copy, handoff, auth stability, leakage checks, and cleanup.
3. **Fresh-context low-effort model matrix** — gives each new session only a natural mixed-trust request, an output schema, and a read-only immutable snapshot of the skill. A host-only scorer gates the semantic decisions and runner evidence.

The fresh-context harness snapshots and SHA-256 digests the skill, runner, fixtures, schema, and scorer once before the first cell. Cells run serially, use only generated trusted workspaces, and retain raw evidence in an ignored local directory. The repo commits the harness, fixtures, scorer, evaluation plan, detailed results, and a redacted per-cell baseline:

- [Evaluation plan](evaluation/run-agents-in-sbx/evaluation-plan.md)
- [Fresh-context harness](evaluation/run-agents-in-sbx/run-fresh-context-matrix.sh)
- [Host scorer](evaluation/run-agents-in-sbx/score-fresh-context.py)
- [Recorded baseline](evaluation/run-agents-in-sbx/baselines/fresh-context-low-effort-20260720.md)
- [Testing index](TESTING.md)

## Recorded results

### Live boundary behavior — 2026-07-15

With `sbx v0.35.0`, host `codex-cli 0.144.4`, `gpt-5.4-mini`, and low effort:

| Posture | Result | Auth cache | Sandbox cleanup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `outer` | 3/3 passed | unchanged each run | removed and confirmed absent |
| `workspace-write` | 3/3 passed | unchanged each run | removed and confirmed absent |

The effective policy included `default-allow-all`, so this proves filesystem and lifecycle boundaries, not egress restriction.

### Fresh-context low-effort behavior — 2026-07-20

With `sbx v0.35.0`, host `codex-cli 0.144.5`, guest `codex-cli 0.145.0-alpha.13`, and low effort in every cell:

| Model | Final semantic result | Runner/auth/cleanup |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gpt-5.6-sol` | 3/3 passed | 3/3 passed |
| `gpt-5.5` | 3/3 passed | 3/3 passed |
| `gpt-5.3-codex-spark` | 3/3 passed | 3/3 passed |

All nine runs produced valid handoffs, left guest auth unchanged, scanned 55 generated files per cell without matching copied credential material, and removed their exact owned sandboxes. Real contention produced lock waits from 0 to 5,318 seconds; the runner respected owner transitions and never bypassed a lock. This is evidence of bounded serialization, not FIFO fairness.

The immutable raw matrix scored 8/9 because one Spark output omitted `codex-logout` from a redundant summary array even though its typed recovery object set `codexLogout: false`, selected stop-and-preserve/manual reconciliation, and explicitly rejected automatic logout. The host-only scorer was corrected to keep the typed safety fields strict without requiring the same decision to be duplicated in the summary. No agent-facing skill, runner, request, schema, or output changed; rescoring the frozen nine-output corpus with the committed scorer produced 9/9. The raw false negative and calibration are retained in the baseline.

These are finite results for three named models on one date. They do not establish that every present or future model behaves identically, and there is no no-skill control measuring causal uplift.

## Validation performed

- `RUN_HOST_CHECKS=1 evaluation/run-agents-in-sbx/run-static-tests.sh`
- skill package validation with the repository's `skill-creator` validator
- shell and Python syntax validation
- repository-relative Markdown link validation
- `git diff --check`
- exact-value and token-shaped secret scan across all changed files
- audit of all nine raw runner/auth/cleanup artifacts and live sandbox absence

Real token refresh, cancellation during a model request, auth ambiguity, and real cleanup failure remain mock-tested rather than deliberately induced with the subscription credential.

## Automation boundary

No CI workflow is added. The meaningful model evaluations require an explicitly reviewed subscription/API credential strategy; putting that credential into unattended CI is outside this PR. The authenticated harnesses are deliberately local, opt-in, and refuse execution unless `ALLOW_REAL_CODEX_AUTH=1` is set after reviewing `--plan`.

author: rezdm
body:
Two features from the post-review ideas discussion, one branch.

## Kernel process-event feed (#60)
Poll-based collection is blind to processes that live less than one refresh tick. New `IProcessEventSource` (start/stop/is_active/drain) beside the existing provider interfaces, wired through the platform factory:

- **Linux**: proc connector (`NETLINK_CONNECTOR` + `CN_PROC`); thread events filtered out (group-leader only), self-pipe shutdown. Needs `CAP_NET_ADMIN` — documented in PRIVILEGES.md with the updated `setcap` line; without it the app runs poll-only, exactly as before.
- **FreeBSD**: kqueue `EVFILT_PROC` attached to all observable PIDs with `NOTE_TRACK` (descendants auto-attached; `NOTE_CHILD` carries the fork edge). Best-effort without root.
- **Solaris**: documented inactive stub (contract informative-event sets are opt-in at contract creation; system-wide observation would need dtrace).

`DataStore` drives the source lifecycle and drains it every tick. The snapshot gains per-tick churn counters plus **short-lived exits** — processes that appeared in no snapshot at all. Both system panels show `Churn: +N fork, N exec, -N exit (N unseen)` when the feed is active.

## Difference highlighting (#61)
Process Explorer's signature visual, driven by a shared, unit-tested `compute_snapshot_diff` recomputed on each snapshot swap (highlights last exactly one refresh interval):

- New processes: green row background, in place, GUI (tree + list) and TUI.
- Exited processes: red ghost rows (state `X`, rates blank, not selectable). GUI renders them **in place** — under the still-living parent in tree view, merged into the sort in list view (fixed after live testing: the first placement at the table top was invisible unless scrolled there). TUI pins ghosts to the bottom of the process panel (functionally verified in a pty: red rows carry the exited process).
- Toggle in the GUI View menu; persisted as `diff_highlight` (default on), honored by both frontends.

**Verification**: 48/48 unit checks (13 new for the diff helper); clean -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic build; TUI red-ghost rendering verified end-to-end in a pty; GUI green/red flow confirmed live by the repo owner; multi-platform CI green on the feature commits (final commit's run linked in checks).

Fixes #60

## Intent

Fix the Firstmate Pi primary watcher tool disappearing after /reload when a later-loaded extension resets the active tool list. Keep only fm_watch_arm_pi active alongside the current selected safety allowlist, without reactivating unrelated tools or weakening plan/review/validation restrictions, and avoid delayed callbacks that use stale extension APIs. Preserve the human command, tool API, attached process wake delivery, and clean shutdown. Treat restart exit 143 as benign only after the canonical home-scoped health predicate verifies a different watcher with a fresh beacon, while retaining genuine failure reporting. Add deterministic and isolated live reload coverage and record exact empirical evidence in the Pi supervision documentation.

## What Changed

- Captain, keep only `fm_watch_arm_pi` active alongside Pi’s current safety allowlist after reloads and later tool-surface resets.
- Transfer watcher restart outcomes safely between extension generations, suppressing exit 143 only when a different healthy watcher is verified and retaining genuine failure delivery.
- Add deterministic lifecycle tests, isolated Workflow Suite live-reload coverage, and documented empirical evidence.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is well-bounded, preserves the selected tool allowlist, avoids stale Pi API calls after shutdown, and safely scopes restart handoff handling.

## Testing

Completed 1 recorded test check.

- ⚠️ `tests/fm-pi-primary-live-e2e.test.sh:124` - The live test copies the user's long-lived Pi auth file beneath the repository in an unignored .pi-live-e2e.* directory. - 🚨 `.pi/extensions/fm-primary-pi-watch.ts:310` - reportPriorRestart() runs unconditionally without verifying session-lock ownership. A read-only Pi session sharing the same FM_HOME can consume and delete the owning session's restart handoff, contradicting the requirement to retain genuine exit-143 failure reporting. If reload occurs before the arm child records `.watch.lock/pid`, `previousPid` is empty; this check then accepts any briefly healthy PID, including the old watcher still shutting down, as “different.” Do not suppress exit 143 unless a valid prior watcher PID was captured and the canonical predicate returns another PID.

That can delete the newer reload's handoff and contradict the requirement to retain genuine failure reporting. Add generation ownership/CAS and clear only the exact handoff originally read.

Treat an owned handoff that remains incomplete at the deadline as an actionable failure so genuine shutdown failures are retained.

author: chouti
body:
## What

Adds an "effective access" column (Workspace / Specific people / Owner-only), an `access` filter dimension, and a "Set access scope" bulk action to the agents list page — forming a see → filter → change loop for agent access-scope management.

## Why

Operators cannot read or change agent access scope from the list page today. The only access signal is a small lock marker derived from the lossy `visibility` field, which conflates "owner-only" and "specific-people" agents. Inventorying which agents were private vs workspace-invocable required raw SQL; changing scope across many agents required a bulk `UPDATE` + `INSERT` (70 agents across 5 workspaces). This PR gives operators the UI tools to answer and change any access-scope question from the list page.

## Key design decisions

- **Three-state effective access, not raw `visibility`**: `visibility` is a derived 2-state projection (`agent.ts:10-15`) that maps `public_to + member target` → "private" — indistinguishable from a truly owner-only agent. The column shows the 3-state value computed from `permission_mode + invocation_targets`.

- **Bulk action gated by `isOwnedByMe`, not `canManage`**: the backend enforces owner-only writes for `permission_mode` / `invocation_targets` (`agent.go:1418-1444`, returns 403 for non-owner admins). The bulk button and target filter use `isOwnedByMe` to match.

- **Bulk dialog reuses `AccessPicker`** (the existing per-agent editor) via `onReadyChange` which passes the actual `AccessChange` value, so the dialog's Apply button captures the scope directly. The picker's draft-reset `useEffect` uses ref-based value comparison to avoid resets from unstable prop references.

- **No backend changes**: `permission_mode` and `invocation_targets` are already present in the list payload (`ListAgents` SELECT * + handler attaches invocation_targets at `agent.go:666,680`). Effective access is computed frontend-side.

## Changes

| Area | Files | What |
|------|-------|------|
| Helper | `packages/core/agents/effective-access.ts` | `effectiveAccessScope()`, `isAccessChangeReady()`, `ALL_ACCESS_SCOPES` |
| Column | `agents-page.tsx`, `view-store.ts`, `agent-list-toolbar.tsx`, 4 locale files | New "Access" column (visible by default, after Owner), `AgentColumnKey` + grid track, `AccessCell`, i18n `columns.access` + `access_scope.*` in en/zh-Hans/ja/ko |
| Filter | `agents-page.tsx`, `agent-list-toolbar.tsx`, `view-store.ts` | New `access` multi-select filter dimension in `AgentListFilters`, toolbar sub-menu, row-filter predicate |
| Bulk edit | `agent-batch-toolbar.tsx` (extracted), `inspector/access-picker.tsx` | `AgentBatchToolbar` (archived to new file), "Set access scope" button (any-owned enables), `AccessPicker` + `hideFooter` + `onReadyChange` pattern, `api.updateAgent` per owned row via `runBatch` (allSettled, partial-failure toast) |

## Verification

- `pnpm typecheck` clean across `@multica/core` and `@multica/views`
- 161/161 tests passing across 25 files:
  - `effective-access.test.ts` (8 states: 3 normal + boundary cases)
  - `view-store.test.ts` (access filter toggle/persist/rehydrate/backfill)
  - `agents-page-access-cell.test.ts` (column renders 3 states)
  - `agents-page-filter-predicate.test.ts` (single-dim, multi-dim AND, cross-dim + drift guard)
  - `agents-page-bulk-access-dialog-state.test.ts` (isAccessChangeReady truth table)
  - `access-picker-bulk-commit.test.ts` (picker commit + onReadyChange)
  - `agent-batch-toolbar.test.ts` (button visible, skip count, default-disabled)
  - `agents-i18n-parity.test.ts` (4-locale key parity + {{count}} tokens)
- `pnpm lint` clean (0 errors)

## Scope boundaries

- **Not in scope**: the #5230 "automation cannot trigger this agent" affordance (separate bug), workspace-level default access for new agents (separate settings concern), `AccessPicker` refactoring to use the shared helper (explicitly deferred — the picker's inline derivation duplicates the same logic; consolidating is a clean follow-up).

## Source references

- Ideation: `docs/ideation/2026-07-14-agent-list-visibility-field-ideation.html`
- Plan: `docs/plans/2026-07-14-001-feat-agent-list-access-scope-plan.md`
- Upstream #5230 (related, out of scope): @agent mentions from autopilot `run_only` tasks silently dropped against private agents

author: fourcolors
body:
## What

The green (zoom) macOS traffic-light button renders as a **gray disabled dot** on non-chat Moon cards (e.g. the **Agents** panel). Red and yellow stay colored, the third looks broken. This switches every Moon window to **standard native macOS traffic lights** with all three controls enabled.

![symptom: red + yellow colored, third dot gray on the Agents panel]

## Root cause

The buttons were already the real native AppKit controls, but the zoom button was disabled by **two stacked `setEnabled(false)` paths**:

1. **tao/wry's own `create_window`** disables the `ZoomButton` whenever the window is built with `maximizable(false)`.
2. **`configure_native_window_chrome`** had `if index == 2 { button.setEnabled(zoom_enabled) }` with `zoom_enabled = desc.kind == "chat"` — so **every non-chat card** disabled it.

A disabled `NSWindow` zoom button is drawn gray, not green. (This is *not* the AppKit inactive-window tint, which would grey all three uniformly — the screenshot shows an active window with red + yellow colored, so it is the disabled-zoom case.)

## Fix

- Build every native window with `.maximizable(true)` (`spawn_panel_at` + `open_artifact_widget`).
- Remove the `zoom_enabled` parameter entirely from `configure_native_window_chrome` / `finalize_native_window_chrome` (both `cfg` variants, all internal + external call sites) and delete the `if index == 2 { setEnabled(...) }` block.
- Correct the in-code doc comment to describe the real `setEnabled` mechanism (not a style-mask bit).
- **Unchanged:** `TitleBarStyle::Overlay`, `traffic_light_position(36,12)`, `FullScreenNone` (green = in-screen zoom, never a fullscreen Space), and the reveal/reposition logic. Minimal, "for now" fix — no re-architecture of the overlay/placement machinery.

## Behavior change worth noting

Compact utility/settings panels that previously showed an inert gray dot will now **actually zoom on green-click**. `FullScreenNone` keeps that an in-screen resize, never a jump to a fullscreen Space. This is the intended consequence of "use the standard native ones."

## Tests

- `moon-native-titlebar.test.ts` gains a regression guard: no `zoom_enabled`, no `setEnabled`, no `maximizable(false)`; both builders use `maximizable(true)`. **6/6 pass.**
- Full moon suite has 8 pre-existing failures in `chat-window.test.ts` + `slash-menu.test.ts` — **verified identical on pristine `origin/master`**, unrelated to this diff.
- The macOS `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]` block cannot be compiled on the Linux CI host used here; **the macOS build in CI is the real compile gate.** Call sites/signatures were verified to match on both `cfg` paths by reading + review.

## Review

Advisor (AppKit mechanism) + auditor passes run before opening. Auditor caught a stale markdown doc (`window-drag-snap.md`), now fixed.

author: modem7
body:
## Summary
Flagged by an automated security review after #33 merged: removing `branch: master` from the `manual` event trigger meant a manual trigger against *any* branch could now reach `build-and-push` - a `privileged: true` step with Docker Hub credentials and the Slack webhook secret. Low practical risk on a single-maintainer instance, but a real trust-boundary widening worth closing.

Split `build-and-push` into two steps:
- **`build-and-push`** - unchanged behavior, now explicitly gated to `branch: master` (push or manual). The only step with secrets.
- **`build-only`** - runs for manual triggers on any other branch. `dry-run: true`, no `username`/`password`/`platforms` settings - validates the Dockerfile builds and the tag is well-formed (exactly what #33 needed to verify) without the step ever receiving registry credentials.

## Test plan
- [x] YAML validated
- [ ] Manually trigger a build on this PR's branch and confirm `build-only` runs (not `build-and-push`) and completes without needing any secrets

body:
[Jenneranalytics.com](https://jenneranalytics.com) provides an API that runs SAS code, with support for more than 200 SAS procedures. You can also use it with AI assistants in a collaborative workspace. It's available for Mac on the Apple App Store, and by license for Windows and Linux.

We support the larger community by
(1) increasing access to SAS-compatible systems,
(2) by providing test coverage and a test coverage framework to public SAS repos in order to encourage the use of best practices in software engineering.

Your Nationwide_analysis.sas runs on Jenner unmodified — this PR adds a small compatibility bundle so you can see for yourself. It's the test we wrote for your project, shared in case it's useful, and was assembled with AI assistance as is most code in modern businesses today.

What stood out reading the code is how deliberately the modeling choices are documented. `nationwide_genmod_gee_analysis.sas` doesn't just fit a GEE model — the header explains *why* GEE rather than mixed-effects (GLIMMIX and Stata `melogit` both failing to converge on 2.7M observations), so a population-averaged model with cluster-robust SEs by state is the honest fallback. And the note in `CS_QR_finalresults17_fixed_inter.sas` about SAS naming the interaction `year_centered*URRU` (continuous term first when a CLASS variable is involved) is exactly the kind of subtlety that bites people building `MODEL 3b` — good that it's written down. The stepwise 1 → 2 → 3 → 3b build across SURVEYLOGISTIC, GENMOD GEE, and the PLM-scored panel is easy to follow end to end.

The `jenner-check/` directory is self-contained: nothing outside it is referenced or modified, nothing runs on merge or checkout, and no workflow files or hooks are added. Each bundle is a copy of one of your scripts (the CSV import swapped for a small inline synthetic sample so it runs on its own), the captured log and listing from running it, and a small runner:

```
jenner-check/
├── README.md
├── run_jenner.sh
├── t001_nationwide_surveylogistic/   # Nationwide_analysis.sas — PROC SURVEYLOGISTIC, survey design
├── t002_nationwide_genmod_gee/       # nationwide_genmod_gee_analysis.sas — PROC GENMOD GEE
└── t003_panel_logistic_plm/          # sas_panel_final.sas — PROC LOGISTIC + STORE + PLM + SGPANEL
```

To run one against the hosted API, check out this PR and run from the repo root:

```bash
gh pr checkout 1
curl -sS --data-binary @jenner-check/t001_nationwide_surveylogistic/script.sas https://api.jenneranalytics.com/v1/quick
```

Or `cd jenner-check && ./run_jenner.sh --all` re-runs every bundle and verifies the pinned fields in each `expected.json`. It's free to try, no signup — full API reference: [the docs](https://docs.jenneranalytics.com/api/).

On data: the runner uploads only the SAS source text it runs (each bundle's `script.sas` plus a two-line autoexec) to api.jenneranalytics.com, which runs it and returns the log and listing. It does not read or upload any data files, so the BRFSS files sitting in `data/` never leave your machine, and nothing is sent unless you run a command yourself — only the code you run is transmitted, as when pasting a snippet into any hosted tool. The bundled scripts use a tiny synthetic sample, so the source itself carries no real data either.

Merge it, close it, or ignore it — all fine, and no response is expected. We won't open further PRs in this repository. To opt out for good, put `no-more-prs` in any comment or open an issue titled `jenner-check: opt out`.

author: jimmy-adams
body:
## Summary
This PR adds handling for 3-D packed hidden states in the DeepSeek-V4
attention forward path.
It is split out from #47972 ("Support DeepSeek-V4 AMD Quark NVFP4 with
emulation kernel", https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47972). During
review of that PR it was pointed out that this attention/MTP change is
orthogonal to the NVFP4/Quark mixed-quant work there, so it is moved here to
keep both changes focused and easier to review. #47972 has been updated to
drop this change accordingly.
## Motivation
HC/MTP passes a packed hidden-state buffer of shape
`[num_tokens, num_slots, hidden_dim]`, where slot 0 is the target token used
for attention and the remaining slots hold auxiliary (multi-token) predictions.
The attention input GEMMs and the attention op should only operate on the
target token.
## Changes
- In `DeepseekV4Attention.forward`, when `hidden_states` is 3-D, select slot 0
  (`hidden_states[:, 0, :]`) as the attention input; 2-D inputs are passed
  through unchanged.
- Use this selected tensor for both `attn_gemm_parallel_execute` and the
  attention op.
## Compatibility
Fully backward compatible: the 2-D path is unchanged and slot selection only
triggers for 3-D inputs, so there is no behavior change for existing
(non-HC/MTP) callers.
## Related
- Split out from #47972 ("Support DeepSeek-V4 AMD Quark NVFP4 with emulation
  kernel"): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47972

Adds [thermo-control-mcp](https://github.com/june4432/thermo-control-mcp) to the OS Automation section.

An MCP server that lets LLM agents monitor Mac thermals (per-die temperature sensors, fan RPM, power draw) and control fan speed on Apple Silicon (M1–M5), including the M3/M4 firmware unlock sequence. Diagnoses heat sources by process and pre-cools the machine before heavy builds or inference runs.

Safety design: fan writes go through a root daemon that enforces a TTL dead-man switch (fans revert to macOS control if the agent stops renewing), a 102°C thermal failsafe, and RPM clamping to the hardware range — the safety policy lives outside the LLM-accessible layer.

- License: MIT
- Language: TypeScript (MCP server) + Swift (daemon)
- Verified end-to-end on M4 Pro hardware

author: zuizui0223
body:
## What changed
- use a unique tempfile for every launcher and runtime JSON write
- remove the shared `.tmp.<pid>` name that collided across Streamlit reruns
- skip `_resume.json` writes when sheet/corolla/stage values did not change
- keep atomic replacement, backup fallback, lazy masks, and per-corolla snapshots

## Root cause
Streamlit can overlap reruns within the same worker process. The previous writer used the process ID as its temporary filename, so concurrent reruns opened the same file. One rerun replaced it first; the other then raised `FileNotFoundError` when attempting to replace a temporary file that no longer existed.

## Validation
- updated launcher passes Python syntax compilation
- runtime patches are guarded by exact single-match checks
- unique temporary files are created in the destination directory, preserving atomic `os.replace` semantics

author: patrick-kappen
body:
## Release

```text
v0.3.0-alpha.1 — Typed workload contracts and explicit hardening
```

Tracks #214. This PR prepares metadata and public documentation only. It does not create a tag or publish a release.

## Highlights

- generated supported Graft v1 schema tied mechanically to Rust
- fail-closed rejection of explicitly configured unsupported intent
- typed workload lifecycles and startup activation
- typed network namespace intent and dependency relationships
- qualified CDI device references
- explicit non-relaxing hardening controls
- multiple ordered configuration roots
- expanded threat model, capability policy, runtime coverage, and security gates

## Changes

- update Cargo package and lock metadata to `0.3.0-alpha.1`
- update the Nix package version to `0.3.0-alpha.1`
- replace stale release-specific `v0.2` scope wording with durable alpha wording
- document the known rootless linger `Result=protocol` compatibility limitation and focused reproducer

## Migration notes

- parser-recognised unsupported intent now fails closed with its exact TOML path
- generated-schema success represents currently supported intent only
- startup remains opt-in through `deploy.activation = "startup"`
- hardening remains explicit and non-relaxing; omission does not apply secure defaults
- CDI remains source-only without direct paths, remapping, permissions, or optional prefixes

## Known alpha limitation

With the tested Podman 5.8.2 and systemd 260.2 combination, a linger-started rootless Quadlet workload can intermittently enter `Result=protocol` during user-manager bootstrap. The generated service follows the upstream notify contract and the activation test reports the terminal result immediately. The focused reproducer passes; #212 and #129 remain open, and `activation-runtime` remains advisory.

Release validation reproduced this advisory result once on the final activation reboot. The VM was not retried and no assertion or timeout was weakened.

## Validation

Passed locally:

- Rust fmt, 181 nextest tests, doctests, clippy pedantic, cargo-machete, cargo-modules
- 80% coverage gate and LCOV generation
- schema and supported-field documentation parity
- Markdown, TOML, links, spelling, Nix formatting, statix, deadnix, mdBook
- cargo-audit, cargo-deny, gitleaks, actionlint, zizmor
- all nine explicit Nix checks, including IFD-backed checks
- `nix flake check`
- package build as `graft-0.3.0-alpha.1`
- required rootless network runtime
- focused notify protocol runtime
- CDI runtime

Advisory result:

- activation runtime: `Result=protocol` on final rootless linger restart, tracked by #212

The previously confirmed running Qdrant workload remains valid production smoke-test evidence because this branch changes only documentation and version metadata.

author: bamr87
body:
## What this is

Backlog item **DOC-021** (kind: doc, P2). A Meta-pillar deep-dive on
`scripts/ci/record_build.rb` — the 24-line script that is the single producer of
the **sev1 `build` finding**, the one severity tier `policy.rb` freezes the whole
fleet's growth on.

It's the next station in the harness deep-dive series (after the router, the
front-matter cop, the word police, the drift check, the box with no internet).
The angle: the more consequential a signal is, the fewer mouths should be allowed
to speak it — so the one signal that halts the factory gets exactly one producer,
guarded by two tripwires.

## What it covers
- The whole 24-line script and why it's a *translator* (exit code → finding), not an inspector.
- The signal chain: shell exit code → `record_build.rb` → `build.json` → `aggregate.rb` → `findings.jsonl` → triage classifies `build` → **sev1** → `policy.rb` freezes growth (`grow=0`).
- The single-source-of-truth contract: exactly one implementation, used everywhere (CI, triage, nightly, sim) instead of four drifting inline heredocs.
- What breaks if a second writer appears — and the two guards that catch it: `simulate.rb`'s *"only the build check yields sev1"* + *"record_build.rb is the canonical sev1 producer"* assertions, and `audit.rb`'s `sev1-contract` check (incl. the subtle "worst case must be the loudest, not the emptiest" early-exit forbid).
- Honest close on where the design leans on trust: the script is only as correct as the exit code handed to it — shape ≠ truth.

## Research / testing (all real, no network)
Every console block is captured from running the scripts on this repo:
- `ruby scripts/ci/record_build.rb 0` and `... 1` (empty array vs the one finding).
- `Triage.classify` on the build finding → `sev1`.
- `Fleet::Policy.decide` against the real `_data/fleet/budget.yml` with one sev1 open → `mode=sev1 grow=0 fix=2`.
- `ruby scripts/sim/simulate.rb` → 50 passed, 0 failed (the two canonical-producer assertions shown).

## Gate
Verified with the full harness (`scripts/ci/run-all.sh`): **gate PASS, 0 errors**.
The two brand-lint `just` candidates the first draft raised were reworded; the
doc is now clean of brand findings. CLI/console-only post, so no screenshot.

## Backlog
Flipped **only** DOC-021 to `status: done` + `published:` link. No other backlog edits.

### Backlog ideas
- **doc**: `aggregate.rb` — the finding that turns every check's `build.json`/`*.json` into `findings.jsonl`, stamps the line-number-free fingerprint, and computes the single gate exit code. It's referenced across the Meta docs but never gets its own deep-dive; it's the confluence where `record_build.rb`'s sev1 actually becomes the gate verdict.
- **post**: a Field Note reproducing the "worst case must be the loudest, not the emptiest" failure for real — patch `run-all.sh` to `exit 1` on build failure in a throwaway branch and show that `findings.jsonl` comes out *empty* instead of carrying the sev1, i.e. the exact bug `audit.rb`'s `sev1-contract` check forbids.

author: miyamura80
body:
## Summary

Clicking **Send** (or **Discard**) in the gmail_composer MCP App now informs the LLM. The composer's tools are `visibility: ["app"]` and app-initiated tool calls never enter the model's context, so the agent previously never learned the user sent or discarded a draft - or that they hand-edited fields after the agent's last update, causing the "I clicked send but the agent doesn't know" miscommunication.

On those two transitions (deliberately not on the debounced autosave) the iframe now calls `app.updateModelContext` (ext-apps >= 1.1, already the pinned SDK) with either the final sent draft (to/cc/bcc/subject/body + message_id, explicitly superseding earlier draft content) or a discard notice. The push is best-effort: call sites use `void pushModelContext(...)` and the helper try/catches, so a host without `ui/update-model-context` support leaves the Sent/Discarded UI untouched.

## Changes

- `types.ts`: `updateModelContext` added to `McpAppLike`.
- `modelContext.ts` (new): `sentContextText`/`discardContextText` builders for the pushed text.
- `draft.ts`: new `draftFields()` helper - canonical enumeration of the user-editable fields, shared by `persistDraft`/`onSend`/`sentContextText` (was three hand-kept copies).
- `Composer.tsx`: fire-and-forget `pushModelContext` wired into `onSend`/`onDiscardConfirm` (post-#180 refactored layout; this branch merges main and re-applies the feature onto it).
- `Composer.test.tsx` / `appContract.test.ts`: tests for the send push (carrying a hand-edited body + message_id), host-rejection resilience, the discard notice, and a contract pin of `updateModelContext` on the real ext-apps `App` class.
- `dist/mcp-app.html`: rebuilt committed bundle.
- `MCP_UI_EDGE_CASES.md`: row A7 documenting graceful degradation on hosts without `ui/update-model-context`.
- `dev_preview` harness: the fixture host now renders app-initiated model-context pushes in a panel under the widget (and on `window.__MODEL_CONTEXT__` for headless assertions) instead of silently accepting them; `gmail_composer.send` fixture returns a `message_id`.

(The branch briefly carried its own `.ts`/`.tsx` extension of `scripts/check_file_length.py`; that was superseded by #180's consolidated checker and resolved in favor of main during the merge.)

## Testing

- [x] Tests pass (`make test_fast`: 610 passed; app suite `bun run test`: 21 passed; `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean)
- [x] Linting passes (`make ci`, re-run after merging main)
- Playwright smoke test via the dev_preview fixture host: hand-edit body → Send shows "Sent ✓" and the host receives one context push containing the edited final body and message_id; Discard flow pushes the deletion notice (8/8 assertions).

## Related Issues

None - originated from a UX miscommunication report (agent unaware of user-initiated Send in the MCP App).

author: m0lte
body:
The first write surface on the rig arc, deliberately narrow: set frequency (QSY) and set mode — no keying (PTT stays reserved for a future admin-scoped tune-button design).

## REST (`PdnRigsApi`)

- `POST /api/v1/ports/{id}/rig/frequency` + `/mode` — **operate**-scoped (a retune emits no RF), audit-logged (`rig_set_frequency`/`rig_set_mode`), capability-gated against the rig's advertised `RigCapabilities` (an unadvertised set is refused without touching the rig), run under the host's exclusive gate so a write can't race a port teardown.
- Error taxonomy: 400 bad input · 404 no such port · 409 configured-but-not-attached / capability absent / rig refused or faulted (transient — the backends re-dial).
- Each success returns the **read-back** value and wakes the poller: new `IRigStatusMonitor.RequestRefresh()` (the poll delay now carries a per-cycle wake token), so the `event: rig` SSE feed shows the new dial immediately instead of at the next cadence boundary.

## MCP

`get_rig_status` + `set_rig_frequency` / `set_rig_mode` on the `INodeMcpBackend` seam: mirror `McpRigStatus` record in `Packet.Mcp` (meters flattened; Packet.Mcp can't reference Packet.Rig), operate step-up via the existing `RequireOperate()` discipline, live backend through `RunExclusiveAsync` + audit + poller wake (an exact twin of the REST guard chain), stdio/REST bridge backend through the endpoints above with `{error}` bodies surfaced verbatim.

## Web UI

Operate-gated **Tune** control on the rig card: modal with MHz-or-Hz frequency entry (parsed preview), mode select; applies only changed fields; the SSE tick refreshes the card — no client re-fetch.

## Guardrails note

Frequency validation is sanity-only (positive Hz) — band-plan validation lands with the channel-plan/QSY-policy slice, where a wrong-band QSY actually becomes reachable from automation.

## Gates (local, per the working pattern)

- `dotnet build` clean (warnings-as-errors)
- Full default suite `Category!=HardwareLoop&Category!=Interop`: green across all projects (one unrelated Tailscale sidecar SIGHUP test flaked under full-suite load, passes in isolation in 189 ms)
- `Packet.Mcp.Tests` 40/40; node rig tests 62/62; `RigMutationApiTests` 4/4
- Web: `npm run build` + `npm run test` (120 tests) green

Plan §17 amendment ("Rig mutation slice") is in this PR (a0107b7). No ax25-ts parity leg needed — no `Ax25ParseOptions`/session-quirk/listener change.
