author: kaeawc
body:
## What

Adds three `always()` roll-up **gate jobs** to `pull_request.yml` that report **stable context names**, so the deterministic iOS build legs, CodeQL scan, and BATS shell tests can be promoted to **required** status checks:

- **iOS Build** — rolls up `ios-swift-packages` + `ios-xcode-build`, deliberately **excluding** the simulator-flaky `ios-xctest-runner-simulator-tests` (that stays covered by the existing non-required `iOS` gate).
- **CodeQL** — rolls up `codeql-node` (per-language matrix).
- **Shell Tests** — rolls up `bats-tests` (OS matrix).

Each gate follows the same *structure* as the existing `iOS` / `Android` / `IDE Plugin` gates: `if: always() && auto_chore != 'true'`, fails only on `failure`/`cancelled`, passes on `success`/`skipped`. (Note: those existing gates are **not** currently required — this PR introduces the first gates intended to be required, so the required-check behavior is new to the repo, though it matches how already-required matrix checks like `Installer Development (*)` behave when skipped.)

## Why

These checks are always green but weren't required. They couldn't be required directly because of a **matrix-skip footgun**: when a matrix job is gated out, the matrix never expands and the check reports its **literal** `(${{ ... }})` context name instead of the expanded one (e.g. `Build Xcode Projects (${{ matrix.config.name }})` vs `Build Xcode Projects (Xcode 26.5)`). Requiring the expanded name would leave the check permanently *Expected* → **blocking merges** on any PR where the family doesn't run. A non-matrix `always()` gate reports one stable name in every path (runs, gated-out, sha256/docs/auto_chore), which is safe to require.

Companion change (already applied to the `green-main` ruleset): 7 non-matrix always-green checks were made required — `Bun Security Audit`, `Memory Leak Detection`, `SwiftLint`, `Swift Code Coverage`, `Build Root SPM Package`, `Build CtrlProxy APK`, `JUnit Runner Kotlin Consumer Compatibility`.

## Review follow-ups included in this PR

- **Drift guard** — `test/bats/pr-gate-wiring.bats` (mirrors `release-workflow-wiring.bats`) pins each required gate's `needs` and asserts the flaky simulator leg stays out of `iOS Build`. Since required-checks config lives in GitHub's ruleset API (no in-repo source of truth), a renamed/dropped rolled-up job would otherwise silently turn a required check into a false-green; now it fails Fast Validation (via the required `Shell Tests` gate) instead.
- **De-dup** — `ios-gate` now depends on `ios-build-gate` rather than re-listing `ios-swift-packages`/`ios-xcode-build`, so iOS build-leg membership is declared in exactly one place. A comment documents the required-subset (`iOS Build`) vs non-required-superset (`iOS`) split.

## Reviewer notes / follow-up (post-merge)

1. **After this merges**, add `iOS Build`, `CodeQL`, and `Shell Tests` to the `green-main` ruleset's required status checks. Doing it before merge would hang open PRs that lack the new gates.
2. **Then rebase any already-open PRs** onto post-merge main — until rebased, they will show the three new required contexts as *Expected* (blocked), since their base doesn't contain the gate jobs. Inherent to adding any new required check.
3. `Build Desktop App (*)` is still un-required (same matrix-skip footgun); its unit tests are already required. A `Desktop App Build` gate can be added for parity if wanted.
4. Fork-PR note: `ios-swift-packages`/`ios-xcode-build` run unsigned on forks (empty signing secrets). Confirm a recent fork PR's legs go green unsigned before relying on `iOS Build` as required for external contributors.
5. Pre-existing actionlint warnings in this file (`background:`/`wait:` parallel-steps syntax, composite-action metadata) are unrelated to this change and untouched.

author: missymagic
body:
## Summary

User report: Missy sometimes "misresponds" to a later prompt in a session. Root cause pattern: a tool-free response asserts something false (*"I checked the logs, everything looks fine"*) or promises an action it never takes (*"Working on it..."*) with zero tool calls behind it — the false/unfulfilled claim then becomes part of the conversation history a later turn builds on, producing an inconsistent or confusing reply once the gap surfaces.

Adapted from feedback shared from a comparable system's own two-detector design (fabrication pattern matching + promise-without-action pattern matching, both gated on zero tool calls, each retried once with a corrective nudge) — reimplemented for Missy's own conventions rather than copied verbatim, and wired into the existing retry-on-"stop" machinery in `AgentRuntime._tool_loop()` (same bounded-single-retry + audit-event shape as the existing placeholder-artifact and observation-fabrication guards already there).

## What changed

`missy/agent/response_guards.py` (new):
- `detect_fabrication()` — flags claims of already having run/checked/reviewed something, fake shell-output-shaped code blocks, claims of a produced artifact, or references to "the logs/metrics" — only when no tool was actually called this task.
- `detect_promise_without_action()` — flags "I'll.../I'm .../I will..." and leading "Working on it/On it/Generating/..." acknowledgments with no tool call behind them, with an explicit exemption list for ordinary conversational future tense ("I'll be here if you need anything") that isn't an action promise.

Both are broader and request-agnostic compared to the existing observation-specific check (vision/memory requests only) and the placeholder check (exact internal artifact strings) — tried first in the "stop" branch since they cover more ground; the narrower checks remain as additional nets for anything these miss.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q` — 21,754 passed, 18 skipped, 2 failed (both pre-existing/environmental — a live `missy gateway start` process, not caused by this branch)
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` — clean
- [x] 33 new tests: both detectors' true-positive/true-negative cases (including the promise exemption list), and end-to-end wiring tests in the tool loop proving each guard retries exactly once, never fires when a real tool was called, and never fires on ordinary replies

author: yfshaikh
body:
## Summary
- Add `pixel_to_world` to `frame_tf_service` (srv flag + client + optional pixel overlay).
- Fix `world_to_pixel` (correct camera-frame projection, TF handling, and float64 serialization).
- A pixel `(u, v)` alone is underdetermined: with camera pose it defines a ray, so we need depth.
- Depth source: project the latest LiDAR cloud into the image and associate the nearest return within a pixel radius; return that point in `map`.

### Conventions
Camera optical frame: `+X` right, `+Y` down, `+Z` forward.  
Intrinsics from `CameraInfo.k`: `fx, fy, cx, cy`.

### Algorithm — `pixel_to_world`
1. Parse LiDAR XYZ; TF cloud → camera frame and → `map`.
2. Drop `z_c <= 0` / off-image projections.
3. Project: `u = fx·x_c/z_c + cx`, `v = fy·y_c/z_c + cy`.
4. Pick nearest `(u,v)` within `MAX_PIXEL_RADIUS` (tie-break by smaller `z_c`).
5. Return that return’s map XYZ (`float64` bytes), or `tf_success=false` if none.

Note: this returns a measured LiDAR point near the query pixel (nearby-ray association), not an exact intersection of the query ray with a surface.

### Algorithm — `world_to_pixel`
1. Load `CameraInfo` for `camera_name`; use `header.frame_id` as the camera frame.
2. TF the map point into the camera: `p_cam = R · P_map + t` (`lookup_transform(camera, map, …)`).
3. Reject non-finite points or points behind the camera (`z_c <= 0`).
4. Project: `u = fx·x_c/z_c + cx`, `v = fy·y_c/z_c + cy`.
5. Return `(u, v)` as `float64` bytes, or `tf_success=false` on failure.

Fixes vs the starter code: one TF lookup (no hang loop), project `p_cam` (not raw map XYZ), `Rm.apply(...)` for the rigid transform, stamp `0/0` → latest TF, and `np.asarray([u,v], float64).tobytes()` instead of `bytes(coords)`.

### Camera name → RViz image topic (this stack)
| `camera_name` | Image topic |
|---|---|
| `rgb_front` | `/cameras/camera0` |
| `rgb_right` | `/cameras/camera1` |
| `rgb_back` | `/cameras/camera2` |
| `rgb_left` | `/cameras/camera3` |

`rgb_center` may have **0 publishers** — use `rgb_front` for the main camera.

---

## Test plan — `pixel_to_world`

Requires CARLA + `carla_interface` / bridge + navigator (`launch.carla.py`), same `ROS_DOMAIN_ID`.

### 1. Build
```bash
# inside navigator_carla
cd /navigator
colcon build --symlink-install --packages-select frame_tf_serv frame_tf_service frame_tf_client
source /navigator/install/setup.bash
```

### 2. Confirm sensors
```bash
ros2 topic hz /lidar
ros2 topic hz /carla/hero/rgb_front/camera_info
ros2 topic echo /carla/hero/rgb_front/camera_info --once   # width/height/frame_id (e.g. 800x600, hero/rgb_front)
```

### 3. Start service and wait for data
```bash
# terminal A
ros2 run frame_tf_service service
```

Wait until logs show CameraInfo + LiDAR ready (status should move off `NO`). **Do not call the client before that.**

Sensor subscriptions use Best Effort (and Reliable fallback); without matching QoS the node stays at `No CameraInfo yet`.

### 4. Basic client checks
```bash
# terminal B — ground/center-ish pixel (800x600 → try 400,350)
ros2 run frame_tf_client client 0 0 0 1 rgb_front 400.0 350.0 0.0
# expect: (True, array([X, Y, Z]))

# sky / top of image
ros2 run frame_tf_client client 0 0 0 1 rgb_front 400.0 5.0 0.0
# expect: (False, array([]))
```

Client args:  
`cam_to_world cam_to_pixel world_to_pixel pixel_to_world camera_name x y z`  
For `pixel_to_world`, `x,y` = `u,v`.

### 5. Visual check (overlay + map marker)
```bash
# mark the query pixel on the camera image
ros2 run frame_tf_client overlay 400 350 rgb_front
```

In RViz:
- **Add → Image**, topic `/pixel_query_overlay` (red crosshair = queried pixel)
- Fixed Frame: `map`
- PointCloud2 on `/lidar` (Reliability: Best Effort if the display shows 0 msgs)

Drop the returned XYZ as a marker:
```bash
ros2 topic pub --once /pixel_to_world_debug visualization_msgs/msg/Marker "{
  header: {frame_id: 'map'},
  ns: 'p2w', id: 0, type: 2, action: 0,
  pose: {position: {x: X, y: Y, z: Z}, orientation: {w: 1.0}},
  scale: {x: 1.5, y: 1.5, z: 1.5},
  color: {r: 1.0, g: 0.2, b: 0.2, a: 1.0}
}"
```

**Add → Marker**, topic `/pixel_to_world_debug`.

Pass criteria: crosshair sits on a surface in the image (e.g. road); red sphere sits on that same surface in the map/LiDAR view. The sphere is 3D — it will not appear on the image.

### 6. Other cameras
```bash
ros2 run frame_tf_client overlay 400 350 rgb_left
ros2 run frame_tf_client client 0 0 0 1 rgb_left 400.0 350.0 0.0
# optional: new marker with id: 1
```

Side cameras may return `false` more often (fewer LiDAR hits in view).

### Checklist
- [ ] Build + source succeeds
- [ ] `/lidar` + `/carla/hero/rgb_front/camera_info` publishing
- [ ] Service receives CameraInfo + cloud before client calls
- [ ] Ground pixel → `tf_success: true`
- [ ] Sky pixel → `tf_success: false`
- [ ] Overlay crosshair + map marker agree visually
- [ ] Optional: `rgb_left` / `rgb_right` / `rgb_back`

---

## Test plan — `world_to_pixel`

### Idea
Given a map XYZ known to be in front of the camera, project it to image pixels and confirm `(u, v)` land on the expected feature.

### Smoke checks
```bash
# Use a map point from pixel_to_world (or any known in-view map XYZ)
ros2 run frame_tf_client client 0 0 1 0 rgb_front X Y Z
# expect: (True, array([u, v]))
```

Client args:  
`cam_to_world cam_to_pixel world_to_pixel pixel_to_world camera_name x y z`  
For `world_to_pixel`, `x,y,z` = map XYZ.

Behind-camera / bad TF should return `tf_success: false` without hanging.

### Checklist
- [ ] `world_to_pixel` returns without hanging
- [ ] In-view map point → `tf_success: true` and two floats `(u, v)`
- [ ] Point clearly behind the camera / invalid → `tf_success: false`

---

## Test plan — consistency (`pixel_to_world` ↔ `world_to_pixel`)

These two services are inverses in intent but not bit-exact inverses: `pixel_to_world` returns a nearby LiDAR return, not the exact ray–surface intersection. A few pixels of round-trip error is expected and OK.

### Round-trip: pixel → world → pixel
1. Query a ground/center-ish pixel.
2. Feed the returned map XYZ into `world_to_pixel`.
3. Compare recovered `(u', v')` to the original `(u, v)`.

```bash
# 1) pixel → world
ros2 run frame_tf_client client 0 0 0 1 rgb_front 400.0 350.0 0.0
# save X Y Z from the result, e.g. (48.97, -306.66, 0.22)

# 2) world → pixel
ros2 run frame_tf_client client 0 0 1 0 rgb_front X Y Z
# expect u'≈400, v'≈350 (a few px of error is OK)

# 3) visual: overlay the recovered pixel
ros2 run frame_tf_client overlay <u'> <v'> rgb_front
```

**Pass criteria**
- Round-trip succeeds (`tf_success: true` both ways).
- `|u'−u|` and `|v'−v|` are small (typically within a few pixels; association radius / depth discreteness set the floor).
- Overlay of `(u', v')` sits on the same scene feature as the original query (e.g. same road patch).

### Optional: world → pixel → world (sanity)
If you start from a known map point that is a LiDAR return visible in the camera, `world_to_pixel` then `pixel_to_world` should land near that same 3D location (meters, not necessarily exact — NN association again).

```bash
ros2 run frame_tf_client client 0 0 1 0 rgb_front X Y Z
# → u v
ros2 run frame_tf_client client 0 0 0 1 rgb_front u v 0.0
# → X' Y' Z' near X Y Z in map
```

### Checklist
- [ ] `pixel_to_world(u,v)` → map XYZ succeeds
- [ ] `world_to_pixel(XYZ)` → `(u',v')` succeeds
- [ ] `(u',v')` within a few px of `(u,v)`
- [ ] Overlay of `(u',v')` matches the same image feature as `(u,v)`
- [ ] Optional: world → pixel → world stays near the original map point

author: ironsail-philip
body:
Follows #205. `ROBOTHOR_SANDBOX_DEFAULT_MODE` was scheduled to promote to `enforce` on 07-16 — onto infrastructure that does not exist. #205 pushed the date; this builds the thing.

## The sandbox was decoration

Three independent reasons, any one of which is fatal:

**1. `exec` never consulted it.** `tools/handlers/filesystem.py` called `subprocess.run(command, shell=True, cwd=ctx.workspace)` unconditionally and never called `get_current_sandbox()`. An agent configured `sandbox: docker` still ran every shell command **on the host, as the engine user**. Only `browser.py` and `desktop.py` routed into the container — and none of the would-be-sandboxed agents use browser or desktop tools. The flag said *contained*; the command ran on the host.

**2. The container could not see the repo.** `docker run` passed **no `-v` at all**. Every `exec` inside it would have landed in an empty filesystem.

**3. The container was not a boundary.** No `--network` (Docker default bridge = full outbound internet **and** every host service on the gateway — postgres, the bridge API), no `--cap-drop`, no `--user` (root in-container), no `--pids-limit`.

And the image itself had **no `git` and no `python`** — so an `auto-agent` run, whose entire job is executing the test suite, would have failed on its first command. `infra/sandbox/Dockerfile` has existed for months and **nothing ever built it**.

## What this does

- **Routes `exec` through `sandbox.exec_shell()`**, which wraps the command in `sh -c` — agents' real commands are shell strings full of pipes, redirects and heredocs, so splitting them would break everything. **Fails closed**: a broken container surfaces an error instead of quietly running the command on the host (the #201 rule).
- **Mounts the workspace** at `/workspace` and sets `--workdir`.
- **Makes it a boundary**: `--cap-drop=ALL`, `--security-opt no-new-privileges`, `--pids-limit`, `--user <uid>:<gid>`, and `--network` defaulting to **`none`** — deny by default. Browser agents opt in explicitly with `ROBOTHOR_SANDBOX_NETWORK=bridge`.
- **Parameterizes the runtime.** `\"docker\"` was hardcoded in four places. `ROBOTHOR_SANDBOX_BINARY` (default `docker`) unblocks **rootless podman**, which removes the root-equivalent daemon socket entirely — you cannot fix this by adding the engine user to the `docker` group, because that group *is* root.
- **Builds the image**, with `git`/`python3`/`curl`/`jq`/`psql`, and a build script that **probes** it (runs the tools) rather than trusting a successful build.

## Not yet flipped

`SANDBOX_DEFAULT_MODE` stays where #205 left it. Promotion is gated on a real probe — an `auto-agent` run that *actually executes inside the container* — not on a date and not on an empty events table.

## Test

13 new tests pin the routing, the mount, each isolation flag, the shell semantics, fail-closed behaviour, and the runtime override. Full engine suite green (`3171 passed`); the two remaining failures (`test_outcome_feedback`, `test_channel_bus_crm`) reproduce on unmodified `main`.

# Summary

Connects stateful CDP pages to the existing verified replay executor. `BrowserToolCaller` dispatches deterministic browser tools, captures the resulting page into the executor's observation convention, and lets the existing per-step expects/final verify gate control success.

**Milestone:** P1 / V1 — warm verified replay
**Exit-gate criterion advanced:** Establishes the zero-LLM warm path for stateful B1/B2 through real local Chrome while preserving executor verification and recording.

## Changes

- Add `BrowserToolCaller` implementing the executor `ToolCaller` boundary.
- Support:
  - `browser.navigate`
  - `browser.fill`
  - `browser.select`
  - `browser.click`

author: jamesbarge
body:
## What

Coverage plan **Phase 2b, Track A PR 1**: extract a shared Savoy Systems **modern-JSON** client (`platforms/savoy.ts`) from `rio.ts`, migrate Rio onto it, and fold in Rio's empty-success **P0 fix**. Sets up the Lexi migration + the Arzner direct scraper (next PRs).

## Research finding that reshaped Phase 2b

Savoy Systems ships **two** front-ends and the handoff plan conflated them:
- **Modern JSON** (`var Events` blob) → **Rio, Lexi, The Arzner**.
- **Legacy HTML-table** (`div.programme`, no `var Events`) → **Ciné Lumière, ArtHouse** — need a *separate* table parser, NOT this client.

Playbook mislabels fixed (verified live): **Lexi is Savoy, not "Admit One"**; **the Arzner is Savoy (`TheArzner.dll`), not "Jacro"** (direct scraper is trivial — the biggest 2b coverage win); **Castle is Wagtail+Admit One, not Jacro**.

## Changes

- **`platforms/savoy.ts`** (new): `extractSavoyEventsJson` (brace-matched, **throws** on missing/unbalanced) + `parseSavoyEvents` (UK-local HHMM via `combineDateAndTime`, festival detect, optional `filmTypeOnly`). Per-venue `buildSourceId`/`buildBookingUrl`.
- **`rio.ts`**: `parsePages` delegates to `parseSavoyEvents`; still `extends BaseScraper`. sourceId + booking URL preserved exactly → no reconcile. **P0 fixed** — a missing/malformed `var Events` now fails the run (via BaseScraper) instead of returning `[]` as silent empty-success.
- **`savoy.test.ts`** (new): mapping, BST→UTC, past-drop, `filmTypeOnly` (drop-explicit-non-Film + keep-on-absent + off-for-Rio), nested-brace extraction, and all three throw paths (missing / invalid / truncated).

## Verification

- Fixture smokes (tsx): all pass, incl. the truncated-blob `/unbalanced/` throw + both `filmTypeOnly` branches.
- **Live** Rio scrape via the real scraper (`scrape()`, fetch+parse, no DB write): **57 future screenings**, `rio-dalston-{id}-{ISO}` sourceIds, `Rio.dll/WhatsOn?f={id}` booking — behaviour preserved.
- eslint clean; `tsc --noEmit` clean. CI is the authoritative gate for the unit suite.
- code-reviewer agent: no blockers; confirmed behaviour-identical + P0 fix; its three test-coverage suggestions applied + a forward-looking `filmTypeOnly` TODO for the Lexi/Arzner PRs.

Part of the coverage-expansion plan (Phase 2b, Track A).

## Motivation / Problem

Multi character literals and byte-swaps when the concept of `Label` is available.


## Description

Use the `Label` concept for the NodeIDs of Action14.

Use `AsString` for unknown tags, which will show 4 ASCII characters when all 4 are printable (and not a space), or the normal 8-character hex-string there is something unprintable.


## Limitations

There are more NewGRF things that could use `Label`, but those are for a future PR.


## Checklist for review

Some things are not automated, and forgotten often. This list is a reminder for the reviewers.
* The bug fix is important enough to be backported? (label: 'backport requested')
* This PR touches english.txt or translations? Check the [guidelines](https://github.com/OpenTTD/OpenTTD/blob/master/docs/eints.md)
* This PR affects the GS/AI API? (label 'needs review: Script API')
    * ai_changelog.hpp, game_changelog.hpp need updating.

author: metalmmagic
body:
Closes out the remaining items from the production embedded/iframe deployment feedback. Each was verified against `main` before being written. (C1 shipped in #174; C5 was already fixed on main in #136.)

## C2 — Cross-origin embedding: possible, explicitly opt-in, never by default

Portal-style embedding was **documented but could not work**: `frame-ancestors 'self'` blocked cross-origin iframing outright, and the `ythril:theme` postMessage handler dropped any message whose origin wasn't Ythril's own — i.e. exactly the embedder the feature was designed for.

Operators can now list trusted origins in `config.json`:

```json
{ "embed": { "allowedOrigins": ["https://portal.example.com"] } }
```

A listed origin gets **both** rights together, because they're one trust decision: it may **iframe** Ythril (appended to CSP `frame-ancestors`) **and** push runtime theme tokens.

**Security — fails closed, and the integrator explicitly accepts the risk:**
- With no allowlist, behaviour is **unchanged**: same-origin only.
- **Wildcards are never accepted** — there is no allow-everything mode.
- Exact scheme-qualified origins only: no path / query / fragment / credentials.
- `https:` required (except `localhost` / `127.0.0.1` for dev).
- Invalid entries are dropped with a warning; the resolved list is **logged at startup** so granted rights are visible.

Framing is a clickjacking primitive and theming can spoof UI — hence the deliberate opt-in.

## C3 — Embedded (chrome-less) mode

`?embedded=1` hides the shell topbar, whose logo + **Sign out** duplicate the host's chrome (and whose Sign out misleadingly ends only the Ythril session). Navigation is unaffected — it's in the sidebar. Replaces the customer's brittle `.topbar { display:none }` CSS workaround.

The flag is read **once and cached**: Angular drops unknown query params on navigation, which would otherwise kick the app out of embedded mode on the first route change.

## C4 — Brain Semantic Search exposes the full recall API

The form offered only query / topK / minScore while `recall()` also supports type restriction, per-type minimums, tags, and structured filters — the UI was strictly less capable than the API behind it. Adds a **More options** section: type restriction (checkboxes), **per-type minimums**, tags, and a JSON **filter** (validated client-side so a typo is a form error, not a 400).

Notably `minPerType` and `tags` were supported by the engine but **hardcoded to `undefined` in the REST route** (reachable only via MCP). They're now plumbed through `POST /api/brain/spaces/:spaceId/recall`, with `minPerType` clamped to `topK`.

## C6 — Docs

The embedded-fields table listed **chrono *and* edge** without `properties` — stale since the B4 fix. Corrected, plus a note that pre-existing records need a reindex (`POST /api/brain/spaces/:id/reindex`) to benefit.

## Also: fixes a build bug introduced by #173

Tagging every instance `ythril-test:latest` made `docker compose build` build the **same tag from four services concurrently**, racing on the image export and corrupting it locally (`failed to extract layer … EOF`). Only `ythril-a` builds it now; b/c/d reference the tag. CI is unaffected (it pre-builds the tag itself).

`test:up:rebuild` also gained a `test:prune` step: every `--build` was leaving an orphaned multi-GB image behind and growing the build cache without bound — it had reached **35 GB**.

## Tests

- New `testing/standalone/embed-origins.test.js` pins the origin validator (wildcards rejected, https-only, exact origins, no credentials, junk schemes) and the default CSP.
- Full core suite green: **integration 822, standalone 753, redteam 258, sync 173 — 0 failures.**

author: agrawal-nikita
body:
Adds a GPU-side Automatic Prefix Cache to the vLLM worker, letting content-identical KV blocks be shared across concurrent requests instead of recomputed, with a pluggable eviction policy. On a cache hit the matched prefix blocks are attached and the request goes straight to READY, skipping prefill for those tokens. Evicted prefixes are written through to a lower KVC tier (CPU/DFS) rather than discarded. 

The feature is split into three collaborators with clean ownership boundaries:

- **opal/apc_policy.py**: BaseAPCPolicy interface + LRUPolicy. Manages only the identity of which block hashes are cached and eviction order; ref-counts pinned (in-use) blocks out of the eviction queue so evict() is O(victims) rather than O(resident). Optional TTL keeps recently-touched blocks immune from eviction. Also houses the sharing-aware block resolution (resolve_apc_blocks / commit_apc_blocks).

- **opal/gpu_apc.py**: GpuApc, the cache-mechanics collaborator (policy + block-granularity token DB + block→source map + lookup/commit/evict). Deliberately knows nothing about worker scheduling; mutating methods return capacity deltas rather than reaching into worker state.

- **opal/vllm_worker.py**: orchestrates: keeps free_gpu_blocks accounting and KVC tier write-through, drives resolve → evict-if-short → commit, and prefers an APC hit over a tiered hit when tied (no I/O required).

@animeshtrivedi @raduioanstoica 

**Changes**

**New**
- opal/apc_policy.py: policy interface, LRUPolicy, block resolution/commit
- opal/gpu_apc.py: GpuApc cache-mechanics collaborator
- configs/defaults_apc.json: example config with APC enabled

**Modified**
- opal/vllm_worker.py: APC admit/evict/lookup integration into scheduling
- opal/kvc_manager.py: Per-tier KVC hit-token tracking
- opal/request.py: Per-request APC fields (owned hashes, chain hash, resolved tokens)

**Config**

Enabled via worker.vllm_params:

```
"enable_gpu_apc": true,
"apc_eviction_policy": "lru",
"apc_lru_ttl": 0.0
```

author: allenheltondev
body:
## What & why

Rewrites the Python/Strands AgentCore chatbot in **Node/TypeScript**, following the `readysetcloud/newsletter-service` and `content-tracking` paradigms, and restructures the repo into an **npm-workspaces monorepo** so the reusable pieces lift cleanly into `readysetcloud/rsc-core`. AgentCore Runtime and the browser-direct SigV4 WebSocket transport are kept; the agent, memory, and frontend are rebuilt.

## What changed

- **`packages/agent`** (`@readysetcloud/agent`) — portable, framework-agnostic agent core on **Strands-TS**:
  - `DynamoSnapshotStorage` implementing Strands' `SnapshotStorage` port (replaces AgentCore Memory for conversation continuity)
  - S3-Vectors **semantic memory** + a `recall_memory` tool (replaces the Python `memory` tool)
  - `stream.ts` normalizes `agent.stream()` events into the **original wire protocol** (frontend contract preserved)
  - Strands-free `@readysetcloud/agent/memory` subpath so Lambda consumers don't bundle the SDK
- **`packages/ui`** (`@readysetcloud/ui-chat`) — `Chat`/`ChatMessage`, the `useAgentChat` hook (merges the old context + service + component), and a framework-agnostic `WebSocketChatClient`. Styled with the `@readysetcloud/ui` tailwind-preset tokens; destined to merge into `@readysetcloud/ui`.
- **`example/backend`** — SAM app: TypeScript **AgentCore Runtime artifact (NODE_22)**, conventionized `websocket-connect` (SigV4 presign) + `vectorize-turn` DDB-stream consumer, single table + stream, S3 Vectors, Cognito. **Drops** AgentCore Memory, Step Functions, and the legacy `/query` path.
- **`example/frontend`** — Vite/React app consuming both packages plus the real published `@readysetcloud/ui` for auth/shell.
- CI (lint/typecheck/test/build gate) + deploy workflow, `scripts/package-agent.mjs`, and docs (README, MIGRATION.md, RSC_CORE_HANDOFF.md).

## Reviewer notes

- **Guardrails for SDK churn**: `@strands-agents/sdk` (1.9.0) and `bedrock-agentcore` (0.4.0) are pinned exact. `packages/agent/src/stream.contract.test.ts` constructs **real** SDK event instances and type-binds fixtures via `satisfies`, enforced by a CI typecheck — an SDK bump that changes the streaming contract fails CI loudly and points at `stream.ts` (the single coupling point).
- **Verified locally**: build, lint, and typecheck clean across all 5 workspaces; **22 unit tests pass**; `sam validate` passes; frontend builds; the agent artifact bundles and packages.
- **Not checkable without live AWS** (see MIGRATION.md): the `AWS::BedrockAgentCore::Runtime` `EntryPoint: index.js` literal (cfn-lint's spec doesn't yet know `NODE_22`), and the end-to-end presigned-socket stream / multi-turn continuity / cross-session recall.
- The old `backend/`, `frontend/`, Python agent, and stale `.agents/` task history are intentionally removed (superseded by the monorepo).
- **`RSC_CORE_HANDOFF.md`** is written for the follow-on agent in rsc-core: inherited API surface, ordered integration tasks, contracts to preserve, and gotchas.

body: #### What type of PR is this? /kind feature #### What this PR does / why we need it: Ready Sessions currently expose only their infrastructure phase, so users cannot tell whether an agent is actively running a turn or waiting for input. ## Summary

Captain ability audit of the `percent_damage` filter via `/optc-captain-ability-audit` (OPTC-DB `details.js` + local seed cross-reference, all-sources diff, adversarial internet verification).

**Current LOCAL detection is already correct** — all 33 `captainAbility` matches and all 410 total matches are the genuine `"Deals N% of enemies' current HP in [True] damage to all/one enem(y/ies)"` wording. Zero false positives (0 of 464 matched sentences are HP-threshold conditions like *"if HP is above 50% of MAX HP"* or heals), zero local misses.

Two matcher issues surfaced against **live upstream**:
- The 2nd alternative `/\bcuts?\b … HP … by N%/` is **dead** — `"cuts … HP by N%"` appears nowhere in OPTC-DB crew ability text; the only "cut … HP" text is the **self** HP-cost `"Cutting special, reduces crew's current HP by N%"` (must NOT be tagged as percent damage).
- A real upstream wording is **missed**: `"Reduces (one) enem(y's|ies') HP by N% [(ignoring all defensive effects)]"` — **Law - Finger-Controlled Boulder #4185**, whose upstream special text moved off the older `"Deals N% of enemies' current HP in True damage …"` form. **No LOCAL dataset delta today** (the local seed still ships #4185's old wording) → catalog semantic diff = byte-identical; the change is a forward-looking matcher-completeness fix + dead-code removal, locked in by regression tests.

author: dm2book
body:
The third requested feature: an abandoned-cart reminder.

## What
Signed-in shoppers' carts are now mirrored server-side, and **one** gentle "you left items behind" email goes out if a cart sits idle without an order.

## Details
- Migration **020** adds `saved_carts` (user_id, items, updated_at, reminded_at).
- **CartContext** mirrors the cart to `/api/account/cart` (debounced) while signed in, and **restores** the saved cart on login when the local cart is empty — so a cart follows the shopper across devices. Guests stay purely local.
- **`sendCartReminders`** (runs from the maintenance pass): reminds a cart that has items, is idle **> 4h** (and < 14 days), has **no order placed since it changed**, and hasn't already been reminded for this version. `reminded_at` is claimed atomically; a later cart change re-arms a new reminder. New `cart_reminder` email template auto-installs via `syncEmailTemplates`; the buyer also gets an in-app notification.

## Verification
Real-Postgres e2e (10 checks): idle cart → exactly one reminder, logged + stamped; a second run and a fresh (<4h) cart send nothing; a customer who ordered gets no reminder; changing the cart re-arms one; an emptied cart never triggers one. Regression suite (19) + build green.

---
This completes the batch of three: honest "almost sold out" (#92), custom Forge Shop discount codes (#93), and abandoned-cart recovery (this one).

author: rjamul-elnora-ai
body:
Two batches of the CLI/MCP API-coverage plan, combined into one release.

## Part A — repoint folder mutation to the Knowledge Base

`folders create/rename/move/delete` targeted the **deprecated project-scoped controller**. They now default to the **KB** (the current model, same tree as `folders roots`/`children` + sharing), with legacy behind an escape hatch.

| Command | Default (KB) | Legacy escape |
|---|---|---|
| `folders create --name X` | `POST /folders` | `--project <id>` → project folder |
| `folders rename <id> --name X` | `PATCH /folders/{id}` | `--legacy` → PUT |
| `folders move <id> <parent\|root>` | `PATCH /folders/{id}/move` (root → `{moveToRoot}`) | `--legacy` → PUT |
| `folders delete <id>` | `POST /folders/{id}/archive` | `--legacy` → hard DELETE |

### ⚠️ Behaviour change
- **`folders create` no longer takes a positional `<PROJECT_ID>`** — use `--project <id>` for a legacy project folder.
- rename/move/delete act on **KB folders by default** (`--legacy` for the old ones); `delete` **archives** a KB folder.
- `folders list <PROJECT_ID>` stays legacy — use `folders roots`/`children` for the KB.
- Fixes the folder body field name (`parentFolderId`, was `parentId` — silently ignored).

## Part B — review queue, auto-tidy & task lifecycle

- New `review` group — `review list` / `approve` / `reject` (KB review queue) + the `elnora-review` skill.
- `orgs set-autotidy <org> [--enabled]` — toggle KB auto-tidy.
- `tasks unarchive <id>`, `tasks attachments <id>`, `tasks attachment-content <id> <aid>`; `tasks list --status <active|archived|all>`.

## Testing
- `pnpm typecheck` / `pnpm lint` clean, `pnpm test` — 724 passing
- `pnpm audit:mcp-parity` — **109/109**, 0 mismatches
- Independent code review (approved); verified end-to-end against a local backend (both folder paths, review list, autotidy on/off, task archive→unarchive round-trip)

## Merge order
The MCP-parity check compares against `elnora-mcp-server@main` and stays red until the paired MCP PR merges — please merge that one first, then re-run this check.

author: giladresisi
body:
## Problem

Production logs show, for every Pinterest post:

```
Error fetching Pinterest post analytics: ApplicationFailure: Unknown Error
```

with Pinterest's underlying message: **"You can only get data from the last 90 days."**

Pinterest's analytics endpoints (`/v5/pins/{pin_id}/analytics`, `/v5/user_account/analytics`) only serve the **last 90 days** (evaluated in UTC). But `postAnalytics()` requested `start_date` **2 years** ago, so the call failed every time and pin analytics were always empty. Introduced in `5cca81e0` ("feat: post analytics").

## Changes

- **`postAnalytics`** — `start_date` is now **89 days** back instead of 2 years (89 rather than 90 avoids an off-by-one when the server's local date leads UTC).
- **`analytics`** (account level) — clamps the requested period to `Math.min(date, 89)` so a longer UI selection can't trip the same error.

Replaces #1665: per review there, analytics shouldn't be coupled to `this.fetch`/`handleErrors`, so the `handleErrors` mapping is dropped — #1725 decouples analytics from `this.fetch` across all providers.

Pin metrics older than ~90 days simply aren't available from Pinterest's API; older posts return only the recent-window data.

author: jaggerxtrm
body:
Third child of epic **xtmux-j46**. Console reconstructs its entire graph from this snapshot.

## What

`xtmux topology --json` emits `xtrm.xtmux.topology.v1`: host → sessions → windows → panes, with stable `$`/`@`/`%` ids, pane geometry, indexes, active state, pid, cwd/command, and the full `@agent_*` metadata block (including `@agent_parent_session`, which the existing dashboard JSON omits).

Built from a **single `tmux list-panes -a -F` pass** — no per-pane shell-out — so the snapshot is one coherent sample rather than independently-sampled hierarchy levels.

Absent agent metadata is **omitted**, never emitted as `""` or a fabricated value.

## Host identity is now single-source

The first pass of this work hand-copied host-id generation into the picker, which would have made **three** implementations (`agent-state.sh`, `host-id.ts`, and the new one). Git never reports a conflict on a fresh copy, so they would have drifted silently — the same defect class as `xtmux-j46.17`.

Extracted to `scripts/xtmux-host-id.sh`, sourced by both `agent-state.sh` and the picker, with `scripts/install.mjs` shipping it so the *installed* layout resolves it too. `src/domains/identity/host-id.ts` remains the TS reader of the same file. `topology --json` and `context --current --json` therefore report the same `host_id` by construction, not by coincidence.

This also dissolves a race the seconder flagged in the copied function: the shared implementation re-reads the file after a failed `set -C` create and returns the winner's value.

## A test that could never pass

The geometry assertion originally built its expected rows with `-F '#{pane_id}\t...'`. tmux does **not** expand `\t` in a format string — it emits a literal backslash-t (`od -c` confirms). `IFS=$'\t' read` therefore never split, every expected field arrived empty, and the comparison ran `pane_id == <entire row>` with geometry defaulted to `0`. It could not pass against any implementation. Fixed with ANSI-C quoting, and verified to be **load-bearing**: a corrupted expected width now fails it.

## Validation

`bash test/contract.sh` → **201 pass, 0 fail**, including the pre-existing `xtmux-j46.1` identity assertions, which now run through the extracted host-id function.

body:
The auto-load-paths mechanism added in #187031 generates SafeAutoloadPaths.inc via a CMake configure_file() of SafeAutoloadPaths.inc.in (lldb/source/Core/CMakeLists.txt), gated by the LLDB_SAFE_AUTO_LOAD_PATHS cache variable which defaults to empty. author: mirnaderbieh
body:
## What

Package B2 of the client portal. A signed-in **client** browses the public
pharmacy directory, searches by pharmacy/branch/area, and opens a branch to
see its location, get directions, and view the medicines it currently stocks
(each linking back to the medicine finder). Independent of B1 (My inquiries);
the "Ask this pharmacy" action deep-links into B1's create flow.

## Changes

**Shared** (`apps/api/src/common/geo.ts`)
- Extract `haversineKm` (was inlined in `catalog.service`) so both the catalog
  (nearest availability) and directory (near-me ordering) reuse one copy.
  `catalog.service` now imports it — behavior unchanged.

**Contracts** (`packages/contracts/src/directory/`)
- `branch-directory.request` (`search?`, optional `lat`/`lng` origin override),
  `branch-directory.response` (branches + `orderedByDistance`),
  `branch-detail.response` (branch profile + stocked-medicines rollup).

**API** (`apps/api/src/directory/`) — `@Roles('CLIENT')`, global/public read,
no tenant scope, no writes/audit.
- `GET /directory/branches` — all branches, optional name/address search,
  ordered nearest-first from the caller's saved location (haversine) or
  name-ordered when no origin is known.
- `GET /directory/branches/:id` — branch profile + in-stock medicines
  (`stockBatch.groupBy(medicineId)`, `quantity > 0`, non-expired, joined to
  `Medicine`). 404 on a missing branch.

**Web**
- `hooks/use-directory.ts` (`useDirectory` + `useDirectoryBranch`).
- `/pharmacies` — search + branch cards (distance badge when near-me) + a
  directions link.
- `/pharmacies/[branchId]` — profile, external maps directions link,
  "Ask this pharmacy" (→ `/my/inquiries/new?branchId=…`), and the in-stock
  medicines list (each → `/find/[medicineId]`).
- Enable the **Pharmacies** sidebar item.

## Notes

- **No embedded in-app map:** I use an external maps/directions link instead
  of the shared `LocationMap`, matching how A2's medicine detail already
  surfaces branch locations. `LocationMap` is Lebanon-locked, so it can't
  display out-of-Lebanon coordinates (e.g. the seeded branches), whereas the
  link works for any coordinate.
- **Seed caveat:** seeded branches use `faker` worldwide coordinates, so
  near-me distances look large with seed data. Real branches (created via the
  admin form) are Lebanon-bounded and give sensible distances. No code change
  needed; a `seedBranches` coordinate fix is a separate call.
- The **"Ask this pharmacy"** href targets B1 (not yet built) — append-only and
  correct per the client-portal task doc.

## Testing

- Forced (non-cached) `check-types` + `lint` + `format:check` all pass.
- Drove as a client: browse/search the directory, near-me ordering with a saved
  location vs name-ordering without, open a branch, in-stock medicines →
  `/find/[medicineId]`, directions link, empty/error/404 states, and 403 for a
  non-client hitting the API.

author: jdsears
body:
The whole journey after the first send, built to the same spine: every outgoing word is a draft a human approves, and every automatic action is conservative by construction. Plus the rehearsal lane, so the journey can be tested end to end with a teammate playing the prospect and wiped clean before going live.

Note on ordering: this branch is stacked on `claude/connect-note-polish` (#47), so its diff includes that PR. Either merge #47 first and I will rebase this one down to just the conversation work, or merge this one and close #47 as contained. Both end in the same place.

## Follow-ups

- `FOLLOWUP_DAYS` cadence (default 4,7: three touches in all). A quiet thread gets its next touch drafted into the same review queue, checked against a grounding that includes the previous email, so restating is supported and inventing is flagged. No "just bumping", no manufactured urgency, enforced in the prompt and checked after.
- Any real reply ends the machine's initiative on the thread. Bounced addresses, suppressed contacts, snoozed leads, open drafts and finished sequences are all excluded in the due query, and bounces and away-replies do not count as engagement.

## Reply triage

- With reply capture on (kv switch on the Outbound page), the five-minute tick polls the mailbox and classifies each new reply: interested, question, not_interested, out_of_office, wrong_person, bounce, unclear. Reply text is data to classify, never instructions.
- Actions within minutes: internal notification to the team list; a grounded response drafted for interest and questions; automatic suppression **only** on a high-confidence clear no; snooze until the stated return date on out of office; `email_bounced_at` on bounce (and the send route refuses bounced addresses); everything ambiguous left for a human, deliberately.
- Bounces are recognised without a model call (postmaster and NDR shapes), and bounce or away-reply reverts the lead stage the poller advanced.

## Grounded responses (objection handling)

- `respond.mjs` answers from the thread, the reply itself, and corpus extracts retrieved the co-pilot's way. A question the documents cannot answer defers to engineering in plain words; no invented specs, prices or lead times, and the same end-customer and supplier guardrails as every draft, blocking flags included.
- Every response works towards one goal, a short meeting (video or face to face), with `MEETING_LINK` included verbatim when configured. An approved response sends as a true threaded reply to the prospect's own message via Graph.

## Meeting goal and handoff

- Meeting booked (kind and optional time) moves the lead to qualified and notifies the team. Hand off emails the pack: contact, meeting, originating signal, the full thread with verdicts, any note, then the engine stops writing on that thread.
- New Conversations tab on the Outbound page: every live thread, stage, last verdict, snooze and meeting state, expandable thread, and the Meeting booked / Hand off / Stop actions.

## The rehearsal lane

- Start a rehearsal (Outbound banner) clones the latest clean cold-open draft onto a rehearsal lead whose stand-in contact is an internal allowlisted address, tagged `campaign 'rehearsal'` end to end (migration 017). The original draft, lead and contact are never touched.
- The production path then runs unmodified: real tracked send, reply capture, triage with "Rehearsal" labelled notifications, response drafts, follow-ups on the same cadence in **minutes** instead of days, meeting, handoff. Isolation is by data, not by code branches, so what is rehearsed is what happens live.
- Rehearsal rows are excluded from the digest and carry a pill in the app. End rehearsal and wipe deletes every tagged row, so going live starts from zero.
- Kill switch invariant, proven in the gate: with `MAIL_KILL_SWITCH` on, mail can only reach the internal test allowlist, and only while `OUTBOUND_TEST_SENDS` is on. A prospect address is refused whatever the other switches say.
- Legacy hole closed: a reply matched to a plain internal test send is recorded for visibility but never advances a lead and never reaches triage, so a teammate's test reply can no longer suppress a real contact or start real machinery.

## Sender identity and deliverability

- Real and test sends now carry a footer: `SENDER_NAME`/`SENDER_TITLE` (or `SENDER_SIGNATURE` whole) plus a plain opt-out line. An opt-out is then honoured automatically by triage.
- `scripts/check-mail-dns.mjs` checks SPF, DKIM and DMARC with plain DNS lookups. pctflow.com already passes all three (run from this build).
- The weekly digest gains the outcome line: sends, replies, reply rate, live conversations, clear nos, meetings booked, handoffs. No open-rate pixels, by choice.

## Verification

- Migrations 016 and 017 (additive columns only). Conversation gate: 17 offline checks covering the cadence arithmetic in both units, the cautious triage decision table, the classifier fencing, the footer, the kill-switch invariant corners, the follow-up guardrails (planted end-customer name blocked), the response grounding and the handoff pack. Full gate now 101 checks, all green; `npm run build` in web/ clean.

Deploy notes after merge: `npm run migrate`; optionally set `FOLLOWUP_DAYS`, `SENDER_NAME`, `SENDER_TITLE`, `MEETING_LINK` on Railway; flip Reply capture and Follow-ups on from the Outbound page (both off until switched); rehearse via the banner once the `salesengine@pctflow.com` mailbox exists.

author: nishimirwe
body:
# Description

This PR resolves an issue where malformed requests (for example, requests containing invalid properties such as `c_nonce` in the request body) sent to the VCI issuance endpoint resulted in a generic `unknown_error` with an HTTP `500 Internal Server Error` status.

With this change, JSON parsing and deserialization errors are properly intercepted, parsed, and translated into OpenID4VCI specification-compliant error responses, returned with an HTTP `400 Bad Request` status.

---

# Changes

## Global Exception Handling (`ExceptionHandlerAdvice.java`)

### VCI Controller Exception Handling

- Added direct interception of `HttpMessageNotReadableException` for the `/issuance/*` endpoints (`handleVCIControllerExceptions`).
- Extracted specific nested Jackson exceptions to provide more meaningful error responses:
  - `UnrecognizedPropertyException`
    - Returns details on unrecognized fields.
    
  - `InvalidFormatException`
    - Returns: Invalid field format in request
    
  - `JsonMappingException`
    - Returns: Invalid request structure
      
- Returns a structured VCI error response using `invalid_request` instead of the generic `unknown_error`.

---
When an invalid field ```c_nonce```
## Before Change (Actual)

```json
{
    "error": "unknown_error",
    "error_description": "JSON parse error: Unrecognized field \"c_nonce\" (class io.mosip.certify.core.dto.CredentialRequest), not marked as ignorable"
}
```

## After Change (Expected / Current Response)

```json
{
    "error": "invalid_request",
    "error_description": "Unrecognized field 'c_nonce' in request"
}
```

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved handling of malformed or unreadable request data, including invalid JSON.
  * Added clearer error messages for unrecognized fields, invalid formats, malformed syntax, and invalid request structures.
  * Such requests now consistently return a `400 Bad Request` response with an OAuth-style `invalid_request` error, helping clients identify and correct invalid credential issuance requests.

author: chris-olszewski
body:
<!--- Note to EXTERNAL Contributors -->
<!-- Thanks for opening a PR! 
If it is a significant code change, please **make sure there is an open issue** for this. 
We work best with you when we have accepted the idea first before you code. -->

<!--- For ALL Contributors 👇 -->

## What was changed
- Workflow implementation no longer handles the conversion of outputs to payloads and instead returns `WorkflowOutputValue` that allows interceptors to inspect/modify outputs before serialization.
- `continue_as_new` no longer takes reference to input since interceptors might modify/swap the input. In retrospect taking a reference was also awkward IMO.
- Add `WorkflowInterceptor` trait and update workflow machinery to use interceptors.
- `add_workflow_interceptor_factory`/`WorkflowInterceptorFactory` which constructs an named array of workflow interceptors.
- `WorkflowInterceptorFuture` a named future that is the expected future to be produced by interceptor futures. We could expose `LocalBoxFuture` directly instead if we're willing to expose that 3rd party type as an external API type.

### `WorkflowInterceptor`
Interceptors look like the following:
```
fn handle_signal<'a>(
        &'a self,
        ctx: WorkflowInterceptorContext,
        input: HandleSignalInput,
        next: WorkflowNext<
            'a,
            HandleSignalInput,
            WorkflowInterceptorFuture<'a, HandleSignalResult>,
        >,
    ) -> WorkflowInterceptorFuture<'a, HandleSignalResult> {
        next.run(input)
    }
```
They take a context with a subset of functionality of a workflow context, input for the operation and a `next` continuation that calls the next interceptor in the chain. They are always sync forcing users to do any async work in a `WorkflowInterceptorFuture`.

## Why?

The changes to the workflow machinery and the "construction" polling are to allow the interceptor chains to not delay command creation/handler execution if there isn't any async work. This was especially apparent with sync handlers that were eagerly executed previously. Without this special handling, the existence of an interceptor chain would at least one yield point before the execution of the handler/command creation. The construction poll is our way of ensuring we drive the chain as forward as possible.

An alternative for this would be to make the interceptor API where `Next` would have some explicit `.then` methods to remove any yield points. I felt this diverged too much from all other SDKs and was generally pretty awkward to work with.

A few other decisions
- We have a singular workflow interceptor trait over 2 separate ones to make registration a singular method instead of spliting inbound/outbound.
- WASM interceptors have to be defined inside the component

## Checklist
<!--- add/delete as needed --->

1. Closes #1139 

2. How was this tested:
See integration tests.

3. Any docs updates needed?
Once released should add interceptors page for the Rust SDK docs.

## What

New Dolt-oracle suite `vc_oracle_fetch_pull_convergence_test.sh` built on the consume-once remote harness, covering the incremental "remote advances, consumer catches up" surface that the existing `vc_oracle_remotes` suite (single fetch/checkout) didn't:

| Scenario | Asserts |
|---|---|
| fast-forward pull | table contents, log messages, log count after `dolt_pull` |
| fetch + track `origin/main` | active branch + row count on a topic branch off the fetched ref |
| divergent fetch + merge | merged row set + count (disjoint local vs remote rows) |
| multi-branch fetch | contents on each of two tracked branches (`origin/featA`, `origin/featB`) |

8 assertions, deterministic across repeated runs. Hashes/dates excluded; row sets, counts, commit messages, branch lists, and active branch compared against Dolt 2.1.8.

The oracle caught that **doltlite's `dolt_pull` is fast-forward-only** — on divergent histories it errors (`cannot fast-forward — use dolt_merge with the tracking branch instead`) where Dolt's pull auto-merges. Verified the documented workaround `dolt_fetch` + `dolt_merge('origin/main')` converges identically to Dolt's pulled result (3 rows), so the oracle locks in that supported path for both engines and #1611 tracks giving `dolt_pull` its fetch-then-merge fallback.

author: mjbshaw
body:
This PR exposes the primary item’s Image Spatial Extents (`ispe`) property through a new public API:

```rust
parser.spatial_extents() -> Option<&ImageSpatialExtents>
```

`ImageSpatialExtents` contains the container-declared `width` and `height`.

The parser already reads `ispe`, but callers previously had no direct way to access the primary item’s container-level dimensions. They instead had to parse the AV1 sequence header through `primary_metadata()` or inspect the BMFF structure themselves.

Exposing `ispe` is useful for callers that need inexpensive container metadata for inspection, validation, resource planning, or indexing without parsing the encoded AV1 payload. It also preserves an important semantic distinction: these are the dimensions declared by the AVIF container, not dimensions inferred from the bitstream.

The accessor deliberately returns `None` when the primary item has no associated `ispe` property. It does not silently fall back to AV1 metadata, so callers can reliably determine whether the container property was actually present and avoid unexpected parsing work or AV1 parsing errors. It also allows the caller to determine whether they want to consider a missing `ispe` an error or not.

Only the property associated with the primary item is exposed; an `ispe` belonging to a thumbnail, auxiliary image, grid tile, or another item is not returned.

author: got3nks
body:
## Problem

amuleapi's Boost.Beast HTTP server runs on a single `io_context` thread, and non-streaming request handlers execute **synchronously on it** (`m_handler(r)` inside the read-completion). Any handler that blocks — most importantly a synchronous EC roundtrip — freezes the **entire** server: accept stops, every other client hangs (static routes included), connections pile up unaccepted / in CLOSE_WAIT. One slow or stuck request takes everyone down.

## Fix

Run the non-streaming handler on a dedicated **worker pool** (`boost::asio::thread_pool`, 16 threads) instead of the io_context thread. The io_context thread now only does socket I/O (accept / read / write); the handler's response is posted back to the session strand (`m_stream`'s executor) so all socket operations stay single-threaded. The SSE path (already worker-per-session) is unchanged.

Handlers now run concurrently, so I audited the handler-path shared state: State, `TtlCache`, the ETag cache, rate limiters and the session store are all already mutex-protected. The one gap — the lazy static-root resolve — is now a `std::call_once`.

Shutdown drains the pool (`stop()` abandons queued tasks; `join()` lets in-flight handlers finish) before tearing down the io_context.

## Validation

Relay-freeze rig (withhold amuled's reply so an EC op is stuck) with **4 EC requests parked indefinitely** plus the refresher blocked on `m_ec_mtx`:
- `GET /` and `GET /status` stayed **1–3 ms** on every probe; no accept backlog, no CLOSE_WAIT pileup.
- On master, the same freeze wedges `GET /` completely.

Builds clean (macOS); clang-format + Tier-2 clang-tidy clean.

## Scope

- Composes with #486 (EC read timeout): #486 bounds *how long* an EC op can be stuck (so pool threads and shutdown drain are bounded); this PR ensures a stuck EC op can't block *other* clients at all.
- Residual: during a total EC stall, up to 16 pool threads can be held by stuck EC handlers; beyond that, further requests queue. A dedicated EC service with backpressure (so the EC lane can't exhaust the general pool) is a planned follow-up.

body:
## One-tap Go from Trainer prompts (0.9.1)

Random **key**, **mode**, and **improvise** prompts now carry a structured fretboard action: a **Go → Fretboard** button under the prompt applies root, scale, and tempo (shared with the metronome), switches to the Fretboard tab, and starts the practice runner — one click. Prompts with no fretboard meaning (chords, progressions) hide the button. New bus event `fb:practice {root?, scale?, bpm?}`.

## Mode switcher rework

The chip row is gone. Regular view gets a compact **Mode dropdown**; fullscreen gets a **horizontal swipe** on the board (flick left = next mode, wraps 7→1, a transient pill shows "4 · C Lydian · fr 8"). Both drive the same state, and a running exercise restarts in the new window. Swipes don't interfere with pinch-zoom, pan, or double-tap.

## Practice patterns: Scale / 3s–7s / intervals 2nd–16th, with a direction toggle

- Pattern list: **Scale**, sliding **groups of 3–7**, and **diatonic interval drills 2nds–16ths**. Random and thirds removed.
- **↑ / ↓ / ↕ direction toggle** applies to every pattern (down = exact reverse; up-down skips the repeated apex).
- Pre-0.9 stored patterns migrate (`updown` → Scale + ↕).

## Settings tab

Theme moves into a new **⚙ Settings tab** (`js/settings.js`): **Dark / Light / Auto** — Auto follows `prefers-color-scheme` live. Fullscreen overlay buttons keep light glyphs in both themes.

## 🎤 Android tuner mic fix (`NotReadableError`)

`getUserMedia` in an Android WebView requires **`MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS`** alongside `RECORD_AUDIO`; without it the capture device fails to open with exactly the reported error, even with permission granted. Added to the manifest (source + inserted into the binary AXML by the cloud builder — string-pool append + element clone, verified parsing as 3 permissions). Tuner also retries with plain constraints and error messages now give per-failure instructions.

## Verification

- 28/28 checks (0.9.0 features): dropdown/swipe linkage, wrap-around, sequence-length math, migration, live auto-theme, contrast.
- 12/12 checks (0.9.1): Go visibility per prompt type, prompt→board root/scale match, tempo applied + stored, runner + wake lock running.
- APK deep-verified: 3 permissions parse, `settings.js` present, alignment intact, same signing cert as 0.7.x+ (in-place update).

## Release

`APP_VERSION` 0.9.1 · `version.json` · versionCode 16 · `sw.js` `guitarlab-v21` · APK rebuilt in-cloud.

APK SHA-256: `d5145c4c07c2cd63c27ca4aa48c35624e3071412ef0c28c2883d4a09ffd006cc`

author: abijith-suresh
body:
## Summary

Migrate the project from the ESLint + Prettier toolchain to Biome, matching the setup in `abijith.sh`. Also removes `DESIGN.md` (aspirational design spec that diverged from the actual implementation).

## Changes

### Migration to Biome
- **Add** `@biomejs/biome@^2.5.1` (1 devDep)
- **Remove** 8 devDeps: `eslint`, `@eslint/js`, `eslint-plugin-astro`, `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y`, `eslint-config-prettier`, `prettier`, `prettier-plugin-astro`, `typescript-eslint`
- **Remove** 3 config files: `.prettierrc`, `.prettierignore`, `eslint.config.ts`
- **Add** `biome.json` — Tailwind-aware CSS parser, Astro experimental support, `organizeImports`, same rules as abijith.sh

### Scripts update
- `lint`: `eslint .` → `biome lint .`
- `lint:fix`: `eslint . --fix` → `biome lint --write --unsafe .`
- `format`: `prettier --write .` → `biome format --write .`
- `format:check`: `prettier --check .` → `biome format .`

### Code fixes (no suppressions, no `biome-ignore` comments)
- **Add `type="button"`** to 8 `<button>` elements missing explicit type (a11y)
- **Add `<title>`** to favicon.svg (a11y)
- **Add `for/id` association** for token generator length label (a11y)
- **Add `role="none"`** to 3 drag-and-drop container divs — these are enhancement-only wrappers; keyboard users have the "Open file" button as an accessible alternative
- **Replace `while ((m = re.exec(s)) !== null)` with `for (const m of s.matchAll(re))`** in two places — the modern ES2020 pattern that avoids assignment-in-expression and handles empty-match edge cases natively
- **Remove unnecessary `useAnchorContent: "off"` override** from biome.json — never triggered on this codebase
- Auto-formatted all source files with Biome

### Removal
- `DESIGN.md`: aspirational design spec that diverged from the actual implementation in `themes.css` and `global.css`. The color tokens, type scale, spacing, and elevation systems in the spec are not used anywhere. Reference removed from `.prettierignore` too (which also referenced non-existent `DESIGN.json` and `PRODUCT.md`).

### Verification
- ✅ `bun run type-check` (both tsconfigs)
- ✅ `biome lint .` (128 files, **0 issues, 0 suppressions**)
- ✅ `biome format .` (119 files, 0 issues)
- ✅ `astro build` (26 pages)
- ✅ `vitest run` (31 files, 172 tests)

author: yoshihiko555
body:
Refs #139（再スコープ後の残タスク: check-trigger 接続・スキルシナリオ写像・design §3.3 追記を本 PR で実装。共有 facet のクロススキル回帰評価〔PR2〕マージ後のクローズを推奨）

## Summary

- `target=skill:<slug>` の登録・評価・target 別 frontier・promote freshness を追加
- skill overlay を composition closure かつカテゴリ限定（instructions / composition / scripts）で検証。共有 facet（policies 等）は `regression.enabled: false` 既定で register/propose 拒否（PR2 のクロススキル回帰評価実装まで fail-closed）
- handoff / issue-create の train・holdout シナリオを追加（fake gh stub は `path_prepend` による環境レベル PATH 注入）
- 実 Docker + Claude Max OAuth による handoff bootstrap E2E を追加
- skill-evolution の check-trigger から `orchex meta propose --target skill:<slug>` へ疎結合で誘導（`suggested_command` 出力。import 結合なし）

## Review fixes（3 並列レビュー 1 巡 → round 1 修正 → 再検証済み）

- evaluator hash の組み立てを共通ヘルパーに一元化し、loop との不整合（全 target が stale 判定になる回帰）を修正。実経路を通す回帰テストを追加
- PR1 allowlist を refcount 方式からカテゴリ方式へ変更（ユニーク参照 policy の拒否境界テスト追加）
- purge の frontier 再計算失敗を fail-closed（error + EXIT_VALIDATION_ERROR、非削除保証テスト）へ正規化
- facet_builder を実際に呼ぶ真の同値性テスト + インライン instruction の 100/101 文字境界を追加
- fixture PATH を prompt ではなく scenario 実行環境（`path_prepend`）から注入
- 複数 init イベント時の skill activation 判定を OR 蓄積へ修正
- broker の既知 client beta と count_tokens 並行要求を固定 CLI 実測へ追従

## Design decisions and deviation

M0（headless スキル起動スパイク）は「不成立時に停止・報告」の予定だったが、実測中に broker の client beta 不一致とローカル予算拒否を特定し、修正して続行した。この認証方針（proposer=codex ChatGPT OAuth / scenario・judge=Claude Max OAuth broker / PAYG API key へのフォールバックなし / 固定 beta allowlist）は **ADR-20260714-036 としてユーザー承認済み（accepted）**。

security レビューで確認済み:

- 未知 beta・未知 query は fail-closed
- PAYG API key へフォールバックしない
- `--tools` による schema 公開と `--allowedTools` による permission 付与を分離
- 同時 upstream request は 1 件を維持（bounded 直列化）

`facets/instructions/handoff.md` の `python` → `python3` は M0 コンテナに `python` が存在しない実測に基づく修正。詳細設計 §14 には broker ローカル 429 と upstream 制限応答の区別・Max OAuth と PAYG 経路の非混同・固定 CLI の request envelope 実測管理を追従。

## Testing

- [x] Package tests: 737 passed, skip 0（sandbox 解除）
- [x] Full tests: 3685 passed, 17 skipped（既存 agent-routing 条件付き 15 + 空 parameter set 2。本 PR 由来の skip 0）
- [x] Real Docker + Max OAuth E2E: passed（bootstrap 一周 + Skill 未起動 run error）
- [x] ruff check / format: passed
- [x] codd validate: errors=0

## Release Note

- ユーザー向け変更点: `orchex meta` が `skill:<slug>` target に対応（スキル単位の自己改善ループ基盤）
- `CHANGELOG.md` 更新: 済（Unreleased）

## Checklist

- [x] PR タイトルが GitHub Release にそのまま載っても読める
- [x] 適切なラベルを付けた（enhancement）
- [x] ユーザー向け変更がある場合は CHANGELOG.md の Unreleased を更新した

## Notes

- 環境 drift（`.claude/config/meta-harness/meta-harness.yaml`・`.claude/orchestra.json`・`.claude/handoffs/*`）はコミットから除外済み
- Claude CLI pin 更新時は client beta allowlist の再実測が必要（未知 beta は fail-closed）
- 後続: PR2（クロススキル回帰評価、`regression.enabled` 既定 true 化で共有 facet 解放）

author: constantine-png
body:
Fixes the broken build and makes the site deployable on Cloudflare Pages, without changing the existing Vercel setup.

## 1. Fix the build (was broken on `main`)
Four field-guide scenarios used `category: "Car Care"` — a value only valid for **blog**. The field-guide collection uses a different enum, so `astro build` failed at content sync (blocking *every* build, Vercel or Cloudflare). Corrected each to the right enum:

| File | → category |
|---|---|
| `ceramic-coating-maintenance-schedule.mdx` | `coating` |
| `contact-drying-technique-clear-coat.mdx` | `paint` |
| `leather-seat-conditioning-schedule.mdx` | `interior` |
| `wheel-iron-removal-step-by-step.mdx` | `wheels` |

## 2. Add opt-in Cloudflare Pages target
- **`astro.config.mjs`** chooses the adapter at build time. Default is **Vercel (unchanged)**; Cloudflare is auto-selected on Pages (which sets `CF_PAGES=1`), or forced anywhere with `DEPLOY_TARGET=cloudflare`. Nothing about the current Vercel deploy changes.
- Adds **`@astrojs/cloudflare` 12.6.13** (the line that supports Astro 5.18; 13/14 require Astro 6/7).
- **`wrangler.toml`** sets `nodejs_compat` + build output `dist`, so the existing `process.env.*` code resolves at runtime.
- **`public/_headers` + `public/_redirects`** port `vercel.json`'s security headers and sitemap redirect. Vercel ignores these files; Cloudflare applies them — so both hosts behave the same.
- **`DEPLOY-CLOUDFLARE.md`** documents Pages setup, env vars/secrets, and caveats.

## Verification
- **Vercel path** (`pnpm build`): adapter `@astrojs/vercel`, content sync passes, all pages build. (Local build's final step hits the known Windows-only `@astrojs/vercel` symlink `EPERM` — environment, not code.)
- **Cloudflare path** (`DEPLOY_TARGET=cloudflare pnpm build`): worker + all pages build cleanly, sitemap generated.

## Caveats flagged (need runtime attention on Cloudflare, documented in DEPLOY-CLOUDFLARE.md)
- **OG images** (`api/og.png.ts`) use `@vercel/og` — bundles fine; runtime on Workers is unverified. Test `/api/og.png` after first deploy; swap to `workers-og` if needed.
- **`pro.bayshine.net`** host rewrite from `vercel.json` isn't reproduced in `_redirects` (can't match host). Recreate as a Cloudflare rule / middleware before pointing that subdomain at Pages.
- Set `DATABASE_URL`, `RESEND_API_KEY`, etc. as Pages env vars/secrets. Missing ones degrade gracefully (per `src/lib/db.ts`), they don't crash the site.

Independent of #16 (homepage). Merge order doesn't matter.

author: gerrrt
body:
## Why

Evaluated [linkarzu's 2025 macOS ricing guide](https://linkarzu.com/posts/macos/macos-ricing-2025/) against this layer to decide what, if anything, was worth adopting. The finding: the post is almost entirely a **subset** of what this repo already runs.

**Already here (no-op):** Ghostty, tmux, AeroSpace, JankyBorders (`borders`), SketchyBar, Karabiner, btop, starship, Neovim, CaskaydiaCove/JetBrains Nerd Fonts.

**Deliberately passed on:** Yabai (needs SIP disabled — AeroSpace was chosen to avoid exactly that) and simple-bar/Übersicht (SketchyBar is the pick).

**The one clean net-new win:** `fastfetch` — a host/system info banner that complements the git-only `onefetch` already installed.

Raycast and a linkarzu-style live multi-theme switcher were considered and **left out**: Raycast cuts against the intentional keyboard-first launching (Karabiner hyper + AeroSpace), and a runtime theme switcher fights the committed single-theme (Tokyo Night Storm) design and would require edits to the read-only vendored `core/` (tmux/starship/nvim).

## What changed

- **`Brewfile`** — add `fastfetch` in the Productivity group, with an inline note distinguishing it from `onefetch`.
- **`fastfetch/config.jsonc`** (new) — curated module list. Colors are ANSI truecolor sequences single-sourced from `sketchybar/colors.sh` (accent `#7aa2f7`, magenta title, grey separators) and keys use Nerd Font glyphs, so the banner reads as part of the same rice rather than a stock fetch.
- **`bootstrap.sh`** — symlink the config into `~/.config/fastfetch/` as a new `[5/8]` wire step (mirrors how `ghostty`/`sketchybar` are linked), bump `WIRE_TOTAL`, and add the dest to the `--uninstall` list so it's cleanly reversible.
- **`os/macos.zsh`** — `ff` alias, guarded on the binary being present.
- **`README.md` / `CLAUDE.md`** — list the new `fastfetch/` tooling dir.

## Verification

- `bash -n bootstrap.sh` and `zsh -n os/macos.zsh` clean; `shellcheck -x bootstrap.sh` exits 0.
- `fastfetch/config.jsonc` parses as JSON (comment-stripped).
- `bootstrap.sh --links-only --dry-run` shows the new step and the `~/.config/fastfetch/config.jsonc` link in the plan.
- On a Mac: `brew bundle --file=Brewfile` installs fastfetch, then `ff` in Ghostty should render with the accent matching the SketchyBar/starship blue (`#7aa2f7`).

author: rearsilvergaming
body:
## What changed

- replaces plain TCP Twitch IRC with `QSslSocket`
- connects to Twitch's TLS IRC port 6697
- waits for a completed encrypted handshake before sending OAuth credentials
- fails closed on certificate errors instead of ignoring them
- validates and normalises channel, login, and token inputs before connecting

## Why

The previous implementation sent the Twitch OAuth token over unencrypted IRC on port 6667. This change prevents credentials from being transmitted unless the TLS certificate is successfully verified.

## Validation

- clean Windows `RelWithDebInfo` configure completed
- full plugin build completed successfully and produced `RearSilver-Stream-Suite.dll`
- `git diff --check` passed

This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## @cat-factory/orchestration@0.107.4

### Patch Changes

- c1028cc: Give every execution failure kind an actionable board hint (error-message initiative G3).

  The execution engine's `EXECUTION_FAILURE_HINTS` map omitted `preflight`, yet the engine
  produces that kind whenever a precondition rejects a run before dispatch — most commonly a
  `github_not_connected` `ConflictError` raised while building the job for a workspace with no
  connected repository (`classifyDispatchFailure` → `preflight`). Those failures reached
  `AgentFailureCard` on the board with `hint: null`, so the card showed the terse message with
  no "what to do next" guidance.

  `preflight` now carries a hint (connect GitHub and link a repository, or pick a configured
  model in the workspace settings, then retry), and the map is retyped from
  `Partial<Record<AgentFailureKind, string>>` to an exhaustive `Record<AgentFailureKind,
string>` — the engine is the primary producer of the full union, so a total map is correct
  and its type is now the drift guard: adding a new failure kind without a hint is a typecheck
  failure. The two other hint maps were already safe (bootstrap is exhaustive over its narrow
  alias; env-config-repair keeps a `?? unknown` fallback over the subset it produces) and are
  unchanged.

body:
### Description

Add optional `world.runs.getMany()` for one-operation snapshots of multiple workflow runs. It lets GraphQL list resolvers and bulk orchestration fetch many run snapshots in a single storage call, avoiding N+1 reads.

Results preserve input order, fetch duplicate IDs once, and use `null` for missing runs. `getMany` remains optional so existing community Worlds are source-compatible.

**local/vercel:** delegate to the per-ID `runs.get` handler via `Promise.all`, sharing the same read, schema validation, resolveData, and error handling.

**postgres:** uses a single `IN (...)` query for an indexed batch read.

### How did you test your changes?

- `pnpm --filter @workflow/world-local test` — 465 tests pass, including order, duplicate-ID, missing-ID, and metadata-only `getMany` coverage.
- `pnpm --filter @workflow/world-postgres exec vitest run test/storage.test.ts --testNamePattern getMany` — Postgres integration coverage passes for result mapping and a single-query assertion with duplicate IDs.
- `pnpm --filter @workflow/world-vercel test` — 295 tests pass, including MockAgent coverage of individual GET delegation with duplicate-ID deduplication and missing-run null handling.

### PR Checklist - Required to merge

- [x] 📦 `pnpm changeset` was run with minor changesets for `@workflow/world`, `@workflow/world-local`, `@workflow/world-postgres`, and `@workflow/world-vercel`.

body:
## Slice

CB-010 — MySQL migration and access foundation

## What changed

- pin MySQL 8.4.10 by digest in a one-instance/two-database Compose topology
- generate distinct synthetic local credentials without committed defaults or implicit rotation
- create bootstrap, three migration, and three runtime identities with tested denial boundaries
- add a non-default bootstrap grant role and a separate one-shot grant job with a fixed exact manifest
- keep `activate_all_roles_on_login=OFF`, reject a fresh active role before mutation, explicitly activate/clear the role, and propagate grant failures through `make up`
- add three separately invokable, rerunnable migration streams with independent fail-closed histories
- preserve the MySQL volume on ordinary `make down`

## Security and rejection evidence

- missing or malformed local configuration rejects startup
- caller-supplied grant arguments and same-count non-allowlisted business SQL reject before execution
- automatic role activation and an already active default role reject; a revoked privilege remains revoked, proving no pre-rejection grant mutation
- invalid bootstrap and migration credentials make `make up` non-zero
- runtime identities cannot execute DDL or hold global/admin grants
- bootstrap cannot read migration/business data by default
- auth and commerce migration identities cannot read each other's history
- agent migration/runtime identities cannot access `commerce_db`; auth/commerce runtime identities cannot access `cs_db`
- wrong stream/database/identity combinations reject
- failed migration history remains failed and blocks automatic retry
- migration services and their inherited anchor contain no bootstrap credential or grant role

## Checks run

- `uv run pytest tests/test_local_config.py` — 4 passed
- `make test-integration` — passed against a clean temporary MySQL volume and all listed rejection paths
- `make ci` — passed at final closeout head `51a9a09`, including the full clean-volume MySQL integration suite

The Docker/JVM-inclusive checks were run outside the Codex sandbox because the sandbox blocks the Docker socket and Mockito/Byte Buddy agent attachment.

## Review

Independent read-only review examined acceptance criteria, rejection paths, false-green risks, role activation order, exact allowlisting, configuration inheritance, migration histories, and failure propagation. All reported closeout blockers were fixed and the final review found none remaining.

## Known out of scope

- business schemas and auth-versus-commerce owning-table grants, deferred to CB-020/CB-030
- API/worker containers and application-startup migrations
- Redis, Elasticsearch, RocketMQ, and aggregate runtime closure

author: colocarletti
body:
Builds on part 1 (#803). Extends the device-resident trace-gen seam to the rest of the per-op tables and moves the remaining tables' LDE onto the GPU.

## What this PR does

**7 more table fills go device-resident** (built directly in VRAM, feeding the LDE/commit with no host upload, same seam as part 1):

  EQ, BYTEWISE, MUL, DVRM (ALU) · BRANCH · CPU32 · MEMW (general)

With part 1 this puts the **entire per-op arithmetic / control / memory family on GPU** (14 tables total).

**Preprocessed tables now LDE on GPU.** The 6 lookup tables that commit two Merkle trees (BITWISE, DECODE, PAGE, GLOBAL_MEMORY, REGISTER, KECCAK_RC) can't use the device full-column Merkle, so their fill + Merkle stay on host, but the **LDE (the dominant cost) now runs on GPU every proof** via a new no-Merkle device LDE path.

**Net:** essentially all main-trace fill + LDE now runs on GPU.

**Also:** dedupes the per-table dispatchers into one `gpu_build_tables<T>` helper, and moves the GPU fill-parity tests out of production code into `prover/src/tests/gpu_fill_tests.rs`.

## Correctness

- Per-table byte-parity (multiset for the order-independent dedup ALU tables) between each device fill and its CPU `generate_*_trace` — 14 tests, all green on RTX 5090.
- e2e `prove → verify` green, incl. the preprocessed GPU-LDE (proofs with BITWISE/DECODE LDE'd on device still verify; the static-root assert is unchanged and the opening path is untouched).

## Performance

- ~4.2% faster on ethrex-10tx (device fills, GPU-on vs CPU-on kill-switch A/B); the preprocessed GPU-LDE is on top of that.

## What's left for future PRs

- Trace-gen stages 1–5 on GPU — the **memory-model walk** is the biggest remaining lever.
- The precompile / continuation tables (COMMIT, HALT, KECCAK×3, ECSM, ECDAS,  LOCAL_TO_GLOBAL) — low row-count, low value.
