author: whg517
body:
## Problem

The chainsaw e2e product-version matrix is dead, for two stacked reasons:

1. CI (`test.yml` / `release.yml`) sets a `PRODUCT_VERSION` env var per matrix leg, but chainsaw only populates `$values` from `--values` files and the `chainsaw-e2e` Makefile target never passed one — so `($values.product_version)` in the observability manifest always resolved to `null`.
2. The other `SparkHistoryServer` manifests read `(env('PRODUCT_VERSION'))` directly (which bypasses the values mechanism and breaks local runs where the variable is unset), and the logging manifest pinned a fixed version.

Net effect: the matrix legs (3.5.2, 3.5.5) did not reliably test what CI requested. (A third link in the chain — `GetImage()` dropping `spec.image.productVersion` — was already fixed on main by #263.)

## Fix

- Add a `chainsaw-values` Makefile target that generates `test/e2e/.values.yaml` from `$PRODUCT_VERSION` (writes `product_version: null` when unset, preserving the default fallback for local runs), pass `--values` in `chainsaw-e2e`, and gitignore the generated file.
- Point all six e2e `SparkHistoryServer` manifests at `($values.product_version)`, with a `spark_version` binding per chainsaw-test.yaml (same pattern as zookeeper-operator). This replaces the `env()` lookups and the hardcoded pin in logging, and drops a dead commented-out debug step there.

## Verification

Verified live in a kind cluster before the rebase onto current main: ran the `smoke/override-pdb` suite with `PRODUCT_VERSION=3.5.2` (the non-default matrix leg) — the applied CR carried `productVersion: "3.5.2"` and the StatefulSet ran `quay.io/zncdatadev/spark-k8s:3.5.2-kubedoop0.0.0-dev`, confirming the values → CR → StatefulSet image chain end to end; the suite passed. The CI matrix on this PR re-runs both legs on top of #263.

author: mstomar125
body:
## Problem

The registry-driven Pro UI gates its collaboration surfaces on the active database's `DatabaseSettingsNode` `sync_enabled` / `auth_status`, but **no production code ever wrote those fields** (#1645), so the admin/collaboration UI was permanently locked at the enable prompt. And there was no consent gate before local data could reach the shared public workspace (#1654).

This is the **core half** of a cross-repo feature. The Pro daemon `EnableSync` handler and the `auth_status → connected` mirror land in a follow-up nodespace-sync PR that pins the core rev this adds; the two `closes` when both land + the Monday two-user isolation check passes.

## What this adds

**Backend (core)**
- `NodeService::set_sync_enabled` / `set_auth_status` — merge single fields into the `database-settings` singleton, preserving siblings (shared merge helper). These are the authoritative writers the Pro UI's variant machine needs.

**Bridge (desktop-app src-tauri)**
- New `nodespace.pro.v1` `EnableSync` RPC (client copy) + `pro_enable_sync` Tauri command, modelled on `pro_signout` (no-op in community mode).

**Frontend consent flow (Pro-gated; community build unchanged)**
- First-Pro **consent modal**: *merge into the shared public workspace* — with a required, checkbox-gated **irreversible** warning, and the confirm button is never the default focus — vs *keep this database local-only*. Merge records consent via `pro_enable_sync` (flips `sync_enabled`), then starts sign-in; **nothing leaves the device before the opt-in**. Declining shares nothing.
- The enable-sync pill and the previously dead-end locked-Collaboration placeholder now open the modal; registered as the `enable-prompt` app-shell modal contribution.

## Consent sequencing

Consent-first: the modal is opened from the enable-sync affordance and the merge choice happens *before* sign-in / any cloud contact — strictly safer than prompting after sign-in, and it needs no "first-signed-in" detection. Re-clicking the pill re-opens it, so there's no auto-prompt to suppress.

## Tests
- NodeService roundtrip: `sync_enabled` / `auth_status` merge preserves the tenant binding.
- Modal gating + irreversible warning; slot merge → `pro_enable_sync` → sign-in; pill opens the modal; updated ui-extensions contribution counts.
- Full frontend suite (4037) + `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` + pre-push gate (`test:all` + build + `test:e2e`) green locally.

Part of #1645, #1654.

author: itomek
body:
Closes #1892
Closes #1891
Closes #1889
Closes #1439

Before this train, the email agent had no pinned context envelope (baselines weren't ctx-comparable and a ctx change could silently move accuracy past the release gate), every published token number undercounted the real LLM cost, a long thread either overflowed the model or got blunt-clipped, and NPU users were stuck on the heavier E4B default. After it: the 16K-target/32K-max envelope is a documented, importable, gate-wired requirement; tokens-per-triage is a real, honestly-accounted scorecard metric; over-budget threads are condensed (never clipped or failed) with one extra hardened LLM call; and NPU hardware auto-selects `gemma4-it-e2b-FLM` with server-side detection, a servable guard, and embedder-thrash protection.

What each issue contributed (each landed via its own reviewed, stacked PR):

- **#1892 — context envelope** (this PR's original scope): `context_budget.py`, `gaia eval benchmark --ctx-size` with fail-loud readback + comparison guard, instance-scoped exact-pin in `LemonadeClient`, `GET /v1/email/init` reporting the actually-loaded ctx, data-driven `--require-ctx-match` release-gate wiring (shipping OFF until the first ctx-stamped scorecard exists — transition safety), envelope docs in CONTRACT.md/specification.html.
- **#1891 — token accounting** (#2075): per-call `usage` captured from the completion response (no extra HTTP), aggregated across mailboxes onto the triage tool result, merged into benchmark totals (`cost_estimate` rises — it was undercounting), `tokens_per_triage = triage_llm_tokens / llm_classified_count` as a reported-only scorecard metric.
- **#1889 — summarize-to-fit** (#2077): both thread surfaces (REST `kind:"thread"` — previously fully unbounded — and `summarize_thread`) gate on the budget; over-budget threads keep the latest message verbatim and condense the rest via a single injection-hardened fold call with fail-loud errors; committed adversarial long-thread corpus + hermetic scorer.
- **#1439 — NPU auto-select** (#2078): server-reported NPU detection, auto-select with servable guard and success-only caching, `model=` wired through the REST chat construction, device-aware embedder threading (the #1746 thrash pattern), explicit `model_id` as the opt-out.

(#1890, the token-reduction spike, ships no code by design — its deliverable is the [ranked evidence comment](https://github.com/amd/gaia/issues/1890#issuecomment-4970677985).)

**Measurement follow-through:** the consolidated eval pass ([#1319 plan](https://github.com/amd/gaia/issues/1319)) is running on AMD hardware now — accuracy-vs-ctx sweep (16K 3-run / 4K / 32K), ctx-stamped `baseline_accuracy.json` re-record, live long-thread baseline, tokens-per-triage before/after, and the FLM accuracy leg. Results will be posted to each issue; anything it surfaces becomes a patch per the milestone's eval-last model.

## Test plan

- [x] Widened suite at the tip: **1837 passed, 1 deselected** (the deselect is the pre-existing `test_claude_judge` machine-`.env` artifact — passes in CI) · `util/lint.py --all` 0 FAIL · `stamp_version.py --check` @ 0.5.0 · capability-matrix drift guard green · npm `tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] Real-world exact-pin smoke (Strix Halo): before ≠ pin → after = pin at deliberately-non-default ctx 20480, zero errored rows, scorecard stamped — full transcript in [the original evidence](https://github.com/amd/gaia/pull/2072#issue) below
- [x] Real-world NPU auto-select smoke: live `/v1/email/triage` verifiably ran `gemma4-it-e2b-FLM` (health readback: recipe `flm`), explicit-model and non-NPU controls — see #2078's evidence
- [x] Every review finding across the train (2 bot passes + stacked-PR reviews) addressed with a pushed fix and a thread reply

<details>
<summary>Original #1892 evidence — exact-pin smoke (real Lemonade, Gemma-4-E4B)</summary>

Probe value is deliberately **20480** (not the 16384 default a dropped override would silently fall back to).

```
$ curl :13305/api/v1/health   # BEFORE — slot held by another model at a different ctx
loaded: [("Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GGUF", ctx_size=32768)]

$ gaia eval benchmark --model Gemma-4-E4B-it-GGUF --ctx-size 20480 --limit 5 ...
[CTX] pinning 'Gemma-4-E4B-it-GGUF' to ctx_size=20480 (#1892 envelope: target 16384, max 32768)
summary: passed=1 failed=0 errored=0 pass_rate=1.0
scorecard.json: "ctx_size": 20480 stamped

$ curl :13305/api/v1/health   # AFTER — exact pin verified by readback
loaded: [("Gemma-4-E4B-it-GGUF", ctx_size=20480)]
```

**PASS** — before ≠ pin, after = pin, readback verified. AMD Strix Halo hardware, live Lemonade.
</details>

author: stanislavbreadfulai
body:
# What ❔

> Re-opened copy of #2287 (same branch, same content): the original was merged and then removed from `ad-atomic-interop` by a force-push, and GitHub cannot reopen merged PRs.

Follow-up to #2283 on `ad-atomic-interop`, addressing [the `_decodeExecuteData` review comment](https://github.com/matter-labs/era-contracts/pull/2279#discussion_r3579004547) and syncing the branch with `atomic-imt-interop`.

**1. Elegant execute-data decoding (the review comment).**

The two-pass 8-tuple `abi.decode` in `BatchDecoder._decodeExecuteData` is gone: the wire data after the version byte is now `abi.encode(DecodedExecuteData)`, so the whole struct is decoded directly in one pass — no stack gymnastics. Encoders updated accordingly (`Utils.sol`, `BatchDecoder.t.sol`, `test/unit_tests/utils.ts` — the latter was already stale: 7-tuple, no `InteropRoot.timestamp`, no `imtRoots`). Wire-format note: struct encoding wraps the old top-level tuple in one offset word; the server-side encoder must match (same caveat class as the #2283 tuple import).

**2. Merge `origin/atomic-imt-interop` (conflict resolution).**

- `IAtomicInterop.sol` / `AtomicInteropProof.sol`: kept our chain-batch-root-leaf design — the base edits (dropping the `slBlock` return etc.) applied to the removed message-based adjacency protocol; `slBlock` is load-bearing in the current protocol (it keys the anchor-root tuple lookup).
- **Adapted the new atomic-interop unit-test suite from #2278** (`AtomicInteropProofBuilder.sol` / `AtomicInteropProof.t.sol`, written against the old adjacency protocol) to the current one: `settlementProof` blobs with the enforced `TREE_DEPTH` top section + batch-leaf path, `verifyTimeoutAbsence` branches (anchor root strictly after the deadline; begin-root for late batches; last-batch + end-root for in-time batches, incl. the empty-subtree-cascade positive and not-last negative), anchor tuples served by a REAL `L2InteropRootStorage` etched at its canonical address and seeded through the production bootloader entry point. Mutual-exclusivity and boundary/fuzz coverage preserved and extended.
- `MessageRoot.t.sol` (base assertion vs genesis seeding): the first-batch chain-root check now combines the seeded genesis leaf with the first real batch leaf.
- `L2MessageVerification.t.sol`: kept the base's golden-root constant, returning the `(root, timestamp)` tuple.
- Generated files (`selectors`, zkstack-out, anvil-interop chain states, zksync-os genesis config) regenerated after the merge.

**3. Dead-code sweep of the PR's surface** (everything made unused by this PR family or already dead in files it touches):

- `ProcessLogsInput` + `BatchImtRoots` (IExecutor) — their consumer (`GWAssetTracker.processLogsAndMessages`) was removed with the asset-tracking machinery; nothing references them.
- `DecodedExecuteData.logs` / `messages` / `multichainBatchRoots` / `imtRoots` / `settlementFeePayer` — decoded and length-checked in `executeBatchesSharedBridge` but never consumed (same orphaning); the wire struct is now just `{batchesData, priorityOpsData, dependencyRoots}`, and `dependencyRoots` finally gets an explicit length check (previously a short array panicked instead of reverting cleanly).
- `ExecutorFacet.L1_CHAIN_ID` + its constructor arg — its only use was the pruned empty-on-L1 enforcement branch; all `new ExecutorFacet(...)` sites and the GatewayCTMDeployer constructor-args encoding updated.
- `ChainBatchRootTree.LOGS_ROOT_LEAF_INDEX` / `MULTICHAIN_ROOT_LEAF_INDEX` — unused (the leaf layout stays documented in the library header).
- `Executing.t.sol`: the long-dead commented dependency-roots block and the no-op `test_logExecuteData` (hardcoded old-format blob whose decode was commented out) + its `decode` helper.
- `Utils.sol`: the `encodeExecuteBatchesData`/`...ZeroLogs` split collapsed into one encoder (the distinction only existed for the removed fields; the old version also silently encoded `L2Log[]` where the wire expected `L2Log[][]`, which only worked for empty arrays).
- `DummyL2InteropRootStorage`: unused mappings (`batchNumberFrominteropRoot`, `chainIdFrominteropRoot`, `interopRootSides`, `pendingMessageRootIds*`) and `addThisChainInteropRoot` removed; reduced to the production-mirroring read/write surface.

## Why ❔

The direct struct decode is both the reviewer-requested cleanup and removes the double decode; the merge keeps `ad-atomic-interop` mergeable into `atomic-imt-interop` with a compiling, tested tree (the base's new test suite would not compile against the current protocol otherwise).

## Testing

- Full CI-equivalent foundry run (`forge test --threads 1 --ffi --match-path 'test/foundry/{l1,zksync-os}/*' …`) green, including the 25 adapted atomic-interop unit tests.
- `yarn test:hardhat:interop` — all 10 workers green on regenerated chain states.
- `selectors` / `zkstack-out` / chain states regenerated; lint + prettier clean.

## Checklist

- [x] PR title corresponds to the body of PR (we generate changelog entries from PRs).
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added / updated.
- [x] Documentation comments have been added / updated.

body:
## Summary

Resuelve los tres problemas de matemática y control detectados en la evaluación del proyecto:

### Arduino Nano — parser robusto (closes #19)

Reemplaza `sscanf` por un parser carácter por carácter con:
- Timeout de 100ms para evitar bloqueo en líneas parciales
- Validación estricta: solo dígitos y comas, exactamente 6 campos
- Validación de rango 10–170 por servo
- Skip de líneas vacías (ruido de nueva línea)

### ESP32 — firmware completo (closes #20)

Implementa el protocolo serial completo, idéntico al Arduino:
- Parser carácter por carácter (mismo algoritmo)
- Respuesta `OK` / `ERR`
- `ESP32Servo` con PWM a 50Hz, rango de pulso 500–2500μs
- Mensaje `READY` al iniciar

### SerialRobotController (closes #21)

Nuevo adapter en `bombolab-gui` que une `ArduinoNano` (core) con el trait `RobotController`:
- `connect()` → abre puerto serie real vía `ArduinoNano::connect()`

author: rongxin-liu
body:
## Summary

Route the org-owner UX gate on five org-scoped surfaces through the central `can("manageOrg", { orgRole })` policy (via a new shared `useIsOrgOwner()` hook) instead of a hand-copied `membership?.role === "admin"` literal. This finishes the migration `OrgRoleProvider`/`can()` started (the org layout route was already converted; five consumers were not).

- **Removes duplicated, security-sensitive authorization logic** — the `role === "admin"` derivation lived in five places, each bypassing the fail-closed `unresolved` handling.
- **Fixes a latent correctness gap** — the raw literal read a loading/transient-error membership as "not admin", flashing a denial at a real owner mid-load. The verdict now holds (`unresolved` → spinner) or offers retry on a settled transient error, and only denies on a definitive non-owner. Net posture is strictly tighter (the new path also requires membership `state === "active"`), so no surface can grant access it previously denied.
- **Encapsulates the tri-state once** in `useIsOrgOwner()` (`{ isOwner, isPending, isError, retry }`) so callers stop re-inlining the `can(...)` + `isError` branch.

### Converted surfaces
- `components/drawer/index.tsx` footer (label logic extracted to a pure, tested `orgFooterRoleLabel` helper; owner-pending gated on `org` presence so the app-global footer never pins a spinner on the org-less `/orgs` route).
- `pages/orgSettings/{TeardownSection,RerunOrgSetup,OrgPolicyAuditPane}.tsx` — these sit behind `<RequireTeacher allow="owner">`, which already owns pending/error/deny, so the internal check is a defensive belt; the redundant membership fetch is dropped.
- `pages/OrgSetupPage.tsx` — not behind `RequireOwner`, so it owns the tri-state render branches inline.
- Deleted the now-orphaned `hooks/useGetOrgMembership.ts` (last callers removed).

### Out of scope (deferred)
`OrgsPage.tsx` and `hooks/github/queries.ts` still hold `role === "admin"` literals — they operate on a *list* of org summaries with no `OrgRoleProvider` mounted, so `useOrgRole()` doesn't apply. A different (list-item-scoped) approach; separate task.

Titled `refactor:` — no release-please changelog entry, by intent.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run check` green in `web/` (tsc + eslint + prettier + vitest): 0 errors, 1482 tests pass across 130 files.
- [x] New unit tests: `useIsOrgOwner` (four tri-states), `orgFooterRoleLabel` (owner/setup/student/blank/pending/owner-error/roleLoading), `OrgSetupPage` (pending→spinner, error→retry, definitive non-owner→NotAdminAlert, owner→steps).
- [x] Existing `RequireTeacher`, `OrgPolicyAuditPane`, `TeacherSidebarMenu` tests still pass.
- [x] No-literal sweep: `rg 'role === "admin"' web/src` matches only the documented out-of-scope sites + the canonical `resolveOrgRole`.
- [ ] Manual: org owner sees Instructor label / owner-only affordances; a non-owner sees the denied surfaces; a real owner sees a spinner (not a denial flash) during a slow membership read.

author: andrew2net
body:
## Summary

Adds a **3GPP flavor** (`Pubid::Tgpp`) so `relaton-data-3gpp` can migrate from its plain-string index to the pubid-structured `_type: pubid:3gpp:…` form.

Parses `[3GPP ]<TR|TS> <NN.NNN>[suffix][-part…]:<release>/<version>` — e.g. `TS 23.207:REL-4/2.0.0`, `TR 00.01U:UMTS/3.0.0`, `TS 29.198-04-1:REL-5/5.0.0`, `TS 02.68:Release 2000/9.0.0` — into `TechnicalReport` / `TechnicalSpecification` identifiers carrying a release and a three-part version. Modeled on `lib/pubid/jis/` (no supplement layer).

## Digit-leading flavor name

`3gpp` can't be a Ruby constant, so the module is `Pubid::Tgpp` while the **external contract stays `3gpp`** everywhere it's observed:

- registry key `:"3gpp"`, `_type` `pubid:3gpp:…`, URN `urn:3gpp:…`
- bridged by overriding `Identifier.polymorphic_name` (`sub(/\Apubid:tgpp:/, "pubid:3gpp:")`) and `UrnParser#flavor_name`
- the export layer registers `:tgpp` (not `:"3gpp"`, which `FlavorExporter`'s `const_get` can't resolve); on-disk paths follow the module (`lib/pubid/tgpp/`, `spec/fixtures/tgpp/`)

Documented as a new pattern in `CLAUDE.md`.

## Behavior

- `PREFIXES = ["3GPP"]`; the parser also accepts the bare index form. Default `to_s` omits the `3GPP ` token (matches the index id); `to_s(with_publisher: true)` includes it. The transient publisher flag resets in an `ensure` so it never leaks past the `to_s` that set it.
- Release captured **verbatim** (`REL-N` / `PhN` / `UMTS` / `Release 2000`), grammar excludes `:` so the `:`-delimited URN scheme can always encode it. Letter suffix (`U`/`dcs`/`ext`) parsed generically. Parts may be zero-padded (`-02-01`).
- The single legacy no-release record (`TS 29.215/2.0.0`) is supported (optional release segment).

## Testing

- **100.0% exact round-trip on all 87,526** real `relaton-data-3gpp` records (0 mismatches, 0 parse errors)
- New specs under `spec/pubid/tgpp/` (identifier, serialization, urn, urn_parser, fixtures); joins the cross-flavor `identifier_roundtrip_spec` and export specs
- `bundle exec rake` (test:all + integration) green; rubocop clean apart from the baseline `identifier_types` helper offenses shared by every sibling flavor

Unblocks the downstream `relaton-data-3gpp` structured-index migration (separate, already-scoped).

author: prasanthlevelup
body:
## Sprint CI-2 — Coverage Report + CoverageDecision Enum

Second slice of **Coverage Intelligence**. Aggregates the per-scenario decisions (CI-1) into a simple count summary.

This is exactly the scope you defined: **NOT** a coverage score, **NOT** a health metric, **NOT** a reuse %. Just the breakdown so CI-3 (Planner Integration) can decide what to generate.

### What it does
Input: N × `ScenarioCoverage` (from CI-1).  
Output:

```
Coverage Report
  12 Planned
   8 Reuse
   2 Extend
   2 Generate
```

Smoke test (CI-1 → CI-2 integration):

```
4 Planned → discoverExistingTests → 1 Reuse, 1 Extend, 2 Generate → aggregateCoverageReport → formatted output
```

### The CoverageDecision enum
Per your architectural suggestion, I introduced `CoverageDecision` as a **platform-wide enum** (not string literals):

```ts
export enum CoverageDecision {
  REUSE = 'reuse',
  EXTEND = 'extend',
  GENERATE = 'generate',
}
```

This becomes the stable contract between Coverage Intelligence and all consuming systems (Script Generation, Healing, Migration, Chat, Release Readiness). String literals → enum migration done across `existing-test-discovery.ts` and all tests — no behavioral change, just the type system upgrade.

### Files
**New:**
- `src/coverage-intelligence/types.ts` — `CoverageDecision` enum + label map.
- `src/coverage-intelligence/coverage-report.ts` — `aggregateCoverageReport` (count by decision) + `formatCoverageReport` (log/CLI text block).
- `tests/unit/coverage-report.test.ts` — 6 tests (aggregation + formatting, including edge cases: empty input, all-same-decision, breakdown sum === planned).

**Updated:**
- `src/coverage-intelligence/existing-test-discovery.ts` — migrated `recommendation: 'reuse'|'extend'|'generate'` to `recommendation: CoverageDecision`.
- `tests/unit/existing-test-discovery.test.ts` — updated assertions to use enum values (`CoverageDecision.REUSE` etc.).

### Validation
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean (0 errors).
- `npx jest` — **21/21 tests pass** (15 CI-1 + 6 CI-2).
- Smoke test — CI-1 → CI-2 flow produces expected format.
- **Not run live end-to-end** — no DB/keys here, verified via comprehensive deterministic tests.

### Next (after your review)
CI-3 — Planner Integration. This is where Script Generation stops deciding reuse on its own and defers to Coverage Intelligence, so generation only touches the scenarios that need it (the EXTEND + GENERATE buckets).

author: infra-tdp
body:
## Qué es

El **plano de control** del enrutado por app: gestion se convierte en el registro `app → [nodos]` que alimenta el módulo OpenTofu `app-routing.tf` (PR [tdp-tienda-infra#107](https://github.com/infra-tdp/tdp-tienda-infra/pull/107)). Registrar/mover una app pasa a ser una entrada en un mapa, y desde la UI se lanza el `plan`/`apply` del LB.

## Cambios

- **Esquema + migración** (`0001_apps_registry`): tabla `apps` (slug único, name, host, repo, port, `nodes` jsonb, health_path, coolify_app_uuid, enabled).
- **`lib/infra/apps.ts`**: `renderAppsTfvars()` construye `var.apps` (`{slug: {host, nodes, health_path}}`) desde el registro (solo apps activas con ≥1 nodo); `runAppRouting(plan|apply)` lo inyecta y lanza tofu.
- **Runner de tofu**: nuevo hook `prepare(stackDir)` que se ejecuta **después** del `git reset --hard` y **antes** de init/plan/apply → escribe `apps.auto.tfvars.json` generado sin que el sync lo borre.
- **Acciones + RBAC**: `apps.view` (ADMIN/INFRA/DEV), `apps.manage` (ADMIN/INFRA); el `apply` exige `tofu.apply` (separación de funciones).
- **UI `/infra/apps`**: alta/edición/pausa/borrado de apps + botones **Plan / Aplicar enrutado** (enlazan al run de tofu) + entrada en el sidebar.

## Flujo

1. Registras la app (slug, host, nodos, puerto).
2. **Plan enrutado** → tofu `plan` del stack `coolify-prod` con el `var.apps` generado.
3. **Aplicar enrutado** → tofu `apply`: el LB crea backend + regla por Host + health por app. El túnel de Cloudflare sigue apuntando al LB.

## Verificación

- `tsc --noEmit` y `next build` en verde (`/infra/apps` compila).
- Migración `0000+0001` aplicada en un PostgreSQL real: tabla `apps` correcta (unique slug, FK a users).
- Forma del `var.apps` renderizado verificada — coincide con el tipo del módulo tofu.

## Siguiente fase (no incluida)

Desplegar el contenedor en Coolify por nodo desde gestion (API de Coolify) y fijar el Public Hostname del túnel automáticamente — este PR deja el registro y el enrutado del LB, que es la pieza que resolvía el incidente de `gestion`.

author: gonzalo-radio
body:
## Qué incluye

Deja el `Containerfile` listo para **producción** y añade una forma de **publicar la imagen en cualquier registry** (público o privado) con Podman.

### Imagen de producción (`Containerfile`)
- Labels OCI + `ARG VERSION` (metadatos visibles en el registry).
- `MOJO_MODE=production`.
- Corre como **usuario no-root** (`appuser`).
- **HEALTHCHECK** vía Perl core `HTTP::Tiny` contra `/ping` (sin depender de curl).
- `CMD` pasa de `daemon` a **`prefork`** (multi-worker).

### Configurable en runtime (`container/resque-web.conf`)
- Lee `RESQUE_REDIS` / `RESQUE_NAMESPACE` del entorno con fallback a los defaults de compose. Así la imagen publicada apunta a cualquier Redis con `-e RESQUE_REDIS=host:port` **sin reconstruir**.

### Publicación (`image.mk`)
- Makefile dedicado (`make -f image.mk build|push|release|login`), parametrizable con `REGISTRY`/`IMAGE`/`TAG`.
- Se construye con `--format docker` para preservar el healthcheck.
- Separado de `Makefile.PL` a propósito: la instalación nativa Perl (`perl Makefile.PL && make install`) sigue funcionando.

### Otros
- `README.md` (raíz) con uso: compose, build/publish, config en runtime e instalación nativa.
- `.gitignore`: ignora los artefactos de ExtUtils::MakeMaker.

## Uso
```sh
make -f image.mk build
podman login ghcr.io
make -f image.mk release REGISTRY=ghcr.io IMAGE=gonzalo-radio/resque-web TAG=0.1.0
```

## Verificación (contenedores reales)
- Build → `localhost/resque-web:0.1.0` + `:latest`; labels OCI con `version=0.1.0`; `User=appuser`.
- Override por env: `RESQUE_REDIS=r8:6379` → conecta (redis 8.8.0), API responde.

author: g9000
body:
## Summary

- make root `bun dev` own server reloads, debounce rapid file changes, and wait for `/health` before declaring the replacement ready
- preserve authenticated unlock sessions, DEKs, and the SQLCipher key across those development-only reloads through an ephemeral AES-GCM snapshot available only to the server child
- validate Ollama chat capability before saving config and fall back from an invalid background extraction target to the primary chat model for compaction and segmentation

## Root cause

Commit `99ff2876` added nested uvicorn reloads beneath the root launcher. Replacing the Python process discarded its in-memory unlock session store, so the desktop kept a token the new process could no longer recognize. Background extraction also trusted configured Ollama model names without checking that they supported completion, allowing embedding-only models such as `all-minilm:latest` to reach chat generation and return HTTP 400.

## Impact

Saving Python files during the same root `bun dev` session no longer logs the desktop out. Invalid background chat targets are rejected during config save, while existing bad configurations degrade to the primary chat model instead of breaking compaction.

## Affected areas

- root development launcher and launcher tests
- `apps/server` auth-session continuity, config validation, compaction, and segmentation
- design and implementation-plan documentation
- no schema migration or setup change

- `bun test tests/dev-root.test.ts` — 12 passed

author: purendar950
body:
This pull request was created by @kiro-agent on behalf of @purendar950 :ghost:

Comment with **/kiro fix** to address specific feedback or **/kiro all** to address everything.
<sub>[Learn about Kiro Web](https://kiro.dev/web/)</sub>

---
## The bug
Generating notes on **Cerebras** (`zai-glm-4.7` / `gemma-4-31b`) fails hard with:
> `400: Please reduce the length of the messages or completion. Current length is 30690 while limit is 8192`

No notes at all.

## Root cause (two compounding issues from PR #307's fixed 30000-char chunk)
1. **Cerebras models have an 8192-token context window** — they are *not* big-context, but the proxy flags every study provider as `big_context: True`, so it sent a 30000-char chunk that overflows the window.
2. **The transcript is Hindi/Devanagari**, which is ~**1 token per character** (English is ~1 per 4). So 30000 chars became **~30690 tokens** — exactly the number in the error.

## The fix (`_notes_sections`)
Size each chunk to the **model's real context window** *and* the **transcript's script**:
- `_model_ctx_tokens()` — per-provider context window (`cerebras = 8192`; others large, env `STUDY_DEFAULT_CTX_TOKENS`).
- `_chars_per_token()` — script-aware ratio measured on the actual transcript (Latin ~4, Devanagari ~1.2).
- Chunk from a token budget (`STUDY_CTX_INPUT_FRAC`, default **0.40** of the window) converted to chars via that ratio, and cap per-part output to the same budget.
- **Big-context providers (Bynara/Mistral/NVIDIA/OpenRouter/custom) are unchanged** — still the full 30000-char single pass.

## Verified
Simulated the exact failing case:
- Cerebras + Hindi → splits into parts; largest call ≈ **6.5k tokens** (< 8192). No more 400.
- Cerebras + English → fits.
- Bynara (big-context) → still single 30000-char pass.
- `python3 -m py_compile app.py` passes.

## Notes / recommendations
- On an 8192-token model, a long Hindi lecture **must** split into several parts (single-pass is impossible) — the existing `_covered_note` dedup keeps parts from repeating. For the most coherent single-pass notes, use a **big-context** model (Bynara `mistral-large`, or NVIDIA `deepseek-v4-pro`).
- Complementary to open PR **#308** (auto-continue on output-cap truncation). Both are independent and safe to merge; together they make notes robust across models.

author: draquel
body:
## Summary
Two playtest-reported dungeon issues, root-caused:

**Tile metrics were assumed, not derived** — the tile mapper scales floor/ceiling/wall slabs to `0.2 × CellWorldSize` along their thin axis, but the POI entrance info hardcoded a 20uu floor. At the demo''s 400 cell the floor is **80 thick**: the loot chest stood buried to its lid, its burst items spawned *inside* the floor slab (invisible/unreachable), and the elevator car + bottom call post parked ~60 below the walkable floor. Fix: `FDungeonTileMapper::TileThicknessFraction` / `TileThickness(CellWorldSize)` become the exported single source of truth; the parent PR derives the walkable floor top and wall inner faces from it.

**1-voxel shaft shell streaked in smooth worlds** — where the entrance shaft crosses open cave space, its wall shell was exactly one voxel; a single-voxel skin meshes as a pinched thin feature under MC (unstable normals → streaky triplanar texturing, user-reported). Both carvers (square column + noisy cave-opening) now place a **2-voxel shell**, giving the mesher a solid interior sample so both faces mesh cleanly.

## Testing
- `Dungeon.TileMapper` suite green (mapper behaviour unchanged — same 0.2, now named)
- PIE via the parent PR: chest stands proud on its plinth on the tile floor, burst items rest ON the tiles inside the room; shaft re-stamps with the thicker shell
- Measured ground truth: pawn feet at cellBottom+80 on the demo tile floor (capsule-calibrated), exactly `TileThickness(400)`

author: joshrkay
body: ## Why AI conversation dictation fails with **Could not start dictation. Please try again.** Root cause (verified against live Railway `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY`): Deepgram `POST /v1/auth/grant` returns **403 Insufficient permissions**. Browser dictation depends on that grant; a usage-scoped key cannot mint the short-lived JWT. The API previously mapped this to a generic 502, so the UI looked like a transient failure. ## What - Typed `DeepgramTokenPermissionError` for grant 403 → **503** with an explicit Member-permissions message - Dictation hook prefers the server error message - Assistant conversation UI surfaces `voiceConversation.error` (was silent) - Prod env checklist documents the Member permission requirement ## Operator action required to restore dictation 1. Deepgram Console → Create API key with **Member** (or higher) permissions 2. Update Railway `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` on `@serviceos/api` (production + Development) 3. Redeploy API 4. Confirm `POST /v1/auth/grant` returns 200 with `access_token` See `/opt/cursor/artifacts/DICTATION_DEEPGRAM_FIX.md` for the probe details.

author: calebbutcher
body:
## What

Vendors the **Traefik Official Kubernetes Dashboard** (grafana.com ID [17347](https://grafana.com/grafana/dashboards/17347)) as a `grafana_dashboard: "1"` ConfigMap so the kube-prometheus-stack Grafana sidecar auto-imports it. Fully GitOps-managed — no outbound access to grafana.com required.

- `kubernetes/apps/monitoring/traefik/dashboard.yaml` — the ConfigMap (mirrors the existing `loki/dashboard-*.yaml` pattern)
- `kubernetes/apps/monitoring/kustomization.yaml` — references the new file

## Why it's a safe fit for Traefik v3.7

Checked against the live cluster before choosing this dashboard:

- Every panel uses `traefik_entrypoint_*`, `traefik_service_*`, `traefik_open_connections`, and `traefik_config_reloads_total` — **all emitted by our v3.7 install**.
- **No `traefik_router_*` panels**, and Traefik doesn't emit router metrics by default (`addRoutersLabels` off), so nothing renders "No data".
- Metrics were already being scraped via `metrics.prometheus.serviceMonitor` in the traefik HelmRelease.

## Datasource / retention

The `DS_PROMETHEUS` variable defaults to the auto-provisioned **Prometheus** datasource (recent ~2d local retention). It's left as a variable so the whole board can be flipped to **Thanos** for long-term history from object storage. Traefik metrics are already retained in both tiers (verified: 30 live series in Prometheus, 75 series with 30d history via Thanos).

## Upstream cleanup

`__inputs` / `__requires` stripped, `id` nulled, and `["traefik","ingress"]` tags added so the JSON provisions cleanly via the sidecar.

## Validation

- `kubectl kustomize kubernetes/apps/monitoring` builds cleanly (19 resources)
- Server-side dry-run: `configmap/traefik-official-dashboard created (server dry run)`
- Embedded 1,500-line JSON round-trips through a real YAML+JSON parser intact

author: diego777rey
body:
## Qué resuelve

Mueve la impresión de prueba al desktop (Electron) y arregla varios problemas del alta/compartir de impresoras.

- **Impresión de prueba 100% frontend**: el ESC/POS se genera e imprime en Electron (RED→socket TCP; CUPS/USB→`lp -d <cola> -o raw`). No pasa por ningún backend. Se elimina el cliente de impresión por backend.
- **El Nombre define la cola CUPS** al instalar: la cola se crea con el nombre que cargás, para identificarla igual en la interfaz web de CUPS.
- **Térmica por Tipo (no por nombre)** al compartir: evita `-m everywhere` en una térmica RAW (que fallaba con *Unable to create PPD*) si renombraste la impresora.
- **retry-current-job** al instalar la cola: no se pausa ante un error del backend (evita el `stop-printer` por defecto que deja los jobs pendientes).
- **URI de cola compartida por `rp`**: la detección de red usa el resource path anunciado por DNS-SD; una cola CUPS compartida apunta a `ipp://ip:631/printers/<cola>` en vez del genérico `/ipp/print` (que fallaba con *"la impresora ya no existe"*).
- **Inputs sin uppercase** en el diálogo de impresoras (las colas CUPS son case-sensitive).

## Cómo probarlo

1. `npm run check` (AOT) sin errores.

## Techniques worth noting

- The mesh-particle triple (`func_80159E50`/`func_8015AF30`/`func_8015B904`) reuses PREHST `func_80163C4C`'s VentSprayData conventions; LOONEY/FINAL got the struct typedef and SCIFI's opaque `char[]` head/tail was filled in with the named fields (layout unchanged).
- `func_8015A4C8`'s 16-byte copy showed that memcpy alignment comes from field types: with `int* next` / `int _58[5]` in the struct, a bare `memcpy(spray->_58, spray->next, 0x10)` emits the aligned 4+4 block move — casts at the call site produce lwl/lwr instead.
- `func_80163EE0` and several spray-family functions pass a zero-cost second argument through to `func_80016894(p, arg1)` — the a1 liveness is what pushes the struct pointer's copy into a2 (PREHST's old `(void*)` extern was relaxed to unprototyped to allow it).

- MOOSHU `func_8015A084` looked like it had a dead `player` load; it's actually a hoisted argument to `func_8004B23C(instance, player)` that only one call path consumes.

## Outcome

`POST /api/live/query` with `query_backend="hermes"` now routes one authoritative, revision-pinned World Graph turn through the merged PR353 host and returns a grounded answer, qualified answer, stable abstention, or typed execution error without invoking any legacy Hermes retrieval or fallback path.

## Scope and verification

- Base: `d4fdb6c8f7b9fe855f1d0062883ce56521986fb6` — merge of PR #353
- Changed paths:
  - `apps/live_control_server/services/hermes_graph_query.py` (create)
  - `apps/live_control_server/services/live_agent_loop.py`
  - `apps/live_control_server/routes/live.py`

  - `Docs/Plans/HANDOFF-pr354-hermes-single-turn-backend-cutover.md`

  - `Docs/Roadmaps/ROADMAP-campaign-supergraph.md`
- Host contract consumed: `HermesGraphAgentHost.execute(HermesGraphAgentTurnRequest)` via `get_hermes_graph_agent_host()`
- Deferred successor: PR355 Plan presentation, source-anchor citations, persistence migration, and live dogfood proof

## Exact call path

```text
POST /api/live/query
  -> Hermes-only validation (context required; reject manifest_path / hermes_session_id / campaign mismatch)
  -> resolve_agent_world_graph_query_context(...)
  -> HermesGraphAgentTurnRequest(
       question=text,
       world/campaign/focus/admissibility from resolved envelope,
       revision_pin=resolved revision_id,
       root=world_graph_root(),
       conversation_history=None,
       session_id=None,
       capability_policy=None,

  -> get_hermes_graph_agent_host().execute(request)  # once
  -> classify from status + final_response + tool_events (messages ignored)
  -> dmb_live_query_response_v1 + grounding + agent_trace.tool_events
```

## Grounding state machine

| State | Top-level status | Answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| grounded | `ok` | trimmed `final_response` |
| partial | `partial` | trimmed `final_response` + partial warning |
| abstained | `partial` | stable product abstention (model prose discarded) |
| error | `error` | stable execution-error wording + typed diagnostics |

Evidence-bearing completion requires `state=completion`, matching dispatched scope/revision, non-empty/denied/unavailable outcome, and ≥1 `source_anchor_id`.

Stable abstention:

> DungeonBuddy’s World Graph does not currently contain enough admitted evidence to answer this question reliably.

- `mode` / classification intent: `hermes_graph_agent`

Instrumented forbidden paths raise in Hermes scenarios: `run_hermes_conversation`, `_process_hermes_context_query`, `_process_hermes_cli_query`, `run_context_lookup_turn`, `handle_live_turn`, `subprocess.run`. Live sibling requests do not call `get_hermes_graph_agent_host()`.

author: kenhayward
body:
**Phase 2B** — the last piece of the merge specced in #307. 2A made a meeting type *point at* a formula; this makes the minutes actually **be** that formula's run.

## The formula decides what the model sees

The strategies used to build the transcript for themselves, so minutes always got exactly the transcript and nothing else. They now take an **assembled context**, built from the primary formula's `FormulaContext` flags by the same `FormulaContextBuilder` a Formulas-tab run of that formula would use.

**This changes the minutes prompt — deliberately, and as you agreed:**

| | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Transcript | `Speaker: Text` | **`[mm:ss] Speaker: Text`** — the model can place what it reads |
| What else it sees | nothing, ever | whatever the formula declares — **summary, actions**, … |

The `Minutes` bit is **ignored for a primary**: these *are* the minutes, so including it would ask the document to read itself.

`MinutesContextTests` pins all of it, so this is a visible change rather than a silent drift.

## Additional formulas

After the minutes are saved, the meeting type's additional formulas are queued in `Ordinal` order — **after**, so one may legitimately declare the `Minutes` context and read them. Each lands as an ordinary `FormulaResult` in the Formulas tab. A **disabled** Platform/Diariz formula is skipped (only the *primary* is protected from being disabled), and one failing to queue never touches the minutes or the others.

## Re-runs replace — and never eat your edits

Those formulas re-fire on **every** minutes regeneration, so appending would leave a re-transcribed recording with a pile of near-identical documents. A run now **replaces** that formula's previous result, reusing the row and keeping its `Id` and `Ordinal` — so the list doesn't reshuffle and an open deep-link stays valid.

**But results are hand-editable**, and a blind replace would silently destroy someone's document. The guard mirrors the rule minutes have always had:

- an **automatic** run (the pipeline) **skips** a result with `IsUserEdited` — exactly as `MeetingMinutesProcessor` refuses to overwrite hand-edited minutes;
- an **explicit** run replaces it and clears the flag — exactly as `ApplyMeetingType` does.

Deliberately **no unique index** on `(RecordingId, FormulaId)`: enforcing one would mean de-duplicating existing rows on upgrade, and those are **real user documents**. Legacy duplicates are left alone and collapse the next time that formula runs.

## Testing

- **1399** .NET unit + **166** integration + **1032** web. Clean build, zero warnings.
- New: `MinutesContextTests` (the transcript gains timestamps; a primary can ask for the summary; what it didn't ask for isn't sent; the `Minutes` bit is ignored) and `MinutesFormulaPipelineTests` (additional formulas queued after the minutes, in order; regenerating replaces rather than duplicates; **an automatic re-run leaves a hand-edited result alone**; an explicit one replaces it; a disabled formula is skipped).
- Two existing tests changed to assert the *new* rule rather than the old one — the ordinal test asserted append-on-re-run, which is precisely what this PR replaces.

## Release

`0.140.0` — functional enhancement. The `IsUserEdited` migration is **additive**, so **no `CurrentFormat` bump**. Schema + synopsis docs updated.

## Deployment surface

**Server redeploy only.** Note the minutes prompt changes on the next generation — existing minutes are untouched until they're regenerated.

author: spranab
body:
## Live provenance-laundering bug in replication

sol's pre-build design review for v0.10 Item 4 (the anti-laundering write gate) traced the replication path and found the gate would be undermined by a bug **already shipping on `main`** — a T06 anti-laundering violation independent of Item 4.

### The bug
`materialize_record` (the peer-sync "record" apply handler) inserted only 11 of the `memories` columns, **dropping `source`, `certainty`, `domain`, and `emotional_state`**. A replicated `source="inference"` record therefore fell to the schema default **`source='user'`** on the follower's durable row — provenance silently rewritten to `user` across replication. Worse, the scoring-cache insert right below *did* read those fields from the payload, so the durable row and the in-memory cache disagreed, and `get()` returned the laundered `'user'`.

The oplog `"record"` payload already carries all four fields, so the fix is just to read and insert them (with the same defaults the cache uses, so the two agree).

### Second issue (same review)
`"record_with_rid"` ops (the cluster/replica apply path) had **no `materialize_op` arm** — they silently hit the unknown-op forward-compat branch, so records created via that path never peer-replicated. Routed `"record_with_rid"` through `materialize_record` (`INSERT OR IGNORE` keeps re-apply idempotent), taught `materialize_record` to accept either `created_at` (secs) or `created_at_unix_micros`, and added the op type to the `memory_entities` backfill trigger.

### Tests
- `test_replicated_record_preserves_provenance` — `source`/`certainty`/`domain`/`emotional_state` survive the replication hop verbatim (not laundered to defaults).
- `test_replicated_record_with_rid_materializes_with_provenance` — the op now materializes at all, with `created_at_unix_micros` correctly converted to seconds.

Full core lib suite **1662 passed**; fmt clean.

body:
Closes #72

## Problem
`services/notification-service/` and `services/batch-processor/` contained only `__init__.py` placeholders while the README/ports table presented them as real services. Worse, `tasks.send_notification` returned `status: "sent"` without sending anything. And the root compose couldn't build *any* service: its `context: ../..` paths are only valid from `infrastructure/docker/`, not the repo root where the file lives.

## What this PR does

**notification-service (:8004)** — `POST /notify` with SMTP email and Slack webhook channels. Unconfigured channels are honest no-ops (`delivered: false`, logged) — notification failure never fails the caller, but never lies about delivery either. `tasks.send_notification` now actually calls it and reports `sent`/`not-delivered` from the real outcome.

**batch-processor (:8005)** — `POST /batch/validate` (dry-run: per-line CSV errors with line numbers) and `POST /batch/process` (validate → enqueue one `tasks.process_single` per valid row on `expense_processing`, producer-only Celery app like the gateway's from #76). `MAX_BATCH_ROWS` cap → 413.

**Wiring** — dedicated Dockerfiles (previously compose ran these with *other services' images*); root compose contexts fixed `../..` → `.`; both services added to compose with env, and to the CI build + GHCR release matrices.

## Verification
- notification-service: 6 tests (fallback honesty per channel, SMTP send path with mocked smtplib, recipient guard, channel validation)
- batch-processor: 8 tests (parser validity/line-number errors/missing columns, dry-run enqueues nothing, process enqueues per row with correct task+queue, base64/type guards)

author: dpaoliello
body:
PR #188372 made Clang's MSVC-ABI deleting-destructor path route global deletes
through compiler-generated __global_delete / __global_array_delete wrappers
instead of referencing ::operator delete directly. This lets a deleting
destructor be emitted in environments (e.g. kernel mode) where no global
::operator delete exists: each wrapper defaults to a trapping
__empty_global_delete fallback, and a real forwarding body that calls
::operator delete is materialized only when the program actually uses ::delete.

This change refines how those wrappers and their fallbacks are emitted, fixing
two problems that made the #188372 mechanism fail in practice.

New behavior:

- The trapping fallback is now emitted as a weak GlobalAlias to
  __empty_global_delete rather than via an /alternatename directive. This lowers
  to a COFF weak-external-with-default -- exactly what MSVC emits -- so a real
  __global_delete defined in any TU overrides the fallback in every other TU at
  link time.

- A ::delete expression now registers the wrapper for its resolved global
  operator delete directly (in EmitCXXDeleteExpr), so the strong forwarding body
  is emitted in that TU regardless of where the class's deleting destructor is
  defined. This matches MSVC, which emits the forwarder at every ::delete site.

Bugs fixed:

1. Arm64EC (miscompile -> LNK2019). /alternatename only names the plain symbol,
   not the backend-generated "$$h" hybrid EC symbol referenced by the exit
   thunk, so Arm64EC images left __global_delete$exit_thunk unresolved. The weak
   GlobalAlias correctly produces the "$$h" symbol, exit thunk, and plain alias
   (verified on both x64 and Arm64EC).

2. Cross-TU ::delete (runtime crash). Previously the forwarding body was only
   emitted in a TU that *both* emitted a matching vector deleting destructor and
   contained a ::delete. A TU that only performed `::delete p` -- with the class
   defined elsewhere -- emitted no forwarder, so nothing overrode the weak-alias
   trap and the program executed a trapping __empty_global_delete at runtime
   (STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION). Registering the wrapper at the ::delete site
   fixes this.

To share wrapper-creation logic between the deleting-destructor path and the
delete-expression path, getOrCreateMSVCGlobalDeleteWrapper is promoted from a
static helper in CGClass.cpp to a CodeGenModule method.

Verified end-to-end: a weak alias in one TU and a strong forwarder in another
resolve to the forwarder under both lld-link and MSVC link.exe, and the
previously-crashing delete-only TU now runs cleanly.

author: rmcd-mscb
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> ## Scope expansion
>
> This PR grew well beyond the endorheic classifier it started as. Reviewers should
> expect **five distinct bodies of work**, not one feature:
>
> 1. **The endorheic classifier** (`gfv2_params.endorheic`, Signals A + B) and its demotion.
> 2. **The dprst clump-veto exemption** (`endorheic_wbody.tif`) — without it the classifier is
>    correct and the *product* is still wrong.
> 3. **Three new NHD/WBD staging modules** (`nhd_burn_components`, `wbd_huc12`, `nhd_waterbodies`),
>    because three of the four hand-made `input/nhd/` files turned out to be defective.
> 4. **BurnAddWaterbody merged into the waterbody layer** (+722 km² of new depression area),
>    with an 8-connected-adjacency guard.
> 5. **A round of review fixes** (below) closing two silent-downgrade paths and correcting
>    three false claims in the docs.
>
> Suggested reading order: the classifier (`src/gfv2_params/endorheic.py`) → the exemption
> (`depstor_builders/dprst.py`) → the guards (`depstor_builders/wbody_connectivity.py`,
> `waterbody.py`) → staging → docs.

## The bug

**The Great Salt Lake was classified as an on-stream waterbody instead of depression storage.**

Both existing classifiers are *local* tests — "does a Network flowline enter and leave *this* waterbody?" NHD draws Network artificial paths between GSL's arms, so it reads as through-flowing. **No local test can see that an entire basin is endorheic.**

## The fix — ask the hydrology, not the attributes

> **A waterbody is depression storage iff its water's terminus lies inside itself.**
>
> `frac_own` = share of the waterbody's cells whose D8 path reaches an FDR **code-0 (terminal)** cell *inside that same waterbody*. Depression storage iff `frac_own > 0.5`.

- Great Salt Lake's water ends **in Great Salt Lake** → `frac_own = 1.000` → dprst.
- A pond upstream in the *same closed basin* ends in **GSL, not the pond** → stays on-stream. (Hence *terminus-inside-itself*, not merely *terminates-at-a-sink* — the latter would demote every on-stream reservoir in the Great Basin.)
- Lewis and Clark Lake — a Missouri mainstem reservoir with one stray terminal cell — ends **in the Gulf of Mexico** → `frac_own = 0.007` → on-stream.

Two properties make this the right rule rather than a better heuristic:

1. **It needs no new input.** `fdr_raster` is already a required profile key and `d8_routing.drains_to_dprst_kernel` already exists.
2. **The classifier and the router agree by construction.** `d8_routing` already treats code-0 as a terminus, so a waterbody the router dead-ends in **is** a depression — by definition, not by validation.

A complementary **Signal B** (majority-inside a WBD type-C closed HUC12) catches Walker Lake, which contains no FDR terminal cell.

The demotion is a **strict subtraction** from the on-stream set — structurally incapable of inflating it.

## CONUS results (validated, gate-passed)

| | before | after | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **dprst** CONUS | 42,535 km² | **51,930 km²** | **+22.1%** |
| **dprst** VPU 16 (Great Basin) | 3,887 km² | **9,566 km²** | **+146.1%** |
| **drains_to_dprst** CONUS | 551,963 km² | **667,677 km²** | +21.0% |

**725 demotions / 8,735 km²**, plus **1,658 BurnAddWaterbody polygons / 722 km²** of genuinely new depression area. Drainage **gained 116,630 km² and lost 916** — purely additive, as a strict subtraction must be.

All **20 named fixtures** pass, and the raster gate confirms it in the *product*:

| | dprst before | dprst after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Great Salt Lake, Salton Sea, Pyramid, Mono** | 0.0% | **100.0%** |
| Lake Michigan, Lake Champlain, Lewis and Clark | 0.0% | 0.0% |

`frac_own` is **bimodal** — 6,298 of 6,427 candidates at ≥ 0.95, only 10 in the whole 0.45–0.55 band. The threshold sweep moves the answer **0.5%** across 0.3→0.7, so **0.5 is not a tuned knob**.

## Two bugs this uncovered that would have shipped silently

**1. `CLAUDE.md` was wrong about the FDR.** It claimed the NHDPlus FdrFac is "fully depression-filled… interior sinks removed." It has **15,262 code-0 cells**, and **15,693 of the 15,728** sinks in NHDPlus's own `Sink.shp` (99.8%) land on one. Those "benign FDR code-0 warnings" from #145 **are** this dataset — and they are what makes this classifier possible. Corrected.

**2. A 49 km² marsh was vetoing a 4,369 km² lake.** The classifier was correct, `connected_wbody.tif` correctly dropped GSL — and GSL still came out **0% dprst**. `clump_regions` 8-connects GSL to a 49.1 km² SwampMarsh that is *correctly* on-stream (its water drains **into** GSL, so its terminus is GSL, not itself), and `regions_touching_mask` excludes any region **sharing ≥1 cell** with the on-stream mask. All 4,854,156 GSL cells went with it.

This is the same pathology `CLAUDE.md` records for impervious (*"one impervious pixel would drop a whole multi-km² waterbody"*, PR #144). Fixed by exempting **endorheic** waterbodies from the clump veto:

> The clump rule is a **heuristic proxy** for connectivity. The terminus rule is **direct hydrologic evidence**. **Evidence overrides proxy — but only where we have evidence.**

A global per-cell carve was rejected: a further **~6,518 km²** of it is waterbodies with *no* endorheic evidence whose clump merely abuts an on-stream feature (reproduce: `scripts/diagnose/measure_global_carve.py`). Those keep today's behaviour, so this cannot re-open the over-extension #145/#158/#161 fixed.

## Every NHD/WBD input now stages from source

Three of the four hand-made files in `input/nhd/` were found **defective**:

- `NHD_sink_points.gpkg` — as measured during design: omitted `PURPCODE 1` entirely, so it had **0 sinks inside Great Salt Lake** where NHDPlus has **29**. ⚠️ *That file has since been replaced on disk (Jul 13) with a near-complete copy of `Sink.shp`, so those numbers no longer reproduce. The architectural reason stands on its own and is what the docs now record: Signal A must read the same FDR grid the router reads, not a lossy point shadow of it.*
- `closed_huc12.gpkg` — **698** type-C HUC12s vs **1,142**; 23 in the Great Basin vs **141**.
- `conus_waterbodies.gpkg`'s second layer — was missing **all 66,488 SwampMarsh** (149,468 km², incl. the Everglades). *(Since fixed upstream.)*

New staging modules — `nhd_burn_components`, `wbd_huc12`, `nhd_waterbodies` — pull everything from NHDPlus/WBD. `nhd_waterbodies` reproduces the existing layer **exactly**: 448,124 rows, 447,907 unique COMIDs, 217 duplicate-COMID rows, 66,488 SwampMarsh, identical COMID set and FTYPE distribution.

**`BurnAddWaterbody` is NOT a sink layer** — only rows with a sink `PurpCode` are sinks. VPU 01 ships **702 NULL-`PurpCode` rows against zero sinks in its own `Sink.shp`**; merging the layer wholesale turns canals and river reaches into depression storage. We keep sink-purpose rows only.

## Not in this PR

- **Profile still points at the hand-made waterbody layer.** `nhd_waterbodies.parquet` is staged and verified, but its shoreline vintage differs by 2.2% in area (same COMIDs). Repointing would shift the validated product — a separate, deliberate change.
- **`dprst_depth` (#173) must be regenerated** — it is masked to `dprst_binary`, which now includes GSL and 1,658 new polygons. Run in progress.

## Review-fix round (7 commits)

A multi-agent review of the branch found two paths where the feature silently
degrades to the pre-fix product with a **zero exit code**. Both are fixed, and every
new guard is verified **inert on the real CONUS data** — no output changes.

**The two silent-downgrade paths** were the same defect: *a guard that doesn't cover the
path operators actually use.*

- **`dprst` treated `endorheic_wbody` as optional.** But `wbody_connectivity` always writes it
  alongside `connected_wbody`, so having one without the other is *always* a stale output
  directory. The documented `--from dprst --force` rebuild against a pre-classifier
  `depstor_rasters/` therefore re-emitted the old product

author: physics515
body:
Autonomous nightly dev routine — worktree-isolated off `origin/master`, delivered as one PR. **9 verified increments**, all green (`fmt`/`clippy`/`test`/`build`) with real-binary boot smokes. No `master` push; not merged.

## Dependency freshness (landed first)
- **`tokio-tungstenite` 0.29→0.30** across `nanna-{channels,client,daemon,mcp}` + gui — compiles unchanged, no source edits. `cargo update` refreshed compatible pins (`open` 5.3.6→5.4.0, `rand` 0.8.6→0.8.7 / 0.9.4→0.9.5). Only major offered by `cargo upgrade --incompatible` this run. (`c/e04`… commit `bf829b1`)

## Increments
1. **`fix(daemon)`: record live model stats** — the daemon's main agent was built with **no** stats tracker and the sub-agent spawner had `stats: None`, so **no live model stats were ever recorded** (only persisted history loaded at boot). Threaded **one** shared `ModelStatsTracker` (clone shares `Arc<RwLock<_>>`) through `AgentService::with_stats` + `AgentSpawnerImpl` + `control.model_stats` (set before `with_storage` so persisted stats load into the shared tracker; router reads it for health-aware routing). 2 tests. *Verified: isolated real boot → "Daemon ready", "Stats-informed routing enabled", `/status` healthy, a heartbeat agent turn ran through the shared tracker.*
2. **`feat(cost)`: per-model USD cost estimation** — new `nanna-agent::cost` (`ModelPricing` + reference list-price table matched by family **prefix** so `claude-opus-4-8` resolves + pure `estimate_cost_usd`). Local/unknown models → `priced:false`, never a silent $0. `ModelStatsTracker::cost_report()` + surfaced on the `SystemAction::ModelStats` IPC response (`costs`). 5 tests.
3. **`perf(memory)`: SIMD cosine in the consolidation clusterer** — the dream-cycle clusterer used a private scalar cosine while the search path already used `nanna_simd::cosine_similarity_f32`; delegated the O(N²)-per-band cosine to the SIMD primitive (AVX-512/AVX2/NEON), guards preserve the "0.0 on mismatch/empty" contract. Parity test vs a scalar reference over random 768-dim vectors (<1e-4) + zero/mismatch/empty edge tests. (The O(N²) structure itself — HNSW — remains open.)
4. **`fix(cost)`: correct Claude pricing to 2026 actuals + research-fold** — the initial table seeded Opus with legacy Opus-3 $15/$75; corrected to **Opus 4.x $5/$25, Haiku 4.5 $1/$5** (cache read 0.1x, write 1.25x). Folded model research (Qwen3.5 universal tool-call template fixes; Fable-5 + config-overridable pricing TODOs).
5. **`fix(stats)`: surface cache-creation tokens in `ModelStatsSummary`** — `record()` accumulated `total_cache_creation_tokens` but `summary()` dropped it, hiding cache-write volume + understating cost. Additive/serde-safe field + regression test.
6. **`fix(daemon)`: `parse_retry_after` non-ASCII byte-offset bug + resilience-parser tests** — it found the prefix offset in the **lowercased** string but sliced the **original** at that offset; a length-changing lowercase (`İ`→`i̇`, 2→3 bytes) shifted the offset → wrong digits or mid-char panic. Fixed to slice the lowercased string. First tests for `is_rate_limit_error`/`is_context_length_error`/`parse_retry_after`/`truncate` (5 tests incl. an `İ` regression guard: old code returned `Some(2)` instead of `Some(42)`).
7. **`feat(channels)`: Markdown tables → plain text** — `strip_markdown` (Signal/WhatsApp) now converts table blocks (row + `|---|:--:|` delimiter) to readable rows and drops the delimiter; disambiguated from prose (`a | b`) and bare `---` rules (delimiter must have both a dash and a pipe). 5 tests. Completes the tables→text slice of the P8 ResponseFormatter.
8. **`feat(cost)`: grand-total spend** — `ModelStatsTracker::total_cost_usd()` (priced models only) surfaced as `total_cost_usd` on the ModelStats response. Test: Sonnet $18 + GPT-5 $11.25 = $29.25 (local excluded).

## Verification
- **Green everywhere:** full non-GUI `cargo build --workspace --exclude nanna-gui`; aggregate tests across touched crates — **nanna-agent 50, nanna-channels 45, nanna-daemon 39, nanna-memory 31, nanna-mcp 10** (0 failed). `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean on every edited region (pre-existing `too_many_lines`/`unreadable_literal` noted, not introduced).
- **Real artifact:** isolated `nanna-daemon run --port 5249 --health-port 5248 --data-dir <scratch> --no-pid-file` boots to "Daemon ready", `/status → {"sessions":1,"memory_available":true,"agent_available":true}`, 0 panics. Ran isolated (custom ports + scratch data dir) so it never touched the live daemon's `nanna.db` lock or ports.
- **Benchmarks:** no memory/clustering bench harness exists yet (a known roadmap gap); the SIMD-cosine change relies on `nanna-simd`'s existing benchmarks + a scalar-parity test. No perf budget in `bench/BASELINE.md` was regressed (none defined for these paths).

## Notes / limitations
- GUI-side items (embedded-run-state leak, `create_llm_client_for_model` caching, `parse_model_id`, context-budget hardcoding) were **not** taken this run: a fresh `cargo tauri build` (pnpm install + V8/turso/wgpu release) is too slow/risky unattended. Confirmed the daemon analogs are already correct where relevant (e.g. `AgentService.active_chats` is not leak-prone; the backend context path is already model-aware).
- P12 runner work stays in Mummu (integration-only here) — none taken this run.
- Deferred/blocked items left logged in `ROADMAP.md` (workspace `cargo test` V8 stack overflow; HNSW indexed clustering; GUI-dependent fixes).

## Research folded into ROADMAP
- Claude 2026 pricing (drove increment 4); Qwen3.5 universal tool-call chat-template fixes + Qwen3.6 VRAM tiers (P12/Mummu); `hnsw_rs` still current (in-search filtering + `insert_parallel`).

body:
## Summary

- replaces the one-line work-in-progress placeholder with a complete local-first browser raster editor
- implements a real layered Canvas 2D document model, drawing and shape tools, crop, transforms, fill, text, eyedropper, filters, undo/redo, import, project persistence, local recovery, and PNG/JPEG/WebP export
- adds a responsive componentized interface, keyboard shortcuts, drag/drop and clipboard input, PWA assets, and offline shell caching
- adds unit tests, static source validation, a reproducible build, GitHub Actions CI, GitHub Pages deployment, Docker/nginx packaging, architecture documentation, project-format documentation, contribution guidance, and an MIT license

## Product decisions

The original repository contained no implementation beyond a README saying it was a work-in-progress GIMP clone. This PR defines a focused v1 rather than pretending to reproduce every GIMP subsystem: a dependency-free, privacy-preserving raster editor whose implemented controls are functional and whose project format remains inspectable.

## Validation

- `npm run check` — passed; checked 15 JavaScript modules, relative imports, and the HTML shell
- `npm test` — passed; 16/16 tests covering geometry, colors, flood fill, filters, and bounded history
- `npm run build` — passed; generated the production `dist/` tree
- `npm run verify` — passed end to end

A local static-server request also succeeded. A Chromium interaction smoke run could not complete in the restricted build container because the browser process could not access required system services; no browser-interaction pass is claimed here. The included CI repeats the deterministic checks on the published commit.

## Deployment

- GitHub Pages workflow publishes `dist/` from `main`
- multi-stage Docker image verifies the source, builds it, and serves it with nginx
- static output uses relative URLs and works at a domain root or repository subpath

body: ### Motivation - Introduce a robust server-side production PDF renderer (versioned) that can render vector PDFs from editor scene data and invalidate stale cached PDFs. - Replace fragile browser-preview/raw-asset flows with explicit preview/production separation so PDFs and uploaded artwork are handled reliably across design, checkout, admin, and print pipelines. - Allow safe admin-only test checkouts in Netlify Deploy Previews using a short-lived preview admin cookie for offline QA without real payments. - Improve asset upload/preview UX, thumbnail/web-preview generation, and surface production metadata in the app/store so server re-rendering is authoritative. ### Description - Added a new print-scene renderer `_shared/print-scene-renderer.cjs` that renders sceneVersion 2 data into vector-aware PDFs and exposes `renderPrintSceneToPdfBuffer`, `sceneHash`, and `effectiveResolution` utilities. - Wire up the renderer into `render-order-pdf.cjs` to support `sceneVersion: 2` cache lookup, upload generated PDFs to Cloudinary, and persist cache metadata (`generated_print_pdf_*`) on `order_items`. - Add `download-print-pdf.cjs` proxy which hydrates request from DB, validates cache metadata (renderer version + scene hash), attempts to download cached Cloudinary PDF, and falls back to regeneration when stale/unauthorized. - Create DB migration SQL files `add-print-pdf-cache-v2.sql` and `add-test-order-flags.sql` to add cache columns on `order_items` and test-order flags on `orders`, plus indexes. - Add validation in `create-order.cjs` to support `admin_deploy_preview_test` checkout_mode which requires a deploy-preview + preview-admin cookie and persists `is_test_order`/`test_order_reason` to the order row; also auto-adds the orders migration defensively. - Implement preview admin flow: new `previewAdmin` utilities, `check-admin-status.cjs` updated to read preview cookie + deploy-preview environment, client `AdminSetup` page and frontend checks updated to set/consume the temporary preview admin cookie. - Upload/preview pipeline changes: `upload-file.cjs` tightened allowed types, returns richer metadata (bytes/width/height/format/resource_type), and chooses `raw` for PDFs; clients now upload originals first and use returned production URLs. - Client-side: many design/preview components updated to separate `previewUrl` vs `productionUrl` and to avoid attempting to render raw PDF URLs as ; new `artworkPreviewSource.ts`, `previewSelection.ts`, `previewAdmin.ts`, and preview-related helpers added to pick proper image sources and crossOrigin behavior. - Artwork upload flow improved in `AssetsPanel`, `Design`, and `GoogleAdsBanner`: PDF previews are generated via `renderPdfToDataUrl`, validated, and used as browser previews while original files upload to Cloudinary; background `web_preview` generation scheduled via `generatePositionedWebPreview`/`generatePositionedThumbnail` updates. - `generatePositionedThumbnail` extended with `calculatePositionedOutputSize`, `maxOutputPixels` support and new `generatePositionedWebPreview` helper to produce high-res web previews for PDFs/images (defaults tuned for 6k longest side + 24M pixel cap). - `renderPdfToDataUrl.ts` implements a robust PDF->PNG preview using `pdfjs-dist`, device scaling, page selection, pixel caps, and reliable cleanup; tests added and handling for abort/password/invalid PDFs included. - UI and store updates: cart/quote/editor types extended to carry production metadata; cart store persists `previewUrl`/`web_preview_url`; admin orders UI displays `is_test_order` badge and excludes test orders from revenue totals; PayPal checkout UI and checkout flow updated to support deploy-preview admin test checkout. - Added tests and helper test files across codebase to cover preview resolution, renderer behavior, PDF preview generation, positioned thumbnail sizing, and deploy-preview admin checks; added `pdf-lib` dependency in `package.json` for server-side PDF tests/embedding. ### Testing - Ran unit tests with `vitest` and node tests; new test suites executed include `print-scene-renderer.test.mjs`, `artworkPreviewSource.test.ts`, `previewSelection.test.ts`, `previewAdmin.test.ts`, `previewSelection.test.ts`, `generatePositionedThumbnail.test.ts`, `renderPdfToDataUrl.test.ts`, and `check-admin-status.test.cjs`; all automated tests passed locally. - Exercised serverless function logic using the added `check-admin-status.test.cjs` (cookie + environment permutations) and `print-scene-renderer` unit tests which validate embedding vector PDFs, raster images, transforms, and error cases; these tests succeeded. - Manual smoke verification steps covered creation of a v2 scene render path: rendering a sceneVersion=2 payload via `render-order-pdf`, Cloudinary upload of generated PDF, cache metadata persistence on `order_items`, and the `download-print-pdf` regeneration fallback when cache is stale; no database migration failures observed during function startup. If you want, I can split this large PR into smaller focused PRs (renderer + DB migration, upload/preview UX, admin preview/test checkout, and tests) for easier review. ------ [Codex Task](https://chatgpt.com/codex/cloud/tasks/task_e_6a554b1766348333bd8b443b3fdb045d)

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Agent builder deploys/deletes could get stuck forever: once an agent entered `deploying`/`deleting`, deploy/edit/delete were all locked on that status, and nothing ever recovered a job whose worker was offline, crashed mid-pipeline, or hung. Three fixes: - **Stale-job reaper** (`worker.reapStale`, run by a new builder-backend `crons.ts` every minute): - `pending` jobs fail after 2 min when no worker heartbeat is live ("No build worker is running…") - `running` jobs fail when their worker's heartbeat is >2 min stale, or after a 45-min hard cap - failing a job resets the agent from `deploying`/`deleting` → `failed` with `lastError`, unlocking the UI - **Worker liveness during long jobs**: the worker only heartbeated via `claim`, so a 10-min `eve build` looked dead. Now `platform/worker` pings a new `worker:heartbeat` mutation every 30 s, and `setStep`/`appendLogs` also bump the job's worker heartbeat. - **Manual escape hatch**: new `agents:cancelJob` mutation + a "Cancel" button in `AgentDetail.svelte` shown while a job is in flight — force-fails the in-flight job and unlocks the agent immediately. Consistency guard: `worker:complete` now ignores jobs no longer in `running`, so a cancelled/reaped job's late completion can't overwrite the reset state. `pnpm typecheck` passes. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/fbc5c17e4d96429b87894968eb9cf956 Requested by: @michaelshimeles > [!NOTE] > ### Add reaper cron, worker heartbeats, and cancel button to recover stuck deploy/delete jobs > - Adds a `reapStale` internal mutation (run every minute via cron) that fails pending jobs with no live workers after 2 minutes, running jobs whose worker has gone silent, and any job exceeding a 45-minute cap; affected agents in `deploying`/`deleting` are set to `failed`. > - Adds a `worker:heartbeat` mutation and a 30-second `setInterval` in the worker process so job liveness can be tracked independently of job claims; `setStep` and `appendLogs` also bump the heartbeat. > - Adds a `cancelJob` mutation (dashboard-auth gated) and a Cancel button in `AgentDetail.svelte` to forcibly fail the active job and agent during busy states. > - Guards `worker:complete` so it no-ops if the job is no longer `running`, preventing races with cancellation or reaping. > - Behavioral Change: jobs that were previously stuck indefinitely will now be failed automatically by the reaper. > > > > Macroscope summarized abdb03e. > >

author: patricktran1
body:
## Why

Human Body Explorer was one of the clearest remaining worksheet-shaped games with meaningful learner exposure: an early-catalog, age-6+ science route made of six static multiple-choice cards, manual Next clicks, fixed content, and no learning evidence.

## What changed

### Human Body Rescue Lab

- starts immediately inside an active body rescue with no setup or Start button
- replaces repeated quiz cards with three subject-native mechanics:
  - **Body Scanner:** diagnose the organ supported by the evidence
  - **Repair Arm:** tap or drag the correct organ or protective structure into the body dock
  - **Signal Router:** launch sensory and movement messages through the correct body pathway
- automatically opens the next repair after verified success
- keeps controls stable after mistakes and provides progressive Med-bot coaching
- visibly brings six body systems online on the patient display
- remixes mission order, opening mechanic, system positions, and lab environment on replay
- includes tap and keyboard alternatives for drag interactions
- supports reduced motion and a 390 px phone viewport

### Grade-adaptive learning

- adds age-fit body-system missions from TK through Grade 5
- progresses from identifying body helpers to reasoning about circulation, gas exchange, stimulus-response pathways, digestion, skeletal structure, and motor signaling
- records every correct and incorrect attempt through the existing learning-evidence system
- sends unsuccessful attempts into the existing review/mastery loop with support metadata

### Integrity and QA

- opening the game creates a play, not a completion
- only six verified repairs complete the run
- cosmetic system lights and lab changes create no rewards or evidence
- preserves the existing game-session SDK and exactly-once completion behavior
- updates the shared completion recipe for automatic flow
- adds focused Playwright coverage for immediate play, coaching, learning evidence, all three mechanics, drag/tap alternatives, grade adaptation, replay remixing, phone safety, reduced motion, and clean completion replay
- registers the focused spec in AdrianOS CI

## Validation

CI is expected to run:

- production build and static contracts
- focused learner-home and changed-feature browser checks
- complete AdrianOS browser matrix

### [`v0.2.3`](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/releases/tag/v0.2.3): vite-plus v0.2.3: config extraction, create, and vp run reliability fixes

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/compare/v0.2.2...v0.2.3)

A patch release that fixes static config extraction for `vite.config.ts` files whose `defineConfig` comes from a preset or custom wrapper (no longer misread as Vite+'s own), fixes `vp create` for org templates on registries that strip custom package fields, cleans up terminal output after Ctrl-C during `vp run`, and updates bundled Vite to 8.1.3.

##### Highlights

- **Custom `VP_HOME` is honored on every run**: the global `vp` now respects a user-set `VP_HOME` for its home directory instead of falling back to `~/.vite-plus`, and persists it in the generated env files, so a custom install location no longer produces multiple instances or unusable packages ([#​2029](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2029)), by [@​liangmiQwQ](https://redirect.github.com/liangmiQwQ)

##### Features

- Upgrade bundled Vite from `8.1.2` to `8.1.3` (inlined CSS after the shebang line, CSS preload for nested dynamic imports, SSR stacktrace column fix) ([#​2042](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2042)), by [@​voidzero-guard](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-guard)\[bot]

##### Fixes & Enhancements

- `vp run` no longer misreads a `vite.config.ts` when its `defineConfig` comes from a preset or a custom wrapper instead of `vite-plus` or `vite`. Such configs are now evaluated at runtime rather than assumed to be Vite+'s own, so projects that use them no longer wrongly report `Task "build" not found` ([#​2060](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2060), [#​2075](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2075)), by [@​liangmiQwQ](https://redirect.github.com/liangmiQwQ) and [@​fengmk2](https://redirect.github.com/fengmk2)
- Killing a `vp run` task with Ctrl-C no longer leaves odd OSC escape sequences in the terminal; `vp` defers its own Ctrl-C handling until the child process exits ([#​2079](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2079)), by [@​forehalo](https://redirect.github.com/forehalo)
- `vp migrate`: rewriting a `package.json` prettier script now emits a single `--check`, so scripts that combined `--check` with `--list-different` / `-l` / `-c` no longer produce a duplicated `vp fmt --check --check` ([#​2044](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2044)), by [@​shulaoda](https://redirect.github.com/shulaoda)
- `vp create @​org:name`: read the org template catalog (`createConfig`) from the published tarball when the registry (e.g. GitHub Packages) strips custom fields from packument metadata ([#​2063](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2063)), by [@​hiro-daikin](https://redirect.github.com/hiro-daikin)
- `vp run`: missing env vars requested through `@voidzero-dev/vite-task-client` now return `undefined` instead of `null`, preserving Vite production `NODE_ENV` semantics when builds run through `vp run` ([vite-task#508](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-task/pull/508), via [#​2076](https://redirect.github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/pull/2076)), by [@​wan9chi](https://redirect.github.com/wan9chi)
