author: sadique-rehman
body:
### Motivation

- Modernize the timer UI and theme system with softer rounded visuals and clearer separators by introducing new CSS tokens and updated component styles. 
- Add a native countdown mode alongside the existing stopwatch to support preset and custom timer durations. 
- Improve readability of the main display and introduce subtle zero-fade rendering for leading zeros. 

### Description

- Added two new CSS variables `--divider` and `--soft-tint` and refactored many styles to use rounded controls, translucent backgrounds, and updated shadows across dark/light/redbull themes. 
- Introduced mode switching UI and logic: a `stopwatch` and `timer` mode, with a countdown editor including presets and numeric inputs, new functions `formatTimeHtml`, `getDisplayMs`, `updateRunningFrame`, `finishTimerRun`, `applyTimerTarget`, and state `timerTargetMs`/`mode`. 
- Reworked control buttons to SVG icon buttons with `aria-label`/`title`, updated zen behavior, and moved time rendering to `renderDisplay` to support per-digit zero styling. 
- Polished modal, leaderboard and rank-list visuals (rounded corners, adjusted paddings, tinting/opacities), updated class handling for locked/eternal ranks, and simplified some redbull-specific shadows. 

### Testing

- Ran static checks and build steps using `npm run lint` and `npm run build`, both completed successfully. 
- Executed the project test suite via `npm test` and existing automated tests passed. 
- Performed a local smoke test of the timer and countdown flows (start/pause/reset, presets, set duration) which behaved as expected.

author: redreceipt
body:
## Summary

- replace the generic Source column with platform-specific freshness signals
- use production Expo runtime observations for iOS and Android
- use stable release tags for tvOS, AndroidTV, and Amazon
- compare Roku builds with the latest `master` commit affecting `templates/roku`
- keep internal and prerelease observations out of production baselines

## Why

The Apps dashboard treated every platform as if it shared one version flow. Internal alpha observations could become the apparent TV baseline, App Store version differences could mark otherwise-current mobile runtimes outdated, and Roku commits were displayed without being checked against the source branch.

The dashboard now follows the actual release mechanism for each platform. Legacy alpha observations are only canonicalized to a stable release when their recorded revision matches that stable tag.

## Impact

The Apps page labels freshness as Expo Runtime, Release, or Commit depending on the selected platform. App Store versions remain visible as informational context, while status reflects the platform's production freshness signal.

## Related

- ApollosProject/apollos-platforms#6724 emits the deterministic deployment-track and source metadata consumed by this dashboard.

## Proof

- `ruff check .`
- `mypy .`
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'` (112 tests)
- live `/apps` request against production BigQuery and GitHub data returned 200 with 210 rows
- rendered Expo Runtime, Release, and Commit flows with zero alpha freshness values and zero internal-track rows

Overall project coverage improved from **52%** to **58%**.

body:
## Que cambia
- agrega un flujo de `Imagen a Bordado` dentro del editor admin existente
- incorpora un nuevo motor `image-digitizer.js` para convertir imagenes en objetos de bordado con criterio practico de produccion
- suma controles de uso, fidelidad, colores, medidas, fondo, preservacion de texto y puff
- mejora el reporte de analisis y el estado de produccion para dejar claro cuando el resultado requiere revision manual
- endurece los mensajes de exportacion para no presentar una preview visual como si ya fuera apta para produccion

## Por que cambia
La conversion actual era demasiado tecnica y determinista por pixeles para un uso real de taller. Esta mejora prioriza legibilidad, reduce micro-objetos y trims innecesarios, y aplica reglas mas cercanas a una digitalizacion profesional.

## Impacto
- el administrador puede probar conversiones mas utiles desde la misma app
- se incorporan advertencias para textos pequenos, degradados, contornos finos y zonas que pueden requerir redibujo manual o validacion para puff
- se adapta densidad, underlay y compensacion segun tejido y tipo de zona

## Validacion

- `node --check frontend/public/bordados-editor/js/engine/image-digitizer.js`

author: tensairod
body:
Implements the RateLimiter interface (application layer) and its concrete in-memory implementation, TokenBucketRateLimiter (infrastructure layer), closing the Rate Limiting milestone (M3). Closes #6.

- RateLimiter interface lives in the application package for the same reason ConfigSource lives in config-validator's application package: the future WAFEngine (#7) depends on this abstraction; the concrete implementation lives in infrastructure and implements it (Dependency Inversion).
- TokenBucketRateLimiter uses the classic token bucket algorithm: each IP gets its own bucket that refills continuously at a fixed rate and is capped at `capacity` (never overflows even after long idle periods — verified explicitly with a 1-hour time jump).
- The internal clock is injectable via WithClock(...) purely for deterministic testing — real time.Sleep-based tests would be slow (seconds of real wall-clock time per refill test) and potentially flaky under CI load. Tests advance a fake clock instantly instead.
- Cleanup() does NOT run automatically via an internal goroutine/ticker — deliberately, to avoid hiding a long-running goroutine whose lifecycle would be hard to control (when does it stop? how do tests avoid leaking it between runs?). The real process entrypoint (cmd/edge-waf-engine, #11) decides the right cleanup cadence based on real traffic volume — not a decision this package should make alone.
- Explicitly tested for concurrency safety with `go test -race`: a rate limiter is inherently accessed by many goroutines at once (each HTTP request arrives on its own goroutine), and a race here would be particularly severe — it's exactly the component meant to prevent abuse, so a race enabling limit bypass would defeat its purpose.

Tests: 9 tests (constructor validation, burst-to-capacity blocking, refill over time, capacity ceiling after long idle, independent buckets per IP, Len(), Cleanup() removing only idle entries, Cleanup() removing nothing when all active, and a 1000-iteration concurrent-access test run under -race). All pass, including with -race enabled.

author: omarcusdev
body:
## Problema

Jean reportou (print WhatsApp) um pedido manual criado **100% consignado** — 2x Vila Império 50L, ambos consignado → "A pagar R\$ 20,00" (só o frete). O cliente não paga nada firme e pode devolver tudo. Risco de negócio.

## Regra

Todo pedido precisa de **≥1 barril firme (não-consignado)**. Bloqueia pedido 100% consignado. Não limita a quantidade de consignado — só exige um firme coexistindo.

## Solução (app-level, sem migration)

Predicado único `hasFirmeItem(items) = items.some(i => !i.is_consignado)` em `lib/pricing.ts`, reusado em 4 guards:

1. **Server, criação** — `manualOrderInputSchema.superRefine`. Pega o caso do print inclusive request forjado que pule o drawer.
2. **Client, UX** — `manual-order-drawer.tsx`: `canSubmit` + aviso âmbar inline (botão desabilitado com motivo).
3. **Server, edição (remover)** — `removePedidoItem`: bloqueia remover o último firme deixando só consignado.
4. **Server, edição (adicionar)** — `addPedidoItem`: bloqueia add consignado num pedido com 0 firme.

O checkout do cliente não tem consignado (itens só `{produto_id, quantidade}`), então nenhum guard lá.

## Revisão adversarial (multi-agente: 3 lentes + verify)

- **2 achados low corrigidos** (`8d6fec8`): os guards de edição descartavam o `error` do supabase — `removePedidoItem` falhava **aberto** (read null → guard pulado → delete prossegue → pedido só-consignado silencioso) e `addPedidoItem` falhava fechado com mensagem enganosa mascarando o erro real. Fix: capturar e propagar o `error` nos dois (fail-closed, erro real à mostra).
- **2 achados refutados** corretamente (TOCTOU race = exige admin forjar 2 POSTs simultâneos p/ se auto-sabotar + fix seria camada DB fora do escopo aprovado; RPC `create_manual_order` sem check = design app-level aprovado, RPC só executável por admin autenticado).

## Verificação

- 356/356 vitest (9 testes novos: `hasFirmeItem` + `manualOrderInputSchema`)
- `tsc --noEmit` limpo
- `next build` ok

Sem eyeball visual do admin (login por senha).

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-trava-consignado-firme-design.md`
Plano: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-14-trava-consignado-firme.md`

author: pinin4fjords
body:
## Summary

Sections sharing a contiguous run of grid columns in one row now share a bbox
top, so their number badges line up on the row's top edge.

The per-section content-hug re-fit (`_fit_bboxes_to_content_top`, Stage 6.15a)
grows one box's top up to seat fanned/off-track content or shrinks another's
down to hug its content, which can leave a flat-trunk row-mate off the row's
shared top edge with nothing to re-level it. A new closing pass,
`_level_row_mate_bbox_tops`, grows each contiguous row-mate's top up to the
row's highest -- the row's rendered height is already set by that tallest box,
so a shorter row-mate gains no canvas by hugging its own content.

- `_row_above_ceiling` (extracted from `_section_fit_top`) bounds the grow so a
  section sitting above a lower row is never grown into the inter-row gap;
  sections held down by that ceiling keep their offset.
- Rail-flagged sections carry a baked centreline and are excluded.
- `_level_row_mate_bbox_tops` subsumes `_top_align_side_entered_vertical_to_feeder`
  (which only re-levelled side-entered vertical sections and ignored the
  ceiling), so that pass is removed.
- Runtime guard `_guard_row_mate_bbox_tops_aligned` fails loudly if a row-mate
  is left off the row top (ceiling-held and rail sections exempt).
- Regression fixture `rowmate_flat_trunk_top_align` in `examples/topologies/`,
  wired into the gallery so CI's render-diff tracks it.

`test_section_bbox_top_hugs_content` and `test_compute_layout_rowspan_section_compacts_content`
are updated: a section flushed up to a taller row-mate keeps an intentional
empty band rather than hugging its own content.

Fixes #1462

## Test plan
- [ ] pytest passes (new invariant test `test_row_mate_bbox_tops_aligned`, updated hug/rowspan tests, regenerated guard golden baseline)
- [ ] ruff check + ruff format clean on whole repo
- [ ] Runtime validator `_guard_row_mate_bbox_tops_aligned` added and confirmed to fire on a forced violation
- [ ] Visual review of render preview
- [ ] Render-preview verdict captured

author: phronesis-cc-bot
body:
## Rotates the `phronesisintel.com` domain-verification token
`.well-known/agentic-verify.txt` → `5c3e5560315d2665411a2c1540b6b331b15d2e3ec8cd9c9096d950581f88837a`

Public by design — a verifier fetches it over plain HTTP; that *is* the mechanism. Not a secret.

## ⚠️ Routing correction — and it's the whole point
The dispatch said *"same `.well-known` static-serving path as the existing manifests"* and *"PR → owner merges."* But the existing manifests (`mcp.json` etc.) are served by the **app on `api.phronesisintel.com` (uvicorn)**, while this token must serve from **`phronesisintel.com` — a separate, Cloudflare-fronted static site whose source is THIS repo**, not the `phronesis` product repo.

**A PR to the product repo would have merged, deployed, changed nothing here, and burned the 24-hour token.** Verified before writing a line:
- `api.phronesisintel.com` → `Server: uvicorn` · `phronesisintel.com` → `Server: cloudflare`
- `agentic-verify` has **never** existed in the `phronesis` repo's history (`git log --all` on that path: empty)
- `phronesisintel.com/.well-known/mcp.json` returns **200 + HTML** — the SPA soft-200 that **ADR-0034 already warned about**. Status-code-only checks lie on this host.

## It's a ROTATE, not a create — and already the one-line design
The file **already existed and already served correctly** (`200 text/plain`), holding the prior token `f2082755…`. So "design it as a one-line change" is already satisfied: **the diff is literally `1 insertion, 1 deletion`.** If the token lapses, regenerate and swap the one string.

## Byte-exactness (deliberate)
- **64 bytes**, **no trailing newline** — matching the previous file, which proves `.gitattributes` `text=auto` leaves a newline-free single line untouched.
- Body is the token and nothing else. No markup, no whitespace.

## Flow
Merge → **Cloudflare Pages auto-deploys `main`** (no Republish needed) → click **"Check verification."**

**Verify the body before clicking:**
```bash
curl -s https://phronesisintel.com/.well-known/agentic-verify.txt; echo
# must print exactly:
# 5c3e5560315d2665411a2c1540b6b331b15d2e3ec8cd9c9096d950581f88837a
```
Check the **body**, not the status code — this host returns 200 + HTML for unmatched paths.

author: mariusstorhaug
body:
Reusable workflows that have co-located composite actions can now be correctly documented. This guide explains how to structure a reusable workflow so that its own composite actions are found and executed correctly, regardless of whether the workflow is invoked on a tagged release or a development branch.

The pattern uses `job.workflow_repository` and `job.workflow_sha` context variables (available on GitHub.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud) to ensure the reusable workflow checks itself out before calling any local actions — avoiding the common pitfall where action paths resolve to the caller's repository instead of the workflow's own repository.

## Technical Details

Added a new section "Reusable workflows with co-located composite actions" to `src/docs/Coding-Standards/GitHub-Actions.md`:
- Explains the problem: reusable workflows run in the caller's workspace, so relative action paths resolve to the wrong repository
- Provides the solution: use `job.workflow_repository` and `job.workflow_sha` to self-checkout the reusable workflow first
- Includes a complete YAML example showing the pattern
- Documents availability on GitHub.com and GHEC (not available on GHES)

Aligns with the same section added to AI-Platform documentation to ensure consistency across organizations.

A timeboxed feasibility study answering one question: **can the backend-neutral
determinism core (`run_workflow`, `WorkflowEvent`, deterministic replay) be
driven by a non-Postgres, embedded, single-writer persistence layer?**

- **Primary deliverable — the report:** [`docs/rnd/sqlite-feasibility.md`](docs/rnd/sqlite-feasibility.md)
  (executive summary + costed go/no-go up front, exhaustive grep-verified
  Postgres-coupling inventory, `StorageBackend` seam sizing, prototype evidence
  with an honest retry-recording fidelity caveat, test-portability analysis,
  edge→hub sync scoping, prior-art scan).
- **Disposable prototype (its exhibit):** `autumn-harvest/src/sqlite_spike/`
  (`mod`/`schema`/`store`/`queue`/`worker`) on embedded SQLite via `rusqlite`,
  reusing the core **wholesale** and reimplementing only persistence.
- **Smoke suite:** `autumn-harvest/tests/integration/sqlite_spike_tests.rs` — 4
  durability scenarios + cross-backend replay **executed in both directions**,
  plus **twelve persistence/handoff regression tests** (below). **20/20 pass.**

## Go/no-go one-liner

**FEASIBLE, but do not port in-crate.** The core is already backend-neutral and
was reused with **zero core-logic changes** (only additive, feature-gated module
registration) and **zero** Postgres-path cost — **recommend a separate companion
crate that depends on the core** (option ii); **decline the in-crate
`StorageBackend` trait** (option i). The decline rests **not** on hot-path
dispatch (a monomorphized generic `StorageBackend` is statically dispatched, zero
vtable cost) but on the two real legs: a **wide-but-half-empty trait** (the
class-(c) modules stub out across all ~35 `AsyncPgConnection` modules) and a **×2
integration test matrix** that covers SQLite only shallowly. Declining entirely
(option iii) is an acceptable fallback.

## Latest revision (round 10) — review loop closed: two prototype edges declined + documented

Wrapping the review loop. **No code change — two Codex P2 prototype edge-cases are
deliberately declined and documented in report §5.1 per the spike's timebox**
(well past the review ceiling; only healthy-run-killers get fixed this late, and
neither is one). **The go/no-go verdict is unchanged.**

- **DECLINED + DOCUMENTED (Codex P2) — workflow-handler panic seal (`mod.rs:642`).**
  A *contained workflow-handler panic* (`WorkflowOutcome::Failed { handler_panic:
  true }`) still seals a durable `WorkflowFailed` rather than being caught and
  retried/held — the same panic-containment simplification as the already-documented
  activity-body site, one level up. The spike deliberately holds the *replay-safety*
  invariant (engine-detected non-determinism is non-sealing/recoverable — issue
  #603, fixed in round 8) but does **not** implement *panic-containment*
  recoverability (issue #782, `catch_unwind` at the dispatch boundary →
  retryable/hold). A coherent scope line — replay-safety is in-scope and honored;
  fault-tolerant panic recovery is the documented simplification the productized
  engine provides.
- **DECLINED + DOCUMENTED (Codex P2) — redrive-reopened import mis-sealed
  (`mod.rs:365`).** The sealed-import reverse seal-scan recognizes the
  terminal-lifecycle set but not the `WorkflowRedriven` (issue #510) marker that
  *un-seals* a failed execution, so an import whose `WorkflowFailed` is followed by
  a redrive + in-flight work is stored `FAILED` and `run_until_blocked`
  short-circuits, never draining the post-redrive work. The real engine derives
  state from the *effective tail lifecycle* (a `WorkflowRedriven` after a
  `WorkflowFailed` ⇒ RUNNING). An advanced import shape unexercised by the four
  required scenarios, untouched on the default Postgres build.

Both live entirely in the from-scratch persistence/worker/import layer a companion
crate rebuilds while reusing the core unchanged — further evidence *for* the
separate-crate recommendation (§9), not against it. **Review loop closed for
prototype edge-cases.**

## Latest revision (round 9) — ctx.info().workflow_type is cross-backend-faithful (Codex P2, AC4)

One bounded AC4-fidelity fix. **The go/no-go verdict is unchanged.**

- **FIXED (Codex P2) — the SQLite runtime now threads `workflow_name` into replay** so `ctx.info().workflow_type` / `ctx.workflow_type()` observe the REAL registered handler name instead of `""`. `drive_one_cycle` reconstructed the `WorkflowContext` via the thin `run_workflow_with_state`, which hardcodes an empty `workflow_name`; a workflow reading the replay-safe `ctx.info().workflow_type` (an idempotency key, an activity input, a branch) therefore recorded `""`, and a PG-shaped import would diverge because the engine worker / `WorkflowReplayer` thread the real name from the execution row / history snapshot. **Fix:** pass the stored `workflow_name` into the full executor entry point (`run_workflow_with_state_history_policy_and_caps`) so both backends agree. New regression test `scenario_ctx_info_workflow_type_is_cross_backend_faithful` (the SQLite runtime observes the real name AND the resulting history replays clean on the engine `WorkflowReplayer` path, which threads `workflow_name` from the snapshot) — confirmed **red** on pre-fix code (observed `Completed(String(""))`), green after. Suite count 19 → 20. **No new `WorkflowEvent` variant, no migration, default Postgres build byte-unaffected.**

## Latest revision (round 8) — ND divergence is recoverable, not sealed (Codex P1); multi-timer drain-order declined (P2)

One deliberate, bounded exception to the otherwise-wrapped review loop: **one P1 fixed, one P2 declined+documented.** **The go/no-go verdict is unchanged.**

- **FIXED (Codex P1) — engine-detected non-determinism is now DETECT-AND-HELD (non-sealing, recoverable), not sealed FAILED.** After round-5 switched `drive_one_cycle` to `run_workflow_with_state` (whose `Failed` outcome carries `non_deterministic_details`), the `Failed` arm still appended a durable `WorkflowFailed` unconditionally — so a replay history/code divergence (e.g. a mismatched cross-backend import) permanently sealed the run FAILED, violating harvest's **core replay-safety invariant** (issue #603 / Phase 3.45: engine-detected non-determinism must **never** terminally fail a workflow — it blocks non-terminally so a rollback / re-import / code-fix can recover). It also risked persisting the divergent cycle's pending bookkeeping (`persist_terminal_bookkeeping`) first, polluting history against a rollback. **Fix:** the `Failed` arm now branches on `non_deterministic_details` — on a divergence it opens **no** persist transaction at all (no `WorkflowFailed`, no divergent-cycle bookkeeping persisted, execution left non-terminal) and surfaces the distinct, recoverable `SpikeError::NonDeterministic` (never `Stuck`, never a durable seal). This is a **scoped analogue** of the engine's non-terminal ND-block gate — the throwaway prototype captures only the essential *non-sealing / recoverable* property, not the engine's backoff + `nd_blocked_*` columns. Directly load-bearing for the spike's cross-backend-import path (a mismatched history is held for re-import, not sealed unrecoverably). New regression test `scenario_nondeterministic_import_is_recoverable_not_sealed` (an `other_activity`-named imported schedule vs. the handler's `work` diverges → recoverable ND, no `WorkflowFailed`, no bookkeeping persisted, byte-for-byte unchanged history, re-drive re-detects) — confirmed **red** on pre-fix code (which sealed `RunState::Failed`), green after.
- **DECLINED + DO

author: coppermilk
body:
The source and sink for live download %, ahead of wiring the relay (Phase 2b).

- **`minion_core/progress.py`**: a thread-local progress sink (`ContextVar`) —
  a caller installs it with `reporting_to`, an adapter feeds it via
  `current()`. Below `minion_core` so the fetch adapter and the services tier
  both use it without importing each other (import-direction law).
- **`fetch.download`**: runs yt-dlp under `Popen` with `--newline` and a
  `--progress-template`; a reader thread parses the percent live and reports
  it to the sink, while `proc.wait(timeout)` keeps the robust total bound
  (survives a silent hang) and the `--print` filepath is read from stdout
  (`PROGRESS:` lines filtered, so a progress leak into stdout can't fool path
  extraction).
- **svc-fetch async job**: `_Job` gains `progress`, `JobStore.progress`
  records it, `/jobs/{id}` reports it, and `_run_job` wraps the run in
  `reporting_to` so a Step's live percent lands on the job.

Phase 2b wires the relay to poll this and edit the bar at an adequate step.

## Note to validate on the NAS
yt-dlp's `--progress-template` output is read from **stderr** (its progress
stream); if a build emits it on stdout instead, live % won't animate (the
filepath extraction still works, since `PROGRESS:` lines are filtered). Worth
a quick check in `svc-fetch` logs after deploy.

## Gates
ruff + format clean, mypy strict (58 files), full pytest + 12 services/tests
green. New tests: a fake yt-dlp emitting `PROGRESS:` lines → `download`
reports `[10, 55, 100]`; a Step reporting via the sink → `/jobs/{id}` shows
`progress: 42`.

## Summary

- New `claude/setup-tool/` Go module: cross-platform CLI for one-command dev onboarding
- New `.github/workflows/build-setup-tool.yml`: builds binaries for linux/amd64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64, windows/amd64 and uploads them to a GitHub Release

## What the tool does

1. **GitHub Device Flow auth** — no client secret needed; user visits a URL and approves
2. **Org membership check** — verifies active membership in `fermrad` org (requires `read:org` scope)
3. **SSH key** — finds `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub`, `id_ecdsa.pub`, or `id_rsa.pub`; generates a new Ed25519 key if none exist
4. **SSH config** — appends `claude-dev.ferm.dk` block to `~/.ssh/config` if not already present
5. **Claude skills** — sparse-clones AI-tools, symlinks skills to `~/.claude/commands/` (macOS/Linux) or copies (Windows)
6. **Server provisioning** — dispatches `provision-claude-user.yml` in infrastructure with `github_username` + `public_key`

## Build

The OAuth Client ID is injected at build time via `-ldflags="-X main.githubClientID=..."`. Store it in the `FERM_SETUP_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` org secret before merging.

To release: push a tag `ferm-setup/v1.0.0` — the workflow builds all platforms and creates a GitHub Release.

## Test plan

- [ ] `FERM_SETUP_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` secret added to the fermrad org
- [ ] Trigger `build-setup-tool.yml` manually — all four binaries build successfully
- [ ] Run the darwin-arm64 binary locally — completes all 6 steps end to end

## Password vertical (#410)

The last of the #404 domain-value verticals: brings `common::password::Password` onto the ADR-0063 §2 **secret** derive and finishes the ADR-0065 client-validation adoption on the two auth forms that still used raw password inputs.

Server/host threading was already complete on `main` (#407/#414), so this is confined to the type surface and the two forms.

### Changes
- **`common/src/password.rs`** — `#[derive(Clone, StrNewtype)]` + `#[str_newtype(secret)]`; the hand-written redacting `Debug` and inherent `as_str()` are gone (the derive supplies the identical `Password([redacted])` `Debug`, plus `AsRef<str>` + `TryFrom<String>`). `FromStr`/`hash`/`verify`/`PasswordError` unchanged. Callers moved to `.as_ref()`.
- **`RegisterPage` / `ResetPasswordPage`** — raw password `<input>`s → `<ValidatedInput<Password>>` with disable-until-valid, mirroring the already-shipped `LoginPage`.
- **e2e** — one too-short-password assertion each on the register and reset forms (inline error + disabled submit); added a `SEL.newPassword` selector.

### Non-goals (deliberate)
- No serde bridge on `Password` and no `#[server]`/storage signature change — the secret exception keeps the wire arg `String`, parsed on entry.
- The stored-hash exfiltration guarantee stays #17's `PasswordHash` territory. The spec records why the #400 `ProfferedInviteCode`/`InviteCode` split does **not** map to a plaintext password (inbound plaintext ≠ at-rest hash; no-serde already makes `Password` un-returnable).

author: posthog[bot]
body:
## Problem

A subset of query-service (personal-API-key) HogQL queries were failing deterministically with an opaque error:

```
Code: 50. Unknown type Variant(DateTime64(6, 'America/New_York'), String)
```

This surfaced as a sustained, user-facing regression for one team on the EU query service, and it materially reshaped that service's failure budget.

Root cause: when a query mixes value types that ClickHouse can't reduce to a common type — the branches of an `if()` / `multiIf()` / `coalesce()` / `CASE`, or the columns of a `UNION` — ClickHouse resolves the column to a `Variant` (via `use_variant_as_common_type`). `clickhouse_driver` has no `Variant` column reader, so it fails client-side during result deserialization with `UnknownTypeError` (code 50).

Because that error is a client-side `clickhouse_driver.errors.Error` and not a `ServerException`, `wrap_clickhouse_query_error` passed it straight through. It then classified as a generic `ERROR` (SLO outcome `FAILURE`) and leaked to the user as an opaque platform crash — even though it's really a query-shape problem, the same class as `NO_COMMON_TYPE` (which we already treat as a user-safe error).

I reproduced the exact type signature through the query path:

```sql
SELECT if(rand() > 0, toTimeZone(now(), 'America/New_York'), 'fallback')
-- Code: 50. Unknown type Variant(DateTime64(6, 'America/New_York'), String)
```

## Changes

Wrap the client-side `UnknownTypeError` for `Variant` types into a new user-safe `CHQueryErrorUnsupportedVariantType` (an `ExposedCHQueryError`, code 50). This means it:

- classifies as `USER_ERROR`, which `_classify_error_for_slo` maps to SLO outcome `SUCCESS` — so these stop eating the query-service error budget, matching how `NO_COMMON_TYPE` is handled.
- returns an actionable message instead of an opaque crash: it names the offending `Variant(...)` type and tells the user to cast the mismatched branches to a common type (for example, wrap them in `toString()`).

The match is scoped to `Variant(...)` specifically. Any other genuinely-unknown type still passes through unchanged, so a real platform gap in type support stays visible as a failure.

> [!NOTE]
> This does not make the ill-typed query return data — there is no sane common type for a DateTime and a String. It converts an opaque, budget-eating platform failure into a clear, actionable user error, which is the right product behavior here.

## How did you test this code?

Added `posthog/test/test_errors.py` (a no-DB `SimpleTestCase`):

- A parameterized case for the `DateTime64/String` and `Float64/String` Variant signatures asserts the wrapped error is user-safe (`ExposedCHQueryError`), classifies as `USER_ERROR`, and carries the actionable `toString()` guidance. Regression it catches: dropping or narrowing the Variant branch in `wrap_clickhouse_query_error` would revert these to opaque generic `ERROR`/`FAILURE`.
- A negative case asserts a non-Variant `UnknownTypeError` is returned untouched and still classifies as `ERROR` — guarding the scope so genuine unsupported-type platform gaps stay visible.

I (Claude) ran the suite locally: `pytest posthog/test/test_errors.py` — 3 passed. `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean. I could not run the full ClickHouse-backed query path in this environment (no local CH/Postgres), but confirmed the exact `Variant(DateTime64(6, 'America/New_York'), String)` signature is what the query path produces via a live query.

## Docs update

<!-- Add the `skip-inkeep-docs` label if this PR should not trigger an automatic docs update from the Inkeep agent. -->

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

Authored by Claude Code (Opus 4.8) from an SLO inbox report about EU query-service `UnknownTypeError` failures. I invoked the `/writing-tests` skill before adding the regression test.

Investigation path: traced `query_service` to personal-API-key HogQL queries; pulled the failing events from the SLO stream to confirm the type signature, region, and that the query type was raw `HogQLQuery` (so PostHog can't rewrite the user's expression); reproduced the exact Variant signature through the query path; found the prior-art fix in `groups_query_runner.py` (which casts branches to `toString` for the `Variant(Float64, String)` case) and the existing `NO_COMMON_TYPE` handling. Rejected two alternatives: globally disabling `use_variant_as_common_type` (would regress currently-working queries that wrap a Variant-producing expression, e.g. `toString(if(...))`), and implementing a `Variant` binary reader in `clickhouse_driver` (high risk, untestable without a live CH producing Variant in the Native protocol). Chose the minimal, precedent-aligned wrap at the single error choke point.

body:
## Why

Multi-coupling papers are common: **51 of 347 GT papers (~15%) have entries in ≥2 coupling types**, and `evaluate.py` correctly grades `predicted ∈ all GT types`. A full-corpus audit (every GT paper × every plane its upstream docs reference) found planes the upstream repo tracks but our GT never ingested — each traceable to an upstream doc-link defect invisible to `build_ground_truth.py`'s same-line `[reference]` parser.

## What

3 new entries (2 papers), data files ingested via the sanctioned `populate_data_from_repo` path (GT numbers remain O'Hare's):

| Paper | New plane | Upstream file | Why it was missed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2009.04517 (Casimir) | AxionNeutron | `limit_data/AxionNeutron/Casimir.txt` (46 pts) | `docs/an.md` links the file **without `.txt`** |
| 2009.04517 (Casimir) | AxionProton | `limit_data/AxionProton/Casimir.txt` (46 pts) | `docs/app.md` links the file **without `.txt`** |
| 2205.01637 (Planck+BAO) | AxionEDM | `limit_data/AxionEDM/PlanckBao.txt` (10 pts) | `docs/aedm.md` Planck+BAO line links the **wrong file** (`SN1987A.txt`) |

Conventions are canonical per file headers (`g_an`/`g_ap` dimensionless, `g_d [GeV^-2]` under this repo's `g_angamma` label); the two Casimir curves are byte-identical upstream, physically right for a nucleon-symmetric fifth-force bound.

## Audit trail — candidates rejected

8 candidate papers surfaced; 6 rejected on verification: 1508.01798 / 1711.08999 / 2102.11740 (projection-only planes — out of measured-limits scope), 1905.13650 (passing citation, not an ingested limit), 2011.08693 (file is the `fa/` plane GT already has), 1902.04644 (upstream docs link a **nonexistent** `AxionProton/CASPEr_ZULF.txt`).

## Impact (before/after, final2_opus_n1 replay)

- `2009.04517` (predicted AxionNeutron): **misclassified + `no_comparable_gt` → correct + curve-graded**. Classification accuracy 289/313 → 290/314; compared pool +1.
- `2205.01637`: no change to its current grading (predicted AxionPhoton, still wrong) — the entry completes GT so a future AxionEDM prediction grades instead of falling into `no_comparable_gt`.
- No existing entry modified; 125 GT/convention tests pass.

Upstream doc defects noted for eventual upstream report: missing `.txt` in two Casimir links, wrong link target on the aedm Planck+BAO line.

author: luddwichr
body:
## Why

A shootout-decided knockout match had to be entered with the penalty goals folded into one final score — a convention that existed only in `docs/requirements.md`, was invisible in the product, and was silently applied by the ESPN sync (REVIEW.md §9.1). The folded scores also polluted team stats: penalty kicks counted as goals and shootout wins as wins (§9.2).

## What

- **Model**: `Result` stores the real regulation/extra-time score plus optional `homeShootoutGoals`/`awayShootoutGoals`. Invariants (both set together, knockout only, level regular score, decisive shootout) are enforced at the persistence boundary.
- **Entry**: while a knockout score is level, `ScoreDialog` automatically shows a second stepper pair ("🎯 Elfmeterschießen") — a knockout match can't end level, so no extra control is needed. Saving a level shootout is blocked with a child-register error.
- **Display**: match cards show the folded score (penalty goals added) with a small "i.E." badge; the accessible label speaks "nach Elfmeterschießen".
- **Semantics**: winner resolution uses the folded score; team stats keep the real goals, so shootout matches count as draws per FIFA statistical convention (fixes §9.2).
- **Sync**: the ESPN provider passes `score` and `shootoutScore` through separately; the provider-agnostic glue folds any feed data violating the invariants instead of producing a `Result` the validator would reject wholesale (which would wipe state on reload).
- **Persistence**: `SCHEMA_VERSION` 2 with a one-shot v1 localStorage migration (adopt → persist under new key → drop old key) and `parseImport` still reading v1 export files. Pre-v2 folded scores are absorbed as-is (indistinguishable after the fact, documented).
- **Docs**: `requirements.md` and `tournament-rules.md` updated; addressed findings removed from REVIEW.md.

## Testing

- `check:code` green: typecheck, format, lint, 705 unit tests (68 files, ~97.4% stmt coverage), opengrep, gitleaks
- e2e: 122 passed (incl. a new shootout entry → folded-score badge → winner-propagation test), PWA suite 3 passed, size-limit within budget
- Verified visually: dialog shows Tore → 🎯 Elfmeterschießen → Karten; card shows folded score with "i.E." between the values

author: sbeurnier
body:
Follow-up to #10872 / #10875, separate because it touches a scheduling parameter rather than strides.

`_p_matmul`'s `NUM_SMS: tl.constexpr` receives the launch grid (`grid if opt_flags.is_persistent else 0`). Below SM saturation the grid is `batch_size * cdiv(M, block_m) * grid_n * split_k`, i.e. a function of the runtime token count, so the persistent matmul recompiles every `block_m` step of M — exactly in the small-batch regime where persistent mode is selected.

`NUM_SMS` is only used as the persistent-loop stride (`tl.range(tl.program_id(0), num_blocks, NUM_SMS, ...)`) and the epilogue tile counter, so it can be a plain runtime argument. `tl.num_programs(0)` equals it by construction if that form is preferred. The non-persistent `_matmul` keeps its constexpr since its caller always passes 0.

Verified on the released package (sglang `triton_kernel` MoE backend, gpt-oss-20b on 1×H100): greedy outputs byte-identical to stock; on top of #10875 it reduced cold-start p95 TTFT 1384ms → 1098ms in a paired 200-request serving A/B.

body:
# WS-AUTH-001-05B PR Trust Bundle

## Chunk

`WS-AUTH-001-05B` - Authority Idempotency And Invalidation Foundation

## Goal

Make the ten sensitive authority mutations concurrency-safe and retry-safe,
with typed replay results and exactly linked success/invalidation evidence.

## Human-Approved Intent

The human approved the repaired L1 contract and its semantic chunk boundary.
The work remains backend foundation only; AUTH-06 must not start automatically.

## What Changed

- Migration `0019` adds immutable actor-scoped idempotency reservations, a
  pending-to-committed transition, typed replay references, database timestamps,
  a deferred pending guard, and guarded downgrade custody.
- Strict frozen request variants cover exactly ten mutation operations and hash
  only canonical, bounded, server-derived facts.
- The authorization service reserves, replays, records privacy-neutral
  mismatches, validates concrete success evidence, constructs invalidations,
  and completes the claim in one caller-owned transaction.
- PostgreSQL links actor, claim, operation, entity, resource, target, concrete
  cause, request, correlation, and project context and closes committed records
  to later evidence.
- Behavior tests cover all ten operations plus project-grant replacement,
  exact and mismatched concurrency, rollback, privacy, direct bypasses,
  immutable state, and upgrade/downgrade races.

## Why It Changed

Later actor, grant, and permission chunks need a trustworthy retry boundary.
Without it, a lost response or concurrent retry could duplicate authority
state, disclose another request's result, or leave misleading audit evidence.

## Design Chosen

The unique namespace is actor kind, actor reference, operation, and client key.
Only the canonical request digest and typed response reference persist. The
existing shared audit service remains the sole application writer, while
PostgreSQL independently enforces linkage and immutability. Repositories never
commit, roll back, retry, or create sessions.

## Alternatives Rejected

- Storing raw requests or response bodies was rejected for privacy and schema
  stability.
- Application-only idempotency and evidence validation was rejected because
  direct SQL must fail closed.
- A parallel invalidation table was rejected because AUTH-05A already owns the
  shared authority evidence envelope.
- Route, grant, actor, cache, queue, and consumer implementation remains in
  later owning chunks.

## Scope Control

No API route, permission evaluator, actor/grant table, token verifier, cache,
queue, invalidation consumer, product authorization decision, dependency,
workflow, or CI threshold changed.

## Product Behavior

There is no new externally reachable product behavior. Internal callers can
claim a mutation, receive an exact committed replay, or receive a private
mismatch signal. Completion requires one concrete success plus one linked
invalidation event.

## Acceptance Criteria Proof

- Independent concurrent retries serialize through PostgreSQL and produce one
  committed result and one evidence pair.
- All ten operations and the project replacement branch have positive typed and
  database-linked proof.
- Request target/project facts are bound to the success, response, and replay;
  cross-actor, wrong-entity, wrong-target, and mismatched-cause paths fail.
- Committed rows reject new success or invalidation evidence and reject update,
  delete, and truncate.
- Rejected secrets and malformed Unicode are absent from strings, args,
  diagnostics, public state, cause, and context.
- Downgrade is observed waiting for an actual PostgreSQL writer lock, refuses
  non-empty custody, preserves compatible pre-0019 rows, and restores head.

## Tests And Checks Run

- Focused behavior/migration suite: 26 passed.
- Authorization subsystem coverage: 96.88 percent.
- Isolated-runner suite: 16 passed.
- Ruff, 95.3 percent docstring coverage, stale contract scans, changed Markdown
  links, internal review evidence structure, and diff integrity passed or are
  rerun after this bundle is finalized.
- A local repository-wide isolated suite reached approximately 94 percent with
  no failure before intentional interruption after two hours on an overloaded
  four-core host. GitHub Backend owns the authoritative full-suite and global
  coverage result.

## Test Delta

Tests are additive or strengthened. Existing audit assertions were adapted for
mandatory idempotency linkage, and positive operation coverage replaced weaker
assertions. No raises guard, skip, xfail, coverage threshold, or test selection
was removed or weakened.

## CI Integrity

No workflow, dependency, package script, exclusion, or coverage setting
changed. GitHub Backend must still enforce the repository-wide 78 percent floor
and the existing artifact-foundation 90 percent floor.

## Reviewer Results

Exact runtime SHA `e0838908dfa19227fab2f73e32c9b0c94dd39bb4` passed senior
engineering, architecture, product/ops, docs, reuse/dedup, QA/test, test delta,
CI integrity, and security/auth/privacy review with no remaining findings.

## External Review

Pending GitHub checks, CodeRabbit, and human review.

## Remaining Risks

- Database-owner or DDL credentials can bypass normal-DML triggers; production
  must use the documented non-owner runtime role.
- This chunk emits invalidation evidence but intentionally has no consumer.
- Replay references are internal; future routes must reload and reauthorize the
  current resource before disclosure.

## Follow-Up Work

After merge, post-merge memory, stop, and a separate human start, AUTH-06 may
implement canonical actor profiles and identity links. Later chunks own the
authorization kernel, grants, resource cutovers, and invalidation consumers.

## Human Review Focus

Review the migration triggers and downgrade lock ordering, canonical digest
boundary, request-to-evidence binding, mismatch privacy, and proof that no
route or product authorization behavior entered scope.

## Human Merge Ownership

Only the human may approve and merge this PR. Internal or external checks do
not authorize merge.

author: scsmith
body:
The pinned SDK (1.11.4) only supported zod `^3.23.8`; the stale Dependabot PR #6 would have bumped zod to v4 alone and broken tool schema validation. That PR's "security-updates" grouping is just a catch-all label unrelated to any actual CVE — `dependabot.yml` groups every allowed update (major-only, since minor/patch are ignored) under that name, and this repo has 0 open Dependabot alerts. 1.29.0 explicitly supports `zod ^3.25 || ^4.0`, so bumping both together is the real fix.

Also bumps axios 1.6.2→1.18.1, fixing 5 unrelated vulnerabilities (1 critical) in this repo's own direct axios usage.

Two compile breaks from the SDK's own API changes (unrelated to zod): `publisher` was replaced by a flat `websiteUrl` field, and the static `capabilities.tools` list (incomplete, schema-less, missing `sendEmail` entirely) doesn't belong in the constructor — capabilities are already derived correctly from the `server.tool()` registrations below it.

Verified by running the built server over stdio and driving real MCP protocol traffic: `tools/list` schema generation, zod v4 validation errors on bad input, and all four tool handlers all behave correctly.

Closes #6 (superseded — that PR bumps zod alone without the SDK).

author: gomessguii
body:
## Problema

`/settings/segments` responde **500** (`INTERNAL_ERROR`) em qualquer ambiente subido a partir deste stack.

A tela é um proxy: o CRM recebe `GET /api/v1/segments` e repassa ao evo-flow via `EvoFlow::Client`. Só que o `docker-compose.swarm.yaml` **nunca declarou o serviço evo-flow**, nem as variáveis que o client precisa. Sem `AUTH_APIKEY_INTEGRATION_LOCAL`, o CRM levanta `EvoFlow::ConfigurationError` já na construção do client (`app/services/evo_flow/client.rb:99`), **antes de qualquer chamada de rede** — o controller só faz `rescue EvoFlow::HTTPError`, então a exceção escapa e vira 500 opaco.

Diagnosticado no staging (`evo_crm_test`), onde nenhum dos três serviços existia:

```
ERROR -- : Internal Server Error: EvoFlow::ConfigurationError - AUTH_APIKEY_INTEGRATION_LOCAL is not set
  /app/app/services/evo_flow/client.rb:99:in 'EvoFlow::Client#validate_config!'
  /app/app/controllers/api/v1/evo_flow/segments_controller.rb:92:in 'Class#new'
  /app/app/controllers/api/v1/evo_flow/segments_controller.rb:28:in '#index'
```

## O que muda

**3 serviços novos.** O evo-flow não sobe sozinho:

- `evocrm_evoflow` — porta 3334 (a porta do projeto, conforme o `.env.example` do evo-flow). Usa um Postgres **dedicado** (`evo_campaign`), criado no boot junto com as migrations; o banco do CRM não é tocado.
- `evocrm_clickhouse` — exigido por `STORAGE_MODE=clickhouse`. O evo-flow cria database e tabelas sozinho.
- `evocrm_rabbitmq` — o `BrokerModule` aborta o boot se `BROKER_TYPE` não estiver setado, mesmo com `QUEUE_MODE=direct`. Usuário dedicado porque o `guest` do RabbitMQ recusa conexão remota.

**4 envs** em `evocrm_crm` e `evocrm_crm_sidekiq`:

```
EVO_FLOW_ENABLED=true
EVO_FLOW_API_URL=http://evocrm_evoflow:3334/api/v1
AUTH_APIKEY_INTEGRATION_LOCAL=    # vazio no template; mesmo valor nos 3 serviços
EVO_FLOW_ALLOW_INSECURE=true
```

`EVO_FLOW_ALLOW_INSECURE` não é opcional aqui: o stack roda `RAILS_ENV=production` sobre uma URL `http://` interna, e sem a flag o client se recusa a mandar a chave em cleartext — ou seja, **o 500 voltaria mesmo com todo o resto cabeado**.

Mais: 2 volumes (`evocrm_clickhouse_data`, `evocrm_rabbitmq_data`) e o cabeçalho de segredos do arquivo atualizado com os 3 novos.

Segredos ficam **vazios**, seguindo a convenção do template (`# Ex.: gere com "openssl rand -hex 32"`).

## Validação

Aplicado no staging (`evo_crm_test`) antes de virar commit. Os 3 serviços subiram, o evo-flow criou o `evo_campaign` no Postgres, rodou as migrations e criou as 16 tabelas no ClickHouse. O caminho que estava 500 agora responde 200:

```
CRM → evo-flow (mesmo client do SegmentsController):
OK: {"success" => true, "data" => {"segments" => [], "total" => 0, "page" => 1, "limit" => 20}}
```

Tela confirmada funcionando no browser.

## Fora de escopo (ficam abertos)

- **`EvoFlow::ConfigurationError` não tratada** no `SegmentsController` → misconfig continua virando 500 opaco em vez de 503 legível. É outro repo (`evo-ai-crm-community`), PR separada.
- **CRM assume porta 3000** (`EvoFlow::Client::DEFAULT_API_URL` e `.env.example:275`), divergindo do 3334 do evo-flow. Mesma PR do item acima.
- **`evo-flow-community:develop` está congelada em 04/jul** — o evo-flow não aparece em nenhum workflow de publish do umbrella (só no `release.yml`, que roda em tag). Mesmo padrão do EVO-1998.
- **Journey triggers** no staging apontam para um Kafka inexistente (`localhost:9092`, pois `KAFKA_BROKERS_INTERNAL` não está setada). Não afeta Segments (`QUEUE_MODE=direct`).

## Summary by Sourcery

Add EvoFlow and its required infrastructure services to the swarm stack so the CRM Segments feature works in swarm-based environments.

New Features:
- Introduce evo-flow service (evocrm_evoflow) to serve segments and event tracking behind the CRM.
- Add dedicated ClickHouse service as evo-flow event storage backend.
- Add dedicated RabbitMQ service as evo-flow message broker.

Enhancements:
- Wire CRM and Sidekiq services to evo-flow via new environment variables, including API URL, shared auth key, and insecure-HTTP allowance.
- Define persistent volumes for ClickHouse and RabbitMQ data within the swarm stack.
- Document new secrets and configuration required for evo-flow, ClickHouse, and RabbitMQ in the swarm compose file.

author: devantler
body:
> 🤖 Generated by the Daily AI Engineer

## Why

Parallel agent sessions are supposed to work in isolated git worktrees. In submodules they often
**silently don't** — they all resolve into the same shared checkout, so two sessions edit one physical
tree and a commit can land on another session's branch. Yesterday this was found actively colliding
three live worktrees, two of them the sibling agent's.

We knew it kept coming back but not *why* — the docs said "some routine submodule operation" rewrites
the setting. **It's `git submodule update --init`, the exact command our own instructions tell agents to
run.** Reproduced: the setting is absent before the command and present after. So every time an agent
populates a submodule, it re-breaks isolation for itself and everyone else. That's the loop, and it's
why the fix never stuck.

## What

Make initialising and repairing a submodule **one operation** instead of two, so isolation can't be
left broken:

- A helper that inits at the pinned commit, repairs, and then **probes** — failing closed if the
  worktree still isn't isolated (it also has a read-only `--check` that sweeps every submodule).
- Point the contract at the helper instead of the bare command.
- Record the reproduced cause in the diagnosis doc, and mark the submodule that regressed again.

Verified both directions: the check exits non-zero on a deliberately broken submodule (naming it), and
clean across all 19 once repaired.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
## Context & Rationale

Currently, our deployment configuration does not enforce HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS). This leaves returning visitors vulnerable to SSL-stripping and transit-modification attacks if they attempt to connect over an unencrypted HTTP connection. 

To mitigate this, we are adding a standard 1-year HSTS header directly to the global route in `netlify.toml`. This ensures returning browsers interact with our service exclusively via encrypted HTTPS. This transport-level configuration is managed at the CDN layer to guarantee zero performance overhead or latency on the application runtime logic.

## Key Decisions

- **1-Year Max Age:** Set to `max-age=31536000` (31,536,000 seconds) to comply with industry standard recommendations for HSTS duration.
- **Isolated Scope:** Explicitly omitted the `includeSubDomains` and `preload` directives. This ensures transport security policies are strictly constrained to the primary domain and do not inadvertently impact independent subdomains.
- **Defensive Alignment:** Carefully preserved all existing security headers (`X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options`, and `X-XSS-Protection`) exactly as they were configured to maintain our current defenses against clickjacking, MIME-type sniffing, and cross-site scripting (XSS).

## Changes

### `netlify.toml`
Updated the global headers definition (`/*`) to include the `Strict-Transport-Security` header.

```toml
[[headers]]
  for = "/*"
  [headers.values]
    Strict-Transport-Security = "max-age=31536000"
    X-Content-Type-Options = "nosniff"
    X-Frame-Options = "DENY"
    X-XSS-Protection = "1; mode=block"
```

## Verification & Testing

- [x] Verified that the `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000` header is returned on the global wildcard path.
- [x] Confirmed the header does not contain `includeSubDomains` or `preload`.
- [x] Verified existing security headers are still served alongside the new HSTS header without modification.

author: iichukissii
body:
Closes #240. **Two production bugs, plus the CI blind spot that hid them.** All three found by box validation on industryflow.local.

## 1. `ml_service` could not load a single notebook-trained model

`inference.py` loaded every model with `runs:/<run_id>/model`. **MLflow 3 does not store a logged model under its run** — it lands in `<experiment>/models/m-<id>/artifacts/`. Listing the box's MinIO bucket after training in the real kernel image:

```
mlflow/7/models/m-f44cdc459a2d4667891f6efc2c2fe091/artifacts/model.skops
```

**No object contains the run id at all.** The tracking server 404s on the run-scoped path and the client retries until it hangs.

| URI | on the box |
|---|---|
| `runs:/<run_id>/model` | **hangs, then fails** |
| `models:/<model_id>` | **resolves** |

The tracking store already holds `source_run_id → model_id`, so `resolve_model_uri()` asks it instead of assuming a path — falling back to `runs:/` for artifacts logged by older clients. **ADR-0027's gate resolves the same way:** a gate that inspects a different artifact from the one the service loads is inspecting nothing.

## 2. The gate refused a model that demonstrably works

It treated *any* declared-but-absent package as fatal, and rejected a model the kernel had just trained because the artifact declared **`psutil`** — a transitive dep of the kernel's mlflow client. That same model then loaded and scored with a delta of **exactly 0.0**.

MLflow's `requirements.txt` is the **training environment**, not the load requirement. So absence is now fatal for exactly two things:

1. **the flavor's own framework** (the torch case), and
2. **the serializers** that wrote the artifact's bytes.

Everything else is recorded, never judged. *A gate that rejects what the service can serve is worse than no gate — it teaches people to route around it.*

The torch refusal is now anchored on the framework being **installed**, not on `import mlflow.pytorch` succeeding: mlflow imports its frameworks lazily, so that import can succeed in an image with no torch and would quietly wave the model through.

## 3. Why CI was green over all of it

The round-trip gate crossed the real image boundary — but used a **local artifact directory**, where `runs:/` still resolves. The deployment proxies artifacts to **S3/MinIO**, and that is where it breaks. The harness now stands up MinIO, passes MLflow the deployment's own artifact flags, and **loads through `ml_service`'s resolver** rather than a URI the product does not use.

ADR-0026 dec 6: the box's job is post-merge discovery, and its findings become CI checks. This is that, exactly.

## Box-validated

```
resolved: models:/m-f44cdc459a2d4667891f6efc2c2fe091
ADR-0027 gate: COMPATIBLE | flavor: mlflow.sklearn
  LOADED and scored in the serving image: max delta vs the kernel = 0.00e+00
```

## Summary

- replace manual `git status --porcelain=v1` parsing with NUL-delimited `git diff --name-only -z` output
- preserve paths containing spaces and Git-quoted characters when staging versioned files
- add a temporary-repository regression test for leading-space unstaged statuses and clean/empty diffs

`changedPaths()` trimmed each porcelain line before removing the two status columns and separator. For unstaged changes, trimming removed the leading status-column space, so the later slice removed the first character of the actual path.

`release:prepare` now stages every tracked file changed by versioning without truncating its path. A clean versioning result still produces no paths, so the existing empty-release refusal remains in effect.

author: ianfrantchesco
body:
## Resumo

Decisão de produto do **ponto 6** da revisão de fallback (você escolheu **"separar em dois campos"**). O campo `is_fallback` codificava **dois conceitos diferentes** conforme o domínio: no agente = card sintético sem eficácia comparativa; no crônico = fármaco não encontrado na tabela de medicamentos. O frontend mostrava o mesmo selo "Diretriz" para os dois — enganoso, porque no crônico o selo na verdade sinalizava "não catalogado", não nível de evidência.

## Mudança — cada campo com UM significado

- **`is_fallback`** = card sintético montado da diretriz por falta de eficácia comparativa. `enrich` (agente real)=`False`; `synthetic` (agente)=`True`; `_build_card` (crônico)=**`False`** (o crônico não tem conceito de eficácia comparativa, então não é "fallback por falta dela").
- **`medicamento_nao_catalogado`** (novo) = o nome do fármaco da diretriz não foi resolvido na tabela de fármacos (via/classe/posologia/interações podem faltar). `synthetic`=`(drow is None)`; crônico=`(med_row is None)`; real=`False`.

## Frontend

O selo "Diretriz" (amarelo) fica só para `is_fallback`; novo selo **"Não catalogado"** (âmbar, cor distinta) para `medicamento_nao_catalogado`. `bacterias.html` não usa o campo (confirmado). Efeito: crônico resolvido → sem selo (igual a hoje); crônico não resolvido → "Não catalogado" (antes mostrava, erradamente, "Diretriz"); agente sintético → "Diretriz", e ganha "Não catalogado" quando o fármaco não foi resolvido (antes invisível).

## Como foi verificado

**Byte-comparison** contra `origin/main` (5 domínios, 352 patologias):
- Todo card ganha a chave `medicamento_nao_catalogado` (bool, **0 ausentes**).
- `is_fallback` muda em **179 cards, TODOS crônicos e TODOS `True→False`** (nenhum card de agente afetado).
- No crônico, `{is_fallback=True antes}` == `{nao_catalogado=True agora}` — semântica migrada **exatamente**.
- `mypy app.py` → 0 erros (o novo parâmetro obrigatório de `_montar_card` confirma que os 3 produtores foram atualizados).
- `pytest` → **86/86** (85 + 1 novo cobrindo a separação nos 5 domínios), verde na raiz e sob a condição do CI (`/tmp`).

## Escopo

Adiciona um campo aditivo, ajusta o significado de `is_fallback` no crônico, e adiciona um selo no frontend. Rótulos do selo/nome do campo ajustáveis se a equipe médica preferir.

Este é o último dos 2 segmentos de produto (S35 → S36) e encerra os 6 pontos da revisão de risco clínico do fallback.

author: llun
body:
Stacked on #76 (`claude/offline-4-conflict-detection`) — the only base where this compiles, since everything it touches lands there. **Retarget to `main` once #76 merges.**

## The bug

Found in the #76 review (round 4) and deliberately deferred, since it needs a change to a persisted model and to what the replay pushes.

A save PATCHes content **and** title, but `DraftBaseline` recorded only `serverUpdatedAt` + `markdown` — so the decision could only ever see the body. A web rename leaves the body untouched, which is precisely the body rule's `.push` (correctly — a rename must not raise a conflict dialog), and the replay's title PATCH then quietly reverted it to whatever title the draft was created with. **The co-author's rename disappeared with no prompt.**

## The rule: a merge, not a dialog

Title and body are independent fields. `DraftBaseline` now carries the server's `title`, and `draftSyncDecision` returns `.push(title:)` — the title the replay must PATCH, resolved by the private `draftTitleOutcome` rather than left for each call site to pick, so **no replay site can push a stale title**. Given the baseline's title `b`, the draft's `d`, the server's `s`:

| condition | outcome |
|---|---|
| `b` or `s` unknown, or the server is no newer than the baseline | push `d` |
| `s == d` (already agree) | push `d` |
| `d == b` — only the server renamed | **adopt `s`** |
| `s == b` — only the user renamed | push `d` |
| all three differ — two renames | **`.conflict`** (the existing pill + sheet) |

`title` is optional, so drafts and cache entries written before this field decode as nil — the established pattern for `baseline`/`lastPushedMarkdown` — and a **titleless legacy baseline behaves exactly as before**: nothing adopted, no conflict invented.

**Adopting advances the baseline's title with it** (`adoptedBaseline`), and only on an adopt. Otherwise a *second* remote rename reads as "both renamed" and raises a conflict the user never created; and writing the *user's* rename into the baseline would make the next reconcile mistake the server's older title for a rename they never made and adopt it back over theirs.

## The part that isn't in the filed bug

Fixing the replay alone leaks. **The editor never refetches on foreground — it only flushes — and foreground/reconnect is exactly when `syncPendingDrafts` runs.** So a background replay can adopt a rename, push it, and land it entirely behind an open screen still showing the old title, whose next keystroke flushes `title` and puts the old name straight back. Closed by three things, each with a named regression test:

- `reconcileDraft` adopts the resolved title onto the screen **and** the stored draft (`adoptServerTitle`, which rewrites the draft without starting a save) — including in its `.pendingSync`/`.failed` early return, whose funnel is `saveNow`, which PATCHes `savedTitle` with no reconcile of its own.
- `apply`'s **dirty** branch adopts too: `reconcileDraft` is unreachable while the screen is dirty, so a stored draft would keep its pre-rename title — and unsaved local work normally outranks the server in the precedence chain, so the rename would be PATCHed away by the very flush meant to merge it.
- `knownServerTitles` (a landed save; every fetch that clears `mayPredateSave`, via `noteServerTitle` in **both** `apply` and `installFetched`) backs `adoptQueuedTitleIfUnseen`, which runs in both save funnels: queued save's title → draft's → known server title. An **unflushed local rename** (`title != savedTitle`) outranks all of them — it is the user's own edit, and it is what makes a reconcile call two titles a conflict rather than a merge.

## Review

Two rounds, three sub-agent reviewers. Round 1 found **three real bugs in the fix itself** — all closed with regression tests I watched fail first (`resolveConflictKeepingServer` bypassing `noteServerTitle` and so reverting the rename *via the backstop*; the missing baseline-title advance; the dirty-branch-with-a-draft revert). Round 2 found no new issues. See the PR comments for the full findings and responses.

Every new test was watched failing first. They read the **title PATCH body** (new shared `PatchedTitleRecorder`), because "a save happened" cannot tell an adopted rename from a reverted one. Coverage includes the flagship scenario end to end with **no hand-seeded baseline** (open online → edit offline → co-author renames → reconnect) — the five sites where the app *builds* the baseline were unpinned, so dropping `title:` compiled green.

**1060 tests, 0 failures.** `swift format` clean. `Core/Yjs` untouched, so no golden-byte risk. `Build & Test` green ([run 29366710147](https://github.com/llun/schrift/actions/runs/29366710147)) — the check does **not** run automatically here, because `pr-checks.yml` triggers only on PRs targeting `main`; I dispatched it manually against this branch.

Docs: the "Known limitation" notes in `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/offline-and-sync.md` are replaced by the shipped rule.

author: iceboundrock
body:
Closes #188 (epic #172, Phase 4).

## What this delivers

The dirty-ratio compaction rewrite goes from stub (`RewritePending`, no-op) to a real full-schema physical merge, plus the two production defects the issue named, plus the six-scenario e2e suite proving before/after query equivalence.

### Production changes

1. **SizeBytes fix** (`a0b5853`): CDC flush and cdc-init now stat the final object and record `FileEntry.SizeBytes` (best-effort — the size only feeds the promotion heuristic). Before this, every CDC-written entry carried `SizeBytes=0` and size-based promotion could never trigger in production.
2. **Byte-precise promotion threshold** (`cf55df8`): `deltaTotalMB = bytes/(1024*1024)` integer truncation meant sub-MB delta tiers rounded to 0 MB forever. `CompactionConfig.TargetBaseSizeBytes` (derived from the MB flag when unset) is compared against raw bytes.
3. **The rewrite** (`c784034`): DuckDB merges the schema's **complete** base+delta parquet set per `row_id` with the read path's exact LWW fold — `changed_at DESC, deleted_at DESC NULLS LAST, row_id ASC` (`source_tier_priority` is constant within cold and drops out) — drops tombstones (safe only under the full-inventory invariant), normalizes survivor `deleted_at` to 0 so equal-ver_ts ties stay base-wins (#183), and carries `changed_at` verbatim (#210).
4. **Tool wiring** (`f8abf52`): `tools compactor` builds the merge engine from the CDC DuckDB export flags; `RewriteApplied` results log merge counters and the new base key.

### Commit ordering & atomicity (manifest-driven reads, #187)

merge to `_tmp` → copy to a **UUID-named** base key (`base-<uuidv7>.parquet`, never reuses a listed key; range naming would let repeated rewrites overwrite an in-read object) → manifest splice under the loaded ETag → best-effort deletion of the now-unlisted sources. The manifest save is the only atomic step: a real conditional-put conflict (`If-Match`; rustfs honors it with 412 — spike-verified) surfaces as retryable `ErrConcurrentModification`, and the retry re-merges from a fresh manifest load, dropping the failed attempt's staged base. Crash windows on either side of the commit leave only unlisted orphans (#203 scope).

Concurrency vs flush is **ETag-only** — no advisory lock, no new PG dependency in the tool: a delta appended between load and save forces the 412→retry path, which folds it in (pinned end to end by the atomicity scenario).

### E2E coverage (issue scenarios → tests)

| # | Scenario | Test |
|---|----------|------|
| 1 | Promotion path (real SizeBytes) | `TestCompactionPromotionEquivalence` — relabel only, zero parquet-object changes, promotion precedence over the rewrite trigger |
| 2 | Rewrite path | `TestCompactionRewriteEquivalence` — trigger, merged content record-level, sources deleted, hot tier untouched, second-pass Noop |
| 3 | No-op | `TestCompactionNoopPaths/NoDeltas` — `assertStateUnchanged` all surfaces |
| 4 | Low dirty ratio | `TestCompactionNoopPaths/LowDirtyRatio` — computed-and-rejected `DirtyRatio` positive control, delta stays delta |
| 5 | Manifest atomicity | `TestCompactionManifestAtomicity` — real 412 via `PausingS3` on the manifest save + concurrent real flush; no lost entries, monotonic versions, no first-attempt orphan |
| 6 | Full lifecycle | `TestCompactionFullLifecycleEquivalence` — deleted entity physically absent from the new base, invisible under every tier hint (#175 criterion transfer) |

Edge coverage: multi-version LWW fold across an equal-ver_ts base/delta pair plus newer delta (`TestCompactionRewriteMultiVersionLWW`), all-tombstone schema-empties-out with the zero-row base entry kept listed as the `QuerySource` glob-fallback guard (`TestCompactionRewriteAllTombstones`). Every scenario asserts the bit-for-bit criterion twice over: literal engine-vs-itself snapshots across the boundary (`assertResultsIdentical`) AND oracle equality on both sides, plus `manifest == S3 inventory` set equality (no orphans, no duplicates, tmp excluded per #226).

Unit level: the merge SQL shape is pinned verbatim (`merge_sql_test.go`), the fold semantics run on real in-memory DuckDB over local parquet fixtures shaped like production exports (`merge_test.go`), and the splice/conflict-retry/staged-cleanup orchestration is pinned with fakes (`rewrite_test.go`). The nil-Merger `RewritePending` degradation stays pinned for manifest-only invocations.

### Tripwire replacement

`assertCompactionPreservesDeletion` (lifecycle) is deleted in the same commit that lands the rewrite, per its own failure message; every other #175 assertion is intact and the lifecycle suite is regression-clean.

### Harness additions

`RunCompactionWith(CompactionOverrides{S3, TargetBaseSizeBytes, DirtyRatioPct})` wires the full compactor (merge engine via `cdc.NewDuckExporter`, decoratable S3); `PausingS3` gains a `KeyContains` predicate; `S3ObjectClient` gains `HeadObject` (new `S3OpHead` for the decorators); `NewS3ManifestProvider` widened to `manifest.S3Client`.

## Adjudications (also commented on the issue)

- **Old-file deletion**: immediate best-effort deletion after the manifest commit (user decision during planning). Residual: an in-flight query that resolved the pre-swap object list can race the deletion and fail loudly (`ErrParquetSetInconsistent` class) within a window of one query duration. Grace-period GC in #203 is the long-term fix.
- **"No orphan objects"**: asserted as `manifest == live parquet set` (tmp excluded, #226 tolerance); crash-window orphans remain #203 scope.

## Verification

- `make lint` clean (golangci-lint v1.64.8)
- `make test` full unit suite green (includes new merge/rewrite tests on real DuckDB)
- `make test-e2e-production` full suite green (110s), including the seven compaction tests and the lifecycle regression
- Red-first discipline: the five rewrite-dependent e2e tests were committed failing (`99a3524`, all `outcome=rewrite_pending`) before the implementation flipped them green

author: peter-l-svk
body:
## What's in v0.1.3

### New Features
- **Multi-dimensional arrays** — nested array literals (`[[1,2],[3,4]]`),
  chained indexing (`@m[1][2]`), nested `for`-loop iteration, and full
  compatibility with existing array methods (`.map()`, `.filter()`,
  `.contains()`) on nested structures.
- **`.contains()` method** — added to both `String` and `Array` value
  methods. `"hello".contains("ell")` → `true`, `[1,2,3].contains(2)` → `true`.
- **`exit(code?)` and `_exit(code?)`** — process termination built-ins.
  `exit()` emits `ExitSignal` (runs `finally` blocks, not catchable).
  `_exit()` calls `std::process::exit` directly for immediate hard stop.
- **`ExitSignal`** — fourth sentinel error alongside `ReturnSignal`,
  `BreakSignal`, `ContinueSignal`. Propagates through all control-flow
  boundaries; `finally` blocks execute before process termination.

### Fixes
- **POSIX constants** — all flag constants (`O_WRONLY`, `O_CREAT`,
  `O_RDONLY`, `SEEK_END`, `SEEK_CUR`, `SIGTERM`) now live under the
  `posix` namespace hash (`posix["O_WRONLY"]`, etc.) instead of
  polluting the global scope.
- **Error handling** — `try/catch/finally` fully working with `throw`/`die`
  catchable `UserError`; `catch e as err` alias syntax; control-flow
  signals (`break`/`continue`/`return`) correctly propagate through
  `finally` blocks.

### Internal
- `RuntimeError::ExitSignal(i32)` variant added to error enum
- `stdlib` now exports `exit()` and `_exit()` built-in functions
- All interpreter control-flow handlers (for, while, try/catch/finally,
  match, call_value) propagate `ExitSignal` correctly

### New documentation
- Table of Contents with darkpurple/mediumpurple styling and dotted leaders
- §14 Multi-Dimensional Arrays (nested literals, chained indexing, nested for, operations)
- `.contains()` registered everywhere (Method Calls, Appendix A dispatch tables)
- `exit(code?)` and `_exit(code?)` — §8.5 Exit subsection, Appendix A Process Control, Appendix B.2
- Design Note: Error Signals updated from 3 → 4 sentinels (adds ExitSignal)

### Fixes
- All POSIX code examples now use namespaced flag constants (`posix["O_WRONLY"]` etc.)
- Removed duplicated open/write/close block in §12.3; restored missing `say` and `close` in lseek example
- Appendix B keyword table converted to `longtable` with continuation headers/footers for proper page splitting
- POSIX function table (Table 9) category labels converted from `\multirow` to `\multicolumn` sub-header rows (fixes vertical misalignment)
- Table 9 Description column shrunk from `p{6cm}` to `p{3.2cm}` (eliminates dead whitespace)
- 3-row keyword entries (catch, print, say) collapsed to uniform 2-row format
- Version badge bumped from 0.1.0 → 0.1.3
- `\usepackage{longtable}` added to preamble

author: xeno097
body:
## Summary

SVM warp-route program upgrades failed `simulateTransaction` on clusters where the
`enable_extend_program_checked` feature gate is inactive (e.g. Solana mainnet-beta).
The program-data "extend" step in `prepareProgramUpgrade` had two independent defects:

1. It always emitted `ExtendProgramChecked` (variant 9), which those clusters reject
   with `InvalidInstructionData`. Local `solana-test-validator` activates all features,
   so this passed in e2e but failed on mainnet.
2. It requested the exact byte deficit; the loader enforces a **10240-byte minimum**
   single extend and rejects smaller requests with `InvalidArgument`.

Either defect leaves the subsequent upgrade hitting `AccountDataTooSmall`.

## Changes

- Select checked (v9) vs. legacy unchecked (v6) extend by querying the feature gate
  via a new generic `isFeatureActive(rpc, feature)` helper.
- Clamp the extend up to the loader's 10240-byte minimum (`requiredExtendBytes`).
- Add a `program-extend-upgrade` e2e that deploys with a tight `maxDataLen` to force a
  sub-minimum extend and runs the upgrade against a validator with the gate deactivated
  (mimics mainnet); wired `deactivateFeatures` through `runSolanaNode` and added the CI
  matrix entry.

## Verification

- Root-caused and the fix validated by direct `simulateTransaction` against the affected
  mainnet program (extend v6 +10240 → upgrade succeeds).
- New e2e passes locally (program-data grows by exactly 10240; new bytecode copied in).
- Unit tests for the clamp, feature-account decode, and the variant-6 builder.
