author: anonymuse
body:
## Summary

This PR completes the remaining M0 hardware, benchmark, and model-artifact contract
freeze assigned by `PROJECT_HANDOFF.md`, then defines the evidence plan and ordered
work needed to execute M1 safely. It does not begin M1 implementation, download model
weights, configure nodes, or run physical cluster benchmarks.

PR #3 remains draft. Review threads remain open for independent reviewer evaluation.

## What was decided

- Treat PR #3 as the remaining M0 contract-completion PR. The merged repository
  bootstrap is durably complete; M1 execution remains unstarted.
- Use `qw5-json-c14n-v1` for exact JSON identity and require Draft 2020-12 structure
  plus versioned semantic validation.
- Make a TB5 `COMPLETE` result evidentiary: exact retained sample counts are required,
  all 246 raw cells resolve through a canonical measurement index, every projection
  reconciles to raw evidence, and non-complete cells retain partial evidence/errors.
- Use the owner-selected option 2 synchronization semantics in ADR-0007:
  `coordinator_observed_window_v1` is an empirical attempt-inclusion score, not an
  actual-start estimate, start-skew upper bound, clock proof, or one-way-timing claim.
  Raw synchronization evidence is content-addressed and mechanically reconciled to
  each referencing attempt. Missing or unqualified evidence cannot become a valid
  simultaneous result.
- Freeze the exact public Network framework route-binding/proof procedure, deterministic
  stream stop rule, 30-second and 32-GiB-per-flow caps, payload generation/verification
  timing, application-buffer accounting, and 108 indexed local controls. Failed
  controls and measurements retain partial observations and structured errors.
- Freeze an immutable, bounded SafeTensors parser profile before Terra implementation:
  scalar `shape: []`, exact dtype subset, strict UTF-8, duplicate-member rejection,
  checked arithmetic/ranges, safety limits, and raw positive/hostile vectors.
- Bind placement outcomes to a resolved `qw5.placement-evidence-graph/v1`: every
  evidence path, digest, schema, acceptance decision, gate rule, allocation formula,
  and memory class must reconcile before a result can be evaluated. Producer-asserted
  or vacuous `GO` is rejected; deterministic GO-rule evaluation remains fail-closed
  until M1-14 freezes the evaluator registry.
- Bind model-manifest completeness to a resolved `qw5.model-acquisition-plan/v1` and
  model-role minimums, so a complete manifest cannot omit weights, tokenizer,
  configuration, license, or the flagship vision component.
- Preserve SafeTensors `__metadata__` only as the pinned string-to-string map and test
  positive plus numeric, boolean, list, nested, and duplicate hostile encodings.
- Require one exact per-node thermal/power regime identity for every valid TB5 attempt,
  cell, and local control; mixed-regime pooling is invalid.
- Decompose M1 into 16 ordered PR tasks. M1-01 remains the first Terra-ready task after
  this PR is accepted; it is not executed here. M1-03 is now contract-bounded for a
  later Terra task.

## What remains open

- Which supported facts and copy observations the real macOS nodes expose.
- Actual solo/simultaneous TB5 results, errors, contention, and thermal regimes.
- Owner-approved immutable model revisions, licenses, file sets, bandwidth, and
  external storage.
- Concrete quantization layouts, safety reserve/headroom policy, workload/state
  formulas, scratch bounds, quality evidence, deterministic M1-14 gate evaluators,
  and any Qwen3.5 text-subset proof. Until those evaluators are frozen, placement GO
  remains deliberately unavailable.
- Every inference, quality, performance, long-context, and deployment claim.

## Why this M1 ordering is sound

Contracts and adversarial oracles precede implementation. The smallest local producer
comes first, followed by exact mechanical fixture expansion. Loopback validation
precedes node access; inventories and clean-node baselines precede route controls;
solo paths precede simultaneous stress. Only then does Sol own model-acquisition and
classification decisions. The smaller model validates the manifest/tensor workflow
before the flagship artifact. Sol freezes layouts, formulas, reserves, candidate sets,
and gate rules before Terra implements the analyzer, and Sol owns final integration.

This ordering fails early on privacy, identity, parsing, route, synchronization, or
arithmetic defects before costly cluster windows or large downloads.

## Model routing

- **First Terra-ready task:** M1-01 public-safe hardware inventory probe, Terra / Medium.
- **Later Terra:** bounded TB5 harness/capture, model inspector/acquisition, and
  placement analyzer after contracts, dependencies, and permissions are frozen.
- **Luna:** only M1-02 exact mechanical fixture expansion.
- **Sol:** architecture, acquisition/classification decisions, parser-profile
  acceptance, quantization layouts, formulas, reserve/subset rules, interpretation,
  amendments, and integration.
- **Ultra or parallel agents:** not authorized.

## Review history

Commit `90032a2d59fd7f7f33cc6b21b57619d2b52c50fa` addressed the original 13 review
findings. Commit `0654af17e6de85c6f86f2c31d8296db0b84e60cc` addressed the subsequent
architecture-team attachment. The EA independent re-review of that exact head raised
six new findings; focused amendment `ad45675088a27c2e05ad7cd89e683bfb169fd4e7`
addresses those six findings and records the owner's Option 2 synchronization choice.
No commit is represented as reviewer closure. The PR remains draft and all threads
remain open for independent re-evaluation.

## Focused second-pass amendment

The latest commit is limited to contract amendments, fixtures, semantic validation,
regression tests, and the corresponding ADR/coordination/provenance updates:

1. removes the circular plan-to-local-control-index reference and validates a real,
   acyclic 108-control/246-cell canonical evidence graph end to end;
2. replaces producer-asserted placement GO inputs with a resolved, accepted evidence
   graph and fail-closed evaluator boundary, including the exact vacuous-GO hostile;
3. forbids pooling valid TB5 attempts across mixed thermal, power-source, or Low Power
   Mode regimes and gives local controls equivalent regime evidence;
4. completes the evidence graph from plan through controls, measurements, indexes, and
   summary with actual path, schema, digest, and projection reconciliation;
5. binds manifest completeness to a resolved acquisition plan and role-derived required
   components; and
6. validates SafeTensors metadata against the pinned format and uses the single exact
   canonical-profile identifier `qw5-json-c14n-v1` everywhere.

This amendment does not implement or execute M1.

## Validation

- 16 schemas pass JSON parsing and Draft 2020-12 meta-schema checks.

- Model-acquisition and placement-evidence bundles pass their cross-artifact invariants.
- 87 committed negative cases fail with their required codes, including the exact
  circular-link, mixed-regime, vacuous-GO, incomplete-manifest, metadata, and legacy
  canonical-profile regressions.

author: tubalainen
body:
﻿Part of #51. There was no way to remove this on Windows — and no way to clean up after the install the WSL bug (v0.30.1) left half-finished.

## `scripts/windows/uninstall.ps1`

- **Finds what is actually there** — install folder, Desktop shortcut, firewall rule, containers, volumes, the installer''s own RunOnce entry and resume dir — prints it, prints what it will and will not do, and only acts when you type `REMOVE`.
- **Removes** the manager and every Arma server container (by *label*, so it catches containers compose never knew about), the network, the install folder (which holds `.env`, i.e. the admin password), the shortcut, the firewall rule (one UAC prompt), and the installer''s leftovers.
- **Keeps your data by default.** Templates, instances, saved games and the ~10 GB of server files live in Docker volumes; a reinstall picks them straight back up. `-RemoveData` deletes them — and says so in red, because it cannot be undone. `-RemoveImages` drops the images too.
- **Never touches Docker Desktop or WSL2.** Other things on the machine may be using them; the script says where to remove them by hand.
- **Works when the install is broken**: run it from `%TEMP%` and it still finds and cleans everything, because it does not depend on the install folder existing. It also survives deleting the folder it is running from (a staged helper finishes the job).

The installer now ships it, and prints the uninstall command when it finishes.

## Verification (all on a real Windows box)

- parse-checked, Defender-clean;
- run against a **clean machine** → finds nothing, changes nothing;
- run against a **fabricated install** → removes it, keeps the volumes, reports what it kept;
- **the confirmation gate proven**: answering `yes` aborts and changes nothing; only a literal `REMOVE` proceeds.

Docs: README "Uninstalling (or starting over after a failed install)" + a Guide FAQ entry.

author: exoridus
body:
## Summary
- Adds retained-batch record/replay support (Track B Slice 3) to the RepeatingSprite renderer's geometry path (TextureRegion source) on both WebGL2 and WebGPU, mirroring the Sprite renderer's seam.
- RepeatingSprite has two internal draw paths sharing one flush loop: a geometry path (fits the sprite-shaped seam as-is) and a shader path (bare Texture source, different stride + wrap-mode sampler, needs a seam extension). Only the geometry path is recorded; any capture containing a shader-path or pixel-snapped draw is poisoned and cleanly falls back to the existing entry-replay tier — no regression, no stale pixels, same defensive pattern the sprite renderers use for custom materials.
- Confirmed tiling mutations (offset/mode/fit/size setters) all call `invalidateCache()` → `_markContentDirty()`, so a recorded instruction set correctly invalidates before any tiling change could replay stale — verified with a dedicated mutation-proof test.

author: faw01
body:
## What changed

- remove the four nested `Effect.runPromise` calls in the pull planner: `ServedRoot` gains `verifySync`, a promise-native identity check for the promise engine, and the Effect-typed `verify` now delegates to it; the planner and its verify pass call it directly instead of re-entering an Effect runtime from inside a running fiber
- export `PullErrorTag` (the pull error tag union) from `@dumbridge/pull-transfer`; the server's `pullFailureCode` dispatches through a `Record<PullErrorTag, PullFailureCode>` table and the CLI message table is `satisfies Record<PullErrorTag, string>`, so both are compiler-checked exhaustive (the CLI gains a `ServedRootChangedError` message; the server table maps the client-side-only tags that cannot occur in its pull path)
- `resolvePullDestination` returns `Result<string, PullPathError>` instead of throwing, deleting the guessing `Effect.try` in `pullRemote`
- stop retrying deterministic connect failures: `openSession` remaps only `BridgeConnectError` and `BridgeDeadlineExceededError` through `Effect.catchTags`, so `BridgeLocatorInvalidError` and the proxy configuration errors keep their identity and `retryConnect` never retries them
- add `Effect.tapCause(Effect.logWarning)` before the serve-loop catch-all, which previously swallowed `ServedRootChangedError` silently; the log carries only error tags (redaction by construction), never payloads, paths, or the key
- add an optional `cause: Schema.Defect` field to `BridgeClientError` and pass the caught error through every remapping in the client, so a proxy or wire failure no longer collapses into generic text; `BridgeKeyError` payloads carry fixed messages only, so the cause can never echo the key
- replace the `Effect.catch` + `instanceof` dispatch in `executeShell` with `Effect.catchTags`, leaving the served root errors in the error channel so inference proves the pass-through
- read `DUMBRIDGE_KEY` through `Config.redacted`, unwrapped with `Redacted.value` only at the run and pull request calls

## Bookkeeping against #25

- `Schema.decodeUnknownResult` for the manifest decode: already resolved by #37, which consolidated the manifest into `packages/wire/src/pull-manifest.ts`; `validatePullManifest` decodes with `Schema.decodeUnknownResult` and returns typed violations that pull-transfer maps at its edge
- direct `process.env` default parameters in the CLI and iroh adapter: declined in the issue itself (parameterized, test-injectable edge behavior); unchanged here

Closes #25

## Verification

- [x] `bun run verify` (changeset status, check, typecheck, all tests, build, tarball install check)
- [x] No behavior changes beyond error-surface fidelity; existing interface tests pass, extended only where an item creates new observable behavior (non-retry of deterministic connect failures, exhausted-retry cause, redacted serve-loop warning, invalid-key CLI text)
- [x] The bridge key and served root content never appear in logs, errors, or test output; the new warning log and error causes are asserted key- and path-free
- [x] User-visible changes include a patch changeset

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches authentication-adjacent config (redacted bridge key), connect retry semantics, and pull/server error mapping; changes are mostly error-surface and runtime-structure with broad test coverage.
> 
> **Overview**
> Improves **error handling and Effect usage** across the bridge client, server, pull path, and CLI without changing core happy-path behavior (patch changeset).
> 
> The **pull planner** stops re-entering the Effect runtime from promise code: `ServedRoot` adds **`verifySync`**, and prepare/verify paths call it instead of `Effect.runPromise` on `verify`. **`resolvePullDestination`** now returns **`Result<string, PullPathError>`**, so `pullRemote` uses `Effect.fromResult` instead of a brittle `Effect.try`.
> 
> On the **client**, **`BridgeClientError`** gains an optional **`cause`**, wired through key decode, connect, request, and wire decode remappings. **Connect retries** only apply to transient **`BridgeConnectError` / `BridgeDeadlineExceededError`**; invalid locator and proxy configuration errors pass through unchanged. The **serve loop** logs swallowed session failures as **warnings that include only error tags**, not paths or keys. **`DUMBRIDGE_KEY`** is loaded via **`Config.redacted`** and unwrapped only when issuing run/pull requests.
> 
> **`PullErrorTag`** is exported for **exhaustive** server wire-code mapping and CLI user messages (including **`ServedRootChangedError`** on pull). Shell execution on the server uses **`Effect.catchTags`** instead of `instanceof` branching for served-root vs shell errors.

author: igor-ponticelli
body:
## Problem

After switching the language and navigating to another page via an internal link, the URL would revert to the previous locale (`pt-BR`) instead of keeping the selected language (`en`).

## Root cause

Several components used `Link` from `next/link` instead of the `Link` from `@/i18n/navigation`. On client-side navigation, Next's Router Cache indexes results by the literal href, without knowing the `NEXT_LOCALE` cookie changed. Since the Navbar first mounts in `pt-BR` (default locale) and prefetches links, that cache stays stuck on the old locale even after switching.

## Changes

- `components/ui/Navbar.tsx`: logo, Feedback link (desktop and mobile), and room link in the "My action items" collapse.
- `components/room/JoinRoom.tsx`: "Back to dashboard" link.
- `app/[locale]/not-found.tsx`: "Back to dashboard" and "Back to home" links.

All of them now use the `Link` from `@/i18n/navigation`, which already embeds the current locale into the client-generated href, removing the dependency on the middleware to resolve the language on internal navigation.

## Out of scope

`app/not-found.tsx` (root, outside `[locale]`) keeps `next/link`, since it's Next's generic fallback with no known locale at that point.

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- No changes to data model, rules, or i18n keys.

body:
Implements `specs/01-jump-nav.md`.

## What
A sticky, horizontally-scrollable chip row under the deep-dive header island that anchor-links to each of the ~15 `<section class="card">` blocks, plus ids on the sections that lacked them (`sentiment`, `snowflake`, `value`, `checks`, `past`, `future`, `dividend`, `insiders`, `news`, `notes` — `trend`/`income`/`peers`/`leadership` already had them).

Plain anchors: no JS, no scrollspy. `scroll-margin-top: 56px` keeps a tapped section's title clear of the sticky bar.

## Note on the chip guards
The spec's chip list was labelled "the intent, the template is the truth." Two things the template settled:

- The scoring/statement sections (Score, Fair value, Revenue, Checks, Past, Future, Dividend) all live inside the `{% if has_data %}` branch, so the chips are gated on `has_data` too — otherwise a still-crunching ticker would show chips pointing at nothing.
- Insiders / News / Notes render their section unconditionally with honest fallback copy, but I kept the spec's `is_us` / `news` / `current_user` guards on the chips: the anchors are never dangling either way, and a chip that jumps to "Otto skips this one" is noise.

## Verification
- `pytest -q` → 29 passed.
- Spec's assertion script → ok.
- Scripted both AAPL and RELIANCE.NS: every chip resolves to a rendered id, zero dangling anchors; RELIANCE.NS correctly drops the Insiders chip.
- Browser at 375px: chips overflow-scroll horizontally, bar pins at top (bottom edge 52px) and tapping Dividend lands its title at 96px — clear of the bar. Reads correctly in both dark and light.

Not deployed — ready when you are.

Currently provides code highlighting using LSP semantic tokens support and inline type-error diagnostics as you type. This is currently set up as a separate dune-project in src/sail_lsp

In order for it to understand the structure of any Sail project a `.sail_project` file is a hard requirement for the LSP to do anything other than the most basic syntax highlighting.

The biggest part of this PR other than the server itself is the testing setup. It's unsuited to our standard end-to-end test approach, so instead there is a python script in `test/lsp` that can send the jsonrpc messages to fake being an editor and test the interactions with the server. The UTF-16 handling is also fiddly, so there are now Libsail unit tests in `test/unit` targetting this. author: selwynpolit
body:
## What this does

HANDOFF.md task #2 — cleans up the macOS Edit menu in `lib/app.dart`.

## Background

The task started from the hypothesis that the Edit menu's empty `onSelected: () {}` handlers were *swallowing* ⌘C/⌘V/⌘X/⌘A in text fields. A **human hand-test on macOS disproved that** — keyboard editing works fine on the current Flutter version. The real problems were:

- **Menu-bar clicks** for Cut/Copy/Paste/Select All did nothing (inert handlers).
- **Redo** did nothing at all — there is no redo in `UndoManager`.
- App **Undo** works, but only for its 7 recorded domain actions (task complete/delete, note delete, card hide/snooze/archive/delete), single-level, surfaced via the undo toast.

## Changes

- **Removed the dead Redo menu item** (no redo feature exists).
- **Wired Cut/Copy/Paste/Select All** `onSelected` to a new `_invokeFocusedEditIntent` helper, which invokes the standard text-editing intents on `FocusManager.instance.primaryFocus` — so the menu-bar clicks now act on the focused field. Keyboard shortcuts were already handled by Flutter and are unchanged.
- **Kept Undo** as-is.

### Docs
- CLAUDE.md: Keyboard-Shortcuts note + Known issues rewritten to state plainly that Undo is single-action/limited and redo is not implemented; the swallowing concern is recorded as tested-and-disproven.
- **"Full multi-level undo/redo" added to the Phase 2 planned list** — a proper history stack across more operations is the intended future work.
- HANDOFF.md task #2 marked done with the verification story.

## Testing
- `flutter analyze` — clean (one pre-existing unused-import warning unrelated to this change).
- `flutter test` — **77 passing**.
- **Human-verified on macOS:** Redo is gone; menu-bar Copy/Paste/Cut/Select All act on the focused field; Undo reverses a domain action. (Native menu-bar click behavior isn't automatable in this environment, so it was confirmed by hand.)

body:
Stage 1 of the retrospective-as-record work (session plan; follows decision 577's converged quality plan with a reasoned sequence flip: retro-as-record before the REM rebuild, so REM is redesigned once against the final anchor set).

## What
- **Non-destructive REM**: a fact's node now carries the original text verbatim (`[:2000]`); the LLM summary lands in `rem_summary` only when the source exceeds `REM_SUMMARY_THRESHOLD` (default 2000). Consolidation reads `coalesce(rem_summary, content)`. Decisions unchanged; new `Retrospective` anchors are enrichment-only.
- **Transition-tolerant NREM**: outcome reads accept both the legacy HAD_OUTCOME self-loop (edge props) and the upcoming `(Decision)-[:HAD_OUTCOME]->(:Retrospective)` node shape; insight-path ledger queries key retro rows on `COALESCE(target_pg_id, pg_id)` so legacy rows (decision's pg_id) and v2 rows (retro's own pg_id) trigger, are consumed, and reconcile identically.
- **Latest-retro-as-verdict** in insight folds: newest retro per decision in full (v2: authoritative Postgres notes + evidence line naming grounding facts with role + derived fact_kind); earlier retros compress to rating+date lines.
- **Spine vocabulary**: `Retrospective` label + outcome-state rating enum (`validated/mixed/refined/pending/reversed`), code-pinned.

## Why
Retrospectives are the why-loop's highest-signal records (measured hindsight) yet today exist only as unsearchable edge annotations; and REM's destructive summary overwrite made every synthesis inherit paraphrase drift for already-curated facts. This PR ships the READERS first (Cloe-concurred ordering: tolerant readers → new write path → one-time conversion) so the system stays live through every later stage.

## Deviation from plan noted
The summary is still *requested* from the LLM for short facts (storage-gated instead of prompt-skipped): prompt-level skipping collides with the batch JSONL null-summary alignment sentinel. Proper prompt-level skip rides the REM rebuild.

## Tests
456 passing (new: non-destructive write paths, retro anchor, dual-shape outcome query, v2 fold block contract, ledger keying).

author: siddhartha-singh01
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Volume metrics collection runs periodically in the kubelet. When `GetMetrics` fails (for example temporary NFS errors), the failure was only logged at V(4), so operators could not see it at default verbosity while investigating missing/zero volume usage metrics.

This PR:
- Logs **new or changed** metrics failures at **Error** (visible at default verbosity)
- Logs **identical repeated** failures at **V(4)** only, to avoid spam from the periodic calculator loop
- Clears tracked state on success so a later failure is logged at Error again
- Leaves `NotSupported` silent (expected for volumes without metrics)

State is stored on the **per-pod** `volumeStatCalculator`, so there is no cross-pod global map or leak across pods.

This incorporates review feedback from the earlier stale PR kubernetes/kubernetes#119169.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes kubernetes/kubernetes#118062

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- No mutex on `lastMetricsErrors`: only the single calculator loop (and unit tests) mutate it
- Unit coverage in `TestVolumeMetricsErrorLoggingState`

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kubelet now logs volume metrics collection failures at Error on first occurrence (and when the error changes), with V(4) for identical repeats, to aid debugging without log spam.
```

author: 0xandi
body:
## The idea

One PRD page per feature, two zones for two readers - and a backlog humans can actually read:

- **Human zone** (top): the argued case - problem, goals, solution, requirements, rollout. Written by `/to-prd` or by hand.
- **Agent zone** (bottom, `## Agent PRD`): implementation decisions, testing decisions, a scope map with tracer bullets, rejected alternatives. Written by `/to-robo-prd`.
- **Few tickets**: `/to-tickets` cuts the work into one ticket per registry scope by default, with the vertical-slice steps as **ordered actions** on the ticket instead of sibling tickets.

## Why

`/to-expo`'s "prefer many thin slices" rule floods the backlog: a medium feature becomes 9-12 tickets, and the chains it produces are serial anyway (each blocked-by the previous, each PR merged before the next starts). Nobody reads those tickets - they're steps wearing ticket costumes. This moves the steps down a level:

| | old (`/to-expo`) | new (`/to-tickets`) |
|---|---|---|
| chain of slice-tickets | N tickets, N branches, N PRs, N QA entries | 1 ticket, 1 branch, 1 PR, 1 QA entry |
| one slice | 1 ticket | 1 action = 1 commit |
| ordering | blocked-by edges everywhere | action order inside; blocked-by only across tickets |

The slicing discipline itself is unchanged - action 1 is the scope's tracer bullet, every action leaves the branch demoable. Parallelism is preserved where it's real: independently-mergeable work becomes its own ticket. Merge gates go from one-per-step to one-per-scope.

## Changes

- **`/to-prd` rewritten**: writes the human PRD as a Knowledge page linked to the Feature. Checks the registry first - adds to an existing feature instead of duplicating, and treats work on a feature with live scopes as an extension (new scope). Emits EARS requirements as native checkable rows (exponential ADR-0039); **user stories are no longer emitted**.
- **`/to-robo-prd` new**: appends/replaces the `## Agent PRD` section on the same page. Idempotent.
- **`/to-tickets` new**: reads the Agent PRD, proposes the ticket/action cut, quizzes the user (same loop as to-expo), publishes tickets + branch names + actions + cross-ticket dependencies + decision comments, and emits a clean-context execution prompt (one PR per ticket, commit per action, `actions update --status COMPLETED` as steps land).
- **`/to-expo` unchanged** - it stays for plans that don't belong to a registry feature. Whether to deprecate it later is your call; both are listed side by side for now.
- READMEs, `plugin.json`, and `EXPONENTIAL-TEAM.md` (skill table, lifecycle table, daily workflow) updated.

## Dependencies

The new skills drive CLI commands that don't exist in releases yet:
1. positonic/exponential#370 - server procedures (requirements, scopes, link-page) - merge + deploy first
2. positonic/exponential-sdk#3 - SDK APIs
3. positonic/exponential-cli#3 - `pages`, `features requirements/scopes/areas/link-page`, `tickets create --scope`

Until those land, the skills document the intended flow but the publish steps will fail.

author: bunnyxt
body:
## What happened

The **2026-07-15 04:00 full scan hung for 90+ minutes** at 72.6% (725,436 of 998,558 aids) and had to be killed. Fetch and writer both sat at **0/s** from ~04:41 onward.

This is a regression from #31 + #32 combined. Neither is wrong alone; together they close a circular wait.

## Root cause: fetchers hold the connections the writer needs

1. **`FetchVideoRecordJob` pinned a pooled DB connection.** It opened a lazy session on its first `CodeError` and held it until `cleanup()`. The full scan hit **465 CodeErrors spread across all 250 workers** (#31 raised 150 → 250), so essentially every worker ended up holding one — **250 workers against a 200-connection pool** (`pool_size=50 + max_overflow=150`).
2. **Pool exhausted → the writer starved.** `BatchInsertVideoRecordJob` couldn't get a connection to drain `record_queue`:
   ```
   QueuePool limit of size 50 overflow 150 reached, connection timed out, timeout 60
   ```
3. **`record_queue` filled to its 20,000 cap** (#32 bounded it), so every fetcher blocked **forever** in `put()` — *while still holding the connections the writer needed to make room*. Deadlock.

The evidence matches exactly: fetch stopped at 725,436, writer at 704,000 — a gap of **21,436 ≈ the 20,000 cap**.

**The unbounded queue had been masking (1)**: fetchers never blocked, so they always finished and released their connections. Bounding it is what closed the cycle. I flagged this as a risk ("R3 — writer deadlock") when writing the merge plan and said *"not fixed here"*. That was wrong; it bit within a day.

## Fixes

**1. Fetchers hold no pooled connection.** The `CodeError → update_video` fallback runs on a short-lived session, closed immediately in a `finally`. A fetcher needs the DB on <1% of aids — holding a connection for the other 99% is what exhausted the pool.

**2. `put()` cannot block forever.** Bounded-queue `put()` now takes a timeout and re-checks the duration limit. A stalled or dead writer costs a dropped record (counted as `record_dropped_queue_full`), not the entire run. Backpressure is preserved — only the *unbounded* wait is gone.

## Verified

- **Deadlock repro** (full queue, no writer draining — the exact 04:00 condition): worker now exits cleanly instead of hanging.
  ```
  thread still alive (HUNG)?   False
  conditions                 : {'record_dropped_queue_full': 1}
  ```
- **Connection hoarding** (50 aids, *all* taking the CodeError path): peak **1** concurrent session, **0** leaked.
- **Healthy path** (100 aids, no errors): **0** DB sessions opened, 100 records produced.

## Impact / damage

04:00 wrote 704k of 998k C30 records; 273k aids got no record for that label, and 14 records are parked in `data/record_recovery_c30_202607150400.csv`. Hourly runs were never affected (they generate far fewer CodeErrors, so they never exhaust the pool) — 05:00 completed normally in 4 minutes.

author: pnathan
body:
## Fix the language: unary float intrinsics reach the native tier

Adds a `Core::FUnary(FUnOp, arg)` node and lowers `sqrt`, `floor`, `ceiling`, `truncate` to native code, wired through **every** Core site: the Cranelift backend (`native.rs`), the Core interpreter (`runtime.rs` — `eval_core_nontail`/`eval_core_traced` + the `core_node_count`/`verify_core`/closure-compile walkers), and the disassembler (`registry.rs`).

```
(defun-typed (rt float64) ((x float64)) (sqrt x))      ; TIER . COMPILED, (rt 2.0) => 1.4142135623730951
(defun-typed (fl int64)   ((x float64)) (floor x))     ; TIER . COMPILED, (fl -2.3) => -3
(defun-typed (hyp float64) ((a float64)(b float64)) (sqrt (+ (* a a) (* b b))))  ; => 5.0
```

### Bit-exact with the evaluator
- `sqrt` → `fsqrt` instruction (`float64 → float64`)
- `floor`/`ceiling`/`truncate` → `floor`/`ceil`/`trunc` instruction, then a **saturating** `fcvt_to_sint_sat` — matching Rust's saturating `f64 as i64` that the evaluator uses (`floor`/`ceiling`/`truncate` return `int64`).

A single `FUnOp::apply_word(f64) -> u64` is the shared source of truth the Core interpreter uses, kept identical to the native emission, so results are bit-identical interpreted or compiled.

### Codegen-only
In checking mode these keep their permissive declared schemes from `lib/28-types.lisp` (argument `any`); the compiled path requires a concrete `float64` argument, else the function stays interpreted — never a silent coercion.

### Soundness
Gated on the full **differential interpreter-vs-JIT fuzzer** (FUZZ-GREEN) + DEFAULT/NDF/CLIPPY.

Second of the "fix the language" changes toward compiling numeric hot paths (after `let`/`progn`, #383). Transcendentals (`sin`/`cos`/`exp`) + half-away `round` need a libm trampoline and land next.

author: hozblok
body:
This PR lands three intertwined pieces of CAPSYSred work — a new canonical ray-recording
format (v3), a standalone recorder (`trace_v3`), and Stage 14, an exact disk-backed
delete-one-mode coherence jackknife with a native C++ core — plus the package restructure,
a new wall type, and the CLI simplification that they forced.

## 1. rays v3: per-mode ray archives

The single monolithic `rays.jsonl.gz` is replaced by a directory archive
(`src/formula/capsysred/rays_v3.py`):

ARCHIVE/
rays-fingerprint.yaml   format 3: geometry (with seed), lean flag, rng scheme
rays-index.jsonl        one entry per section file (authority for budgets)
modes/<scene>-m<mode>-r<r0>-<r1>.jsonl.gz


- Each section file holds a header, the v2-format rows for one `(scene, mode, ray-range)`
  with absolute mode/ray ids, and a trailer. Rows are byte-compatible with v2.
- The index is the integrity authority: modes `0..M-1` all present, sections contiguous
  from ray 0, one common ray count per scene. Readers hash every section while streaming
  and compare against the index.
- Publication is crash-safe: sections go tmp → rename, the index by atomic replace, so an
  interrupted run leaves the archive at its previous budget.
- Readers retry transient device errors (5 attempts with backoff) and resume mid-stream —
  long stage runs survive a flaky external disk.
- The v2 *writer* is removed; v2 recordings remain readable everywhere and
  `convert_rays_v3` migrates them (see below).

## 2. trace_v3: recording is now a separate program

`python -m formula.capsysred.trace_v3 config.yaml --archive DIR [--jobs J]`
(`src/formula/capsysred/trace_v3.py`):

- Scenes and budgets come from the yaml alone. Per scene: absent from the archive → trace;
  below the yaml budget → top up; at budget → no-op; above → error. No shards, no merge,
  resumable per section. `shard_trace` is deleted.
- New rng scheme **lattice-v1**: one seed, an independent stream per `(scene, mode)`, a
  fixed number of aim draws per ray. `--jobs N`, one-shot and top-up runs produce
  identical rays. Legacy sequential-v2 archives (converted Z-26) keep their tail-substream
  top-up path.
- `rays-fingerprint.yaml` is validated on every use; a geometry/seed mismatch stops the
  run without overwriting.
- `convert_rays_v3` turns a v2 `rays.jsonl.gz` into a v3 archive in one strict pass,
  recovering per-mode origins by replaying the recorded rng streams and verifying each
  recovered origin by re-tracing ray 0 against the recorded row; `--verify` fully re-reads
  an archive (hashes, counts, canonical ids).
- Consequence for the main CLI: **stages never trace.** `python -m formula.capsysred`
  only reads `out/rays-modes`, `out/rays.jsonl.gz` or `--replay` paths. `--replay` accepts
  v3 directories and/or v2 files, several archives are read as one recording whose
  `n_modes` is their sum (`MultiRaysReader`); stages match recordings by geometry core.

## 3. Stage 14: exact disk-backed delete-one-mode jackknife

A new opt-in estimator (`--stages 14`) built for archives too large for RAM
(`stages/stage14.py`, ~1.8k lines, plus `src/cpp/bindings_stage14.cpp`, ~1.2k lines):

- The ray archive is decoded **once per cache miss**; the native store writes compact
  per-mode `W/Ic` rows (`[mode, pixel, 3]` float64, headerless canonical little-endian) to
  a disk cache, and every later classification reads only that cache. Dense numerical
  loops live in C++; Python owns provenance, strict JSONL validation, aggregate
  serialization and publication.
- Caches are keyed by an analysis identity (cache schema + estimator version + geometry);
  one cache per replay archive, reusable across runs. `CAPSYSRED_STAGE14_CACHE` relocates
  the cache root away from the archive (e.g. off an external disk).
- **Pixel trust taxonomy** in `stages/stage14_flags.py`: a single normative decision tree
  (flags `no-rays`, `solo-rays-only`, `negative-Ic`, `null-Ic`, `noisy-Ic`,
  `no-ref-realizations`, `over-mu`, `noisy-mu`, `trusted`; reference-pixel statuses
  incl. `weak` / `loo-invalid`). Structural violations raise; statistically unusable data
  is an explicit flag, never a silent NaN. Thresholds are configurable
  (`stage14.flag_thresholds`, `z` renamed to `ic_n_sigma`).
- **Multi-screen**: `capillary.screens:` adds extra planes past the exit, re-binned from
  the same trace — amplitudes are evaluated once per ray and fanned out to the main and
  all extra screens; each screen gets its own figures and report section, caches stay
  separate.
- Output set: μ map/profile/error/flags, slice and intensity figures (linear and log),
  Ic family with errors, mode-density, overlay, ray scatter, and a reference-pixel
  passport figure; recent commits add gap-aware slice rendering and intensity fixes.

## 4. New wall: FunnelWall (conformal bundle)

`walls/wall_funnel.py`: a bore whose axis scales as `center·g(z)` and radius as
`r0·f(z)`, with quadratic `f`, `g` (config: `funnel: {g: [ag, bg], f: [af, bf]}`).
The hit is an exact degree-4 Number polynomial (degenerating to 2 on structural zeros —
a straight cylinder is `f = g = 1`), solved by the torus two-tier machinery (float
Durand–Kerner seeds → full-precision Newton, exact-sign bisection fallback). Marked
experimental: every run cross-checks the first hit against the reference `surface:`
ImplicitWall.

## 5. Stage 11 (beamlets) hardening

- Experimental

## 6. Package restructure and API cleanup

- `capsysred` is split into `shared/` (nums, types, units, physics constants, progress,
  format, utils), `stages/` (stage14, stage14_flags, beamlet, jackknife, altcoh,
  coherence, analytic, sketch, validate) and `walls/` (cylinder, torus, polygon,
  revolution, funnel); duplicated helpers are deduped into `shared/`.
- Physical constants move to `src/formula/physical_constants.py`; unit conversions and
  magic numbers centralized.
- `xray` API: `precision` becomes keyword-only and required (no silent default-30);
  material constants are named.
- Config: `engine_method` is no longer a global trace knob — it is required per
  `surface:` bore and rejected elsewhere; removed knobs: `sample_every`, `rays_gzip`
  (superseded by `rays_jsonl`), `no-jackknife`, `--quick`; stages 4/5 deleted
  (`KNOWN_STAGES` is now `1,2,3,6,7,8,9,10,11,12,14`).
- Docs rename “arbitrary-precision” → “multiprecision”; a commented, complete
  `capsysred.example.yaml` is added.
- Native side: bindings split into separate translation units (`bindings_trace.cpp`,
  `bindings_stage14.cpp`) to bound per-compile memory.

## 7. Tests

~4,400 new test lines: v3 archive unit tests and full-round-trip tests
(`test_rays_v3*.py`), per-wall-kind seed-determinism (`test_trace_determinism.py`),
in-process `--jobs 1` verify, Stage 14 config/flags/integration/multiscreen/native suites
(`test_stage14_*.py`), `test_wall_funnel.py`, tracer audit xfails, replay re-bin test.

## Compatibility notes

- v2 recordings stay readable (stages, `--replay`, converter); only the writer is gone.
- Recording moved out of the stage runner: pipelines that relied on the run tracing
  implicitly must call `trace_v3` first.
- Removed CLI/config knobs above are hard errors, not silent ignores.

author: viraatc
body:
Registers [NVIDIA TensorRT Model Optimizer](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer) (ModelOpt) as a model library, following the pattern of #885, so that ModelOpt-quantized checkpoints get [download counting](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/models-download-stats) and library attribution.

**Download counting rule:** `path:"hf_quant_config.json"` — a single file that every ModelOpt HF export carries alongside `config.json` (avoids multi-counting the safetensors shards).

**Example models:** [nvidia/DeepSeek-R1-FP4-v2](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/DeepSeek-R1-FP4-v2), [nvidia/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-FP8](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-FP8), [centml/DeepSeek-R1-NVFP4-v2-mlpinf](https://huggingface.co/centml/DeepSeek-R1-NVFP4-v2-mlpinf).

Note on the key: `modelopt` follows the pip package name (`nvidia-modelopt`). Some existing model cards carry `library_name: Model Optimizer` (spaced) — happy to change the key if the Hub normalizes that differently.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Adds a single metadata/registry entry with no runtime, auth, or data-path changes; only affects Hub library labeling and download attribution for ModelOpt checkpoints.
> 
> **Overview**
> Registers **NVIDIA Model Optimizer** (TensorRT Model Optimizer / ModelOpt) in `MODEL_LIBRARIES_UI_ELEMENTS` under the key `modelopt`, so Hub models tagged with that `library_name` get proper library attribution, repo/docs links, and download stats.
> 
> Download counting is scoped to **`hf_quant_config.json`** only (one count per ModelOpt HF export, avoiding inflated counts from sharded safetensors). The entry is **not** added to the models filter (`filter: false`), consistent with smaller or newer libraries.
>

author: jepegit
body:
Closes #115 (Stage 1.13).

Three additive helpers in `cellpycore.units` behind the optional `units` extra:

- **`convert_value(value, physical_property, from_units=None, to_units=None)`** — generalized port of cellpy's `to_cellpy_unit`: accepts a bare number (interpreted in `from_units`), a pint quantity string (`"25 mV"`), or a `(value, unit)` tuple; defaults raw → cellpy units.
- **`calculate_scaler(from_unit, to_unit)`** — port of `unit_scaler_from_raw` reduced to `Q(1, a).to(b).m`; offset units documented to raise (use `convert_value` for temperatures).
- **`validate_units(units, strict=True)`** — the loader-boundary validator: labels must be pint-parsable strings; floats rejected with a message naming the legacy v7 artifact; unknown keys warned + dropped; `strict=False` escape hatch for `local_instrument`.

**Label decision (recorded per the issue):** `temperature="C"` means Celsius — validated as `degC`, never coulomb — and `frequency="hz"` is hertz (bare `hz` is undefined in pint). Handled by a per-property alias table used only for parsing; spec labels are preserved.

Tests: 17 new converter cases + extended pint-optional guard (all three helpers raise the clear `ModuleNotFoundError` naming the extra). Full suite: **196 passed**.

Follow-ups: release + re-pin (release-procedure.md), then jepegit/cellpy#451 wraps these.

body: ## Description The SonarQube analysis currently runs as a conditional step (if: matrix.node-version == '24.x') inside the same build job that runs the Node.js 22.x/24.x matrix. This couples static analysis to the matrix job and exposes it to fail-fast behavior: if one Node version's job fails or gets cancelled before reaching the SonarQube step, the analysis can be silently skipped for that commit. This PR splits SonarQube into an independent sonar job that depends on the build job via needs, so the analysis runs explicitly instead of relying on a condition inside the matrix. ## Changes - Extracted the SonarQube Scan step out of the build job into a new sonar job with needs: build. - The build job now uploads the coverage report (coverage/) as an artifact only from the Node 24.x run, since that job no longer shares a filesystem with sonar. - The sonar job does its own checkout (with fetch-depth: 0, required by SonarQube for new-code analysis and git blame) and downloads the coverage artifact before running the scan. ## Test

author: agourakis82
body:
## Harden the signal::fft vertical

Seventh application of the playbook (GUM #860, units #873, linalg #892, prob #902, stats #909). `signal::fft` is a high-value, **self-contained** real-world module (spectral analysis) that **native-compiles under the default Madaros engine** — no lean_single needed. Coordinated: `signal/` is cold (stable, no open PR), disjoint from the active stats/IR/special lanes.

### What's here
- **`ComplexArray` fields made `pub`** (`stdlib/signal/fft.sio`) — the enabling change: the buffer was un-constructible externally, so the FFT was un-importable. Additive, no behaviour change; matches the module's documented "callers declare `var arr = ComplexArray {...}`, pass by `&!`" pattern (which also sidesteps the cross-module by-value corruption #913).
- **Run-proof** (`tests/stdlib/signal/test_fft_stdlib.sio`) — asserts known FFT properties: DC [1,1,1,1]→|X|[0]=4/rest 0; impulse→flat spectrum 1; forward→inverse **round-trip** recovers the input; real cosine cos(2πn/8)→peaks at bins 1,7 = N/2 = 4. `FFT_STDLIB_OK`.
- **Consumer example** (`examples/signal/spectrum_report.sio`) — a two-tone spectrum (bin 1 = 8, bin 3 = 4).
- **Gate** (`scripts/signal_fft_gate.sh`, default Madaros) → `SIGNAL_FFT_GATE_OK`.

### Honesty note
The cosine test bounds bins 3,5 at ≤2e-3 residual — that's `fft_cos` input precision (~1e-3), **not** FFT error (exact-zero bins 0,2,4,6 are asserted strictly). Documented, not retrofitted.

### Verification
Compile-and-run under default Madaros throughout. Math-review (xAI/Grok) PASS on all four FFT properties, logged.

body:
#### Description

The error replaying of `aws_lambda` was incorrectly using S3 service with credential overrides provided for S3 handler path. This PR fixes S3 service usage of the error replaying.

Note that, currently there's no credential overriding capability for error replaying. This means, error destination is expected to use default AWS credentials of the Lambda runtime. This could be enhanced in future if a need arise.

author: fernando-delosrios-sp
body:
### 💡 What
Replaced the non-existent `processConcurrent` chunked `Promise.all` logic with a new, generic worker-pool based `processConcurrent` utility function in `src/utils/index.ts`.

### 🎯 Why
When using chunked `Promise.all` for concurrency, the entire chunk must complete before the next chunk can start. This causes "head-of-line" blocking where one slow API request delays the processing of all other items in subsequent chunks, reducing network throughput. By utilizing a worker-pool model instead, idle workers can immediately pull from the queue and process new items as soon as they finish their current task, ensuring smoother and higher network I/O throughput. 

### 📊 Impact
Eliminates idle wait times in concurrent batch network operations throughout the codebase (already utilized in `src/index.ts` and `src/isc-client.ts`), leading to higher I/O throughput and faster application performance.

### 🔬 Measurement
Run the application with a large dataset (e.g. large numbers of profiles, roles, or endpoints to fetch/update) and monitor the overall time spent on batch processes, which should demonstrate reduced latency in network heavy batch operations compared to sequential or naive chunked implementations.

body:
Two owner-reported UI bugs. Owner is AFK; cross-model review (grok-4.5 max + gpt-5.6-sol max) + unit tests are the gate, GUI feel verified on return.

## Finding 1 — can't drag the (v1) pet while it's wander-moving
The pet window is `isMovableByWindowBackground`; the ~11 Hz wander `setFrameOrigin` kept moving it out from under the cursor, so AppKit's background-drag never established (only grabbable during the 2–6 s stop phase). Now `wanderTick` **pauses when the cursor is over the panel** (geometry poll `panel.frame.contains(NSEvent.mouseLocation)`, self-healing every 90 ms; skipped under click-through) → the pet stops when you reach for it, so it's grabbable. Pure predicate `WanderBand.shouldPauseWanderForCursor` (unit-tested). Chose a geometry poll over `.onHover` on both reviewers' advice (nonactivating panels deliver hover unreliably; a missed exit would freeze wander).

## Finding 2 — Codex weekly-reset truncated + big gap between name and 5h
Rows are now **fixed-width columns** (name flexible + 5h/wk/reset = 50/50/64) so metrics align across rows and reset has its own column; the reset label is **compacted** (drop "resets"/"wk resets" → bare countdown / `wk 6d 3h`) so the worst case (`wk 6d 23h`) fits; panel 320 → 340. a11y now speaks the full reset sentence ("weekly limit resets in 6d 3h"). `countdown` moved to `UsageCore.ResetLabel` (unit-tested); `DashboardViews.countdown` delegates. Chose fixed-width `HStack` over `Grid` deliberately — deterministic layout I can verify by reasoning while the owner can't GUI-test.

## Validation
`swiftpm.sh build` clean; `usagecore-tests` **PASS 26,481** (+7: WanderCursorPause ×3, ResetLabel ×4 incl. 48h/49h countdown boundary + worst-case ≤9-char budget). No engine/V2 change. Both models **CLEAN** (plan + implementation).

author: adamtheturtle
body:
Fixes #2896.

## Problem

`V(heterogeneous_strategy=INTERFACE)` only wrapped scalar leaves in maps that were individually heterogeneous. When sibling dict values are maps whose value types differ, homogeneous sibling maps stayed at their own narrower `map[string]string` value type while their heterogeneous siblings widened to `map[string]IVal`, so the enclosing container emitted mixed inner-map value types and the literal did not compile.

## Fix

Union the reusable `collect_sibling_map_wrap_ids` walk into V's `_v_collect_ids_needing_wrap`, mirroring the Rust #2879, Nim #2898, and Mojo #2895 fixes. Every sibling inner map now wraps its scalar leaves in `IVal` and shares one `map[string]IVal` value type.

### Before
```v
[
	IVal({'input': IVal({'kind': IVal('add'), ...}), 'expected': IVal({'item_id': 'item_1', 'state': 'pending'})}),
	IVal({'input': {'kind': 'remove', 'item_id': 'item_9'}, 'expected': {'error': 'not_found'}}),
]
```

### After
```v
[
	{'input': {'kind': IVal('add'), 'item_id': IVal('item_1'), 'urgent': IVal(true)}, 'expected': {'item_id': IVal('item_1'), 'state': IVal('pending')}},
	{'input': {'kind': IVal('remove'), 'item_id': IVal('item_9')}, 'expected': {'error': IVal('not_found')}},
]
```

## Tests

Added `V_nested_map_widening` compact and multiline golden variants (both verified to compile with `v -check` locally) and updated the `VARIANT_ONLY_CASE_DIRS` note.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Targeted change to V heterogeneous wrap-id collection plus integration goldens; mirrors an established helper already used by other language backends.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **V `INTERFACE`** output when sibling dict values are nested maps with **different scalar value types**: individually homogeneous inner maps no longer keep a narrower `map[string]string` (etc.) while siblings widen, which produced **non-compiling** literals.
> 
> **`_v_collect_ids_needing_wrap`** now unions **`collect_sibling_map_wrap_ids`** with the existing heterogeneous container walk (same pattern as Rust/Nim/Mojo), so every sibling inner map wraps scalar leaves in **`IVal`** and shares one **`map[string]IVal`** value type. Outer containers are no longer over-wrapped compared to the broken behavior described in the PR.
> 
> Adds **`V_nested_map_widening`** compact/multiline goldens, registers V on the **`nested_map_widening`** variant axis, and documents V in **`VARIANT_ONLY_CASE_DIRS`**.

## What

Adds `dev_docs/autopilot-feedback.md` documenting blockers found during a real `/auto-pilot` launch attempt (v1.56.1, `plan` source, `local-full` macOS host).

## Why

The fail-closed pre-flight passed **green** (`PREFLIGHT VERDICT: go`), but pre-detach confinement verification found the launch is **non-functional on this host**. All four would have surfaced as a silently-wedged run overnight — the exact failure class findings #22/#23 exist to prevent.

## Blockers (evidence in the doc)

1. **Fatal:** a linked run worktree can't commit in the jail — its `.git/worktrees/<name>/index.lock` lives under the RO main repo. `Operation not permitted`. Wedges every wake. → use a standalone clone as the run root.
2. **Fatal:** a host-global git hook (`core.hooksPath` → `~/.bootstrap/.../mise-trust-worktree`) is exec-denied by the jail, killing all git ops even in a standalone clone. → neutralize `core.hooksPath` in the run clone.
3. **Likely fatal for push:** the `gh`/osxkeychain credential helper isn't provisioned in the profile (`~/.config/gh` RO mount + exec-allow `gh`). → provision it and add an in-jail credential smoke.
4. **Assembly gap:** no orchestrator prompt template ships; verify-broker wiring is implicit. → ship canonical assets.

## Meta-finding

`preflight.sh` / `smoke-confinement.sh` verify exec, a `$HOME` write-deny, and egress rendering — but never the run's actual load-bearing op: **a git commit from the run worktree, on this host's git config, inside the jail**. A jailed-commit smoke would have caught blockers 1–3. Proposed as a new pre-flight step.

Repro steps and per-blocker fixes are in the file.

author: cmgrote
body:
## Why

AE returns **`Skipped`** as a real DAG status — both top-level (a run deduplicated against an in-flight one, or every node opted out) and per-node (downstream nodes bypassed after an upstream failure). Neither `DAGRunStatus` nor `DAGNodeStatus` had a `Skipped` member, so the defensive parsers (`_safe_run_status` / `_safe_node_status`) fell into their `except ValueError` branch, logged a traceback via `exc_info=True`, and mapped the value to **`PENDING`**.

Mapping a skipped run to PENDING mislabels it as *"never started"*: `poll_native_status` never observes a terminal status, runs out the full `stall_grace_seconds`, and raises a misleading **`NoWorkerOnTaskQueueError`** — even when the worker ran fine.

### Observed
On the openapi canonical-e2e leg in #2657, the connector **completed successfully** (`publish_completed=True … App completed`), yet the test failed with:
```
ValueError: 'Skipped' is not a valid DAGRunStatus      # the swallowed exc_info traceback
...
NoWorkerOnTaskQueueError: No DAG node started within 180s for run ... (top-level status=Pending)
```
The `status=Pending` in that message is the tell — it was really `Skipped`, remapped.

## Fix

- Add `SKIPPED = "Skipped"` to `DAGRunStatus` **and** `DAGNodeStatus`.
- Include it in `is_terminal` (a skipped run/node will not progress without re-submission); it is **not** a success, so `all_nodes_succeeded` / `failed_nodes` still fail the test — but now with the *true* outcome instead of a spurious no-worker timeout.
- Add a `⏭️` glyph for the poll-loop summary.

Because the status is now terminal, `poll_native_status` returns immediately (line ~692) instead of waiting out the stall grace.

## Tests

New `TestSkippedStatus`: parsing (`_safe_*` → `SKIPPED`, no longer `PENDING`), terminal/non-success semantics, and that a `Skipped` run returns fast without tripping the stall guard. Full testing-package suite: **331 passed**. `ruff@0.6.4` check + format clean.

## Note

This makes the harness *report* `Skipped` accurately; it does not address **why** openapi's run came back Skipped (likely AE dedup / idempotency collision on the shared tenant — a separate follow-up, same family as the mysql/metabase `credentials_name_key` duplicate).

## Summary

- rebuild every Origin overlay from the fully resolved source books on each figure apply
- stamp derived overlays with schema version 2 and preserve the existing dataset id
- retain only safe user organization/annotation fields when refreshing; clear stale corrections, formulas, row filters, exclusions, fits, and other geometry-dependent state
- let Graph Builder consume only overlays built with the current schema version
- document the lifecycle and update the Origin decode plan

## Why

PR #39 makes the editable Graph Builder remake use the corrected segmented overlay for one-book `X,Y,X,Y,...` worksheets. Persisted or preview-derived overlays created before those binding fixes could still be silently reused because provenance tracked only the figure id. That could reintroduce stale geometry even when current source-book resolution is correct.

This PR treats overlays as versioned derived data. It does not change Origin parsing, byte decoding, curve bindings, axis semantics, acquisition order, or renderer paths.

## Suggested Claude review / manual checks

1. Test after PR #39 (this PR is stacked on it).
2. Open a saved workspace containing an older Origin overlay, apply the figure, and confirm the overlay data is rebuilt while its dataset id/folder/tags/notes remain stable.
3. Re-run the Moke one-book multi-X Graph Builder remake and verify all three loops retain their own X channels and acquisition order.
4. Re-run a cross-book PNR overlay and verify all source books/curves remain present.
5. Confirm corrections, formulas, excluded rows, and filters from an old derived overlay do not attach to rebuilt geometry.

author: jasoncwang
body:
## Summary

Reworks `OutgoingTransactionFailureReason` so every value is an outcome an integrator acts on, and syncs the docs to match.

**Added** — granular payout failures, set at the payout-partner boundary:
- `PAYOUT_RETURNED` — receiving bank accepted then returned/reversed the payout
- `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — payout exceeds a recipient-, account-, or corridor-level limit
- `ACCOUNT_CANNOT_RECEIVE` — account exists but can't accept the payment (dormant/frozen/restricted/unsupported currency)
- `ACCOUNT_INVALID` — recipient account not found or details wrong
- `COMPLIANCE_REJECTED` — rejected on compliance grounds (sanctions/watchlist/KYC-AML)

**Removed** — the four values #629 added. Each names an internal step of how a payment is processed rather than something an integrator handles differently:
- `EXECUTION_FAILED_POST_DEBIT` and `SETTLEMENT_FAILED` say where on the way to settlement the failure happened. Both collapse into `QUOTE_EXECUTION_FAILED`, whose description now covers that whole path and states that a debited amount is refunded automatically.
- `TIMEOUT` and `MANUAL_REFUND` describe operator-initiated refunds. That outcome already surfaces on the refund object, whose `reason` enum carries `TIMEOUT` and `USER_CANCELLATION`.

`LSP_OPERATIONAL_FAILURE` was on this branch earlier and is removed for the same reason: an operational failure on the provider side reaches integrators as `QUOTE_EXECUTION_FAILED`, the same outcome to act on.

**Deprecated** in the description, still returned: `LIGHTNING_PAYMENT_FAILED` (superseded by `QUOTE_EXECUTION_FAILED`) and `COUNTERPARTY_POST_TX_FAILED` (coarse fallback for historical rows). `SCA_NOT_COMPLETED` (#762) is untouched — a customer letting an SCA challenge expire is a distinct, actionable outcome.

Final enum: `QUOTE_EXPIRED`, `QUOTE_EXECUTION_FAILED`, `FUNDING_AMOUNT_MISMATCH`, `SCA_NOT_COMPLETED`, `PAYOUT_RETURNED`, `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `ACCOUNT_CANNOT_RECEIVE`, `ACCOUNT_INVALID`, `COMPLIANCE_REJECTED`, `LIGHTNING_PAYMENT_FAILED`, `COUNTERPARTY_POST_TX_FAILED`.

## Breaking change

Removing four values is flagged by oasdiff as `request-property-enum-value-removed` (ERR), because `failureReason` also appears in the `webhook:outgoing-payment` and `webhook:agent-action` bodies. The PR carries the `breaking-change` label and needs API-reviewer approval.

The server-side mapping for the removed values has to be updated before clients are regenerated, or `failureReason` renders empty — the regression #629 was fixing.

## Changes

- **OpenAPI** (`OutgoingTransactionFailureReason.yaml` + bundle): the enum above, with per-value descriptions and deprecation notes.
- **Docs**: synced the failure-reasons table in `transaction-lifecycle.mdx` and the list in the `error-handling.mdx` snippet to the enum — dropped the non-existent `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`, reordered to enum order, and fixed a `FAILED` webhook example to use `ACCOUNT_INVALID`.

Rebased onto main, which added #629's values and #762's `SCA_NOT_COMPLETED`.

## Test plan

- `make build` — bundles cleanly; clean rebuild produces no diff
- `make lint-openapi` — 0 errors (redocly + spectral)

author: pfitzseb
body: An `UnresolvedImport` on a name the project declares as a dependency (`regular_packages` / `stdlib_packages` / `deved_packages`) now reports that the dependency's symbols could not be indexed/cached, rather than the generic "Failed to resolve" used for names that aren't in the environment at all (typo or missing dependency). The consequence clause (wildcard vs explicit) is unchanged, so existing messages for undeclared names are preserved.

author: itsneelabh
body:
## Phase 1 of publishing the framework Go modules to pkg.go.dev / deps.dev

This is the **prep** step. It makes every module's `go.mod` release-ready and CI-green, but **publishes nothing** — no tags are pushed here. Tagging (`core/v0.2.0` → … → `v0.2.0`) is a separate Phase 2, done after this merges.

### What this changes (57 `go.mod`s, zero `.go` files)
- **Framework modules** (`core`, `telemetry`, `ai`, `orchestration`, `resilience`, `memory`, root): point all inter-module `require`s at **`v0.2.0`** and add **`retract v0.1.0`** to the root module. The published `v0.1.0` carries a relative `replace` + an unresolvable `core` require, so external consumers cannot build it.
- **Examples** (51): normalize framework `require`s from the phantom `v0.9.1` to `v0.2.0`.

### Why the relative `replace` directives are intentionally KEPT
Go 1.17+ module-graph pruning must read each *required* module's `go.mod`. A `replace` redirects that read to local disk; `go.work use` does **not** (it only redirects package resolution). So removing the replaces before the `v0.2.0` tags exist breaks `go build` / `go test` / `go vet` with `unknown revision core/v0.2.0`.

The replaces are therefore load-bearing until tagging, and are dropped **per-module at tag time** in Phase 2 (`go mod edit -dropreplace` → `go mod tidy` → tag, bottom-up). Example replaces stay **permanently** — the default `Dockerfile.workspace` build resolves the framework from local source through them.

### Why `v0.2.0`
Honest successor to the burned `v0.1.0`; keeps runway before the `v1.0.0` / `/v2` semantic-import-versioning commitment. All seven modules are co-versioned.

### Validation
Full local run of the CI jobs (mirrors `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, on go1.26.5), all green across every module:
- **test** — `go build ./...` + `go test -race ./...`
- **lint** — golangci-lint v2.11.4 `run ./...`
- **vuln** — govulncheck v1.1.4 `./...`
- **examples** — `GOWORK=off`, `go mod tidy && go build ./...`

Rebased onto the latest `main` (including the `x/net v0.55.0` and `go.work → go1.26.5` security fixes); the example dep bumps were merged and only our `v0.2.0` normalization re-applied on top.

author: chaz-clark
body:
## Roadmap: AI conversation grader — engagement-mode scoring (mirror aimodes.ai)

Adds one roadmap entry under **Grading Workflow & TA Management**.

Captures the plan to reverse-engineer [aimodes.ai](https://aimodes.ai/) — Dr. Mark Keith's (BYU IS) research instrument that classifies *how* a user engages with an AI assistant — into our AI Log grader. It builds on `grader_follow_share_url.py` (which already fetches the transcript behind ChatGPT/Gemini share URLs), replacing today's coarse per-turn classifier with the aimodes framework:

- **8 engagement modes × 3 agency tiers** (Passivity → Partnership → Agency)
- per-message classification → tier distribution → intellectual-agency score (/100) → mode distribution vs. target → student archetype → strengths/growth

So permissive-AI-policy courses (m119, DS250) can grade the *quality* of a student's AI interaction on a defensible, published rubric. FERPA-safe (deid transcripts in the existing `grading/` pipeline). Sized **L**.

Doc-only; no code.
